news.Title: Oracle Has Incredible News for Intel Stock Investors
news.Content:
Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) witnessed a brutal sell-off last week after releasing its third-quarter results on Oct. 29, primarily due to weaker-than-expected guidance that led investors to press the panic button.

Intel's personal computer (PC)-focused client business is not in the best shape now due to a steep drop in PC sales. Of course, Intel needed to live up to Wall Street's expectations to justify the impressive surge the stock has witnessed since the beginning of 2025. However, the weakness in the PC market is beyond Intel's control.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Moreover, Intel is doing well in data centers, with its artificial intelligence (AI)-focused server chips in solid demand from hyperscalers and AI companies. Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) is one such company that will deploy Intel's server central processing units (CPUs) in large numbers. Let's look at the reasons why the Oracle contract could be a big one for Intel.

Image source: Getty Images.

Intel is poised to win big from Oracle's AI data center build-out

Just a couple of days ahead of Intel's quarterly report, the semiconductor giant announced a multiyear collaboration with Oracle to deploy its Xeon server CPUs. Oracle will deploy Intel's current and future generations of Xeon server CPUs to handle agentic AI workloads on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).

This bodes well for Intel, given that OCI revenue has been growing at a brisk pace. Oracle reported a 121% year-over-year increase in OCI revenue in the previous quarter to $7.4 billion. This segment can sustain its terrific momentum over the long run owing to Oracle's $664 billion in remaining performance obligation (RPO), the total value of contracts the company has yet to fulfill.

Oracle expects to accelerate the conversion of its RPO into revenue going forward, driven by the company's significant investments to bring additional data center capacity online. Intel will provide Oracle with "additional capacity and planned processor capabilities as customers extend existing enterprise systems with AI."

This should ensure strong growth in Intel's server CPU business. Notably, Intel estimates that the total addressable market (TAM) for server CPUs could increase 5x over the next five years, reaching $400 billion. Chipzilla's ability to land a major customer like Oracle should allow it to capture a significant share of this massive opportunity.

Story Continues

As a result, I won't be surprised to see Intel's data center and AI (DCAI) segment sustain the healthy growth that it has been clocking.

Intel's data center growth is accelerating

Intel's DCAI segment revenue increased by 78% year over year in Q3 to $7.3 billion. For comparison, the company's DCAI revenue increased by 22% year over year in Q1 and by 59% in Q2.

Importantly, Intel management's comments on the latest earnings call indicate that its DCAI revenue will continue to grow at a solid pace, which isn't surprising, given the interest in its server CPUs from a hyperscaler such as Oracle. Specifically, Intel notes that demand signals from its data center customers are strengthening, primarily due to the growing adoption of agentic AI, which is driving increased server CPU demand.

As a result, Intel expects demand for its data center CPUs to outstrip supply in 2027 and 2028. This should allow Intel to implement more price hikes given its position as the dominant player in the x86 server CPU market. Though Intel has been losing ground to Advanced Micro Devices in this niche, it still holds an impressive market share of 65.5%, according to Mercury Research.

The Oracle partnership should help Intel maintain its dominance in server CPUs, paving the way for further growth in revenue and earnings. After all, Intel is expected to increase CPU prices by 10% next year, which could positively impact the company's bottom-line performance.

What's worth noting is that there has been a substantial improvement in Intel's long-term earnings per share (EPS) growth expectations this year.

INTC EPS LT Growth Estimates data by YCharts

So, while Intel stock has taken a big beating after its latest quarterly report, the long-term prospects still appear to be sound. Throw in the fact that Intel is trading at an attractive 34 times forward earnings, a discount to the Nasdaq Composite index's average earnings multiple of 39, and it is easy to see why the stock is worth buying following its recent pullback.

So, savvy investors would do well to look at the bigger picture and consider using this semiconductor stock's drop to buy more shares, as its accelerating data center business could eventually help it step on the gas once again.

news.Title: SpaceX, Tesla stocks tumble as Democratic sweep raises questions on merger prospects
news.Content:
SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) stocks extended declines on Thursday, each dropping roughly 9%. Shares of the Elon Musk-led companies were pounded after Democrats won control of the House and Senate this week, raising concerns over regulatory hurdles for data center buildouts in the US, and merger aspirations between the two companies.

"We will believe a SpaceX/Tesla merger happens but now faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap to get this deal done in 2027 given this new political blue roadmap in DC/Texas," Yorkville's partner and managing director Dan Ives wrote on Thursday.

Worries over a slowdown in data center buildouts also dampened shares of Texas-based SpaceX, which has increasingly leaned into AI compute as a revenue source.

Ives said while Big Tech and hyperscaler capex should still easily exceed $1 trillion in 2027, the growth rate into 2028 "will clearly moderate significantly as the data center buildout comes at a much slower pace given the political map, especially in the state of Texas."

On Wednesday, Goldman Sachs analysts also calculated, "Democratic wins at the state and local level are likely to lead to short-term data center moratoria, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.

news.Title: SMCI Stock Falls 5.7% After Q1 Results: Should You Hold or Fold?
news.Content:
Super Micro Computer SMCI shares have lost 5.7% since it released its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 3, 2026. The stock has plunged 31.9% in the past one month, underperforming the Zacks Computer- Storage Devices industry and the sector's decline of 13.2% and 24.7%, respectively.

SMCI One-Month Performance Chart

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The decline in stock price has led SMCI stock to trade at a discounted price-to-sales multiple of 0.27X, below its industry's P/S of 2.19X. The undervaluation is further substantiated by a Zacks Value Score of B.

SMCI Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Given these dynamics, investors are wondering if it's the right time to buy, sell or hold SMCI stock. Let's delve deeper into the fundamentals, growth drivers, competitive positioning, valuation and risks surrounding the company to better assess its long-term investment potential.

SMCI Stock Declines in Tune With the Broader Technology Market

The decline in SMCI's stock price has come amid a broader sell-off in AI-related stocks spanning hyperscalers, semiconductor companies and AI infrastructure providers, as investors increasingly question whether massive AI investments will generate sufficient returns. Since SMCI supplies its products to these infrastructure providers, SMCI's stock has also been affected.

Furthermore, the recent decline after the earnings can mainly be attributed to investors assessing the sustainability of its rapid revenue growth and the pressure on profitability. The company reported record net sales of $19.95 billion, up 298% year over year and 79% sequentially. However, gross margin declined to 12.7% from 17.5% in the preceding quarter, while non-GAAP gross margin fell 480 basis points sequentially to 12.8%.

Management attributed the decline primarily to an increase in AI-related revenue mix, which rose to 71% from 59% in the previous quarter. Large-scale AI data center deployments carry lower gross margins than the more diversified enterprise and channel businesses, while the recognition of certain lower-margin deferred revenues further weighed on profitability.

Investor concerns were also heightened by Super Micro Computer's high customer concentration. During the quarter, one large data center customer accounted for 44% of total revenue compared with 28% for fiscal 2026 as a whole. Additionally, two customers represented 49% and 17% of accounts receivable at the end of the quarter. However, Super Micro Computer's exposure to AI infrastructure continues to provide a powerful foundation for growth.

Story Continues

SMCI's Strategic Chip Partnerships Accelerate AI Platform Adoption

Super Micro Computer continues to partner with leading semiconductor companies, including NVIDIA NVDA, Advanced Micro Devices AMD and Intel INTC, to bring in the newest AI systems as a competitive advantage. The company is shipping high-volume NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack systems and has launched NVIDIA Rubin and Vera Rubin CPU rack solutions that are ready to ship. It also continues to support the NVIDIA GB300 NVL72, HGX B300 and RTX 6000 Pro platforms.

On the Advanced Micro Devices front, demand for MI350 and MI355X systems remains strong as the company advances its Helios and MI450 Total Solutions. Super Micro Computer is also progressing with Intel Xeon 6+ platforms alongside Arm AGI CPU-based systems optimized for agentic AI workloads. Its broad participation across major processor ecosystems and successive AI platform generations enhances customer flexibility and creates opportunities to capture demand as computing architectures evolve.

Super Micro Computer is expanding its role from a server and storage provider to a comprehensive data-center infrastructure solutions company through its Data Center Building Block Solutions (DCBBS) portfolio. The integrated offering encompasses GPU and CPU servers, enterprise storage, direct liquid cooling, power infrastructure, high-speed switches, networking, data-center management software and lifecycle services.

By combining modular engineering with application-optimized systems, Super Micro Computer can address a broad range of enterprise, cloud, AI and edge workloads. Management highlighted DCBBS' ability to accelerate time-to-delivery and time-to-online, improve system uptime and lower total cost of ownership. The portfolio is further enhanced by SuperCloud Composer, Super Micro Data Center Manager and Super Micro Operations Manager, which provide integrated hardware management, orchestration and operational capabilities.

The increasing power and thermal requirements of AI data centers are creating significant opportunities for Super Micro Computer's direct liquid-cooling capabilities. The company is expanding its liquid-cooled rack-scale portfolio, with solutions designed to support high-density AI infrastructure and integrated data-center deployments. Its DCBBS portfolio incorporates liquid-cooling components, including cold plates, coolant distribution units, manifolds, chilled doors and cooling towers, enabling customers to deploy fully integrated infrastructure.

Following a record first-quarter fiscal 2027 performance, with revenues reaching $19.9 billion, management increased its full-year revenue target to $72 billion to $82 billion, approximately 12% higher than the previous guidance set one quarter ago. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SMCI's fiscal 2027 guidance for revenues and earnings suggests year-over-year growth of 31% and 16.5%, respectively. Estimates for SMCI's fiscal 2027 earnings have been revised upward in the past 30 days.

Conclusion: Hold SMCI Stock Now

Super Micro Computer's strong AI infrastructure exposure, expanding DCBBS portfolio, strategic chip partnerships and upward revision to fiscal 2027 revenue guidance highlight its long-term growth potential. While the company's growth prospects remain compelling, investors should monitor its ability to sustain revenue momentum while improving profitability. Given the balance between strong growth opportunities and near-term execution risks, holding SMCI stock appears prudent at present. SMCI currently carries Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). news.Title: Nvidia vs. Taiwan Semiconductor: The AI Revolution Is Big Enough for Both. Here's the Better Buy.
news.Content:
The semiconductor industry has been supercharged in recent years by the rise and rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), which isn't surprising, as chips are essential for running AI applications in data centers, smartphones, computers, vehicles, robots, and factories.

Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) are two of the most important players in the semiconductor space, which explains why they have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI-fueled semiconductor boom. Let's see why these semiconductor stocks will continue capitalizing on the AI chip market's growth, and which one is the better buy for the long run.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia and TSMC have been the cornerstone of the AI market's growth

Nvidia's dominant position in the graphics processing unit (GPU) space allowed it to quickly capitalize on the booming demand for AI chips, which were primarily used for training large language models (LLMs) during the initial phases of the AI rollout. Popular AI models, such as ChatGPT, Grok, Qwen, and others, have been trained using Nvidia's chips.

The chip giant is now dominating the inference space as well, with a market share of more than 70%. This is great news for Nvidia investors, as AI compute is now shifting from training to inference. In fact, inference is expected to generate more revenue than training-oriented workloads in 2026, according to the Futurum Group.

At the same time, the emergence of new AI niches will expand Nvidia's addressable market. Physical AI, for example, is expected to grow substantially over the long run. Physical AI refers to the integration of AI into objects that can be deployed in the real world, such as humanoid robots, autonomous vehicles, drones, and factory robots. Mordor Intelligence predicts that the physical AI market could clock annual growth of 37% through 2031.

This expansion of AI beyond data centers should ensure that Nvidia's healthy growth continues. Not surprisingly, analysts expect Nvidia's earnings to more than double in just two fiscal years, and the long-term earnings per share (EPS) growth estimate of 50% (per YCharts) suggests it can sustain its momentum for a long time.

YCharts

Meanwhile, TSMC has been riding Nvidia's coattails by virtue of being the latter's foundry partner. Nvidia is a fabless chipmaker that utilizes TSMC's semiconductor manufacturing and packaging services to bring its chip designs into the physical form. However, the good part about TSMC is that it manufactures chips for multiple customers, including Apple , Sony , MediaTek , Broadcom , Marvell , and others.

Story Continues

TSMC's broad customer base allows it to serve multiple AI-focused end markets, including smartphones, personal computers, robots, and data centers. So, TSMC seems better-positioned to capitalize on the semiconductor industry's long-term growth, which will be primarily fueled by AI. Industry association SEMI estimates that the global semiconductor industry's revenue reached $1 trillion in the first eight months of 2026.

McKinsey expects the industry to generate $2.3 trillion in revenue in 2030. TSMC's status as the world's leading third-party chip manufacturer with a 73% market share, according to Counterpoint Research, makes it one of the best ways to play this lucrative space. Also, TSMC's dominant share explains why it is the price maker, meaning its price hikes are likely to be accepted by customers, including Nvidia.

A recent report from Taiwan-based financial newspaper Commercial Times notes that TSMC could increase advanced chip packaging prices by up to 20%. So, I won't be surprised to see TSMC's margins heading higher in the future following an impressive jump this year.

The verdict

Both Nvidia and TSMC can deliver robust long-term growth. In fact, as the following chart tells us, there isn't much difference in the potential long-term EPS growth both companies are anticipated to deliver.

That's why we will look at their valuations to determine which AI stock you should consider buying right now.

So, TSMC and Nvidia are closely matched on the valuation front as well. Also, we have seen that both companies are projected to achieve nearly identical earnings growth over the long run. So, investors can consider buying either of these semiconductor stocks to capitalize on the AI infrastructure boom. Both companies dominate their respective niches in chip designing and manufacturing, which is why they are likely to grow at solid rates in the long run.

Moreover, TSMC and Nvidia are attractively valued despite their healthy growth rates. The tech-laden Nasdaq Composite index, for comparison, has a price-to-earnings ratio of 40. So, investors are getting a solid deal on these semiconductor stocks, and buying either of them could prove to be a profitable long-term move for the reasons discussed in this article.

news.Title: Apple Makes Surprising Move to Rein In AI Spending
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) is cutting how much some employees can spend on artificial-intelligence tools, adding a fresh twist to the company's broader push to make AI a bigger part of everyday work. Apple lowered the daily AI spending allowance for some engineers to $200 from $300 last month, according to Bloomberg. The company is considering further reductions to as little as $100 per day for some engineering teams. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Sign with MELI. Is AAPL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Outside engineering, the limits could become even tighter. Some non-engineering groups already operate with $100 daily caps, while certain teams could eventually be limited to as little as $25 per day . Employees who need more capacity can seek exemptions from senior executives. The budgets cover the cost of AI tokens consumed through tools including OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude and Google's Gemini. Engineers typically have larger allowances because coding and software-development tasks can consume substantial numbers of tokens. The move does not necessarily mean Apple is backing away from AI. Instead, Bloomberg reported that the company is still trying to expand AI usage across engineering and internal operations while simultaneously tightening spending controls. Apple has also encouraged some teams to use cheaper models or shift certain workloads toward on-device AI. That puts Apple at the center of a wider industry shift. Technology companies initially encouraged employees to experiment aggressively with AI coding assistants and other generative tools. Now, as token bills rise, companies are starting to examine whether the productivity improvements justify the expense. Reuters noted that Goldman Sachs has also restricted access to some AI coding tools following reviews of productivity and risk. Investor Takeaway I think the bigger story is that AI spending is starting to face the same return-on-investment discipline as every other corporate expense . Cutting an engineer's daily limit from $300 to $200 does not meaningfully change Apple's balance sheet by itself. What matters is the mindset behind it. Companies spent much of the AI boom rewarding experimentation and usage. Now they increasingly want evidence that every additional token is actually improving productivity. For Apple, that could ultimately be positive if it encourages more efficient model selection, greater use of on-device processing and tighter control over third-party AI costs. Story Continues The risk is that aggressive cost limits slow employee experimentation at a time when Apple is still trying to catch up in AI. For investors, the key things to watch are internal AI adoption, spending discipline, on-device model usage, developer productivity and whether Apple can expand AI capabilities without letting operating costs rise uncontrollably . Apple is not abandoning AI. It is starting to ask what the AI is actually worth. AAPL GF Value chart AAPL GF Value chart Outside engineering, the limits could become even tighter.

news.Title: Meta's AI Buildout Runs Into a Political Problem
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) is warning that the U.S. midterm elections may make new data-center construction significantly harder, adding a fresh political obstacle to the company's massive AI infrastructure expansion. Meta President Dina Powell McCormick said at the Wall Street Journal Tech conference that many different factors contributed to Democrats' election victories, but data-center opposition was clearly one of them. She said starting entirely new projects could become more challenging, while expanding existing campuses may be easier. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with META. Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. That warning is already being backed up by election results. Voters rejected or restricted nearly all of the 41 data-center-related ballot measures tracked across multiple states, while Democratic gubernatorial victories in Texas, Georgia, and Ohio came with promises of tougher scrutiny on AI infrastructure. Texas is especially important. The state represents roughly a quarter of planned U.S. data-center capacity, and governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has called for a pause on new approvals until lawmakers address electricity costs, water usage, environmental concerns, and local protections. That creates a direct challenge for Meta and other hyperscalers. The companies are already spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI infrastructure, but the next constraint may not be chips or capital. It may be political permission to build. There is also an unexpected upside. Needham argues that tighter regulation could improve returns on invested capital for established hyperscalers such as Meta, Amazon, and Google by slowing supply growth and making existing capacity more valuable. That view helped explain why large tech stocks rallied after the election even as smaller data-center developers sold off. Reuters reported that investors added hundreds of billions of dollars in market value to major hyperscalers as they considered the possibility that slower new construction could protect existing infrastructure economics. Investor Takeaway I think the biggest shift is that AI infrastructure has become a political problem, not just a financing problem . Meta can raise capital. It can buy chips. It can sign power agreements. But if communities and state governments increasingly resist new data centers, future capacity could become slower and more expensive to build. That cuts both ways for investors. Story Continues It could delay Meta's expansion plans and raise costs, but it could also make already-permitted campuses more valuable and reduce the risk of industry overbuilding. For investors, the key things to watch are state permitting rules, power costs, Texas policy, Meta's capex guidance, and whether more hyperscalers shift projects overseas or toward existing campuses . The AI race is still about compute. Getting permission to build it may now be the harder part. META GF Value chart META GF Value chart That warning is already being backed up by election results.

news.Title: Apple seeks to raise up to $7 billion in seven-tranche bond offering
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Apple Inc. is seeking to raise up to $7 billion through a seven-tranche U.S. dollar bond offering, returning to the debt market as major technology companies ramp up borrowing amid significant investment requirements.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The iPhone maker's offering is expected to price Wednesday, November 5, with the company marketing both fixed- and floating-rate notes, according to Bloomberg News.

The proposed deal includes floating-rate notes due in 2028 and 2029, alongside fixed-rate securities with maturities in 2028, 2029, 2031, 2033 and 2036.

Initial price guidance on the fixed-rate portions ranges from 45 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries for the two-year notes to 80 basis points for the 10-year securities. The floating-rate tranches are being marketed at spreads equivalent to SOFR.

Bank of America, Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan are managing the transaction. Apple's debt carries expected ratings of Aaa from Moody's and AA+ from S&P.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Apple said proceeds would be used for general corporate purposes, including share repurchases, dividend payments, working capital, capital expenditures, acquisitions and debt repayment.

The offering comes amid a wave of borrowing by major technology companies. Microsoft priced a $25 billion bond offering last week, while Meta Platforms raised $15 billion in a five-part U.S. dollar offering on Tuesday. Oracle also issued $10 billion in bonds, and Alphabet raised €6 billion through a euro-denominated offering.

However, Apple's borrowing comes from a different financial position than that of many of its hyperscaler peers. Bloomberg Intelligence senior credit analyst Robert Schiffman described the offering as more opportunistic than funding-driven, noting that Apple has approximately $137 billion in cash and generates around $145 billion in annual operating cash flow.

With debt of roughly $80 billion and comparatively modest AI infrastructure spending, Apple has considerable flexibility to finance its investment requirements internally. Bloomberg Intelligence argues that additional borrowing is unlikely to materially affect Apple's Aaa/AA+ credit profile or borrowing spreads, while providing the company with additional flexibility to support share repurchases and dividends.

Story Continues

The distinction highlights two different financing priorities across Big Tech: companies such as Microsoft, Meta and Oracle are borrowing heavily amid enormous AI infrastructure commitments, while Apple can tap the debt market without facing the same scale of investment requirements.

Apple's last bond offering was a $4.5 billion sale in May 2025. The new offering would represent a larger transaction if it reaches the indicated maximum of $7 billion, an increase of approximately 56%.

news.Title: CEO Andy Jassy Just Told Investors That AWS Can Grow Revenue 40% in 2027 and 2028 and Eventually Become a Trillion-Dollar Business. Is It Enough to Get Wall Street on Board?
news.Content:
Although investors are extremely worried about an artificial intelligence bubble and when it might pop, it's also become clear that the market has significantly raised its threshold for evaluating large hyperscaler and AI stocks. As of this writing, the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF has declined more than 6% over the past month, despite many earnings reports showing signs that AI is benefiting their businesses.

For instance, on Amazon 's (NASDAQ: AMZN) third-quarter earnings call, CEO Andy Jassy told analysts that he expects the company's cloud business, Amazon Web Services (AWS) , to grow revenue by more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028, becoming a trillion-dollar business at some point in the next five to 10 years.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Is this enough for Wall Street to get on board?

AI is leading to strong growth

It's hard to look at Amazon's third-quarter earnings and say AI isn't significantly benefiting the business. AWS experienced 39.3% year-over-year revenue growth, the highest level seen in nearly five years. Revenue also achieved an annualized run rate of $184 billion.

AWS benefits from AI in several ways, including selling compute capacity, renting out its custom chips, and selling access to AI models, tools, and agents.

In the third quarter, AWS accounted for nearly 23% of the company's total revenue but nearly 64% of its total operating profit, so AWS has by far the best margins of the three business lines.

AWS was Amazon's traditional cloud business, but it's clear that AI has become the big driver moving forward.

On the earnings call, Jassy told investors, "Enterprises are still very early in using inference at scale, and yet inference already accounts for well over half of AWS's AI revenue and is growing, and we have a lot of training revenue as well."

Furthermore, the AWS backlog is now $578 billion, driven by strong demand for core infrastructure and generative AI services.

Will it be enough?

The day after its earnings report, Amazon stock actually fell.

Investors remain concerned about the high spending required to achieve these growth rates at AWS. Amazon continues to guide for $220 billion in capital expenditures this year. Jassy also told analysts the company expects to spend "meaningfully more in 2027."

Story Continues

This intense level of spending has resulted in negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion for the company over the past 12 months, which has concerned the market.

Interestingly, Wall Street believes AWS's growth will materialize. Consensus estimates project at least 40% growth in AWS revenue in 2027 and 2028, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence . On Amazon's third-quarter earnings call, Jassy also came across as increasingly bullish about AWS's ability to generate compelling returns.

"We continue to accelerate our capex payback and have even more conviction than we already had that the investment we're making in AWS will yield a much larger revenue and free cash flow-generating business than we would have imagined a couple of years ago, with strong return on invested capital," Jassy said, adding that he views AI as "a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity." "We have a compelling flywheel spinning in AWS."

One reason the earnings report may not have received the response the company was looking for is that quarterly year-over-year growth expectations had climbed as high as 44% before the quarter, according to analysts at William Blair.

The real issue may simply be the unknown. While AI shows no signs of slowing, safety concerns have mounted, leading investors to wonder what could happen to a major AI company or the AI trade if a major security breach or safety event occurs.

Furthermore, investors also worry that AI might cannibalize existing businesses. For Amazon, there are concerns about how AI agents could impact Amazon's massive e-commerce and ads business.

The concerns might be overblown, but it's really difficult to imagine what AI looks like in the future. Meanwhile, companies like Amazon are spending hundreds of billions on AI, making it a make-or-break bet.

That's why expectations are so high -- because of the risks. Surely, if Amazon executes as Jassy says, the stock will benefit. But it's hard for investors to look that far ahead right now, even if they believe in the company's ability to capitalize on AI.

news.Title: Cisco Systems (CSCO) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
news.Content:
Cisco Systems (CSCO) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended October 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 12. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This seller of routers, switches, software and services is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.33 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +33%.

Revenues are expected to be $18.09 billion, up 21.5% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.12% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

Story Continues

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Cisco?

For Cisco, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.51%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Cisco will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Cisco would post earnings of $1.17 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.22, delivering a surprise of +4.27%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Cisco doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

news.Title: QCOM Q4 Earnings Call Highlights Data Center Ramp and Handset Risks
news.Content:
QUALCOMM Incorporated QCOM positioned data centers and automotive chips as the engines of its next growth phase during its fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call. Management emphasized diversification even as smartphone demand and the Apple modem transition weigh on its legacy business.

The company reported non-GAAP earnings of $2.17 per share against the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.16. Revenue of $10.44 billion topped the $10.15 billion consensus, providing context for a call focused on fiscal 2027 execution.

QUALCOMM Incorporated Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

QUALCOMM Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | QUALCOMM Incorporated Quote

QCOM Sets Out an Ambitious Data Center Ramp

CEO Cristiano Amon said data center revenue should reach $5 billion in fiscal 2027, beginning with more than $650 million in the December quarter. The business is expected to exit fiscal 2027 at a $7 billion annualized rate.

CFO and COO Akash Palkhiwala said two hyperscaler relationships, including Amazon, will account for most of the fiscal 2027 target. Custom AI accelerator silicon will lead the contribution, followed by connectivity products.

During JPMorgan's questions about the customer ramp, Palkhiwala said supply, rather than demand, would constrain upside beyond the target. Amon also highlighted progress in high-bandwidth compute efficiency and new CPU customer prospects beyond Meta.

Qualcomm's Automotive Expansion Gains Scale

Amon said automotive revenue reached an approximately $8 billion annualized run rate at fiscal year-end, exceeding the company's earlier $7 billion expectation. Fifth-generation Snapdragon Digital Chassis shipments began during the September quarter.

Palkhiwala reported automotive quarterly revenue of $2 billion, up 89% year over year. He linked that growth to integrated compute modules and adoption of newer vehicle platforms.

When Melius Research questioned whether advance purchasing ahead of price increases contributed to performance, Amon attributed growth mainly to design wins becoming revenue. He said fifth-generation platforms contain substantially more silicon than older versions.

QCOM Keeps a Restrained Handset Outlook

Amon said the company assumes global handset units will be flat to down in calendar 2027. He described the June quarter as the bottom for its China Android business, followed by sequential growth.

Palkhiwala projected a mid-single-digit sequential decline in first-quarter fiscal 2027 QCT handset revenue as Android growth is offset by reduced Apple sales. Management expects handsets to account for less than half of total revenue in fiscal 2027.

Story Continues

Bernstein challenged whether Android improvements reflected purchases ahead of price increases. Palkhiwala cited lean channel inventories, while Amon said pricing changes primarily apply to newer phone platforms, limiting that effect.

Qualcomm Explains the Margin Trade-Off

Palkhiwala guided first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue to $10.4 billion-$11.2 billion and non-GAAP earnings to $2.15-$2.35 per share. The QCT segment's expected earnings-before-tax margin is 20-22%.

He explained that bringing data center operations into QCT reduces the segment margin outlook by three percentage points because of investment ahead of revenue. The company retains its longer-term QCT margin target of 30%.

In response to TD Cowen, Palkhiwala said product price increases should restore baseline gross margins toward the low end of the historical 48-50% range. Data center custom silicon would dilute gross margins but add to operating margins.

QCOM Secures Licensing and Network Commitments

Amon highlighted licensing renewals with Apple, Huawei and Transsion, extending stability for the company's patent business. Palkhiwala said the renewals leave the licensing revenue run rate unchanged.

Responding to Morgan Stanley, Palkhiwala indicated the agreements preserved underlying royalty economics, without disclosing contract terms. The next major renewal cycle begins in fiscal 2030.

Amon also outlined a multiyear SpaceX agreement to supply technology for Starlink Mobile's terrestrial 5G network. During Wolfe Research's questions, he said deployment begins in 2027, with revenue becoming more relevant in fiscal 2028.

Qualcomm Focuses on Delivering Its Diversification Plan

Amon framed fiscal 2027 as a shift from building new businesses to scaling them. Management expects combined non-handset QCT revenue to grow more than 60% year over year.

The key priorities are scaling data center deliveries, sustaining automotive design-win conversions and managing handset weakness. The call paired confidence in newer businesses with caution about smartphone demand and near-term margins.

QCOM's Zacks Rank and Style Scores

QCOM carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), reflecting an unfavorable earnings-estimate revision profile. Its Value and Growth Scores are both D, while its Momentum Score is A. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

The VGM Score  of D indicates weaker combined value, growth and momentum characteristics despite the strong standalone Momentum Score. Zacks Rank and Style Scores are complementary signals, and the rank can change as analysts revise estimates following the reported results.

news.Title: Qualcomm tops Q4 estimates, but Q1 earnings outlook falls short sending stock lower
news.Content:
Qualcomm ( QCOM ) reported fourth quarter earnings after the bell Wednesday, topping expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated Q1 revenue outlook.

But a lower-than-expected midpoint for its earnings per share (EPS) forecast sent the stock tumbling more than 11% in pre-market action.

For Q4, Qualcomm reported adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.17 on revenue of $10.32 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $2.16 and revenue of $10.12 billion.

The company saw EPS of $3 and revenue of $11.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Qualcomm also offered Q1 revenue guidance of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion, with the midpoint ahead of Wall Street's $10.6 billion outlook.

EPS, however, is set to come in between $2.15 and $2.35, with a midpoint of $2.25. Analysts were looking for $2.32

Qualcomm's QCT segment, which includes handset and automotive sales, declined 8% year over year but topped Wall Street's Q4 expectations on revenue of $9 billion. Analysts were calling for $8.8 billion.

The bulk of that drop came from Qualcomm's handset business, which saw revenue plunge 26% year over year to $5.1 billion. Analysts were looking for $5.3 billion.

Qualcomm stock fell 10% before the bell on Thursday.

But the company's automotive segment helped offset some of that impact, with sales increasing 89% to $2 billion.

Qualcomm's QTL business line saw revenue of $1.3 billion for the quarter.

The chip giant is in the midst of a wide-ranging effort to bolster its data center, automotive, edge computing, and PC businesses, as it works to reduce its dependence on smartphone chip sales.

On Wednesday, Qualcomm announced a deal to provide technology to SpaceX's ( SPCX ) Starlink as the satellite networking giant ramps up its effort to establish a terrestrial network that would rival AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ).

In late October, Qualcomm said it is working with Anduril on a product line called BlueChip focused on reshoring computer manufacturing. The companies say they'll start by focusing on a laptop that will use Qualcomm's Snapdragon X series chips.

And in September, the company signed an agreement with Amazon for custom chips designed for its AWS AI infrastructure.

But Qualcomm, like the rest of the consumer electronics industry, is also contending with the impact of the memory and storage shortage, which has forced companies to raise prices on everything from smartphones to laptops, sending demand plummeting.

During its fourth quarter earnings announcement on Monday, Apple noted that the memory crisis will continue to cut into margins going forward. Intel ( INTC ) and AMD ( AMD ) also said they expect PC sales to decline in the coming quarter, sending shares of Intel plunging nearly 29% .

news.Title: Apple Stock Is Up 22%, but 1 Slowing Business Could Test That Valuation
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) stock is up about 22% this year through Nov. 3, roughly double the S&P 500 's (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) 11% gain. That run has pushed the stock to a valuation of about 38 times earnings. One reason Apple has deserved that premium is steady growth in its high-margin services business, making the recent slowdown worth a closer look.

In Apple's fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, which ended Sept. 26, services growth slowed to 10% year over year, down from about 12% the prior quarter, and management said it expects 8% to 9% in fiscal 2027 Q1, citing headwinds from third-party licensing and shifts in foreign currency exchange rates. Notably, in Apple's annual report for fiscal 2026, it did not describe the App Store as a driver of services segment growth, listing only advertising and cloud services.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The slowing growth of the services business matters because it is Apple's profit engine. Services revenue came with a 76% gross margin last fiscal year, nearly double its 39% gross margin on products. And services accounted for 40% of Apple's gross profit.

Earnings grew 13.5% year over year in fiscal Q4, but analysts are modeling for annual growth of less than 11% over the long term. If growth in services continues to weaken, investors may re-rate the stock to a lower earnings multiple, which could limit its upside potential.

The rest of Apple's business looks strong. Revenue rose 15% in fiscal 2026 to a record $479 billion as iPhone sales grew 17% last quarter and Mac sales jumped 24%. Apple expects the current holiday quarter to be "the best quarter for revenue in the history of the company," as it will be the first full quarter of sales for the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable smartphone.

With the stock trading at about 38 times earnings, investors are paying for a lot of anticipated growth. The one thing to watch is whether the next quarter's services growth lands within or above the 8% to 9% forecast range. If it falls short, the stock's current premium valuation could become harder to justify.

news.Title: Qualcomm, Micron, Sandisk and Arm Holdings stocks sink, leading chip sector lower
news.Content:
Chip stocks slipped on Thursday, extending declines from the day before. Despite a broader market rally on Wednesday following Democrats' midterm election victory, semiconductor stocks moved lower amid the threat that stricter regulation could slow data center construction.

Semiconductor stocks, which drove the AI trade higher this year, have been volatile since the summer. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) fell by more than 3% in premarket trading, trimming the index's year-to-date gains to roughly 40%.

The declines were led by Qualcomm ( QCOM ), which issued an underwhelming profit forecast , signaling that higher-cost components are weighing on the smartphone processor maker.

Shares of Arm Holdings ( ARM ) also fell after the chip designer issued revenue guidance that, while slightly above consensus, failed to impress investors who priced in a higher range amid the AI boom.

Micron Technology ( MU ) stock also declined after the memory chipmaker paused plans for a Taiwanese plant due to labor disputes. Sandisk ( SDNK ) slid 6%, extending declines from 7% in the prior session.

SK Hynix ( SKHY ) was also trading lower in premarket trading after shares of the South Korean memory maker tumbled overseas, alongside Samsung Electronics ( 005930.K S ).

At the same time, shares of US chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) declined nearly 3%, while AMD ( AMD ) plunged 4%; Nvidia ( NVDA ) also extended declines from the prior session.

At the same time, shares of US chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) declined nearly 3%, while AMD ( AMD ) plunged 4%; Nvidia ( NVDA ) also extended declines from the prior session.

news.Title: Morgan Stanley cuts Cisco rating, sees pull-forward risk after strong run
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Morgan Stanley downgraded Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) to Equal-weight from Overweight and cut its price target to $120 from $135 in a note Thursday, telling investors that the stock's strong rally leaves less room for upside ahead of its fiscal first-quarter results.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Analyst Meta Marshall noted that Cisco shares are up 43% over the past 12 months, compared with a 14% gain for the S&P 500.

The stock has rerated to trade in line with the index at about 19 times forward earnings, and Marshall said much of the AI-driven rerating is now reflected in the price.

Morgan Stanley also flagged concerns about pull-forward, or customers ordering early to get ahead of planned price increases, which could flatter near-term sales. The bank added that a rising mix of lower-margin hardware sold to hyperscalers is weighing on gross margins.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

"CSCO can continue to appreciate through earnings growth, but strong expectations and gross margin headwinds from AI business leave less room for upside," Marshall wrote.

The analyst said recent share price reactions to earnings from Fortinet and F5 highlight the higher bar for networking and cybersecurity stocks.

Morgan Stanley still sees several years of double-digit growth for Cisco, largely driven by cloud customers. However, it said growth will rely increasingly on AI revenue once the company laps its pricing increases in fiscal 2028.

"We remain constructive on Cisco's fundamentals, but see a more balanced risk/reward at current levels," the analyst said.

news.Title: Should You Add ANET Stock to Your Portfolio Post Solid Q3 Earnings?
news.Content:
Arista Networks, Inc. ANET reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with revenues and adjusted earnings soaring year over year, driven by robust demand trends. Quarterly revenues surged 58.5% year over year to $3.66 billion, exceeding the consensus estimate of $3.31 billion by 10.41%. This marked the company's strongest annual revenue growth since its IPO, driven by robust artificial intelligence (AI) networking demand, enterprise expansion and improved supply chain execution. Arista also surpassed 100 Etherlink customers.

On a non-GAAP basis, earnings rose 55.8% year over year to $1.20 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $1.08 by 11.11%. Innovative product launches and steady customer additions backed by the company's best-in-class portfolio strength led to top-line expansion, while steady margin improvement contributed to earnings growth.

ANET Rides on Strong AI Networking Demand

Arista witnessed accelerating demand for its AI networking solutions as customers expanded investments in large-scale AI infrastructure. The company's Ethernet-based networking architecture supports AI training and inference workloads across scale-out and scale-across deployments, enabling efficient connectivity across distributed computing environments.

Arista continues to expand its Etherlink portfolio, comprising at least 25 switches designed for AI networking applications. Management highlighted growing adoption of scale-across networking, which connects computing resources across multiple data centers. It expects this architecture to represent an increasing portion of AI networking deployments in 2027. The company is also advancing rack-scale networking designs through partnerships with leading accelerator providers. Initial scale-up trials are expected in 2027, with production anticipated in 2028.

Portfolio Strength Fuels Growth

Arista offers one of the broadest product lines of data center and campus Ethernet switches and routers in the industry, with industry-leading capacity, low latency, port density and power efficiency. Over the years, the company has introduced various products to meet the rising demands of AI/ML-driven network architectures. These innovations have enabled Arista to deliver a superior customer experience and increase customer engagement.

Arista has expanded its software platform beyond cloud data centers through automation, campus networking, routing and AI networking capabilities. The company's unified EOS (Extensible Operating System) architecture enables programmable networking across client, campus, cloud and AI environments while supporting advanced routing, observability and operational automation.

With customers deploying transformative cloud networking solutions, the company has announced several additions to its multi-cloud and cloud-native software product family with CloudEOS Edge. It has introduced cognitive Wi-Fi software that delivers intelligent application identification, automated troubleshooting and location services. The versatility of Arista's unified software stack across various use cases, including WAN routing and campus and data center infrastructure, has helped it to record steady top-line growth.

Story Continues

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Price Performance

Arista has surged 33.2% over the past year against the industry's decline of 3.1%. It has lagged peers like Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company HPE and Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO. While Hewlett Packard has gained 114.1%, Cisco is up 45.8% over this period.

One-Year ANET Stock Price Performance

Estimate Revision Trend

Earnings estimates for Arista for 2026 and 2027 have increased 25.2% and 30.3%, respectively, to $4.13 and $5.12 over the past year. The uptrend in estimate revisions indicates that investors are bullish about the stock's growth potential.

End Note

With healthy revenue-generating potential driven by robust demand trends, Arista appears poised for solid growth momentum. Further, a strong emphasis on quality, diligent execution of operational plans and continuous portfolio enhancements are driving more value for customers. Steady improvement in lead times and easing of supply-chain woes are major tailwinds.

The company delivered a trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise of 10.6%. Arista currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Riding on robust growth dynamics and a favorable Zacks Rank, ANET appears primed for further price appreciation. Consequently, investors are likely to profit if they bet on this high-flying stock now.

news.Title: Premarket movers: Qualcomm, Snap slide premarket; Unity surges
news.Content:
Investing.com - U.S. stock index futures were mixed on Thursday, with Nasdaq contracts falling as semiconductor and data-center stocks remained under pressure, while S&P 500 futures were little changed following a rally in the previous session after Democrats secured a sweeping victory in the midterm elections.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

By 07:30 ET (11:30 GMT), Nasdaq 100 futures had dropped 197 points, or 0.7%, while S&P 500 futures were little changed. Dow futures advanced 263 points, or 0.5%.

Here are some of the biggest premarket U.S. stock movers today:

Qualcomm shares fell about 9% in premarket trading after smartphone chip sales missed Wall Street expectations, raising concerns that weakness in its core handset business could offset growth in newer areas such as data-center chips.

Revenue from the company's handset division, its largest business, fell 26% to $5.14 billion, dragging chip segment sales down 8% to $9.02 billion. Qualcomm is facing pressure from rising memory costs, driven by strong data-center demand, as well as slower smartphone sales.

Snap shares tumbled 9.8% in premarket trading to $5.34 after the Snapchat parent reported third-quarter results that fell short of expectations on revenue and user growth.

Revenue came in at $1.72 billion, just below analysts' estimate of $1.73 billion, while daily active users reached 495 million, missing the 499 million expected by Wall Street. Advertising revenue grew just 4% year over year, slowing from 9% growth in the previous quarter.

Dutch Bros shares plunged 13.7% in premarket trading after the coffee chain issued full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance that fell short of analyst expectations, overshadowing a modest third-quarter earnings beat.

The company reported earnings of $0.25 per share, a penny above estimates, while revenue of $549.84 million narrowly topped consensus. However, its full-year 2026 revenue forecast of $2.10 billion came in below the $2.13 billion expected by Wall Street.

EPAM Systems shares surged 13.6% in premarket trading after the digital transformation company reported third-quarter results above analyst expectations and raised its full-year outlook.

Adjusted earnings came in at $3.51 per share, beating the $3.40 consensus, while revenue of $1.426 billion edged past estimates of $1.42 billion and increased 2.3% year over year. The company also raised its full-year 2026 adjusted earnings forecast to $13.23 to $13.31 per share and lifted its revenue growth outlook to 3.5% to 3.7%.

Story Continues

EPAM also increased its share repurchase authorization by $1.5 billion, bringing its remaining buyback capacity to $1.8 billion.

MNTN shares plunged 45.1% in premarket trading after the advertising technology company reported third-quarter results below its own guidance and sharply cut its full-year revenue forecast, citing disruption caused by changes to its sales compensation structure.

Revenue came in at $80.3 million, below the company's guidance range of $86 million to $89 million, while adjusted EBITDA of $19.9 million missed its target of $22 million to $25 million. MNTN lowered its 2026 revenue forecast to $311 million to $314 million, down from its previous range of $347 million to $357 million and well below analysts' expectations of about $352 million.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The company said changes to its sales compensation model had contributed to the departure of roughly 40% of its experienced salesforce, hurting customer acquisition and revenue generation. MNTN also announced leadership changes, appointing board member Tony Weisman as CEO and confirming the departures of COO Chris Innes and Chief Revenue Officer Garland Hill.

Warby Parker shares surged 22% in premarket trading after the eyewear retailer reported stronger-than-expected adjusted EBITDA and continued gross margin expansion, helping offset weaker-than-expected revenue and earnings.

Revenue increased 10.4% year over year to $244.7 million, slightly below analyst expectations, while earnings of $0.04 per share missed the $0.09 consensus. Adjusted EBITDA, however, reached $28.6 million, exceeding the company's guidance range, while gross margin improved to 54.4% from 54.1% a year earlier.

Warby Parker narrowed its full-year 2026 revenue forecast to $966 million to $976 million and reaffirmed its adjusted EBITDA outlook of $117 million to $119 million. The company also cited investment spending tied to its upcoming Intelligent Eyewear launch with Google.

Unity Software shares jumped 22% in premarket trading after the game-engine developer reported third-quarter results well above analyst expectations and issued a stronger-than-expected forecast for the current quarter.

Adjusted earnings came in at $0.44 per share, compared with analysts' estimates of $0.03, while revenue rose 32% year over year to $622 million, exceeding the $565.82 million consensus. Adjusted EBITDA reached $257 million, also above expectations of $188.9 million.

For the fourth quarter, Unity forecast revenue of $683 million to $691 million, well above analysts' estimate of $601.3 million. It also projected adjusted EBITDA of $290 million to $295 million, compared with the $201.3 million consensus.

Expedia shares fell nearly 7% in premarket trading after the travel-booking company issued a weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue forecast, raising concerns about its growth outlook.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $3.69 billion to $3.75 billion, putting the midpoint below analysts' average estimate of $3.74 billion, according to LSEG data. Expedia shares had risen about 12% this year through Wednesday's close, outperforming Booking Holdings, whose shares had fallen about 20% over the same period.

Planet Fitness shares rose 1.2% in premarket trading after the gym operator beat third-quarter profit and revenue estimates and raised its 2026 outlook.

The company reported adjusted earnings of $0.83 per share, above analysts' expectations of $0.80, while revenue of $360 million topped the $347.68 million consensus. Adjusted EBITDA increased 3.9% to $146.2 million.

Franchise revenue rose 14% to $129.6 million, while equipment revenue increased 11% to $87.6 million. System-wide same-club sales grew 1.5%, and the company ended the quarter with 2,962 clubs, up 6% from a year earlier.

Peloton Interactive shares rose 7.3% in premarket trading after the connected-fitness company reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 results above analyst expectations, alongside stronger cash generation and improved profitability.

Adjusted earnings came in at $0.19 per share, beating the $0.11 consensus, while revenue reached $559.2 million, above estimates of $554.55 million and up 2% from a year earlier. Free cash flow more than doubled year over year to $143 million, while adjusted EBITDA climbed 42% to $168 million.

Peloton also reported net income of $96 million, compared with $13.9 million a year earlier, and said it had reduced gross principal debt outstanding by nearly $500 million, or 32%, during calendar 2026.

news.Title: 台股何時反彈？謝金河預言挑戰5萬點「要等這時候」
news.Content:
即時中心／徐子為報導

美國期中選舉變天，市場擔憂AI監管可能收緊，美股主要指數週三（4日）漲多跌少，費半大跌3.13％。台股今日開盤便下跌282.78點、以42,666.13點開出，之後持續走弱，最後下跌1374.19點，收在41574.72點，4萬2大關確定失守，也使台股單週跌破3600點。對此，《今周刊》發行人謝金河表示，台股今年漲幅最大，這次下跌8113點，跌幅16.24%，已是全球表現最強勢的市場，接下來全球股市要重整，台股要挑戰5萬大關，可能要等到明年！

針對昨日的美國期中選舉民主黨大獲全勝、贏得參眾兩院，謝金河認為，其實冰凍三尺非一日之寒，美國債券殖利率一直飆升，物價飛漲，美國人民的生活壓力越來越大，川普的敗選已在預料中。

他從資本市場分析，其實從10月以來跌跌不休，先反應的是川普的可能敗選，共和黨失去參眾兩院。另一個是龐大的Ai軍備競賽，四大CSP大廠今年資本支出7450億美元，造成沈重的自由現金流的大流出，Amazon的12個月自由現金流負423.6億美元，把大家嚇出冷汗。大家開始擔心龐大的Ai支出，何時能轉化成強大的獲利？另外，市場也擔心民主黨掌控的很多州都抵制資料中心及電力系統的建置，更擔心德州可能變天！結果共和黨輸掉參議員及州長，首當其衝的是馬斯克。川普是Ai建置的大推手，如今跛腳，會不會影響Ai的未來？大家都必須重新評估。

第三是財報衝擊，除了Google，Amazon，這次令市場震驚的是Intel，公布財報當天股價大跌28.58%，台灣很多大型企業像台達電，國巨都受到波及，國巨這次跌到417元，比7月從1220元跌下來的「買到國巨，來生再聚」的低點更低。

第四則是長𨫎科技的4F平方打趴記憶體股價，南韓的三星，海力士才剛從兩倍槓桿撞擊下挺過來，現在又挨了一記重擊，中國的華虹，中芯國際，兆易創新都慘跌。

這次台股跌不停，讓很多投資人心慌慌，謝金河表示，其實把全球巿場比對一下，印尼股市今年最慘，南韓接近腰斬，中國的深圳股市跌幅逾三成，上海，香港大約跌兩成。最近為了救市，中國證監會暫停新股IPO。而台股今年漲幅最大，這一次下跌8113點，跌幅16.24%，已是全球表現最強勢的市場！接下來，全球將進行調整，鞏固整頓，尋找新方向，台股要挑戰5萬大關，可能要等到明年！

news.Title: Tesla vs. BYD: Which EV Giant Is Better Charged Right Now?
news.Content:
Tesla TSLA and BYD Co Ltd BYDDY have emerged as the two biggest contenders in the global electric vehicle (EV) market, but their competitive positions are evolving.

Tesla, once the undisputed EV leader, lost its annual sales crown to BYD in 2025. Although Tesla briefly reclaimed the lead in the first quarter of 2026, BYD regained the advantage in the second quarter and extended it in the third. BYD's BEV sales surged nearly 31% year over year to 762,748 vehicles in the third quarter, while Tesla's deliveries declined 2.1% to 486,532 units.

Yet, the picture is not entirely straightforward. Tesla's demand appears to be stabilizing, whereas BYD is grappling with weakening domestic sales and intensifying competition.

Year to date, shares of Tesla have lost 14%, narrower than BYD's 23% decline.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

With both companies facing different challenges, which EV giant presents the more compelling investment opportunity now? Let's dig deeper.

The Case for TSLA

Tesla's story is gradually strengthening, supported by stabilizing vehicle demand, improving gross margins and tangible progress in artificial intelligence (AI). However, higher research and development (R&D) spending remains a near-term drag on profitability.

The third quarter of 2026 marked Tesla's second consecutive quarter above 480,000 units. Its passenger vehicle order backlog has also reached a four-year high, with management indicating that demand is outpacing production. Rising adoption of Full Self-Driving (FSD) is providing another tailwind. More than 75% of new North American deliveries included a paid FSD subscription at delivery, while Latvia's recent approval made it the 10th EU country to authorize FSD.

Tesla's automotive gross margins are showing improvement, too. The metric increased to 18.5% from 17% a year earlier. Its energy business is gaining traction, with storage deployments rising 10% year over year to 13.7 GWh and energy gross margin climbing to 33.1% from 20.4% in the previous quarter. Megapack supply for 2027 is nearly sold out, providing encouraging forward visibility.

Meanwhile, Tesla's AI ambitions are beginning to show measurable progress. The company started deploying Cybercabs in Austin, where its Robotaxi fleet reportedly expanded tenfold in about a month. Unsupervised Robotaxi miles increased eightfold sequentially to nearly 2 million, offering early evidence of progress toward autonomous mobility commercialization.

The key concern remains operating profitability, as rising R&D expenditure is expected to weigh on earnings while Tesla funds its next growth phase. Nevertheless, improving demand, recovering gross margins, positive free cash flow and tangible AI milestones are strengthening the company's long-term investment narrative.

Story Continues

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Tesla's EPS has moved north over the past 30 days.

The Case for BYDDY

BYD's latest earnings suggest that its growth engine is losing momentum, even as overseas expansion offers temporary relief. While third-quarter revenues rebounded 13.6% year over year to RMB 221.5 billion and net profit climbed 28% to RMB 10 billion, the results fell short of analyst expectations. What's more concerning is the fact that the company's nine-month revenues remained almost unchanged at RMB 566.3 billion, while net profit declined 4.2% to RMB 22.3 billion.

The company's domestic weakness is becoming difficult to ignore. Per CnEVPost, BYD's deliveries in China for the month of October and during the January-to-October period declined almost 11% and 28%, respectively, on a year-over-year basis.

The company's dependence on exports is increasing as competition intensifies in China. Xiaomi's popular YU7, Geely's aggressive product launches and competitively priced Leapmotor models are challenging BYD across price segments. In the premium market, NIO and XPeng add competition, although BYD is targeting the premium segment mainly through its Denza, Fangchengbao and Yangwang brands.

Overseas shipments accounted for approximately 42% of BYD's third-quarter NEV sales and rocketed around 130%, underscoring that exports are cushioning domestic weakness. However, international expansion is not without obstacles. European trade arrangements surrounding Chinese hybrid imports introduce uncertainty, while 100% U.S. tariffs effectively shut BYD out of direct EV exports to America.

Per Electrek, BYD's inventory has climbed approximately 60% since January, while receivables increased 52.6% from year-end. These trends raise concerns about working-capital requirements and cash conversion. With nine-month profits declining and domestic competition intensifying, BYD faces a risk that sustaining volume growth could pressure margins.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for BYDDY's EPS has moved south over the past 30 days.

Our Take

While Tesla is no screaming buy, it is the higher-quality story and appears better placed than BYD. Tesla's vehicle demand is stabilizing, margins are improving, and its energy and Robotaxi businesses offer additional growth opportunities. BYD, meanwhile, is facing tougher competition at home and relying more on exports to drive sales. Rising inventory, weaker earnings and trade uncertainties add to its challenges. While Tesla still has its own profitability concerns, its business outlook appears more encouraging. We prefer TSLA over BYDDY.

While Tesla carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), BYDDY has a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).
