news.Title: Qualcomm tops Q4 estimates, but Q1 earnings outlook falls short
news.Content:
Qualcomm ( QCOM ) reported fourth quarter earnings after the bell Wednesday, topping expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated Q1 revenue outlook.

But a lower-than-expected midpoint for its earnings per share (EPS) forecast sent the stock lower following the report.

For Q4, Qualcomm reported adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.17 on revenue of $10.32 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $2.16 and revenue of $10.12 billion.

The company saw EPS of $3 and revenue of $11.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Qualcomm also offered Q1 revenue guidance of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion, with the midpoint ahead of Wall Street's $10.6 billion outlook.

EPS, however, is set to come in between $2.15 and $2.35, with a midpoint of $2.25. Analysts were looking for $2.32

Qualcomm's QCT segment, which includes handset and automotive sales, declined 8% year over year but topped Wall Street's Q4 expectations on revenue of $9 billion. Analysts were calling for $8.8 billion.

The bulk of that drop came from Qualcomm's handset business, which saw revenue plunge 26% year over year to $5.1 billion. Analysts were looking for $5.3 billion.

But the company's automotive segment helped offset some of that impact, with sales increasing 89% to $2 billion.

Qualcomm's QTL business line saw revenue of $1.3 billion for the quarter.

The chip giant is in the midst of a wide-ranging effort to bolster its data center, automotive, edge computing, and PC businesses, as it works to reduce its dependence on smartphone chip sales.

On Wednesday, Qualcomm announced a deal to provide technology to SpaceX's ( SPCX ) Starlink as the satellite networking giant ramps up its effort to establish a terrestrial network that would rival AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ).

In late October, Qualcomm said it is working with Anduril on a product line called BlueChip focused on reshoring computer manufacturing. The companies say they'll start by focusing on a laptop that will use Qualcomm's Snapdragon X series chips.

And in September, the company signed an agreement with Amazon for custom chips designed for its AWS AI infrastructure.

But Qualcomm, like the rest of the consumer electronics industry, is also contending with the impact of the memory and storage shortage, which has forced companies to raise prices on everything from smartphones to laptops, sending demand plummeting.

During its fourth quarter earnings announcement on Monday, Apple noted that the memory crisis will continue to cut into margins going forward. Intel ( INTC ) and AMD ( AMD ) also said they expect PC sales to decline in the coming quarter, sending shares of Intel plunging nearly 29% .

news.Title: Qualcomm stock slumps 10% on margin headwinds, rising costs
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ: QCOM) shares slumped roughly 10% in premarket trading Thursday after the chipmaker reported weaker-than-expected handset revenue and warned of rising semiconductor input costs, overshadowing quarterly earnings that topped analyst estimates and fueling margin concerns.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Qualcomm reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.17 per share, slightly above the $2.16 consensus, while adjusted revenue of $10.44 billion exceeded expectations of $10.12 billion. However, handset revenue fell 26% year over year to $5.14 billion, missing estimates of $5.25 billion.

Total revenue declined 7% from $11.27 billion a year earlier. Qualcomm forecast first-quarter revenue of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion, with a midpoint of $10.8 billion above the $10.55 billion consensus. Adjusted earnings guidance of $2.15 to $2.35 per share, however, came in slightly below the $2.32 estimate at the midpoint.

Gross margin for the quarter contracted to 52.4%, missing the consensus estimate of 53.2%.

The company said the semiconductor industry is facing broad-based increases in costs across wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, advanced packaging, memory and other materials. Qualcomm expects pricing actions to deliver their full benefit in the second half of fiscal 2027.

"Although we believe investor positioning was relatively balanced heading into the quarter, we think investors will want to see more evidence of the magnitude and timing of the Datacenter ramp through FY27 - especially in light of near-term smartphone weakness," Goldman Sachs analysts said in a post-earnings note.

"We also believe investors may look for more evidence of gross margin stabilization before getting more constructive on the stock," they added.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Raymond James analysts shared similar views. "Elevated manufacturing costs continue to pressure margins, with expected pricing benefits largely offset by Data Center custom silicon dilution," they wrote. "We believe the key investment debate has shifted toward execution of the Data Center roadmap and look for further evidence of customer ramps and margin recovery before becoming more constructive."

Automotive revenue surged 89% year over year to $1.99 billion, beating estimates of $1.69 billion and marking the segment's first quarter approaching $2 billion. Internet of Things revenue rose 4% to $1.89 billion, also exceeding expectations.

Story Continues

The QCT semiconductor business generated $9.02 billion in revenue, down 8% year over year but above the $8.8 billion consensus. QTL licensing revenue declined 7% to $1.30 billion, slightly ahead of estimates of $1.29 billion.

"We are pleased to deliver fourth quarter non-GAAP revenues at the high end of our guidance, along with 36% year-over-year growth in combined QCT Automotive and IoT revenues," said Cristiano Amon, Qualcomm's president and chief executive.

"Fiscal 2027 marks the start of our non-handset revenue inflection, including the ramp of our Data Center business," Amon added.

For fiscal 2026, adjusted revenue declined 2% to $43.24 billion, while adjusted earnings per share fell 12% to $10.54.

Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.

此外，測試大廠精測（6510）靠著HPC需求帶動，上看4125元；耕興（6146）有望迎來美國轉單效應，目標價235元；矽晶圓大廠環球晶（6488）則因特殊矽光子晶圓逐步放量，目標價上看757元。

記憶體谷底反撲　伺服器與載板火力全開

記憶體市場迎來供需反轉，DDR4供給收縮讓南亞科（2408）議價力大增，本土法人喊出635元目標價；晶豪科（3006）更因同業減產成為DDR3市場核心供應商，目標價上看294元。

伺服器整機與零組件方面，緯穎（6669）靠著新一代液冷平台出貨，目標價達2456元；高階伺服器滑軌廠南俊國際（6584）目標價上看579元；電源廠康舒（6282）在企業用電源發力，目標價來到50元；ABF載板大廠景碩（3189）受惠高階運算稼動率回升，上看1085元。

光學網通迎出貨旺季　電子零組件各擁題材

鏡頭霸主大立光（3008）因美系新世代AI系統急迫需求，目標價喊上9000元；

news.Title: Arm stock dips as lack of blowout guidance offsets quarterly results
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Arm on Wednesday delivered a quarterly top- and bottom-line beat, but its current-quarter profit and revenue guidance failed to comfortably top expectations.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

U.S.-listed shares of the British chip designer fell more than 3% in premarket trading Thursday.

Arm is a well-known player in the semiconductor market, with its chip designs being used by companies such as Qualcomm, Apple, and Samsung Electronics in graphics processing units (GPUs) in smartphones, and by cloud computing giants and hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms.

ARM brings in revenue from licensing its technology to these companies and then charging a royalty fee for each product that uses its design.

The British chip designer's technology is used in developing artificial intelligence-focused server chips. The firm earlier this year also said it was expanding its strategy beyond offering intellectual property and compute subsystems to producing silicon products. This included the launch of a new central processing unit (CPU) designed for AI data centers, called Arm AGI CPU.

"AI is driving unprecedented demand for compute across the cloud, devices and autonomous systems, with Arm being the compute platform of choice. Our business is now driven by two areas, both of which are showing rapid growth: The IP business, where partners increase their investment in Arm technology and deploy record numbers of Arm-based silicon, and our new silicon business, where demand for Arm AGI CPU is extremely strong," ARM top boss Rene Haas and finance chief Jason Child said in a letter to shareholders.

HSBC analysts said Arm reiterated its bullish AGI CPU tone bot noted that "server royalties remain a key driver."

"We believe server royalties remain the key earnings catalyst upside with the clearest visibility over the next 12 month given increasing server CPU TAM and Arm market share along with rising CPU core count which increases royalty ASP per chip," they wrote.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The Cambridge, England-based company's results come at a time when the broader AI trade on Wall Street has been under pressure. Concerns have soared about the massive amounts of debt being issued by companies to fund their AI infrastructure buildouts and whether such spending will ultimately be rewarded with comparable returns.

Story Continues

Chip stocks in particular have been some of the hardest hit by the downturn in sentiment around AI. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index - a key barometer of chip stocks - slumped 15.4% in October. Meanwhile, U.S.-listed shares of Arm tumbled nearly 29% last month.

Against this backdrop, investors have been closely watching quarterly results from chipmakers and chip designers to gauge the demand for AI chips and whether that demand was strong enough to warrant the unprecedented spending on AI.

"Arm continues to gain share across the data center, driven by growing demand for performance and power efficiency as AI infrastructure scales. Data center royalties doubled year over year, and Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers more than tripled—from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in calendar 2025," the company's top executives said in the letter to shareholders.

"Based on current ramps across Google Axion, AWS Graviton, Microsoft Cobalt, and NVIDIA platforms, we expect that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026," they added.

Raymond James analysts said the management's commentary "suggests it is incrementally confident that it has enough supply and customer commitments for the CPU business for up to $2B of sales through the end of FY28, but we opt to remain conservative until we can discern more tangible trends."

Arm said it earned 52 cents per share on an adjusted basis on revenue of $1.44 billion for its fiscal Q2 2027. Analysts had expected an adjusted profit of 47 cents per share on revenue of $1.38 billion.

For its fiscal Q3 2027, ARM sees adjusted profit per share of 56 cents plus/minus 4 cents on revenue of $1.54 billion plus/minus $50 million. The consensus estimates had been for a profit of 55 cents per share on revenue of $1.53 billion.

Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.

news.Title: GlobalFoundries (GFS) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Nov. 4, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Head of Investor Relations - Eric Chow

Chief Executive Officer - Tim Breen

Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer - Sam Franklin

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Thank you for standing by, and welcome to the GlobalFoundries Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speaker's presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this session, you will need to press star one on your telephone. If your question has been answered and you would like to remove yourself from the queue, simply press star one again. As a reminder, today's program is being recorded. Now I would like to introduce your host for today's program, Eric Chow, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead, sir.

Eric Chow: Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalFoundries Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. On the call with me today are Tim Breen, CEO, and Sam Franklin, CFO. A short while ago, we released GF's Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results, which are available on our website at investors.gf.com, along with today's accompanying slide presentation. This call is being recorded, and a replay will be made available on our Investor Relations webpage. During this call, we will present both IFRS and non-IFRS financial measures. The most directly comparable IFRS measures and reconciliations for non-IFRS measures are made available in today's press release and accompanying slides. Please note that these financial results are unaudited and subject to change.

Certain statements on today's call may be deemed to be forward-looking statements. Such statements can be identified by terms such as believe, expect, intend, anticipate, and may, or by the use of the future tense. You should not place undue reliance on forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially from these forward-looking statements, and we do not undertake any obligation to update any forward-looking statements we make today.

For more information about factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements, please refer to the press release we issued today, as well as risks and uncertainties described in our SEC filings, including in sections under the caption Risk Factors in our annual report on Form 20-F and in any current reports on Form 6-K furnished with the SEC. In terms of upcoming events, we will be participating in a fireside chat at the UBS Global Technology and AI Conference in Scottsdale, Arizona, on December 1st.

Story Continues

We will begin today's call with Tim providing a summary update on the business environment and technologies, followed by Sam, who will provide details on our third quarter results and fourth quarter guidance. We will then open the call for questions with Tim and Sam. We request that you please limit your questions to one with one follow-up. I will now turn the call over to Tim.

Tim Breen: Thank you, Eric, and welcome everyone to our Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. GF delivered strong results in the third quarter, with revenue and non-IFRS profitability metrics at the high end of our guidance ranges. We delivered record non-IFRS gross margin, which demonstrates the meaningful progress we are making to enhance the mix of our business by ramping our differentiated technologies in high-value, high-growth applications. Our communications infrastructure and data center end market saw record levels of growth, led by accelerating demand in optical networking across our silicon photonics and silicon germanium platforms. We also delivered strong growth in automotive and home and industrial IoT, reflecting broad-based secular momentum across our key markets.

Thanks to the accelerated growth across several end markets, the proportion of revenue outside of smart mobile devices was the highest level in our company's history and is driving a richer, more diversified, more resilient revenue base. Thanks to the team's excellent efforts and execution, we are ahead of plans to deliver the strategic and financial targets we set out at our Investor Day earlier in the year. We will look back at 2026 being a pivotal year for GF. In recent weeks, we have made several significant announcements that meaningfully advance our strategy, support our financial objectives, and reinforce our foundation for durable long-term growth.

We are proud to have announced a significant number of new customer and investment partnerships, such as our agreements with Marvell to accelerate capacity for our industry-leading high-performance SiGe, with Monolithic Power for critical power management solutions, with TSMC to establish a U.S.-based supply of silicon interposers for the CoWoS ecosystem, and the landmark U.S.-Japan fab expansion plan that will transform our Malta, New York site. These milestones firmly position GF as a diversified, holistic technology provider, critical to governments and partners around the world. Let me cover these areas in more detail, beginning with our strong investment partnerships.

Announced last month, the U.S.-Japan initiative provides a new and innovative model for GF to expand our critical U.S. semiconductor manufacturing capacity at accretive economic returns. This initiative will unlock substantial capacity growth, support significant future customer demand, and bring the scale of our U.S. operations in Malta, New York to mega-fab level. The unique and innovative partnership structure allows GF to expand capacity faster without investing capital, with an economic model that is accretive to our long-range plans. Through a robust structure of technology, construction, and operations fees, cost reimbursements, and EBITDA sharing, the initiative is designed to generate the profit per wafer comparable to if we had built and owned the capacity ourselves.

As another indicator of our deepening partnership with the U.S. government, GF reached an agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce to reallocate $955 million of our existing CHIPS and Science Act award to accelerate investments at our Malta, New York, and Burlington, Vermont facilities. The amended award will accelerate CapEx and R&D investments in our highest value differentiated technologies that our customers demand, such as silicon photonics, silicon germanium, and advanced packaging, including the first U.S.-based source of silicon interposers.

In recognition of the growing role that GF is playing in the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem, a separate agreement will be entered into to issue 4% equity to the U.S. government, which provides a vehicle for the American people to share in GF's future success. Combined with previous announcements across our quantum, silicon photonics, and advanced packaging investments, we anticipate the total equity ownership of the U.S. government to be approximately 7% when all agreements are finalized. Having attained a meaningful position in GF, our board of directors and our U.S. government partners do not plan on any further government equity position beyond these announced equity stakes.

In summary, this landmark agreement represents a strong vote of confidence in GF and underscores our critical role in advancing U.S. semiconductor leadership. Let me now turn to our significant and expanding opportunity in the AI data center. We see significant momentum with customers for our optical networking solutions, where customers value GF's unique combination of high-performance photonic devices, advanced fiber coupling, RF integration, and advanced packaging. Backed by more than a decade of investment and substantial clean room space within our modern, highly automated 300-mm footprint, GF can deliver differentiated performance and scale capacity rapidly as customer demand grows. Our competitive advantages are translating into strong design win momentum and robust customer demand.

We are actively engaged with more than 50 silicon photonics customers, including seven of the top 10 optical transceiver suppliers, with active designs slotted to ramp in 2027 and 2028 to scale across, scale out, and scale up networks. In 2026, we expect to deliver half a billion dollars of revenue from silicon photonics, and on the back of the strength of customer demand, order visibility, and our capacity growth plans, we now expect to exit 2027 at an annualized silicon photonics revenue run rate of approximately $1 billion, a full year ahead of prior expectations.

To support the ramping demand for optical networking in 2028 and beyond, we plan to approximately triple our silicon photonics capacity over the course of next year, which Sam will cover in more detail. In addition to silicon photonics, silicon germanium is another important and complementary driver of GF's growth in optical networking. Our SiGe technology enables high-speed optical transceivers through transmit drivers and receive amplifiers, key interface elements between the electrical and optical domains. Customer demand for our SiGe technology continues to increase beyond current capacity, and supported by customer prepayments, we are accelerating our capacity investments to ensure that we can meet this demand.

Our recently announced multi-year strategic partnership with Marvell will help support significant SiGe capacity expansion in our Burlington fab to enable next-generation optical solutions. Together with the reallocated U.S. government funding from our prior CHIPS grants awards, this gives us additional resources and strong customer alignment to scale a highly differentiated platform, meaningfully accretive to GF's long-term margin targets. Lastly, advanced packaging is another key enabler of our AI data center strategy. Under our five-year, $2 billion manufacturing agreement with TSMC, GF will establish a U.S.-based supply of silicon interposers for the CoWoS ecosystem, with volume production expected to ramp at our Malta site in the first half of 2028, and with a framework to expand the agreement over time.

The economics of this arrangement are attractive for GF, and the strategic benefits are clear. This agreement establishes a new multi-year revenue stream for GF, with gross margins above our long-term targets, and with co-investment from TSMC that will help fund the necessary capital associated with this project. The silicon interposers are yet another way GF can serve growing AI and high-performance computing infrastructure demand. By combining GF's trusted U.S. manufacturing capabilities with the leading advanced packaging ecosystem globally, we are expanding into another essential layer of AI infrastructure and supporting the tighter integration of compute, memory, and connectivity.

We believe we are in the early innings of GF's AI data center opportunity, underpinned by the critical needs of our customers for higher bandwidth connectivity, tighter integration of compute and memory, greater power efficiency, and secure, scalable supply. The result for GF, more avenues to win, greater content and value in each system, and a clear path to growth and a structurally richer business mix. Let me turn to physical AI, as well as the meaningful progress we are making across IP, software, and custom silicon, or ISC.

GF's physical AI opportunity spans a wide variety of applications across connectivity, compute, power, actuation, and sensing, and our IP software and custom silicon capabilities unlock even more ways for GF to win. We believe the deployment of intelligence into vehicles, factories, robots, drones, satellites, medical devices, and other edge systems represents a significant and long-duration demand vector for GF. Together with the Synopsys ARC Processor IP business we acquired earlier this year, MIPS expands our role into that of an holistic technology partner, servicing a broader set of customers with our custom silicon platforms.

MIPS recently announced three physical AI-native reference platforms focusing on compute, AI inference, and real-time control, and we are now working with several customers designing systems focused on physical AI, leveraging our expanded capabilities. The combination of RISC-V compute and AI IP, design capability, and AI-native platforms based on GF's broad manufacturing capabilities puts us in a unique position to accelerate share gain in this area. Just over one year after we initially acquired MIPS, we are very encouraged by the strong customer traction, which is now driving several platform-level wins. During the third quarter alone, we secured custom silicon design wins that total nearly $1 billion of lifetime revenue.

These included platform wins for a radar system-on-chip and a RISC-V-based processor core designed for real-time control. In addition, we secured a win with a leading provider of high-performance data center computing solutions to design their custom board management controller system-on-chip, integrating our processor technology with third-party IP. We also secured a notable aerospace and defense win to support the engine control processor for a leading global aerospace and propulsion company. Ultimately, these wins demonstrate how GF can capture more opportunities and support our customers across the semiconductor value chain, deepen our relationships with industry partners, and convert initial design engagements into concrete, long-duration growth opportunities. In summary, the multifaceted progress we demonstrated this quarter shows our strategy in action.

We are scaling differentiated technologies into high-growth AI markets and driving meaningful customer value with our capabilities in IP, software, and custom silicon. We are transforming GF into a more diversified, more durable, and more profitable business, propelled by the defining megatrends of our time. I'll now pass the call over to Sam for a deeper dive on third quarter 2026 financials.

Sam Franklin: Thank you, Tim. For the remainder of the call, including guidance other than revenue, cash flow, and net interest income, I'll reference non-IFRS metrics. The third quarter was a significant milestone for GF, not only for the continued progression in our profitability metrics, but also for the continued mix shift in our portfolio. For the first time in our history, more than 2/3 of our Q3 revenue came from outside smart mobile devices, a record for GF and further evidence of our increasingly diversified and margin-accretive mix. We delivered record non-IFRS gross margin while continuing to fund the strategic investments that will drive GF's next phase of growth.

Our strategic decisions are already enhancing our earnings power, and we believe that we're only in the early innings of this evolution. Now on to the results. We delivered third quarter revenue of $1.899 billion, up 6% sequentially and 13% year-over-year. We shipped approximately 647,000 300-mm equivalent wafers in the quarter, up 4% sequentially and 7% from the prior year period. Revenue from manufacturing services accounted for approximately 88% of total revenue. Revenue from technology services, which includes revenue from IP licensing, software, reticles, non-recurring engineering, expedite fees, and other items, accounted for approximately 12% of total revenue for the third quarter.

As we continue to invest in a broader range of capabilities for our customers, we expect technology services revenue will represent approximately 12% of total revenue in 2026, which is at the upper end of the range we indicated, and with a gross margin profile that continues to be above our long-term target. Beyond 2026, we expect that the growth of revenue from technology services associated with IP licensing and software, combined with strong momentum in customer design wins and tape-outs, will be important drivers of GF's revenue growth and gross margin appreciation. Let me now provide an update on our revenue and outlook by end markets. Communications infrastructure and data center represented approximately 17% of third quarter total revenue.

Revenue increased 14% sequentially and 81% year-over-year, driven by robust growth in optical networking, which includes silicon photonics and silicon germanium. Not only did Q3 represent record year-over-year growth for this end market, it also marked the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit percentage year-over-year growth for communications infrastructure and data center. With accelerating customer demand and improved manufacturing productivity, our expectation is that revenue from communications infrastructure and data center will grow in the range of 60%-70% in 2026. Furthermore, our design win momentum across this end market has continued to strengthen. In the third quarter, we secured design wins for both silicon photonics and SiGe at a new optical transceiver customer for hyperscaler demand.

In data center power, we taped out a smart power stage gate driver on our BCD platform and secured a design win on our 650-V GaN platform. Automotive represented approximately 19% of third quarter total revenue. Automotive revenue increased 11% sequentially and 20% year-over-year. Consistent with our prior commentary, our expectation is that automotive revenue will grow low double-digit percentage in 2026, marking another strong year of growth for this end market, and GF continues to win with our customers to support the expansion of automotive semiconductor content. Smart mobile devices represented approximately 32% of third quarter total revenue, the lowest proportion in our history, and a step forward to our long-term strategic goal to enhance the diversification of mix.

Revenue decreased 5% sequentially and 19% from the prior year period. Consistent with the commentary from our customers, we continue to expect smart mobile devices to decline by a low teens percentage year-over-year in 2026. We continue to have a skew towards the premium end of the smart mobile market, and we expect to largely track the broader demand dynamics as the market adjusts to the challenges associated with memory-related supply constraints. The long-term demand indicators continue to be positive. In the third quarter, we secured new design wins across form factors spanning both smartphones and smart glasses. These included additional content wins in mobile power and a first-ever design win for fuel gauge ICs in premium-tier handsets.

Customer engagement continues to be strong for GF's differentiated and high-performance RF, power, audio, display, and imaging capabilities to service the demand for smart and connected mobile devices. Finally, home and industrial IoT represented approximately 20% of third quarter total revenue. Revenue increased 16% sequentially and 49% year-over-year on broad-based strength across connectivity, tracking, and sensing applications. As workloads for edge AI applications continue to grow alongside the requirement for Bluetooth, wireless, cellular, and power management components to perform at higher standards, we have seen strong traction with our customers in this end market for GF's highly differentiated platforms. As a result, we continue to expect home and industrial IoT to grow in the range of 10%-15% in 2026.

Looking ahead to the future growth opportunities, the design win momentum has continued. In the third quarter, we taped out next-generation cellular IoT and Bluetooth products on our FDX platform for wireless connectivity. We're encouraged by the momentum we're seeing across the end markets we serve and believe keep us on track with the strategic diversification objectives that we set out during our Investor Day this year. Moving now to other key financial performance metrics in the quarter. In the third quarter, we delivered gross profit of $597 million, which translates into approximately 31.4% gross margin, up 540 basis points year-over-year. Q3 gross margin achieved a company record and was at the high end of our guidance range.

R&D for the quarter was $164 million, and SG&A was $93 million. Total operating expenses of $257 million represented approximately 14% of total revenue and were up 9% quarter-over-quarter, reflecting recent acquisitions. We delivered operating profit of $340 million for the quarter at an operating margin of 17.9%, at the high end of our guided range and up 250 basis points from the prior year period. Third quarter net interest income was $9 million, and other expense was $6 million, and we incurred tax expense of $45 million in the quarter. We delivered third quarter net income of approximately $298 million, an increase of approximately $66 million from the prior year period.

Diluted earnings of $0.53 per share was at the high end of the guidance range, based on a fully diluted share count of approximately 558 million shares. Let me now provide some key cash flow and balance sheet metrics. Cash flow from operations in the third quarter was $341 million. Third quarter CapEx, net of proceeds from government grants, was $205 million, or roughly 11% of revenue. Adjusted free cash flow for the quarter was $136 million. Free cash flow in the third quarter benefited from approximately $150 million of customer prepayments and government grants received. At the end of the third quarter, our combined total of cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities stood at approximately $3.2 billion.

Our total debt was $1.1 billion, and we also have a $1.5 billion revolving credit facility, which remains undrawn. On October 9th, we paid a quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share. On October 27th, the board of directors approved a dividend of $0.12 per share, payable on January 14th, 2027, to shareholders of record as of December 22nd, 2026. In the third quarter, we also repurchased $100 million of our shares. Let me now provide you with our outlook for the fourth quarter of 2026. We expect total GF revenue to be $2 billion, ±$25 million. We expect gross margin to be approximately 31.5%, ±100 basis points, which at the midpoint reflects approximately 250 basis points of year-over-year expansion.

Excluding share-based compensation, we expect total operating expenses to be $235 million, ±$10 million. We expect operating margin to be in the range of 19.8%, ±170 basis points. At the midpoint of our guidance, we expect share-based compensation to be approximately $68 million, of which roughly $16 million is related to cost of goods sold. We expect net interest and other income for the quarter to be between -$5 million and $1 million, and income tax expense to be between $44 million and $68 million. Based on a fully diluted share count of approximately 575 million shares, which reflects the expected issuance of equity to the U.S. government, we expect diluted earnings per share to be $0.59, ±$0.05.

Subject to the timing of the closures associated with the remaining equity issuances to the U.S. government, we expect that our fully diluted share count will be approximately 600 million shares commencing 2027. Now, let me provide an update on some broader financial drivers, milestones, and outlook. With respect to pricing, the third quarter saw meaningful blended ASP growth, both sequentially and year-over-year. This marked the first quarter of year-over-year blended pricing improvement since 2023 and is consistent with the commentary we provided on our last earnings call, especially as we execute the continued mix shift of our business.

With respect to tax, we continue to expect a non-IFRS effective tax rate in the mid-teens percentage range for the full year 2026. Net CapEx for 2026 is expected to be approximately 15%-20% of revenue, which remains below our long-term model, and we continue to expect free cash flow margin of approximately 10% in 2026. Touching briefly on the CapEx outlook for the year ahead, we expect 2027 to represent a year of accelerated investment for GF. Throughout the second half of this year, our customers have substantially increased their demand for our differentiated solutions across critical technologies such as silicon photonics, silicon germanium, FDX, and advanced packaging.

Importantly, we have the ability to grow our capacity quickly and efficiently within our existing four walls manufacturing footprint, resulting in a strong return on investment for new CapEx spending. Robust demand and customer commitments form the foundation of our capacity investment principles. As these signals strengthen, we expect approximately 1/3 of our net CapEx in 2027 to be supported by customer prepayments for incremental capacity agreements. In parallel, we also expect to secure CapEx offsets from investment tax credits and government grant frameworks, including a proportion of the recently announced $955 million repurposing from our previously awarded CHIPS grants.

Against this backdrop of customer demand, prepayments, and government support, we now expect net CapEx investments of approximately $4 billion into our manufacturing footprint in 2027, while continuing to deliver our free cash generation targets. These critical investments will unlock capacity constraints, accelerate future growth, and continue to evolve our business into a more diversified, resilient, and accretive portfolio. Our third quarter results demonstrate that GF's strategy is translating into stronger financial performance. Importantly, we believe these improvements are structural. Our revenue mix continues to shift towards differentiated high-value technologies and services, while our government and customer partnerships are enabling us to make capital-efficient investments to scale and accelerate key technologies with favorable economics.

All of these drivers reinforce our confidence in the long-term financial targets we presented at our Investor Day. GF today is more diversified and better positioned to capture more value than it ever has been. In closing, I want to thank our employees around the world for their continued focus and execution. Their work made this quarter's performance possible and gives us confidence in what GF can achieve next. With that, let's open the call to Q&A. Operator?

Sam Franklin: Yeah, Chris, I think that we've been relatively under-investing from a CapEx point of view over the last, call it, three years. If you look at the aggregate over the last three years, it's only been a little north of 10% of revenue versus what we said previously was targeting a 20% net CapEx to revenue and what we reiterated earlier this year. The principal reason for that is the foundation of our investment decisions into capacity is demand. We've seen a step change function in that demand outlook as we go through this year. It's for technologies across silicon photonics, FDX, advanced packaging, SiGe, more recently what we announced with TSMC on interposer.

This has been the single biggest change in terms of how we think about that investment into the footprint. Our customers recognize that as well. Actually, to Tim's earlier comments, there's been very, very constructive conversations in terms of the prepayment capacity reservations for incremental capacity discussions that we've been having. We expect those largely to close in, call it, the fourth quarter and into early 2027 as well. That $4 billion net number that I gave you, obviously we don't net customer prepayments from that in terms of how we calculate net CapEx.

Think of that as $4 billion net CapEx to GF, but within that $4 billion, we expect that we'll get about, call it, a third of that supported by customer prepayments. You won't see that flow through as a net to CapEx, but you will effectively see it flow through towards our free cash flow. That's why we feel good about still remaining the targets around our free cash flow margin for 2027. Then the other dynamic, as you said, is around government grants and broader support frameworks. If I take the ITC as an example, that's now 35%. We don't get all of that 35% in year.

In fact, some of what we'll get as a net for CapEx next year will be from ITC that was accrued in, call it, the 2025 timeframe. We will, however, get as an offset to CapEx next year the government grants that we've announced during the course of this year. Some of that is in relation to quantum computing. We've also got the $955 million repurposing from the original CHIPS office grants. About 80% of that $955 million we expect we'll allocate towards CapEx. Not all of that will be allocated in 2027 as an offset, but we'll probably get the majority of that coming through in 2027 as well.

All points towards good indicators from a free cash point of view. Then look, the way we think about the ROI is really a function of payback. When you take that combination of the government grants, the ITC, the offset to our overall CapEx burden, we see strong paybacks inside a sort of two-year time horizon for most of those technologies that we outlined. It forms an important part of our investment decision-making. Given the margin profile and the mix associated with these corridors, we see a strong ROI and a relatively quick ramp to demand and revenue. Obviously, it's really a function of how quickly you can get those tools installed, qualified, and ramped.

The beauty of our expansion footprint is that we can do it within our existing four walls. So, we're not reliant like some others are around building incremental capacity to do it. We can do it within our existing four walls. So, that accelerates the time to revenue as well.

Tim Breen: I mean, the way we've been thinking about this is, it's a unique moment for us to accelerate our business with the participation of our customers, with the participation of governments, maintaining a very strong balance sheet, maintaining our free cash flow generation objectives. It's the right way to navigate the current situation that we're in.

Operator: Thank you. This does conclude the question and answer session of today's program. I'd like to hand the program back to Eric Chow for any further remarks.

Eric Chow: Thank you very much for joining today. We look forward to seeing you at the UBS conference on December 1st. Thanks again.

Operator: Thank you, ladies and gentlemen, for your participation in today's conference. This does conclude the program. You may now disconnect. Good day.

news.Title: Earnings live updates: Cava stock falls after cyclospora outbreak dented Q3 results
news.Content:
The third quarter earnings season is over halfway done, and the reports continue to pour in. This week brought another shot of major earnings courtesy of Apple ( AAPL ), Palantir ( PLTR ), and AMD ( AMD ).

In addition to those tech heavyweights, investors are watching the results out of Roku ( ROKU ), Arm Holdings ( ARM ), McDonald's ( MCD ), QUALCOMM ( QCOM ), Novo Nordisk ( NVO ), Uber Technologies ( UBER ), Toyota Motor Corporation ( TM ), ConocoPhillips ( COP ), and Moderna ( MRNA ).

S&P 500 corporations continue to demonstrate robust earnings growth. According to FactSet data , approximately 60% of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings, with an overall earnings growth rate of 30.2%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25% for the index.

LIVE 10 updates

Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:23 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Qualcomm tops Q4 estimates, but Q1 earnings outlook falls short

Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports:

Qualcomm ( QCOM ) reported fourth quarter earnings after the bell Wednesday, topping expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated Q1 revenue outlook.

But a lower-than-expected midpoint for its earnings per share (EPS) forecast send shares lower following the report.

For Q4, Qualcomm reported adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.17 on revenue of $10.32 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $2.16 and revenue of $10.12 billion.

The company saw EPS of $3.00 and revenue of $11.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Qualcomm also offered Q1 revenue guidance of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion, with the midpoint ahead of Wall Street's $10.6 billion outlook.

EPS, though, is set to come in between $2.15 and $2.35 with a midpoint of $2.25. Analysts were looking for $2.32

Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:18 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma

Cava results fall just shy of estimates due to impact of cyclospora outbreak. Company raises outlook.

Mediterranean fast-casual chain Cava ( CAVA ) posted earnings and revenue that fell short of Wall Street's expectations as the company saw strength to end the quarter, following industry pressure.

Cava revenue came in at $353.7 million, below the $358.7 million the Street expected, per Bloomberg estimates. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.11, one penny lower than forecasts. Same-store sales grew by 3.1%, a touch lower than the 3.3% the Street hoped for.

"We saw obviously broader concerns around fresh produce consumption early in the quarter that certainly impacted trend, we saw that bounce back as we worked through the quarter and then toward the end of the quarter," CEO Brett Schulman told Yahoo Finance.

Schulman added, "Post Labor Day, we did see a bit of choppiness around the re-emergence of high gas prices as they spiked, but then saw that abate, things firm up and strengthen as we exited the quarter and have seen that carryover into Q4."

He said that gave the company confidence to raise its outlook for the full fiscal year. It now expects same-store sales to increase between 6% and 7%, up from the previously expected range of 4.5% to 6.5%. The updated forecast is in line with the Street's 6.7% expectation.

The company plans to open 76 to 78 restaurants this year, but the company noted that pre-opening costs did get more expensive, driven by pre-opening labor costs. Its new restaurant design is also resonating with customers, who are seeing an increase in in-restaurant dining, especially at dinner. Schulman said that's not at the expense of digital orders, which account for 38.5% of revenue.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 9:33 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

AMD beats Q3 estimates as data center revenue climbs 97%

AMD ( AMD ) reported its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines, as the company's data center revenue grew 97%.

AMD stock climbed more than 4% following the news.

"Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production," CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years."

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 on revenue of $13.38 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $1.97 on revenue of $13.08 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 9:32 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Duolingo stock jumps as daily users surge, company raises guidance

Duolingo ( DUOL ) stock jumped 10% after the company reported that its daily active users (DAUs) rose 29% year over year to 64.9 million. Paid subscribers for the language learning platform grew 14% annually to 13.1 million.

But the company is eyeing stronger user growth as it targets a goal of 1 billion users. Duolingo said its operating expenses increased 24% year over year. Those expenses included $11.4 million that the company set aside for a company-wide performance bonus for employees if it achieves DAU growth of 25% or greater in Q4.

Here's what Duolingo reported in Q3, versus estiamtes compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:

Revenue: $309 million, up 12% year over year, versus estimates of $303 million

Earnings per share: $0.58, versus estimates of $0.56

Guidance: Raised across all key financial metrics. Revenue is expected at $1.22 billion, ahead of the Street's forecast of $1.20 billion

"We expect to finish 2026 at the high end of both the 10% to 12% bookings growth and 15% to 18% revenue growth targets we set at the start of the year. We expect full-year Adjusted EBITDA of $323 million, or a 26.5% margin, up $3 million from our previous guidance, and $21 million above the midpoint of our original 2026 guidance provided in February," the company stated.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 9:19 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Super Micro tops Q1 estimates, offers strong Q2 outlook

Yahoo Finance's Daniel Howley reports:

Data center infrastructure company Super Micro ( SMCI ) reported its fiscal first quarter earnings after the bell on Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated outlook for Q2.

The company said it anticipates Q2 sales of between $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion. Analysts were calling for $16.35 billion.

Super Micro stock rose more than 5% immediately following the news.

"Supermicro's transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate, delivering record revenue of $19.9 billion for the first quarter fiscal 2027," CEO Charles Liang said in a statement.

"DCBBS is driving significant value for our customers—from gigawatt-scale datacenters down to single-container PODs—which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, superior up-time and more cost-effective for our customer base."

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:20 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Pfizer focuses on GLP-1, oncology drug development as COVID product sales decline

Pfizer ( PFE ) stock fell slightly on Tuesday despite reporting an earnings beat and upbeat guidance. The pharmaceutical company said it saw operational revenue growth contributions from several treatments, including Eliquis, Paxlovid, the Vyndaqel family, Nurtec, and Lorbrena, during the quarter, though its COVID-19 products declined.

In the earnings call, Pfizer said it expects to spend $10.8 billion-$11.8 billion on research and development this year, particularly on developing its oncology and obesity pipeline. Pfizer is working on berobenatide, a GLP-1 injectable administered only once a month rather than weekly, as well as several cancer drugs.

"Pfizer had another strong quarter with commercial momentum and disciplined execution while advancing our strategy for creating long-term shareholder value," CEO Albert Bourla said in a release. "Our obesity program continued to advance and recent milestones in oncology, immunology and vaccines further demonstrate the potential of our pipeline."

In the third quarter, Pfizer reported revenue was little changed year over year at $16.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $15.9 billion, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. Earnings per share came in at $0.56, beating Wall Street's estimates of $0.48 per share.

Pfizer lifted its full-year revenue guidance to a range of $62 billion to $64 billion, up from $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion previously. The company also raised and narrowed its 2026 earnings per share guidance to $2.95 to $3.05.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 4:37 PM UTC Ines Ferré

Shopify stock tanks as Q3 revenue, total order value miss Wall Street estimates

Shopify ( SHOP ) stock plunged 7% on Tuesday after reporting third quarter results that missed the mark on several key metrics.

The cloud-based e-commerce platform's Q3 revenue of $3.74 billion came in just shy of consensus estimates of $3.75 billion for the first time since 2022, according to Bloomberg data. Subscription revenue for the quarter of $836 million also missed Wall Street expectations of $850.2 million, raising concerns about growth in its main recurring-revenue business.

Gross merchandise volume, or the total dollar value of orders sold through Shopify's platform, was $119.15 billion, also falling short of estimates of $120.08 billion.

Shopify's adjusted earnings per share of $0.49 topped estimates of $0.48.

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 9:39 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Apple tops Q4 estimates on strong iPhone sales, but misses on China revenue

Apple ( AAPL ) stock is declining in extended trading after beating on earnings but missing on China revenue.

Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports on the quarter:

Apple reported its fourth quarter earnings after the bell on Monday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines on strong iPhone sales.

This is Apple's first earnings call with new CEO John Ternus , who took over the role from Tim Cook on Sept. 1.

For the quarter, Apple reported earnings per share (EPS) of $2.10 on revenue of $114.48 billion. Wall Street was looking for EPS of $2 on revenue of $113.46 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates.

The company saw EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $102.46 billion in the same period last year.

Read live updates and analysis from the quarter and earnings call >

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 9:24 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Roku sales grow 24% year over year ahead of Fox acquisition

Roku ( ROKU ) reported a substantial earnings beat on Monday, driven by its ninth straight quarter of double-digit advertising growth.

Here's what Roku reported, compared to Wall Street analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:

Revenue : up 24% year over year to $1.5 billion, versus estimates of $1.41 billion.

Advertising revenue grew 23% YoY to $727 million.

Subscriptions revenue grew 23% YoY to $581 million.

Earnings per share: $1.20, versus estimates of $0.55.

Guidance: None given.

Roku stock was little changed following the report.

In June, Roku entered an agreement to be acquired by Fox ( FOX ). The company said that, in light of its pending takeover, it would not host an earnings call or provide a forecast.

"Our third quarter demonstrated that we succeed when our partners succeed, whether it is a streaming service gaining subscribers through Premium Subscriptions, a content company monetizing its library on The Roku Channel, an advertiser buying through a third-party DSP, or a TV brand choosing the Roku TV OS," CEO Anthony Wood wrote in a press release.

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 9:11 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Palantir raises full-year revenue outlook as US commercial sales accelerate

Yahoo Finance's Ines Ferré reports:

Palantir ( PLTR ) beat Wall Street estimates on its third quarter revenue and profit on Monday and raised its full-year revenue outlook as the data software company's US commercial business surpassed its US government sales for the first time ever.

Palantir reported Q3 revenue of $2.313 billion, a 96% increase from the previous year. Wall Street had expected revenue of $2.17 billion, according to Bloomberg data.

Palantir now sees full-year revenue between $8.530 billion and $8.534 billion, topping analyst estimates of $8.2 billion. The company also raised its US commercial sales target to more than $3.559 billion. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.44 also beat consensus estimates of $0.40.

news.Title: 不只輝達！三星、台積電與美光第三季自由現金流更勝一籌
news.Content:
人工智慧(AI)基礎建設投資持續升溫，市場焦點長期集中在輝達(NVIDIA) (NVDA-US)等晶片設計業者，但半導體供應鏈另一端的記憶體與晶圓代工廠，同樣成為AI資本支出的重要受益者。

《Benzinga》報導指出，三星電子、台積電與美光在第三季創造的自由現金流，甚至超越輝達，凸顯AI熱潮帶來的資金效益，正大量流向提供晶片、記憶體及製造服務的企業。

這項變化反映AI產業獲利模式的另一面。輝達雖然掌握AI加速器市場的重要地位，但雲端服務業者與大型科技公司為建置資料中心投入龐大資本，必須向晶片供應商採購GPU、記憶體及其他關鍵零組件。

相較之下，晶片供應商直接承接設備與零組件需求，能將客戶的資本支出轉化為營收與現金流。

三星電子第三季業績創下新高，營收達195.3兆韓元，季增14%，營業利益達107.4兆韓元，成為全球首家單季營業利益突破100兆韓元的科技企業。

其中，半導體部門營收達147.1兆韓元，營業利益達106.5兆韓元，顯示AI相關記憶體需求已成為獲利主要動能。

三星表示，AI應用帶動高頻寬記憶體(HBM)、伺服器DRAM及固態硬碟(SSD)需求，記憶體業務第三季營收與營業利益均創新高。

公司也指出，2027年AI基礎設施投資預期將進一步擴大，相關需求可能明顯超過產業供給。

三星第三季資本支出達29兆韓元，較前一季增加12.2兆韓元，年增19.8兆韓元；今年前9個月累計資本支出為56.9兆韓元。

公司預估2026年全年資本支出約84.4兆韓元，其中76.8兆韓元將投入半導體部門，以擴充產能並因應AI與高效能運算(HPC)需求。

台積電 (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company) (TSM-US)同樣受惠於先進製程需求。台積電第三季合併營收達1.494兆元新台幣，約467.2億美元，年增50.9%。

同期稅後淨利達7,630.6億元，年增68.7%，每股稀釋盈餘29.43元。毛利率達66.4%，營業利益率58.7%，展現先進製程在AI晶片供應鏈中的獲利能力。

從製程組合來看，台積電第三季2奈米製程已貢獻晶圓營收8%，3奈米占33%，5奈米占28%，7奈米占10%。

7奈米及更先進製程合計占晶圓營收79%。公司預估第四季營收將達523億至543億美元，毛利率介於65%至67%，營業利益率介於56.5%至58.5%，顯示先進製程需求仍維持強勁。

美光 (Micron Technology) (MU-US)則是AI記憶體需求的另一大受益者。隨著AI伺服器需要大量高頻寬記憶體與高容量DRAM，記憶體產品的需求與價格同步受到支撐。

美光2026會計年度第四季營收達1,331.88億美元，全年調整後自由現金流達623.1億美元；第四季單季調整後自由現金流為332億美元，反映記憶體市場景氣改善後，獲利與現金創造能力大幅提升。

news.Title: Qualcomm (QCOM) Q4 Earnings: How Key Metrics Compare to Wall Street Estimates
news.Content:
For the quarter ended September 2026, Qualcomm (QCOM) reported revenue of $10.44 billion, down 7.4% over the same period last year. EPS came in at $2.17, compared to $3.00 in the year-ago quarter.

The reported revenue compares to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $10.15 billion, representing a surprise of +2.92%. The company delivered an EPS surprise of +0.46%, with the consensus EPS estimate being $2.16.

While investors closely watch year-over-year changes in headline numbers -- revenue and earnings -- and how they compare to Wall Street expectations to determine their next course of action, some key metrics always provide a better insight into a company's underlying performance.

As these metrics influence top- and bottom-line performance, comparing them to the year-ago numbers and what analysts estimated helps investors project a stock's price performance more accurately.

Here is how Qualcomm performed in the just reported quarter in terms of the metrics most widely monitored and projected by Wall Street analysts:

Revenues- QCT : $9.02 billion versus the six-analyst average estimate of $8.74 billion. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of -8.2%.

Revenues- QTL : $1.3 billion versus $1.3 billion estimated by six analysts on average. Compared to the year-ago quarter, this number represents a -7.5% change.

Revenues- QCT- Automotive : $1.99 billion versus the five-analyst average estimate of $1.71 billion. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of +89%.

Revenues- QCT- Handsets : $5.14 billion versus the five-analyst average estimate of $5.22 billion. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of -26.2%.

Revenues- QCT- IoT (internet of things) : $1.89 billion versus the five-analyst average estimate of $1.82 billion. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of +4.5%.

Income / (loss) before taxes- QTL : $918 million versus the two-analyst average estimate of $907.53 million.

Income / (loss) before taxes- QCT : $2.14 billion versus the two-analyst average estimate of $2.09 billion.

View all Key Company Metrics for Qualcomm here>>>

Shares of Qualcomm have returned -9.2% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -2% change. The stock currently has a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), indicating that it could underperform the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Here's What a $1,000 Investment in AMD Could Be Worth by 2030
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) has been one of the top-performing stocks in 2026, clocking impressive gains of over 120% as of this writing, and the good news is that it can deliver further gains to investors thanks to an acceleration in growth.

AMD released its third-quarter results on Nov. 3, and the stock soared the following day. Let's see why that was the case and check how much upside this fast-growing semiconductor stock could deliver by the end of the decade.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

AMD's data center business has supercharged its growth

AMD's Q3 revenue increased 45% year over year to $13.4 billion. The company's non-GAAP earnings per share of $2.09 increased by 74% from the year-ago period. AMD's data center business was the primary driver of its impressive growth, with the segment's revenue nearly doubling year over year to a record $8.5 billion.

It is worth noting that AMD's revenue and earnings easily exceeded Wall Street's expectations. The company noted healthy demand for its Epyc server processors and Instinct data center graphics cards. The good news for AMD investors is that the company expects data center revenue to accelerate in the current quarter. What's more, its full-year data center revenue is on track to double from 2025 levels.

Looking ahead, AMD expects the data center segment to account for 80% of its top line in 2027. That implies a major improvement over the previous quarter, when the data center segment produced 64% of AMD's top line. Moreover, the increasing reliance on the data center business is a good sign for AMD, given the ongoing weakness in the personal computer market.

AMD reported an 8% year-over-year decline in its client and gaming segment revenue last quarter to $3.7 billion. Notably, its PC-focused client processor revenue increased 7% from the year-ago period despite a 21% decline in PC industry shipments last quarter. The gaming segment continues to struggle due to the aging gaming console generation. However, the potential arrival of a new generation of gaming consoles next year could lift this segment and complement the healthy growth AMD has been witnessing in data centers.

Importantly, AMD expects significant acceleration in growth despite challenging conditions in the gaming and PC markets. The company expects revenue to increase by 66% year over year in the current quarter, a substantial step up from the 45% growth seen in the previous one.

Story Continues

Here's why you can invest $1,000 in this stock

If you have $1,000 in investable cash right now after paying your bills, clearing expensive loans, and saving enough for tough times, buying AMD stock could be a smart move before it soars higher. That's because the company has tremendous earnings growth potential, as evident from the following chart.

YCharts

Assuming its bottom line increases by even 20% in 2029 and 2030, its earnings per share could reach $33.41 by the end of the decade (using 2028's estimated earnings per share of $23.20 as the base). If AMD trades at 30 times earnings at that time, in line with the tech-laden Nasdaq-100 index's earnings multiple, its stock price could reach $1,002. That's 93% higher than AMD's current stock price.

So, AMD can turn a $1,000 investment into more than $1,900 in just over four years, making it an ideal investment for anyone looking to add a growth stock to their portfolio.

news.Title: 台股跌成廢半！「這顆」未爆彈成隱患　散戶凹單挫咧等
news.Content:
台股融資維持率降至143.7%，指數回檔14%但融資僅微減5.7%。本土法人指出，散戶越跌越買導致籌碼沉澱不足，加上美股費半劇烈震盪，隱含多殺多風險。（AI製圖）

台股近期震盪劇烈，指數從高點回檔的同時，散戶的融資動向也成了一場微妙的心理戰。當美股費半指數在夜盤牽動台指期上沖下洗、漲幅從千點急縮之際，市場正悄悄上演一齣籌碼未清的戲碼。對一般投資人而言，看懂這波融資與夜盤的變化，才能在震盪行情中看清多空真正的底牌。

融資維持率暗藏玄機　散戶越跌越買成隱憂

回顧台股下半年的軌跡，7月30日加權指數落在39,384點的相對低點，當時融資餘額為4,938億元，預估融資維持率為132.5%，經過一波洗盤後籌碼相對乾淨；隨後指數一路向上攀高，在10月5日來到49,968點的相對高點，漲幅達26.87%，融資餘額也同步擴增至6,333億元，維持率回升到176.8%。

然而，到了11月4日最新收盤狀態，加權指數回落至42,948點，自高點回檔14.04%，但同期的融資餘額卻僅從高點微降5.74%、仍高達5,969億元，導致預估融資維持率下滑至143.7%。

這其中的貓膩就在於指數跌幅明顯大於融資減幅，顯示許多投資人在回檔過程中選擇越跌越買或捨不得停損，籌碼沉澱不夠徹底。

夜盤費半急殺震撼　漲勢收斂考驗持股信心

除了籌碼面的觀察，國際股市的牽動同樣牽動著投資人的神經。從盤中即時資訊來看，台指近全（TXF8）夜盤一度大漲來到43,348點，盤中漲幅達145點或0.34%，但美股費半指數盤中遭到重挫，跌幅擴大至3.81%、滑落至10,196點附近，直接衝擊夜盤表現，讓原本預期大漲上千點的氣勢瞬間急凍，收斂僅剩小漲百點左右。

這種劇烈震盪不僅讓期貨與現貨市場的短線交易人捏一把冷汗，也反映出科技與半導體族群在高檔震盪時的脆弱度，投資人在面對融資壓力與國際盤勢夾擊時，更需要嚴控資金風險，避免遭到被動斷頭的殺盤風險。

news.Title: Qualcomm (QCOM) Tops Q4 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
news.Content:
Qualcomm (QCOM) came out with quarterly earnings of $2.17 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.16 per share. This compares to earnings of $3 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +0.46%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this chipmaker would post earnings of $2.22 per share when it actually produced earnings of $2.21, delivering a surprise of -0.45%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

Qualcomm, which belongs to the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, posted revenues of $10.44 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.92%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $11.27 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates two times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Qualcomm shares have lost about 3.9% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 10.6%.

What's Next for Qualcomm?

While Qualcomm has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Qualcomm was unfavorable. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to underperform the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $2.37 on $10.65 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $10.02 on $44.49 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Electronics - Semiconductors is currently in the top 35% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

nLight (LASR), another stock in the same industry, has yet to report results for the quarter ended September 2026. The results are expected to be released on November 5.

This laser maker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.06 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -25%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

nLight's revenues are expected to be $67.96 million, up 1.8% from the year-ago quarter.

news.Title: 不買輝達、英特爾！外媒揭退休投資人「只押台積電」 致勝底氣曝光
news.Content:
全球AI浪潮持續席捲半導體產業，台積電憑藉先進製程技術，成為這波科技革命最重要的受惠者之一，儘管近期股價出現明顯回檔，截至4日，台積電ADR短短1個月下跌逾15％，卻有退休投資人逆勢加碼，甚至表示今年只要手中有多餘資金，就會持續買進台積電。

外媒《24/7 Wall St.》報導，金融作家Alex Sirois指出，台積電最大的競爭優勢，在於掌握全球先進晶片製造的核心地位，隨著輝達、蘋果及各大科技巨頭積極布局AI，不論晶片由哪家企業設計，最終都需要仰賴晶圓代工廠生產，而台積電正是目前先進製程市場的關鍵業者。

支撐投資台積電信心不只是AI題材，更包括亮眼的營收成長、優異的獲利能力，以及充沛的自由現金流。台積電第3季營收年增41.2％，達467.2億美元，毛利率更高達66.4％，營業利益率58.7％，股東權益報酬率（ROE）45.5％，均高於公司設定的長期目標。

此外，先進製程需求持續升溫，也帶動台積電7奈米及以下先進製程占晶圓營收的79％，2奈米製程營收占比從單季內從3％提高至8％。而且，台積電不僅具備強大的資本支出能力，還持續提高單季股利，從每股新台幣6元調高至7元，讓長期投資人有機會同時掌握資產增值與現金收入。

相較於直接投資輝達或承受英特爾晶圓代工業務的轉型風險，文章認為，布局台積電等於參與多家AI晶片業者的成長機會。不過，地緣政治風險及海外擴廠帶來的成本壓力，仍是投資人不能忽視的隱憂。

news.Title: 台股盤中暴殺1451點！達人曝「大舉進場黃金時機」：鎖定2大轉折點
news.Content: 台股4日遭遇猛烈賣壓，加權指數盤中一度暴跌1451點，最低下探41,855.82點，摜破42,000點整數關卡，終場跌幅雖然收斂，仍下跌358.63點，以42,948.91點作收。面對台股劇烈震盪、電子股與半導體族群重挫，以及市場傳出融資斷頭壓力，投資人開始尋找低檔布局機會。 投資達人《小犬的投資日誌》 提醒，現在還不是急著進場撿便宜的時候，真正值得留意的是融資斷頭潮結束，以及美國大選結果明朗後的兩個轉折訊號。 【台股盤中暴跌1451點！小犬提醒別急著接刀】 《小犬的投資日誌》在臉書發文指出，11月4日台股走勢宛如坐大怒神，盤中一度狂瀉超過千點，終場仍重挫358點，市場成交量更爆出1.1兆元天量。電子、半導體族群全面遭到賣壓襲擊，融資交易也面臨斷頭壓力。 眼看不少個股股價大幅修正，甚至跌到相對低檔，不少投資人難免心動，想趁市場恐慌時進場撿便宜。不過，小犬提醒，市場劇烈震盪時，盲目進場反而容易被套牢，與其急著搶反彈，不如先觀察籌碼是否真正沉澱，等待更明確的止跌訊號。 【第一個進場訊號：融資斷頭潮結束】 小犬認為，第一個值得留意的時間點，是融資斷頭潮結束的隔天。當市場出現融資追繳、強制賣出等壓力，往往會加速短線籌碼汰弱留強，但投資人不能只因為股價大跌，就認定市場已經落底。 他建議觀察大盤是否出現爆量長下影線，或隔天開盤大幅走低，卻能迅速拉升、收出長紅K棒。這類走勢代表低檔有買盤承接，市場賣壓可能逐漸獲得消化，也有機會成為短線止跌的重要觀察訊號。 【第二個進場訊號：美國大選結果明朗】 第二個關鍵則是美國大選結果出爐。小犬指出，市場最害怕的往往不是已經發生的利空，而是不確定性。當美國大選開票結束、政治局勢逐漸明朗，原本觀望的資金可能重新回流股市，市場也有機會迎來利空出盡的反彈行情。 因此，他認為，投資人可以留意美國大選結果，以及後續市場資金動向，等待不確定因素逐步消除，再評估進場布局的時機。簡而言之，現在要做的功課就是觀察選舉結果對美股、台股及資金流向的後續影響。 【小犬喊先守住現金：等待台股反攻訊號】 小犬最後提醒，現階段先不要急著進場接刀子，應該好好守住手上的現金，耐心等待市場出現更明確的轉折。他特別點出，美國大選結果明朗，以及新台幣止貶回升，都是接下來觀察台股能否重新轉強的重要指標。 換句話說，台股急跌後雖然可能浮現低接機會，但真正值得把握的，不只是股價跌了多少，而是融資賣壓是否告一段落、資金是否重新回流。等這些訊號逐漸明朗，才是評估是否擴大布局的時候。 三立新聞網提醒您：

news.Title: 台股大怒神 外資狂砍1499億元
news.Content:
台股4日上演驚險「大怒神」行情，早盤上漲逾400點、最高4萬3741點，美期中選舉牽動投資人敏感神經，加上市場對蘋果財測疑慮難除、外資狂砍台股1499億元，台股恐慌賣壓湧現，指數一舉摜破42K，最低下探4萬1855點，如雲霄飛車般驚險，上下震盪逾1885點；尾盤跌勢收斂、跌358點，收在4萬2948點，成交量1.17兆元。惟部分分析師、科技大老仍看好台股未來表現，認為台股水草豐盛，如遊牧民族的熱錢，終將會回流具備高可靠度與成長潛力的標的。

外資單日狂賣台股1499億元，創下史上第五大賣超紀錄，台積電跌1.53％，收在2260元，聯發科一度跌到3455元，台達電跌幅更是超過4％，最低來到1160元，幾乎是高點腰斬價格。不過，昨晚10時40分許，台指期夜盤呈現反彈，上漲逾300點。

國泰證期顧問部分析師郭經緯分析，美國科技股財報不如預期，現在又遇上美國期中選舉政策不確定性，讓台股跌跌不休；但他認為，現在是好股票大拍賣時刻，是加碼有獲利、持續成長權值好股的好時機，點名加碼台積電、台達電、聯發科與大立光。

台股走弱，摩爾投顧投資長郭哲榮昨宣布，再砸5000萬元買進元大台灣50（0050），前後累計買進金額達1.5億元。

郭哲榮公開自己在永豐金證券板新分行的代碼是9A9J，透露買進512張以上0050，買進價格為97.8元，由於0050終場拉尾收在99.85元，若不計手續費帳面獲利約105萬元，報酬率約為2.1％。

郭哲榮分析，美國期中選舉結束、台股利空出盡、狂拉千點下影線，民主黨大獲全勝，投資市場最大風險不是AI資料中心建置，最大疑慮其實是通膨，他認為選後有助於美國總統川普與伊朗談判。

對於台股動盪，和碩董事長童子賢表示，台灣科技產業底氣十足，投資人不必恐慌，並分析，台股總市值逾5兆美元，台積電占比近4成，推估台積電全年每股純益（EPS）有望突破百元大關，以目前股價換算本益比僅約20倍，在全球前10大市值科技股中「老實誠懇」，完全沒有高估疑慮。

至於外資大舉提款，童子賢把熱錢比喻成「逐水草而居的遊牧民族」，短期撤出僅是為了追逐國外新股掛牌或短線熱潮，但台灣科技產業的「水草一向豐盛」，過個2到4周熱潮退去，資金終究會回流尋找具備高可靠度與成長潛力的標的。他也建議投資人回歸產業基本面，「最好久久看一次，不要天天盯盤搞得心情七上八下」。

news.Title: What a $115 Billion Deal to Buy Lumentum Really Means for Marvell Stock Investors
news.Content:
Semiconductor company Marvell Technology (MRVL) is all set to acquire Lumentum (LITE), a leading supplier of optical and photonic technologies, for $115 billion in an all-stock deal. Under the terms of the agreement, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell for each share of LITE stock they own. Marvell shareholders will own 67% of the combined company, while the rest will be held by Lumentum shareholders.

Marvell investors made their displeasure about the development clear, with shares ending almost 13% lower on Nov. 2 and down again today. They appear to believe the price tag of the deal is too high while the heavy dilution is also undesirable. Notably, the $115 billion consideration is an 86% premium to Lumentum's current market capitalization of $61.6 billion.

More News from Barchart

Why Investors Should Load Up on Google Stock Now

Billionaire Mark Cuban Says the Hardest Part of Fixing Health Costs Isn't the CEOs or Insurance Companies, 'Employees Fight Any Change'

Coca-Cola Pays Warren Buffett's Berkshire $848 Million a Year as Jim Cramer Says Buy KO Stock

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

However, Marvell management believes that the deal has the potential to result in cost savings of more than $1 billion. "The companies that move first and help define this transition will set the standard for decades to come," said CEO Matt Murphy, describing the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market's focus on optical connectivity as a "once in a generation" opportunity. "By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, exceptional talent and specialized manufacturing capabilities, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional stockholder value."

About Marvell Technology

Founded in 1995, Marvell is an AI infrastructure company centered on data-center connectivity, custom silicon, optical interconnects, switching, and storage. Its custom silicon business in particular includes custom AI accelerators, XPUs, networking chips, storage and memory controllers, and data-center interconnect products. Marvell has an impressive customer base that includes Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), and Alphabet (GOOGL), among others.

Marvell currently commands a market cap of $150.8 billion, with MRVL stock up an impressive 86% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. Notably, the stock also offers a modest dividend yield of 0.14%.

So, keeping the immediate market reaction aside, how will Marvell's impending acquisition of Lumentum impact its operations? Let's take a closer look.

Story Continues

Lumentum Is Legit for Marvell in the Long Haul

One rationale being bandied about the deal is that Marvell will gain access to Lumentum's expertise in optical transceivers, which allows for faster data transfer with less power. However, Marvell is buying more than faster optical transceivers. The bigger ambition of the deal is to control more of the technology connecting AI processors — from custom silicon and networking chips to lasers, optical modules, and optical circuit switches.

Notably, Marvell wants to design the electrical and optical signal chain together rather than optimize individual components separately. Bringing its silicon photonics, switching, and custom processors together with Lumentum's lasers and optical manufacturing could reduce engineering friction, simplify customer qualification, and shorten development cycles, resulting in the development of a vertically integrated semiconductor player that is harder to replace once its technologies are incorporated into a customer's design.

Meanwhile, Lumentum also brings indium phosphide capabilities and specialized laser production that complement Marvell's semiconductor design strengths. Additionally, optical circuit switching provides a separate growth opportunity beyond transceivers.

On Nov. 2, amid its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results, Lumentum said that optical circuit switch (OCS) demand visibility could support a business generating several billion dollars annually. Management also disclosed a second major win involving optics placed near or alongside processors, supported by purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion. Those commitments give the Marvell acquisition thesis more substance than a broad forecast for rising AI traffic alone.

Finally, with Lumentum, Marvell will be able to offer potential customers a more complete alternative to its larger peer and biggest competitor, Broadcom (AVGO). However, integration also creates a potential channel conflict. Customers that currently buy components from independent suppliers may hesitate if their supplier becomes a broader competitor. Marvell must preserve those relationships while pursuing more integrated sales.

Marvell Reports a Super Q2

Before examining Marvell's Q2 figures, we should look at the company's updated commentary on fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 revenue. Marvell raised its revenue outlook for both years, now projecting fiscal 2027 revenue of $12 billion and fiscal 2028 revenue of $18 billion, up from previous guidance of $11.5 billion and $16.5 billion, respectively. Within the fiscal 2028 outlook, Marvell anticipates data-center revenue growth of 60%, underscoring continued strength in the largest segment of the AI infrastructure buildout.

That momentum was visible in the latest quarterly results as well. Marvell reported record net revenue of $2.74 billion in Q2 fiscal 2027, representing a 37% increase from the prior year. Although that absolute figure set a new high, the growth rate lagged Broadcom, which recorded a 48% rise in its corresponding Q2 results. Meanwhile, Marvell's data-center revenue advanced 46% year-over-year (YOY) to $2.17 billion in Q2.

Gross margins contracted modestly to 58.9% from 59.4% in the year-ago period as stock-based compensation rose to $15.9 million from $13.4 million. Nevertheless, EPS increased 40% YOY to $0.94, just above the consensus estimate of $0.93.

For Q3, Marvell guided EPS between $1.05 and $1.15. Gross margins for Q3 are expected to fall in the range of 57.5% to 58.5%.

Net cash from operating activities improved to $605.5 million from $461.6 million in the prior year. Overall, Marvell closed Q2 with $3.93 billion in cash and no short-term debt. Long-term debt of approximately $5 billion, however, continues to appear as higher interest expense on the income statement. Interest expense rose to $61.6 million from $51.9 million in the same period last year.

Meanwhile, the searing rally in MRVL stock this year has led to punchy valuations. Its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 56.1 times, price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 18.3 times, and price-to-cash flow (P/CF) multiple of 47.1 times are all above the sector medians of 21.1 times, 3.2 times, and 18.7 times, respectively.

What Do Analysts Think of MRVL Stock?

Taking all of this into account, analysts have a consensus "Strong Buy" rating for MRVL stock overall. Out of 39 analysts covering the stock, 28 have a "Strong Buy" rating, three have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and eight have a "Hold" rating. The mean target price of $317.05 denotes potential upside of 102% from current levels.

news.Title: Tesla Wants to Build 20,000 Optimus Robots a Week. Here's the Supplier That Gets Paid for Every Single One -- and It's Not Nvidia.
news.Content: Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) aims to produce up to one million Optimus robots in 2027. To achieve that ambitious goal, it plans to ramp up its production to 20,000 units per week. That's great news for Tesla's suppliers , but one hot chipmaker that was left out of the loop was Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). Instead of using Nvidia's AI chips , the Optimus uses Tesla's own custom Full Self-Driving (FSD) inference chips. But Texas Instruments (NASDAQ: TXN), which doesn't get as much attention as Nvidia, actually produces ...
news.AI_Summary:
• Tesla plans to produce up to 20,000 Optimus robots per week by 2027, utilizing its custom FSD inference chips instead of Nvidia's AI chips.
• Texas Instruments (TI) is a key supplier for Optimus, providing power, driver, and signal-chain components for its servo motors and battery management systems.
• TI could generate $250 million to $500 million in annual revenue from Optimus components if Tesla reaches its production targets.
• TI's diversified business model, supplying essential components across various industries including AI and automotive, offers stability and growth potential, with analysts projecting strong revenue and EPS growth.
