news.Title: Nvidia Stocks Decline 1.35% as $108 Billion Guide Sets the Next Revenue Hurdle
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) has a high bar to clear: $108 billion in quarterly revenue. Shares fell 1.35% to $203.90 at 8:41 a.m. ET on November 4 in premarket trading, as investors weighed the next earnings test. A Trefis review put the Vera Rubin rollout in focus, but the revenue target comes from Nvidia's existing guidance. The challenge is turning another product transition into profitable growth.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with NVDA.

Is NVDA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Nvidia's fiscal second-quarter release showed approximately $96.2 billion in revenue and a 75% non-GAAP gross margin. Its third-quarter outlook puts revenue within 2% of the $108 billion midpoint and gross margin at 74%, plus or minus half a percentage point. That forecast excludes China data-center compute sales. Using rounded figures, Nvidia needs another $11.8 billion in sequential revenuea 12.3% increasewhile absorbing a projected one-percentage-point margin decline. At the midpoint, those assumptions imply roughly $79.9 billion in gross profit.

The GuruFocus chart adds perspective: Nvidia's GF Score of 96/100 reflects strong profitability, growth, financial strength and momentum, while GF Value is visibly its weakest dimension. That suggests business quality may offer more support than valuation. The next report therefore needs to show more than rising sales. Shipment execution and transition costs could determine how much of that additional revenue reaches gross profitand whether operating performance can support investor expectations.

news.Title: Why Cricut Stock Soared 50% Today
news.Content: Creative-tech pioneer Cricut (NASDAQ:CRCT) posted Q3 2026 results on Tuesday evening. Today, the stock is up by exactly 50% as of 1:40 p.m. ET. It trades for prices not seen since the fall of 2023. Yep, Cricut smashed expectations in the last quarter. Image source: Getty Images. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Low bar, high jump The average Wall Street analyst expected a lukewarm report. Earnings were supposed to rise from $0.04 per share in the year-ago period to $0.05 this time. On the top line, the consensus called for 4.7% growth to $164.4 million. Cricut left those targets far behind, posting $0.13 of earnings per share on $188.6 million in sales. The installed base is paying off The Platform segment saw single-digit revenue growth and flattish revenue per user. In the Products division, on the other hand, sales roared 17% higher and international sales jumped 30%. In all fairness, Q3 2025 was a soft quarter, which made this year's comparison easier. Still, Cricut is building a critical mass of installed machines in America and a few overseas markets. As a result, marketing pushes and new product introductions can move the financial needle much further. The stock still looks affordable at 19.2 times trailing earnings, after Wednesday's massive price jump. Not bad for a company Wall Street had nearly written off as a pandemic fad in 2021. Cricut just reminded Wall Street that machine-aided crafting never really went out of style. Missed Nvidia in 2009? If you'd invested $5,000 then, you'd be sitting on $2,686,757 today.* Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. news.Title: 〈美國期中選舉〉選完也別急著追AI股！華爾街提醒贏家輸家要挑清楚
news.Content:
民主黨在美國期中選舉拿下國會兩院，美股周三上漲，部分AI概念股卻逆勢走低。華爾街分析師認為，選舉結果可能讓資料中心建設面臨更多限制，但算力需求並未消失；真正的變數在於建設速度、成本，以及放慢投資能否緩解市場對過度舉債的疑慮。

據《彭博》報導，那斯達克100指數上漲逾1%之際，CoreWeave(CRWV-US)、輝達(NVDA-US)及邁威爾(MRVL-US)等AI相關股票下跌。對分析師而言，這場選舉既帶來政策風險，也可能促使產業重新檢視支出紀律。

需求不會消失 資料中心恐蓋得更慢更貴

Truist投資長暨首席市場策略師Keith Lerner認為，選舉增加了資料中心發展路徑與速度的不確定性，但龐大算力需求仍會支持建設。業者可能面臨租稅優惠調整、地方反對，必須改變設廠地點，或接受更多限制與配套條件。

Wealthspire投資長Brad Long指出，德州選舉結果可能讓兩黨政治人物更加重視反資料中心民意。為了爭取連任，更多地方官員可能跟進，主張保護社區免受資料中心擴張影響。

他認為，市場需要消化的問題，不是資料中心會不會蓋，而是「蓋在哪裡、需要多久，以及得通過多少行政程序」。這些阻力可能延後資本支出，也推遲AI投資效益實現的時間。

RWA Wealth Partners投資長JP Powers則認為，市場擔憂可能有些過度，既有計畫未必受到太大影響。不過，業者若須增加地方回饋或因應更多法規，確實可能推升建設與營運成本。

擴張放慢未必全是壞事 有助緩解燒錢壓力

野村跨資產策略師Charlie McElligott提出另一種解讀：選舉若迫使美國資料中心建設放慢，可能緩和大型雲端業者不斷加碼資本支出的競賽，減輕市場對大量發債、股票籌資及自由現金流消耗的疑慮。

這也是選後市場可能偏向樂觀看待的原因之一。在此之前，投資人已開始擔心，AI投資規模持續膨脹，相關融資需求與回報前景是否能夠匹配。

盈透證券首席策略師Steve Sosnick表示，市場對業者支出過於激進、借款規模過大的擔憂有其道理。若建設速度降至較可控的程度，雖然對供應商不利，卻可能替產業帶來市場願意接受的財務紀律。

他也指出，資料中心建設已有龐大動能，牽涉大量就業，幾位州長當選及國會權力更替，不至於讓整體發展完全停下來。

年底行情添阻力 科技股反彈仍須挑選贏家

Miller Tabak首席市場策略師Matt Maley則提醒，AI產業面臨的阻力正在增加，可能讓市場更難出現期中選舉年份常見的年底漲勢。他預期，反對資料中心進駐社區的聲音，也將迅速成為2028年選舉議題。

加拿大皇家銀行資本市場美股策略主管Lori Calvasina認為，即使國會未採取明顯行動，州長選舉結果仍帶來政策風險，因為AI與資料中心已是部分激烈選戰的重要議題。她也對選舉能否成為市場風險解除的轉折點抱持保留態度。

摩根大通(JPM-US)全球市場情報主管Andrew Tyler則維持短線看多科技股的立場。他指出，德州候任州長Gina Hinojosa主張，在新規範建立前立即暫停資料中心建設，但實際影響仍有不同解讀。

一種可能是既有工程與許可繼續推進，新計畫轉往其他州；另一種則是整體建設放慢，帶動資本支出下降。Tyler表示，不會放棄科技股交易，仍看好戰術性反彈，但市場可能更加挑剔科技與AI領域的贏家及輸家。

news.Title: Should You Buy Anthropic's IPO on Day 1?
news.Content:
Anthropic's upcoming initial public offering (IPO) is sure to pique investor interest over the next few weeks. While management has not yet made public the exact date it has in mind, most expect the stock's debut to occur before Thanksgiving. So, investors need to start thinking about whether they want to buy the stock on Day 1, or if they'd be better off to stay patient.

I think there's a clear answer, and it's best to look at a prior IPO to see why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Day 1 hype can be powerful

When a company goes public, its management team sets an initial price for the stock, based on a specific target value for the whole company. However, that's the price that institutions and high-net-worth investors are able to get by buying at the start. For the rest of us, that share price is rarely available on the first day because usually, none of those early buyers are willing to sell at that price. Instead, the stock usually rises a fair bit until a market on both sides can be found, which results in a Day 1 pop. There are normally a few days of strong buying. Then short-term traders look to take their gains, start selling, and the price tumbles.

This pattern has been seen time and time again , most recently with the Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) IPO.

SPCX data by YCharts.

SpaceX went public at $135 per share, and its first trading price of its opening day was $150. It got up to an intraday high of just over $225 in the days that followed, then began an extended tumble that took it to a low of around $108. Then, a well-received earnings report caused the stock to rally. But even now, it's trading in the area of $140 -- below the first price at which the average retail investor could have picked up shares.

I could see this same pattern occurring with Anthropic. There is going to be a lot of hype around the stock. This is likely warranted, as it's the first of two major AI labs that will likely go public in the near future ( the other being OpenAI ). It's also growing its top line at an incredible pace.

During the first six months of 2026, Anthropic's revenue rose to $16.3 billion, up from $1.2 billion during the first six months of 2025. That's an astounding 1,305% growth rate. Most investors never see a figure like that, let alone from a company the size of Anthropic.

Story Continues

At the same time, Anthropic's losses are just as impressive. During the first six months of 2026, it lost $80.7 billion. That's about 5 times as much as it generated in revenue.

That's a huge imbalance, and it's blatantly obvious why Anthropic needs to go public: It needs greater access to outside funding through the public equity market. This could be a polarizing stock, and there are a lot of questions about Anthropic that need to be answered. As a result, I think investors would be better off investing in other AI stocks (such as Anthropic's computing unit suppliers).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again

In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. If you'd invested $5,000 then, you'd be sitting on $2,686,757 today.*

Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It's a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast.

Continue »

news.Title: Super Micro's AI Boom Just Got Much Bigger
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Super Micro Computer ( NASDAQ:SMCI ) jumped after delivering a massive fiscal first-quarter revenue beat and issuing guidance well above Wall Street expectations, giving investors fresh evidence that demand for AI servers remains extremely strong.

The company reported $19.9 billion in revenue , up 298% from a year earlier and far above the roughly $16.26 billion analysts expected. Adjusted earnings reached $1.81 per share , compared with consensus around $1.23.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with SMCI.

Is SMCI fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The outlook was arguably even more important.

Super Micro expects current-quarter revenue of $19.5 billion to $21.5 billion , comfortably ahead of the $17.51 billion consensus estimate. Adjusted EPS is projected at $1.66 to $1.90 , versus Wall Street's roughly $1.14 forecast.

For the full fiscal year, management now expects revenue of $72 billion to $82 billion , putting the midpoint at $77 billion versus consensus around $70.27 billion.

That strength reflects continued demand for the company's Nvidia-powered AI infrastructure as cloud providers and technology companies race to add data-center capacity. Reuters reported that shares climbed more than 9% in extended trading after the results.

One of the more encouraging developments was profitability.

Gross margin improved to 12.8% from 9.5% a year earlier , also beating expectations around 11%. That matters because rapid AI-server growth has historically come with concerns about expensive components, aggressive pricing and relatively thin margins.

Still, margins remain the key issue.

Even with the improvement, Super Micro's profitability is much lower than that of chip suppliers such as Nvidia, meaning the company needs enormous sales volumes and disciplined execution to translate its AI demand into equally impressive earnings growth.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest takeaway is that AI infrastructure demand is clearly not the problem for Super Micro .

Revenue nearly quadrupled, guidance crushed expectations, and management sees another enormous year ahead.

The question is how much of that growth reaches the bottom line.

A 12.8% gross margin is a major improvement, but it still leaves Super Micro exposed to component costs, pricing pressure and customer concentration as it scales.

For investors, the key things to watch are gross margins, Nvidia system availability, backlog conversion, cash flow and whether fiscal 2027 revenue ultimately lands toward the top of the $72 billion to $82 billion range .

Super Micro just proved it can generate extraordinary growth.

Now investors need to see whether it can generate equally strong economics.

news.Title: Cathie Wood Picks a Side Between Palantir and Google
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Cathie Wood made a notable shift inside ARK Invest's AI portfolio Tuesday, buying roughly $11.2 million of Palantir ( NASDAQ:PLTR ) while selling about $3.5 million of Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ) .

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with PLTR.

Is PLTR fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

ARK purchased 63,638 Palantir shares on Nov. 3 after the stock slipped 1.65% despite reporting another strong quarter. At the same time, the firm sold 12,530 Alphabet shares , taking some money off the table after Google's parent had fallen nearly 14% since its earnings release.

The contrast is interesting because both companies are delivering strong AI growth, but investors are questioning very different things.

Palantir reported 96% year-over-year revenue growth , with Q3 sales reaching $2.31 billion versus the $2.17 billion analysts expected. Adjusted EPS of $0.44 also beat the $0.40 consensus. U.S. commercial revenue surged 148% to $984 million , overtaking domestic government revenue for the first time.

Still, investors remain uneasy about valuation and future contract growth. Total contract value increased only 6%, while U.S. commercial contract value grew 11%, raising questions over whether Palantir can maintain its current pace.

Alphabet's problem is different.

Its Q3 revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion , while Google Cloud more than doubled to $30.71 billion . But advertising revenue missed expectations, and the company's enormous AI infrastructure buildout pushed quarterly free cash flow to negative $9.1 billion . Alphabet expects 2026 capex of $195 billion to $205 billion , with spending set to rise again in 2027.

Interestingly, Wall Street is currently more bullish on Alphabet. TipRanks shows an average Alphabet price target implying roughly 43% upside , versus about 30% for Palantir.

Investor takeaway

I think the important point is that Wood is not simply choosing AI over something else.

She is rotating within AI .

Palantir offers explosive software growth and much lower capital intensity, but at a very demanding valuation. Alphabet trades at a more conventional multiple, but investors are increasingly questioning how much cash its AI infrastructure will consume before the returns become obvious.

That makes the trade revealing.

ARK appears more willing to add to Palantir's valuation risk than Alphabet's capex risk right now.

For investors, the key things to watch are Palantir's contract growth and valuation, Alphabet's free cash flow and capex, and whether ARK continues building PLTR while trimming GOOGL .

Story Continues

Wood's latest trades suggest she still wants AI exposure.

She just prefers a different part of the stack.

news.Content:

news.Title: California's billionaire tax on track for defeat as the state continues to count votes
news.Content: California's proposed billionaire tax appeared headed for defeat on Wednesday in one of the final verdicts from voters in an election week that saw a wave of anti-billionaire sentiment elsewhere. The latest results on Wednesday afternoon showed California's Proposition 40 down by over 11 percentage points, with 60% of votes counted but the race not yet formally called. The referendum would amend California's constitution and impose a one-time 5% tax on California residents and trusts with assets over $1 billion on Jan. 1, 2026. The revenue would primarily go toward healthcare, as well as food assistance and education. Some assets, such as real property and certain retirement accounts and pensions, were excluded. The measure was estimated to impact about 200 billionaires in the state. It faced fierce opposition from many in Big Tech and lost steam with voters as Election Day neared. Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) co-founder Sergey Brin was one of the measure's most vocal opponents. He contributed a reported $102 million to a political committee to fight the measure. Other billionaires made detailed plans in case it passed. Meta ( META ) CEO Mark Zuckerberg told his board, according to a New York Times report, that they needed to take steps to shield him from the tax or he would publicly list his home in Palo Alto for sale. The measure was also opposed by some Democrats, who argued it wouldn't work. Outgoing California Gov. Gavin Newsom emerged as an opponent, arguing that billionaires would both dodge the tax and leave the state. He cited a report from the California Legislative Analyst's Office that estimated the measure might temporarily boost state revenues but could be an overall drag on regular income taxes and "would reduce state revenues by less than $1 billion per year." Across the country, voters in red and blue states delivered verdicts on wealth inequality and the influence of the ultrarich. In Texas, where Elon Musk spent more than $200 million to keep the state's Senate seat in Republican hands, voters flipped the seat for Democrats and made clear their unease over AI data centers . Tuesday's results also saw a series of wins by candidates who represent the Democratic Socialists of America , many of whom ran on explicitly anti-billionaire platforms. At least seven DSA members will take seats in Congress next year, as well as the mayors' offices of Los Angeles and Washington, D.C. California voters were also weighing competing measures: Proposition 41 and Proposition 42 , which were introduced by opponents of Proposition 40 to prevent the wealth tax from taking effect. Story Continues Proposition 42 would prohibit taxes on personal savings, assets, and retirement holdings. It was on track to pass based on the latest results. The wealth tax had support from progressives like Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Rep. Ro Khanna of California, who called the measure "the most important ballot initiative in America." Khanna on Tuesday night acknowledged the measure's fading prospects, saying in a press conference , "I'm proud of our efforts wherever we end up [and] I am going to be right there, first in line supporting this in the next election cycle if it doesn't pass this one." On Wednesday, Khanna wrote an op-ed for MS Now calling for a new federal tax on billionaires. Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance. news.Title: AMD Stock: Buy, Hold or Sell After 97% AI Data Center Growth?
news.Content:
Strong third-quarter performance and a robust fourth-quarter outlook underscore Advanced Micro Devices, Inc .'s AMD growing presence in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence (AI) market. While rising demand for AMD's advanced data center solutions supports growth, weakness in the gaming segment and valuation concerns remain major apprehensions for investors. Against this backdrop, is AMD stock a buy, hold, or sell now? Let's take a closer look –

AMD's AI Boom Drives Record Growth and Strong Q4 Outlook

AMD is rapidly expanding its business, with third-quarter revenues of $13.38 billion, up 45% year over year and 16% sequentially, according to the company's Nov. 3 press release. The most striking part is the company's Data Center segment, where revenues jumped 97% year over year to a record $8.5 billion, making it the company's primary growth engine. This strong growth was driven by robust demand for AMD's Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs, and integrated rack-scale AI systems.

Alongside NVIDIA Corporation NVDA, AMD has now strengthened its position as an alternative supplier of AI infrastructure. Additionally, the company's profitability is growing faster than revenues, indicating positive operating leverage. Its operating income soared 123%, highlighting improving operational efficiency, while non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 increased 74% year over year. Higher earnings growth could provide meaningful support to AMD's long-term price appreciation.

AMD's fourth-quarter guidance is also strong. The company expects revenues of $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, in the fourth quarter, up 66% year over year and a sequential rise of approximately 27%. This indicates that management is confident that demand for AMD's AI and Data Center products will remain strong.

AMD Stock After Earnings: Buy, Hold or Sell Now?

Strong third-quarter results indicate that AMD is significantly benefiting from the AI infrastructure boom. Its accelerating Data Center business and improving profitability highlight its growing competitiveness in AI infrastructure. Furthermore, management expects revenue growth in the fourth quarter. All these should encourage stakeholders to stay invested.

However, new investors should exercise caution before investing in AMD stock. This is because its strong earnings growth in the third quarter was partially impacted by the weakness in the gaming business. Moreover, the non-GAAP gross margin for the fourth quarter is projected to be approximately 55%, which is slightly less than the reported 56% in the third quarter, signaling potential profitability headwinds.

Story Continues

Finally, AMD's elevated valuation remains another major concern, leaving the stock highly sensitive to negative sentiment and potential steep declines during a broader market correction. AMD seems significantly overvalued compared to its peers. It has a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 64.09 compared to the Computer - Integrated Systems industry's 13.99.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AMD currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Greg Abel Just Plowed Another $27 Million Into One of Berkshire Hathaway's Top 20 Holdings That's Up 62% This Year and Has a 3.3% Dividend Yield
news.Content:
Recent filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission show that Berkshire Hathaway purchased an additional $27 million in one of its top 20 holdings, SiriusXM (NASDAQ:SIRI).

The purchases were made between Oct. 30 and Nov. 3 for an average price of roughly $29 per share.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The satellite radio company Sirius now accounts for 1.1% of Berkshire's massive, roughly $368 billion equity portfolio, and Berkshire controls over 37% of Sirius's outstanding shares.

Berkshire has owned a significant stake in Sirius for quite a while, but when Liberty Media split off Sirius XM and two of its tracking stocks in 2024, Berkshire went in again, purchasing another $1.2 billion of Sirius stock in early 2024.

While the stock has struggled significantly in recent years, it has found its footing this year and is now up nearly 62%.

Greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images.

The turnaround plan is starting to work

Sirius is the only company in the U.S. that has obtained satellite radio broadcast licenses from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC), and therefore the only commercial satellite radio operator in the U.S.

This is the kind of thing that former Berkshire CEO Warren Buffett and his team would love, because these licenses effectively make Sirius a legal monopoly . However, the FCC granted Sirius these licenses because it believed they wouldn't prohibit competition.

Sirius has struggled as companies like Spotify have grabbed significant attention from listeners, leading to very little subscriber growth in recent years and, at times, attrition, making investors very bearish on the stock.

In 2024, the company launched a major turnaround strategy focused on a new pricing structure, a new in-car tech platform, new ad-supported offerings, and a foray into podcasting, along with expanded social media and video efforts around those brands.

Sirius went on to acquire exclusive distribution and advertising rights to major podcast brands for high prices. The company in 2024 also laid out longer-term goals, including growing total subscribers by 25% to roughly 50 million, and growing free cash flow by 50% to $1.8 billion.

The company has made progress as well, implementing structural cost reductions and guiding for a decrease in annual satellite capital expenditures between this year and through 2028. There have also been improvements in subscriber growth over the past year.

Story Continues

On Sirius' most recent earnings call, management once again raised its full-year guidance by $25 million each for revenue, EBITDA, and free cash flow. Free cash flow is expected to come in at $1.4 billion this year, with management guiding for roughly $1.5 billion in 2027.

"Subscriber trends remain stable, engagement is growing, and our advertising reach and inventory are expanding while disciplined execution continues to drive stronger profitability and cash flow," Sirius' CEO Jennifer Witz said on the company's third-quarter earnings call.

Reasonable valuation and healthy dividend

This recent buy by Berkshire confirms that CEO Greg Abel and the rest of Berkshire's investing team are encouraged by Sirius' progress.

Investors should also be encouraged by Sirius' results this year, although it would be great to get more confirmation that the company can continue to grow its subscriber base.

Even after the big run, Sirius stock trades at roughly 11 times forward earnings, which is not unreasonable. Furthermore, the company has a trailing dividend yield of 3.25%, which is very well covered with a trailing free cash flow yield of 13.66%.

news.Title: Was Elon Musk the Midterms’ Biggest Loser? What It Means for Tesla and SpaceX Investors
news.Content:
Republicans across the country woke up licking their wounds after the worst midterms drubbing in 50 years, but few politicos were bigger losers than Elon Musk.

The CEO of Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) has gone all-in with the Republican Party since COVID and spent nearly $500 million on midterm races nationally and around $200 million in Texas.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

That spending delivered zero in return as voters in Texas, Musk's adopted home state and the headquarters of both SpaceX and Tesla, voted for a slate of Democratic candidates, pushing back against data center land grabs and billionaire interests.

While stocks soared on Wednesday with the Nasdaq Composite up 2% after investors had time to digest the results overnight, Musk's two trillion-dollar companies were well into the red. SpaceX was down 3.4% as of 1:11 p.m. after falling as much as 7% in pre-market trading, while Tesla was off 2.3% at the same time.

Election consequences are not easy to predict, but it's more than just Musk putting his thumb on the scale that has his stocks on the losing end.

Image source: The White House.

The data center debate takes center stage

Texas has more data centers than any other state except Virginia, and one of the biggest takeaways from Democrats winning every statewide race in Texas is that voters want more say on data centers.

Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa made the data center boom a key part of her campaign, and they are likely to face significantly more oversight, at least in Texas. Among her proposals for data centers in the state are that they not be subsidized, not jeopardize community water supply, and ensure that they don't raise electricity and water prices on surrounding communities. Hinojosa also campaigned on a temporary moratorium on data centers to protect the power grid and local water supplies.

Those measures aren't draconian by any means, and it's unclear where any restrictions on data centers in Texas will ultimately land.

Musk's companies are heavily dependent on data centers on Texas, and SpaceX recently began its Terafab mega-project in Grimes County, Texas, which could cost as much as $119 billion. SpaceX's plans to add 10GW of AI compute by the end of next year, which already required a gargantuan build-out, now seem less likely to be achieved.

Story Continues

Additionally, the election result could disrupt the desired combination of SpaceX and Tesla, though Democrats won't have direct control over antitrust regulations.

Musk's unique position

Musk and his companies have become a flashpoint on a number of issues, both in politics and beyond, but SpaceX and Tesla are both valued in the trillions of dollars largely because of Musk's own forecasts around AI, in areas like robotaxis and Optimus for Tesla and in data centers and infrastructure for SpaceX.

Investors have put a ton of faith in his ability to achieve those aims, and that looks more difficult for him after the election results, as his companies are likely to face increased oversight now that he's out of favor with the party on the rise in both his home state and nationally.

It's difficult to extrapolate the consequences of the election for Musk and his companies, and investors often overreact to election results. However, there's a good reason why Tesla and SpaceX are down today, while the rest of the market is up.

news.Title: 台股連日重挫！該停損還是加碼？專家曝小資族「必做5件事」
news.Content:
台股連日重挫，11月4日再跌358.63點，收在42,948.91點，失守43,000點大關，連帶讓不少ETF投資人帳面虧損擴大。尤其元大台灣50（0050）等市值型ETF也受到市場修正衝擊，讓小資族開始猶豫究竟該停損還是逢低加碼。對此， 理財專家「小資理財教主」Dr.Selena（楊倩琳博士） 分享股市大跌時應掌握的5件事，提醒投資人先檢查基本面、保留現金，也別因為市場震盪就打亂原本的投資紀律。

【台股跌跌不休！ETF也重挫 小資族陷兩難】

Dr.Selena在臉書發文指出，台股這波跌勢又急又猛，11月3日加權指數重挫1,612.60點，跌幅3.59%，收在43,307.54點，創下史上第7大收盤跌點。若回顧近期4個交易日，10月29日下跌667點、10月30日下跌1,156點、11月2日下跌291點，11月3日再跌1,612點，累計跌幅約7.93%。

11月4日台股再度開高走低，盤中一度下探41,855.82點，終場收42,948.91點，下跌358.63點。短時間內指數大幅修正，也讓不少投資人擔心手中ETF是否該停損，還是趁低點加碼。

Dr.Selena認為，投資成果不只取決於股市上漲時賺多少，更重要的是市場下跌時如何應對。面對劇烈震盪，小資族可以先做好以下5件事。

【第1招：別恐慌殺低！先確認企業基本面】

Dr.Selena提醒，股價下跌不代表企業基本面一定變差，投資人應先分辨這次修正是市場情緒造成，還是企業營運、獲利真的出現問題。

以元大台灣50（0050）等市值型ETF為例，若原本看好的投資邏輯沒有改變，不必只因短期下跌就急著賣出，但仍要定期檢視成分股與投資組合，確認持有理由是否依然成立。

【第2招：準備兩筆資金！下跌5％、10％分批布局】

Dr.Selena一直強調，投資最好準備兩筆錢，一筆是「固定投資資金」，用來持續定期定額；另一筆則是「機會投資資金」，等待市場回檔時分批布局。

她建議，可以依照個人風險承受能力，設定指數或標的下跌5%、10%、15%、20%時分批加碼，不必急著猜最低點，更不要一次把所有資金投入，避免市場繼續修正時失去調整空間。

【第3招：定期定額別輕易停！下跌時能累積更多單位】

不少投資人股市上漲時願意持續投入，一遇到大跌卻開始害怕，甚至暫停扣款。Dr.Selena指出，定期定額的優勢之一，就是在價格下跌時，相同金額可以買進更多單位數。

不過，是否繼續扣款仍須回到投資標的本身。如果企業或ETF追蹤的市場基本面沒有明顯惡化，且投入資金短期內沒有使用需求，就可以依照原本計畫持續投資。

news.Title: AI股選後能翻身？小摩看科技股反彈 加碼先看四大訊號
news.Content:
美國期中選舉結果出爐後，美股周三(4日)扭轉稍早跌勢走高。摩根大通(JPM-US)交易部門認為，近期遭到拋售的科技股有望迎來短線反彈，市場漲勢也可能從少數大型權值股，擴散至更多產業。不過，團隊尚未全面看多AI交易，配置上仍較偏重景氣循環股。

由Andrew Tyler領軍的美國市場情報團隊在周三報告中表示：「我們不會放棄科技股交易，並會布局戰術性反彈。」團隊建議採取槓鈴式策略，同時配置科技股與景氣循環股，但給予後者較高權重。

科技股有望反彈 AI加碼仍待四大訊號

民主黨取得國會控制權後，投資人持續評估科技業面臨的政策變化，尤其是AI基礎建設支出前景。德州州長當選人Gina Hinojosa主張，在建立更多規範前立即暫停新資料中心建設，一度引發隔夜賣壓。不過，以科技股為主的那斯達克100指數周三轉而上漲1.8%。

摩根大通交易部門認為，市場對德州政策可能轉向的疑慮或許過大，因為資料中心仍可選擇在其他州興建，新規也不代表所有建設都將完全停擺。

儘管看好短線反彈，團隊並未對AI交易全面亮綠燈。投資人在重新增加曝險前，仍希望看到幾項訊號，包括市場持倉充分出清、大型雲端業者確認資本支出計畫、半導體與記憶體企業交出正面財報，以及資本市場活動改善。

這也意味著，科技股回升不等於AI相關企業將全面受惠。隨著市場更加重視投資回報與資金來源，投資人將更仔細區分AI產業的贏家與輸家。

巴克萊同日上午也提醒，選舉結果本身不足以替美股掃除年底上漲的障礙，顯示華爾街對選後行情能否持續仍有不同看法。

科技業之外，摩根大通交易部門也關注，民主黨是否會推動結束與伊朗的衝突。團隊指出，新一屆國會明年1月就任後，議員可能採取撤回資金支持或要求撤軍等措施，針對未獲國會授權、持續逾90天的軍事衝突施壓。該行認為，市場似乎正逐漸反映達成協議的可能性。

選後漲勢可望擴散 偏好消費與金融股

歷史表現則為團隊的樂觀看法提供另一項依據。報告引述摩根大通Craig Cohen的統計指出，自1950年以來，每次期中選舉隔年，標普500指數均上漲，平均漲幅約15%。

若觀察選舉後不同期間，標普500過去在三個月內平均上漲5.4%，六個月內上漲11.4%，九個月內上漲12.5%。這些歷史數據為選後行情提供參考，但並非未來報酬的保證。

整體而言，團隊預期漲勢將擴及更多產業，但能源股的上漲空間相對有限，科技股下跌空間則可能縮小。在景氣循環類股中，團隊偏好消費與金融股，尤其是在殖利率曲線持續變陡的情境下。

news.Title: Got $5,000? Buy These 2 Growth Stocks Powering the AI Memory Boom (Hint: Micron Isn't One of Them)
news.Content:
The memory chip boom has been helping lift the whole market over the past two years, as memory stocks have enjoyed massive gains.

Demand from data center operators for memory chips and storage devices has far outpaced supply. This is due to the pace at which hyperscalers and others are building new data centers and the infrastructure to power AI computing. AI workloads require processors to handle massive volumes of data quickly, so those servers need more memory to store and rapidly retrieve all that data.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The result has been a supercycle for memory makers. Though they are all building new production lines to increase supply (and their sales volumes), so far, supply has not caught up with demand. As such, the memory-chip and storage device makers enjoy incredible pricing power, and they've been taking full advantage.

This supercycle has been going on for about two years now, and some believe it could last another two years, or more. Eventually, the supply will catch up with demand as these companies churn out more chips and the infrastructure boom flattens. At some point, supply will once again exceed demand significantly, and prices will start to sink again. But most experts believe the shortage will last through 2028, potentially into 2029, and perhaps beyond.

One of the biggest names in the memory space is Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU), but there are two other great AI memory chip stocks powering the AI memory boom that deserve your attention.

1. SK Hynix

Just three companies dominate the globe in the design and manufacture of high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips for data centers and high-performance computing: Micron, SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY), and Samsung .

SK Hynix and Samsung are based in South Korea, but the former cross-listed on the Nasdaq on July 10, so U.S. investors can now easily buy its shares.

SK Hynix is actually the dominant player in the HBM chip market, with a 50% global market share by revenue. Last week, it released its third-quarter results, and the numbers showed that the supercycle is not slowing down.

It generated record revenue of 104.6 trillion South Korean won, which translates to roughly $78 billion. That was up 32% from Q2 and 348% year over year. Its operating profit was 83.3 trillion won, or $62.5 billion. That was up 38% from Q2 and 638% year over year. Its operating margin rose to 80% from 76% the previous quarter and from 47% in the prior-year period.

Story Continues

Further, management said it expects demand to outpace supply through 2030, meaning this supercycle could last another four years, at least. It is in the process of ramping up capacity to meet that demand. It also has signed 14 long-term agreements (so far) with major customers that, at present, account for 50% of total production capacity for 2027 and 2028.

The U.S. stock price is down about 9% since July, a decline that coincided with broader negative sentiment toward tech stocks due to their high valuations and massive AI capital expenditures. But that just creates an incredible opportunity for investors. SK Hynix stock is trading at 9 times earnings and 3 times forward earnings, and it has a price/earnings-to-growth (PEG) ratio of just 0.1, which indicates it's a long-term value.

2. Sandisk

Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) may be the stock that has benefited the most from this memory and storage supercycle. Since it was spun off from Western Digital (NASDAQ: WDC) in February 2025, Sandisk stock has returned a staggering 3,000% or roughly 641% on an average annualized basis. It has returned 372% year to date and is trading at $1,122 per share.

Sandisk sits on the longer-term storage side of the equation, as its solid-state and NAND flash drives store data for AI data centers and AI computing. Those storage products are experiencing the same supply-and-demand imbalance as memory chips.

Sandisk released its fiscal 2027 Q1 earnings last week. For the period, which ended Oct. 2, revenue rose 23% sequentially and 378% year over year to $11 billion, while earnings soared 20% from fiscal 2026 Q4 to $52.60 per share.

Sandisk anticipates a 40% increase in bit demand in calendar 2027. Also, through its new business model framework, it has inked numerous long-term sales agreements with hyperscalers out to 2030 with commitments for 50% of its bits for fiscal 2027 and two-thirds for fiscal 2028.

In addition, it announced that on Nov. 19, it will conduct an 8-for-1 stock split to make its shares more accessible to investors. That would bring the share price down to around $140 per share.

Finally, Sandisk stock, like SK Hynix, is cheap, trading at just 9 times trailing earnings and 5 times forward earnings.

A $5,000 investment in these two AI memory and storage juggernauts would not be a bad play based on their earnings power, low valuations, and the data center industry's insatiable demand for their technologies.

news.Title: AI Regulation Was on the Ballot In These States. Here Are The Elon Musk Stocks That Could Be Impacted.
news.Content:
The Democrats rolled to sweeping victories in the midterm elections on Nov. 3, reclaiming control of both the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate.

While not all results are final, the Democrats appear to control 258 seats in the House, with the Republicans controlling 177. Meanwhile, the Dems now appear to have 54 Senate seats, compared to the Republicans' 44, with two races still undecided.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The results show a clear repudiation of President Donald Trump and the Republicans' agenda over the past two years. While the Iran war, high oil prices, and overall affordability were likely at the top of voters' agenda, make no mistake: artificial intelligence was also on the ballot in many different elections.

Here are the Elon Musk stocks that could be impacted.

Image source: The White House.

Data centers and AI safety laws

Many stakeholders have been concerned about the threats posed by AI, including how many jobs it will replace, data and security breaches, and its impact on humanity as a whole.

Musk runs both Space Exploration Technologies Corp (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Tesla , two companies deeply involved with AI.

AI became an issue in many key Congressional races and state elections in Texas, Pennsylvania, Georgia, Ohio, and Virginia, among others. Some candidates focused more on the impact of data centers, while others promised stricter AI regulation.

Generally speaking, Democratic candidates leaned toward caution and favored regulation or stricter requirements for data centers. Some candidates sought to outright ban data centers for at least a period.

SpaceX has data centers in Tennessee and Mississippi, but other states of interest for both SpaceX and Tesla include Texas and Georgia, among others.

Musk was a heavy spender in the midterm election cycle, allocating at least $474 million. Nowhere did Musk spend more than in Texas, a historically Red state the Democrats just swept.

James Talarico became the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate seat in Texas since 1988, while Gina Hinojosa became the first Democratic governor of Texas since 1995.

Musk and his super PAC reportedly spent $224 million on the Texas races. Hinojosa defeated the incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott, who Musk reportedly had close ties to. In fact, Tesla's policy chief used to be Abbott's deputy director for legislative affairs.

Story Continues

Tesla is currently expanding its Cortex AI training supercluster in Austin, Texas, while SpaceX has reportedly been looking to build another data center campus in Texas with an additional 1 gigawatt (GW) of compute capacity.

SpaceX and Tesla will face higher barriers on data centers

Heading into midterms, there was already a lot of scrutiny of AI, particularly regarding data centers, which can raise electricity costs and consume critical resources.

Many citizens, worried about losing their jobs, are also not particularly inclined to endorse AI right now, while Democrats seemingly have little to gain by cozying up to Musk, given the party's current direction.

As of 10:45 a.m. ET, the major market indexes were soaring higher, yet SpaceX and Tesla traded roughly 3% and 2.2% lower, respectively.

Hinojosa's win is a clear blow to Musk and both of his companies. Not only did Musk have much closer ties to Abbott, but Hinojosa has talked about imposing measures, such as an immediate moratorium on data center development.

On SpaceX's recent earnings call, Musk told analysts that the company expects to build and bring online at least an additional 10 GW of AI compute capacity in 2027 via data centers. That task likely just got a lot harder.

news.Title: Why Lockheed Martin Stock Dropped Today
news.Content:
The Midterm Elections 2026 are over, and the Democrats won in a landslide. So what does this mean for Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT) stock? Apparently, nothing good.

Shares of the major military contractor fell 5% through 10:35 a.m. ET Wednesday morning on no bad Lockheed Martin-specific news at all. No analysts have downgraded the stock (yet). No one's cut any price targets (also yet). But the stock's still down.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

In fact, one analyst defied sentiment and upgraded Lockheed stock today!

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Bad news for defense budgets

President Donald Trump had pushed a $1.5 trillion fiscal year 2027 defense budget in the months leading up to November's election. It's unlikely, however, that a Democratic Congress will approve anything like that.

At last report, the U.S. Senate is looking to number 54 Democrat votes to just 44 Republicans, with the House of Representatives tilting blue 228-139 (with 68 seats not yet confirmed). And even before the results are all in, Politico reports the Pentagon plans to reduce its spending request from $1.5 trillion to $1.1 trillion.

What's next for Lockheed Martin stock

Despite all this, Guggenheim analyst Michael Ciarmoli chose today to initiate coverage of Lockheed Martin stock with a buy rating and a $735 price target, as StreetInsider.com reports. Why?

Priced north of 22 times earnings and with an historically pricey 1.9x price-to-sales ratio, Lockheed doesn't look like a particularly cheap stock, especially if it can no longer count on a massive increase in defense spending to help it. Lockheed's free cash flow, however, looks very healthy at $8.4 billion; for every $1 in "earnings" Lockheed reports, it actually generates $1.29 in real cash profit.

Valued at 17.6x FCF and pegged for nearly 18% annual earnings growth on Wall Street, Lockheed stock still looks like a buy to me.

news.Title: Apple's AI problem could reach your next iPhone
news.Content: The artificial intelligence boom may be about to reach a place most consumers were not expecting: the price of their next phone or laptop. Apple (AAPL) is warning that the cost of memory chips is rising sharply as AI data centers compete for increasingly valuable semiconductor capacity. These processors are crucial parts of MacBooks, iPhones, and other consumer gadgets. This is an issue for both regular consumers and investors. Apple is able to endure reduced profit margins and absorb a portion of those increased expenses. Ultimately, however, it will ask consumers to cover more of them. While it has not implemented a significant wave of price hikes, Apple has increased the prices of several items this year. According to Reuters , these increases have helped offset rising component costs. It seems that Nvidia chips and trillion-dollar data centers are no longer the main factors in the fight for AI infrastructure. Eventually, it may alter the prices that customers pay at the Apple Store. Apple says memory costs are climbing fast Apple's most recent financial results demonstrated how rapidly the economy is evolving. With iPhone sales breaking a September-quarter record, the business posted fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% from the same period last year. The gross margin was 47.9%. Apple now anticipates that during the Christmas quarter, that percentage will drop to between 45% and 46%. One of the main causes is rising memory chip prices. According to Reuters , as the business worked to acquire components, Apple's obligations for manufacturing and supplier purchases rose by $33 billion to $89.7 billion. Ternus said that while Apple had secured supply, he anticipated memory costs rising into the next year. This is important because DRAM is needed to operate programs on modern computers and smartphones, whereas NAND memory is needed to store data, images, and apps. As businesses compete to increase computational power, AI data centers are using massive amounts of sophisticated memory. The pressure has become strong enough to reach companies such as Apple that are not spending anywhere near as aggressively on data centers as some of their Big Tech rivals. The AI boom could eventually reach Apple shoppers The memory pressure is particularly intriguing because of Apple's customer exposure. The iPhone 18 Pro already starts at $1,199 in the U.S., and the newly announced 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip starts at $1,999. Neither pricing indicates that Apple will raise prices due to memory inflation. However, they demonstrate the significance of even very small price rises. Story Continues For a $1,199 phone, a 5% increase would cost about $60. On a $1,999 MacBook Pro, the same increase would cost approximately $100. More Apple: Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge Apple secret new device is a challenge to Amazon Bank of America warns Apple investors because of Meta's Muse Apple may try to avoid passing the full price increase to customers by redesigning parts, negotiating with suppliers, cutting other costs, and accepting smaller margins. Additionally, because of its size, it has buying power that smaller tech companies would not have. However, the cost is already apparent to investors. Apple shares fell after the company forecast weaker holiday-quarter margins, with Reuters reporting that higher memory costs threatened to erase more than $170 billion in market value at one point. Apple investors now have a new AI number to watch The irony is that Apple has remained relatively insulated from one of Wall Street's biggest AI concerns. Data centers have been receiving massive investments from Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta. Apple spent about $9 billion on capital expenditures over the past year while generating roughly $145 billion in operating cash flow. However, the same boom is still impacting the company. AI businesses need not directly compete with Apple to impact its bottom line. They simply need to fight for the same chips, production capacity, and supply chain. Because of this, gross margin is becoming a more significant indicator of the indirect cost of AI for Apple stockholders. For customers, the number to watch is simpler: device prices. Apple may be able to withstand much of the pressure if memory costs stabilize, but it will ultimately have to decide between preserving profits and shielding customers from rising costs. Apple's most recent warning is unique because of this. Even if an iPhone customer never uses ChatGPT, owns Nvidia stock, or cares how many AI data centers Silicon Valley builds, the AI boom could still end up on their receipt. AppLovin近來更清楚地把成長主軸鎖定在AI驅動的廣告平台，而非自有遊戲內容。資料顯示，公司已出售自有手遊業務，現階段核心產品是廣告推薦引擎AXON與廣告平台，並把服務從手機遊戲開發者延伸到電商品牌。這項轉變的關鍵，在於AppLovin正把營運模式集中到演算法驅動的投放與變現，而不是承擔內容開發的不確定性。主題資料也指出，AXON持續處理跨遊戲廣告競價與投放決策，廣告主只需提供App、關鍵事件與投放目標，模型即自動決定受眾。同期調整後EBITDA利潤率已升至84%，高於2023年第三季的70%，反映平台化後的獲利能力仍在擴大。

First Solar（FSLR.US）： 成交價203.79美元，上漲9.62%，開盤205.76美元，盤中高點214.87美元，盤中低點201.62美元，均價208.4美元，成交量60.52萬股。

First Solar近14日沒有可直接對應的公司新公告，現有資料也未揭露新的產能計畫、客戶合約、財報更新或財測修正，因此暫時看不到足以重新界定公司營運方向的新增事件。現階段與First Solar較接近的外部訊號，反而是太陽能產業仍受高借貸成本與政策不確定性干擾，顯示專案融資環境仍是影響整體族群的重要變數。不過，這類內容較偏產業背景，並非First Solar本身已經公布的經營變化。就本次資料而言，更保守的判讀仍是公司近期缺乏明確公司特定催化，後續需等待管理層對出貨、模組需求或全年展望的更新。

Uber（UBER.US）： 成交價72.43美元，上漲8.75%，開盤68.28美元，盤中高點72.47美元，盤中低點67.36美元，均價70.11美元，成交量331.25萬股。

Uber近14日沒有符合條件的公司新聞，現有輸入內容也未顯示新的監管進展、重大合作、平台功能更新或財測調整，因此目前缺乏足以解釋營運方向變化的公司專屬事件。對Uber而言，真正會改變市場判讀的通常是叫車與外送成長節奏、抽成率與補貼策略，或自駕、廣告與會員業務的新增進展，但這次資料並未提供相關更新。換言之，現階段較難把近期走勢直接連結到已揭露的基本面轉折，後續仍需等待財報或管理層對需求與獲利結構提出更明確的新資訊。

3M（MMM.US）： 成交價191.57美元，上漲8.2%，開盤192.7美元，盤中高點194.14美元，盤中低點187.75美元，均價192.33美元，成交量95.63萬股。

3M近期沒有可驗證的公司特定更新，現有資料多為公司簡介與業務範圍描述，未顯示新產品進展、重大訴訟處理、資產交易，或管理層對營運展望的新增說法。以目前可用資訊判斷，尚無單一事件足以重新定義3M的近期營運方向。對這家公司來說，真正重要的變化通常來自工業需求、電子與資料中心材料、以及事業組合調整，但本次資料沒有提供新的證據。因此較合理的寫法，是把目前狀態視為缺乏新增催化，而非基本面已出現明確轉折，後續仍需等待更直接的公司公告或季度更新。

Moderna（MRNA.US）： 成交價247美元，上漲8.12%，開盤235.13美元，盤中高點253.64美元，盤中低點230.26美元，均價246.12美元，成交量69.8萬股。

Moderna已把mRNA平台從單一疫情產品推向腫瘤與季節性疫苗多產品線，最關鍵進展是與Merck合作的個人化mRNA癌症療法intismeran autogene，在高風險黑色素瘤第三期試驗中，讓復發或死亡風險較單用Keytruda降低42%。試驗納入1137名已完全切除腫瘤的患者，兩年無復發率為82.2%，高於對照組的70.0%，且未見新的安全訊號。另一項已落地的商業化進展，是mRNA流感疫苗mFlusiva已於8月5日獲FDA核准，其中50至64歲族群為完整核准，65歲以上則為加速核准並需補做確認性試驗。這代表Moderna正把平台能力轉成可上市的癌症與疫苗產品，而不再只依賴新冠相關收入。

Carvana（CVNA.US）： 成交價76.71美元，上漲7.62%，開盤73.24美元，盤中高點77.1美元，盤中低點72.98美元，均價75.78美元，成交量107.62萬股。

Carvana眼前最具體的變化，是市場正在檢驗它能否把高成長延續到新一季財報。資料顯示，華爾街對截至2026年9月的當季預估營收為77億美元、每股盈餘0.44美元，分別較去年同期成長36%與113%，且過去4季有3季優於預期，代表外界仍把焦點放在平台交易量與獲利效率是否持續改善。公司治理面也出現一項相對少見的正面訊號，董事Michael E. Maroone於7月31日公開市場買進2.5萬股、金額約150萬美元。不過同期間也有多筆高階主管依10b5-1計畫賣股，顯示公司目前仍處在成長期待與估值拉鋸並存的階段。

D.R. Horton（DHI.US）： 成交價156.08美元，上漲7.47%，開盤152.44美元，盤中高點157.1美元，盤中低點152.44美元，均價155.19美元，成交量15.53萬股。

D.R. Horton近14日未見符合條件的公司新聞，輸入資料也沒有揭露新推案節奏、交屋指引、土地收購，或財測調整等可直接影響營運方向的新增事件。對大型住宅建商而言，真正重要的訊號通常會來自接單、取消率、價格折讓與融資條件變化，但這次資料並未提供相關更新。因此，目前較難以公司自身消息解釋近期變化，也不足以判定其基本面已出現新的轉折。後續若要重新評估D.R. Horton的營運節奏，仍需等待管理層對住房需求、庫存與促銷策略提出更明確的季度說法。

news.Title: Strategy CEO puts his Bitcoin firm alongside SpaceX, Alphabet
news.Content: Wall Street's biggest fundraisers this year read like a who's who of the future: a rocket company, Google's parent and America's most famous chipmaker. And then, according to its CEO, there's Strategy (Nasdaq: MSTR), a company that used to sell business software and now mostly buys Bitcoin (BTC). Strategy ranks fourth among U.S. companies raising money by selling stock in 2026, behind only SpaceX (Nasdaq: SPCX), Alphabet (Nasdaq: AAPL) and Intel (Nasdaq: INTL), CEO Phong Le wrote on X. He added that Strategy was No. 1 in 2025 and No. 2 in 2024. "The AI investment cycle is massive. So is the Bitcoin capital cycle," Le wrote. What 'equity issuer' means When a company issues equity, it sells new shares to investors in exchange for cash. Most companies do it to raise capital to build factories, hire employees, or develop products. SpaceX builds rockets. Alphabet builds AI. Intel builds chips. Strategy builds a pile of Bitcoin. For a sense of the company Strategy is keeping, SpaceX raised $75 billion in June in the largest IPO ever. The deal valued Elon Musk's rocket and AI company at about $1.77 trillion, Reuters reported. Strategy's haul is smaller but still eye-popping. The company has raised about $21 billion from selling shares so far this year, it said in its third-quarter results released last week, and has spent $14.33 billion buying Bitcoin. That pile is now enormous. Strategy holds 849,327 Bitcoin, bought for about $64 billion in total, according to a filing on Monday. That's roughly 4% of all the Bitcoin that will ever exist . Strategy bought another 811 Bitcoin last week, paying an average of $80,846 per coin, Monday's filing showed. The timing wasn't perfect. Bitcoin traded near $77,000 on Tuesday. Across its whole stash, though, Strategy's average cost is $75,451 per coin, so its giant bet is still slightly in the green. Cofounder and executive chairman Michael Saylor, who is among Bitcoin's loudest cheerleaders, isn't worried. "We're at the beginning of the next bitcoin bull market," he remarked. How the money machine works Strategy raises cash in two main ways. The first is selling its regular common shares, known by the ticker MSTR. This works best when investors pay more for Strategy's stock than the Bitcoin behind each share is worth. The second is preferred stock, a kind of hybrid between a stock and a bond. Buyers get regular dividend payments, much like interest, and get paid before ordinary shareholders. But they usually don't get a vote. Strategy sells several of these with names that might sound like a gym class: Stretch, Strike, Stride and Strife. Story Continues Saylor has described the business as a company that sells credit to investors and uses the cash to buy Bitcoin. That credit isn't free. Strategy's preferred dividends cost about $1.76 billion a year . More on TheStreet Roundtable Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX protest NYSE parent's new plan Nvidia's new 51% rule could shut China's backdoor to AI chips CFTC opens U.S. stocks to crypto-style futures that never expire The year 'never sell' got complicated For years, Saylor's message to the world was simple: never sell your Bitcoin. Then 2026 happened. As Bitcoin slid from its October 2025 record, Strategy made its first Bitcoin sale since 2022 in May, and then sold 3,588 coins for about $216 million in late June and early July . Saylor later explained that "never sell" was advice for regular people holding Bitcoin, not a rule for how a company like Strategy manages its money. The buying resumed soon after, and the company is now back near its record stash. Same league, different game Le's comparison is bold, but the money is real. Investors handed Strategy about as much cash this year as some of the biggest names in tech. The difference is what that cash becomes. SpaceX's money turns into rockets, Alphabet's into data centers. Strategy's money turns into Bitcoin, and its fortunes rise and fall with it. The Roundtable 100 If you follow our market coverage, don't miss the Roundtable 100 . Updated every Friday, it's a power ranking of the 100 most investable tech stocks, including digital assets. Check out the latest RTB 100 rankings at roundtable100.com . news.Title: Stock market today: Dow jumps over 1,000 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq gain after Democrats win control of Congress
news.Content: US stocks glided higher on Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in a seismic midterm election, paving the way for a divided government. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 2.5%, while those on the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) climbed 1.5%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) traded up by 1.7%. AMD ( AMD ) stock fell slightly following the company's Q3 earnings beat . Markets swiftly repriced a Democratic sweep of the House and Senate — and the potential for ballot measures and newly elected officials to restrict data center construction . Chip stocks, including Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Micron ( MU ), fell more than 1%. Meanwhile, other parts of the tech sector offset some of those losses with Apple ( AAPL ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) each hitting all-time highs. Investors will also be watching for policy actions on housing and pharmaceuticals in the aftermath of the election. As Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre pointed out on Tuesday , midterm elections have a history of shaping stock performance in the near term but don't move markets much over the long term. The economic calendar for Wednesday features S&P and ISM data on economic activity indexes, while ADP's private payrolls will offer a glimpse at the state of the "low hire, low fire" labor market. Earnings reports from Arm Holdings ( ARM ), McDonald's ( MCD ), Qualcomm ( QCOM ), Novo Nordisk ( NVO ), and Uber Technologies ( UBER ), and more, meanwhile, offer alternative data points on the health of the consumer and AI demand. LIVE 13 updates 26 mins ago Ines Ferré Apple, Microsoft hit all-time highs as Nasdaq surges 2% in post-election rally Stocks surged on Wednesday, with most sectors green across the board after a Democratic mid-term election sweep. Tech ( XLK ) bounced as Apple ( AAPL ) shares hit all-time highs, sending the iPhone maker's market cap above $5 trillion. Microsoft ( MSFT ) also surged 6% to hit a new record. The Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) composite rallied more than 2%, while the Dow ( ^DJI ) surged more than 1,100 points, or about 2%. 35 mins ago David Hollerith Why the stock market is unexpectedly rallying in the wake of the Democratic blue wave Call it a contrarian move, Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports: It has been a riveting 12 hours or so in the markets as investors slice and dice the midterm election outcomes. Initially, stocks got hammered as the results trickled in. The thinking was that Democrats are less pro-business than Republicans, and since they will control the House and the Senate, there goes the corporate profit miracle that has driven the markets over the past two years. But something very interesting has emerged after that initial knee-jerk reaction. Stocks are rallying on Wednesday — big-time! 56 mins ago David Hollerith US services growth slows in October as inflation pressures persist US services activity expanded at a slower pace in October as growth moderated and businesses continued to grapple with elevated costs and supply chain disruptions. The Institute for Supply Management's services index fell to 54.5 from 54.9 in September, missing economists' expectations of 54.8, though still marking its 28th consecutive month in expansion territory. New orders dropped 3.9 points to 55.9 as business activity ebbed. Employment picked up for a second consecutive month, with its index rising to 51.4 from 50.1. Meanwhile, a measure of prices paid eased to 73.0 from 74.0 but remained elevated as businesses faced higher fuel costs, tariffs and shipping delays. A separate survey from S&P Global also showed slower growth, with its services index falling to 56.1 from 58.8 in September. Businesses reported strong demand but raised selling prices more quickly as they passed on higher operating costs. Today at 3:09 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Apple hits new high. Why the Democratic blue wave may be good for the stock. Apple ( AAPL ) stock jumped 6% to a new all-time high on Wednesday as investors perceived the stock as a winner from the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections. Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi breaks down what analysts are saying is behind the move higher: One winner could be Apple ( AAPL ) for two reasons, opined Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani. The first is more of a defensive play amid the unknown that is fresh D.C. gridlock. "Apple offers a different earnings driver through iPhone mix/pricing and services rather than data-center construction; our work points to resilient demand, with gross-margin recovery and price elasticity the key tests. This is THE name to keep working when investors want to get defensive," Daryanani said. The other aspect is cooling memory chip prices, a major headwind for Apple, as data center projects get delayed or outright blocked by the Dems. Daryanani added, "Memory input inflation (DRAM & NAND) has been a sizable headwind for a host of names in our coverage (AAPL for example, talked about 140bps GM headwind in Dec-qtr due to memory, but also PC names). Could a slowdown in DC buildouts actually temper memory demand and, in a way, help companies that have been impacted by the sizable memory inflation (AAPL is the key one but there are many others)?" Today at 2:38 PM UTC David Hollerith US stocks open higher after Democrat midterm sweep US stocks opened higher Wednesday as investors digested Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress along with fresh earnings and economic data. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 2%, while those on the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) and the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) climbed 1.1% each. Investors are also weighing what business policy shifts election results could bring to specific sectors, including possible moves on housing, pharmaceuticals, and data center construction. Chip stocks also came under pressure, with Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Micron ( MU ) lower, while AMD ( AMD ) slipped after its quarterly results. Today at 2:22 PM UTC David Hollerith 'Pretty solid job growth:' Private US employers added 86,000 jobs in October Hiring in the private sector showed continued strength in October, according to payroll processor ADP, as employers across a variety of industries added roles , Yahoo Finance's Claire Boston reports: Private companies added 86,000 jobs this month, matching a revised 86,000 in September, data released Wednesday showed. Economists had been expecting a gain of 67,000 jobs. Base wages for private-sector workers rose 3.2%, a figure that still trails inflation , while gross pay, which includes additional compensation such as overtime and bonuses, was up 4.7%. "You have back-to-back, two consecutive straight months of pretty solid job growth," ADP chief economist Nela Richardson said. Today at 2:15 PM UTC David Hollerith Block stock jumps as Jack Dorsey's AI bet shows signs of paying off Eight months after Jack Dorsey made one of corporate America's boldest bets on shrinking its workforce to prepare for the age of artificial intelligence, investors are finding more reasons to buy into the Silicon Valley billionaire's pivot. Shares of Dorsey's Block ( XYZ ), the payments company behind Cash App and merchant processor Square, jumped 9% in premarket trading Wednesday after it reported better-than-expected third quarter earnings and raised its gross profit outlook for next year. Today at 1:32 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma McDonald's Q3 sales growth slows amid tough consumer backdrop, new drinks push McDonald's ( MCD ) sales growth slowed in the third quarter as consumers faced a challenging economic backdrop and the fast food chain unveiled its growth strategy. The results showed that same-store sales grew by 1.5% year over year, a tick above the 1.4% growth Wall Street expected, according to Bloomberg estimates. In Q3 last year, McDonald's posted same-store sales growth of 3.6%. In the US, the company posted a 0.2% decline in comparable sales, slightly narrower than the expected 0.5% drop. Data from Placer.ai showed visits to the Golden Arches declined from a year ago, but the company said customers spent more when they did go. Promotions in October led to some strength ahead of the holiday season. CEO Chris Kempczinski said the company is "encouraged by improvement as the quarter progressed following our intervention on value." Today at 1:29 PM UTC Ines Ferré CVS announces plan to split into 2 companies, separating pharmacy from insurance CVS ( CVS ) announced plans to separate into two independent, publicly traded companies on Wednesday, reshaping one of the largest healthcare companies in the US. The company intends to separate CVS Health's insurance, pharmacy benefit management, and healthcare services operations from its retail pharmacy and community healthcare segments. The planned separation represents a significant shift from CVS Health's long-term strategy of bringing together insurance, pharmacy benefit management, and direct healthcare services under a single corporate structure. Under the proposed structure, one company will retain the CVS Health name and house Aetna, CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health, and Signify Health. The second entity, which will operate under the name CVS Pharmacy, will include approximately 9,000 retail pharmacy locations and MinuteClinic locations, among other services. Today at 12:00 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Democrats won control of Congress. Their economic agenda is set to target healthcare, tariffs, and Trump's allies. Yahoo Finance's Ben Werschkul reports: Democrats retook power in Washington on Tuesday night after flipping key House and Senate seats to command majorities in both houses of Congress. Democrats secured control of the Senate after winning races in historically red states including Texas, South Carolina, and Kansas. The party was also "marching toward control of the U.S. House" late Tuesday night, according to the Associated Press, after flipping seats from Florida to New Jersey to Kentucky. All four major networks said Democrats' control of the House was assured. The power shift creates a new platform for Democrats to launch investigations of President Trump's economic allies — Elon Musk to name one — and pass bills that may be unlikely to become law but will mark a sharp change in the political climate for business leaders and economic issues after two years of unified Republican control. The change also appears set to elevate figures like Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren and others to prominent positions with oversight over economic policy. Today at 11:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell The AI sell-off saved Apple from a sell-off of its own Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban writes: Despite an earnings beat and strong iPhone sales, investors focused on Apple's ( AAPL ) weaknesses, slowing services growth, and projected lower margins as the stock fell 2% on Tuesday. But the iPhone maker may have also been cushioned by its unique position among the tech giants — and the massive sell-off they had just a few trading days ago. While everyone else has been spending lavishly on the AI build-out, Apple has been biding its time , as if content to let its competitors simply do their business on its hardware. To some, this is the "wrong" end of the AI trade. But in the jittery moments of AI angst, when that lavish spending's meaning shifts from "potential" to "risk," it sends investors running from Google, Amazon, and Microsoft into the arms of Cupertino, safe from the risky AI bets . Today at 10:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell A Democrat won the Texas governor's race after promising to halt new data center construction A strong showing by Democrats in Texas swept Gina Hinojosa into office as the state's first Democratic governor since 1990 in a contest closely watched by Big Tech companies. The state is considered a bellwether for government restrictions on AI data centers. Incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott conceded the race late Tuesday, calling Hinojosa and then telling his supporters , "mathematically we are not going to be able to win this election." The Associated Press declared Hinojosa the winner at 11:17 p.m. ET. Hinojosa, Texas' first Latina governor, has pledged to impose a moratorium on data center construction in Texas, which accounts for more than 25% of planned US capacity by 2030. Today at 9:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Good morning. Here's what's happening today. Economic data: MBA mortgage applications, week ended Oct. 30 (+3.4% prior); ADP employment change, October (+70,000 expected, +90,000 prior); S&P Global US services PMI, October final reading (57.9 prior); S&P Global US composite PMI, October final reading (57.6 prior); ISM services index, October (54.7 expected, 54.9 prior); ISM services new orders, October (75 expected, 74 prior); ISM services new orders, October (58.8 expected, 59.8 prior); ISM services employment, October (50 expected, 50.1 prior) Earnings calendar: Arm Holdings ( ARM ), McDonald's ( MCD ), QUALCOMM ( QCOM ), Novo Nordisk ( NVO ), Uber Technologies ( UBER ), McKesson Corporation ( MCK ), CVS Health ( CVS ), Emerson Electric ( EMR ), Datadog ( DDOG ), MercadoLibre ( MELI ), Motorola Solutions ( MSI ), Manulife Financial Corporation ( MFC ), The Allstate Corporation ( ALL ), MetLife ( MET ), Kraft Heinz ( KHC ) Catch up on some other top stories from overnight: Gold rises as dollar weakens; Democrats score early wins in US midterm elections Asian shares fall on selling of tech shares as markets watch for results of US midterm elections Duolingo stock jumps on user growth, upbeat guidance Bettors vs. pollsters: The midterm showdown AMD's data center sales nearly double, topping Wall Street's forecast LIVE 13 updates Initially,

news.Title: How to Play the Selloff in Arm Stock
news.Content:
The recent tech selloff has been especially tough on semiconductor stocks, with Arm Holdings (ARM) suffering the most. Shares fell more than 11% during the Friday trading session on Oct. 30, before recovering somewhat to end down by around 10%. The selling sentiment continued on Monday, though ARM had been bouncing back to around $203.71 during Tuesday's session before dropping again as trading kicked off Wednesday morning.

Importantly, the decline wasn't caused by poor earnings results from Arm itself. Rather, concerns over returns from investments in AI infrastructure have been putting a lot of pressure on the overall semiconductor group. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Nvidia (NVDA), and Broadcom (AVGO) have all seen significant declines. Nevertheless, with Arm set to report earnings on Nov. 4, there are additional reasons to rethink the company's valuation and prospects for growth.

About Arm Stock

Based in Cambridge, England, Arm Holdings develops and licenses semiconductor IP, including energy-efficient CPU architectures that are used in a wide array of applications ranging from smartphones and data centers to automotive systems and AI devices. Instead of selling chips itself, Arm makes its money mostly from licensing and royalties; however, the recent move into producing its own silicon has changed that somewhat. At Monday's close, the company had a market cap of around $210 billion.

Although the company has seen a noticeable correction, ARM stock has performed well this year. Shares have been up by around 86% year-to-date (YTD), easily outperforming the 12% gain in the Nasdaq-100 Index. Nevertheless, the stock has lost about 34% over the past month and currently sits at around 55% below its 52-week high of $452.70.

The most serious concern right now is valuation. ARM trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 178.76x and a P/S ratio of 44.71x. In contrast, a peer group valuation dataset for semiconductors puts the median price-to-sales (P/S) ratio at around 14.6x.

Therefore, even despite this steep selloff, Arm still looks expensive. Investors are paying a very high price for the company's exposure to AI infrastructure and for its ability to generate more revenue per generation of chips.

Story Continues

Beats on Earnings as AI Demand Accelerates

The recent earnings results of Arm provide quite a different story compared to the recent price performance. During the July 29 conference call, the company reported Q1 2027 earnings that beat expectations on both top and bottom lines. Revenue came in at $1.29 billion, rising 22% year-over-year (YoY) and beating Wall Street's expectation of approximately $1.26 billion. EPS was $0.45, above the consensus of $0.40 and up 29% from the year before.

What attracted my attention was the performance of Arm's royalty business, which saw its revenue rise by 22% to $715 million, while licensing revenue increased 23% to $574 million. Importantly, data center royalties have grown more than two times YoY, implying that Arm is now benefiting more and more from the transition to power-efficient AI infrastructure.

Moreover, Arm's newly introduced AGI CPU provides another opportunity. According to management, the demand for the product from customers now exceeds $2 billion over fiscal years 2027 and 2028, compared to the previously mentioned initial $1 billion opportunity. However, it shouldn't be confused with actual revenue recognition, since the company is still struggling with increasing manufacturing capacity.

There are also some worries. While reporting robust revenue growth, the company's GAAP operating income decreased by approximately 20% YoY to $91 million. That was due to higher operating expenses and investments in R&D. With Arm moving beyond its traditional licensing business model, execution and profitability have now become more and more important.

Looking forward, the company guided Q2 revenue to be around $1.38 billion, ±$50 million, and EPS to be $0.47, ±$0.04. Wall Street expects the company to bring in approximately $1.38 billion in revenue and earn $0.48 in EPS, meaning that analysts expect another quarter of double-digit revenue growth.

It has been confirmed that Arm will publish its Q2 2027 results on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after the market close. Given the recent volatility, the upcoming earnings report may be quite critical for determining whether shares stabilize or suffer another correction.

What Do Analysts Expect From ARM Stock?

Despite the sharp drop, Wall Street has remained fairly optimistic about Arm's outlook. Analysts assign ARM stock a "Moderate Buy" rating consensus with a mean price target of $289.14. Based on the recent price of $199, its mean target implies a potential upside of approximately 47%. At the same time, the highest price target of $480 implies a potential upside of approximately 136%, while the lowest target of $130 offers a potential downside of roughly 34%. This rather large range reflects the uncertainty concerning Arm's earnings potential and its valuation.

news.Title: 〈美國期中選舉〉年底行情別高興太早！巴克萊潑冷水：AI兩大難題還沒解
news.Content:
據《彭博》報導，美國期中選舉結果出爐，市場期待政治不確定性消退，能為美股年底行情掃除障礙。不過，巴克萊(BCS-US)警告，近期壓抑股市的核心問題，仍是AI投資能創造多少營收，以及企業如何籌措龐大建設資金，這兩項疑慮都不會隨投票結束而消失。

民主黨拿下國會控制權、川普表態接受選舉結果後，美股指數期貨由跌轉漲，顯示不確定性降低帶動投資人逢低買進。但巴克萊全球股票戰術策略主管Alex Altmann認為，短線情緒改善，未必足以支撐市場期待的年底漲勢。

選舉並非下跌主因 AI營收與融資才是關鍵

Altmann指出，華爾街經歷艱難的10月後，愈來愈期待期中選舉成為股市反彈的催化劑，讓投資人重新加碼，迎接令人振奮的聖誕行情。

然而，他強調：「那斯達克並不是因為期中選舉風險才下跌10%。」在他看來，這波回檔主要反映市場對AI融資及營收成長前景的擔憂，選情不確定性雖有影響，卻只是次要因素。

投資人真正需要釐清的是，企業投入AI基礎建設的龐大資金，能否帶來足夠營收，以及後續支出將如何籌措。Altmann直言，目前牽動股市的兩大因素就是AI營收與AI融資，而這兩個問題短期內都難有答案。

儘管投資人先前已降低股票曝險，仍有重新建立部位的空間，但今年剩餘交易時間有限，感恩節與聖誕節期間通常也伴隨較清淡的交易與流動性，成為年底布局必須考量的因素。

德州監管可能收緊 AI擴建再添變數

選舉結果仍可能透過政策影響科技股。Altmann認為，州政府與聯邦層級採取措施限制AI基礎建設擴張的可能性增加，是這次期中選舉影響AI交易最直接的管道。

德州便是重要觀察點。當地有數十個AI資料中心園區開發計畫，民主黨候選人James Talarico贏得聯邦參議員選舉，Gina Hinojosa也當選州長，提高了資料中心建設面臨更嚴格監管的可能性。Hinojosa在競選期間曾多次呼籲暫停資料中心開發。

Altmann表示，德州約占預計資料中心建設量的四分之一，凸顯當地政策變化對AI產業的重要性。不過，選舉結果帶來的是監管收緊的可能，並不代表相關建案已確定停工。

整體而言，AI投資的挑戰遠超出政治範疇。由於AI仍是長期投資題材，最終回報難以衡量，市場情緒仍可能反覆波動。Altmann認為，即使期中選舉被視為短期不確定性消除的轉折點，也不太可能就此化解AI交易面臨的核心疑慮。

news.Title: 台股震盪跌勢收斂　上市和櫃買融資餘額減84.72億元
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中台北2026年11月4日電）台股今天持續走跌，上市指數盤中一度重挫3.35%，櫃買指數更是大跌5.39%，不過中午過後買盤湧入，跌勢同步大幅收斂，連帶影響上市和櫃買市場融資餘額合計減少新台幣84.72億元，減少金額較3日減逾7成。

台股今天震盪劇烈，上市指數盤中一度跌破42000點關卡，滑落至41855.82點，終場跌勢收斂，收在42948.91點，下跌358.63點。自10月6日的高點累計下跌7020.01點，跌幅達14.05%。

櫃買指數今天盤中一度滑落至326.88點，終場收在343.5點，下跌2.02點，跌幅約0.58%。自10月6日的430.86點累計下跌87.36點，跌幅達20.28%。

上市融資餘額在3日大幅減少229.25億元後，今天持續減少，不過，僅減少28.28億元，降至5969.46億元。自10月6日以來，融資餘額累計減少407.11億元，減幅僅約6.38%，幅度遠小於指數跌幅。

櫃買市場融資餘額今天減少56.44億元，降至1909.19億元。自10月6日以來，融資餘額累計減少352.32億元，減幅約15.58%，同樣小於指數跌幅。

兆豐國際投顧副總經理黃國偉表示，當前市場信心低迷，觀察上市融資餘額維持高檔水位，若反彈力道不夠，指數進一步修正，融資餘額追繳壓力可能增大。

news.Title: 民主黨橫掃參眾兩院 道指暴衝1200點 台指期夜盤44K沒站穩
news.Content:
（23：20更新）美國期中選舉民主黨大獲全勝，橫掃國會參眾兩院，川普總統也表態願意接受選舉結果，懸在華爾街頭上的政治不確定性風險暫時得以消除。周三（4日）美股一開盤，3大指數同步走高。道瓊工業指數早盤狂飆逾1200點，那斯達克指數暴漲逾600點。但與台股連動密切的費城半導體指數逆勢走低，早盤一度下挫逾2%，市場擔憂更嚴格的監管審查可能阻礙AI行業的快速增長。

台指期夜盤稍早一路狂飆，衝破44000點大關，一度飆漲1071點，報44274點，在美股早盤時段，雖仍有逾600點漲幅，但未能站穩44K大關。

截至台北時間4日晚間11點20分，道瓊工業指數上漲1061.30點（或2.05%），暫報52848.02點；那斯達克指數上漲629.628點（或2.48%），暫報26001.638點；標普500指數上漲132.14點（或1.75%），暫報7701.06點；費城半導體指數下跌81.96點（或0.77%），暫報10518.44點。

5大科技巨頭同步走強，蘋果漲6.26%，谷歌母公司Alphabet漲5.62%，微軟漲6.43%，亞馬遜漲7.18%，臉書母公司Meta漲2.20%。半導體類股方面，輝達跌1.03%，超微漲2.22%，台積電ADR跌0.28%，聯電ADR漲0.09%。

投資者最初認為，民主黨在選舉中取得壓倒性勝利可能對股市構成不利影響，因為新一屆國會可能加強監管審查，尤其是針對高成長的科技企業。不過，隨著美國國債殖利率下降，以及市場對美國經濟基本面依然穩健的信心增強，股市隨後獲得支撐。

Lombard Odier Investment Managers的總體經濟主管Florian Ielpo表示，「政治僵局應該會降低美國再次實施大規模財政擴張的可能性，而伴隨而來的國債殖利率下降，最終可能為股市提供一定支撐。」他指出，基本面環境並沒有突然發生變化，美國經濟成長依然穩健。

news.Title: 台股崩跌怎沒人畢業？網曝「跌不夠深」：到這數字再說
news.Content: 財經中心／綜合報導 台股近期震盪劇烈，大盤加權指數從 7 月底約 4 萬點低點起漲，一路狂飆攻上近 5 萬點高位，未料 11 月剛開盤便遭遇極速修正，台指回落至約 4 萬 3400 點附近。短時間內大幅拉回讓不少高檔進場的投資人傻眼，就有網友質疑，許多人持股均價都在 4 萬 5000 點以上，如今回檔如此兇猛，為何網路上卻鮮少看到散戶的「畢業文」？文章曝光後引發討論。 有網友質疑，許多人持股均價都在 4 萬 5000 點以上，如今回檔如此兇猛，為何網路上卻鮮少看到散戶的「畢業文」。（圖／民視新聞網） 一名網友在 PTT 以「 跌這麼深都沒有畢業文？ 」為題發文指出，雖然大盤點位對比年初或去年仍屬相對高檔，但過去幾個月不少散戶持續加碼，甚至有許多股民是衝到高檔才追價進場，推估不少人的持股成本均價都在 4 萬 5000 點以上的位階。如今台指迅速崩跌至 43400 點，原PO感到十分納悶，直言「這幾個月怎麼都沒看到畢業文？難道台灣散戶都賺錢，外資買高賣低、法人在賠錢嗎？」。 貼文曝光後迅速掀起熱烈討論，留言區更湧入大批網友瘋狂酸爆，有網友無奈自嘲「要跳樓了，哪有時間PO文」、「已經升天了」、「腳麻了」或是「已經被救護車載走了」，直言根本沒空發文。也有人認為現在跌得還不够深，留言嗆聲「代表還有得殺」、「43000深在哪？」、「跌到3萬9再說」、「沒到3萬5000點以下，不會有畢業文」。 許多股民相對淡定，表示大家都賺爛了所以沒感覺。（圖／民視新聞網） 不過，也有許多股民相對淡定，表示大家都賺爛了所以沒感覺，或是認為身邊不少人都是現股長期投資、漲也沒賣，甚至有人直言因為目前很多人都只是少賺而不是真的賠錢，大家還在繼續凹單，才會遲遲不見畢業文。

news.Title: 盤中暴跌1400點！陳嘉偉曝「台股最慘結局」：恐一路下修至26,825點
news.Content:
台股4日上演驚天洗盤行情，盤中一度重挫近1,400點，隨後在買盤進場下收斂至下跌300餘點。分析師陳嘉偉於《股市總司令》節目中指出，尾盤急拉並非V型反轉，而是大盤高點「M頭」型態確立後的初跌段逃命波。指標股台積電表現相對疲弱，顯示市場信心已因上週跌破半年線及季線下彎而受挫；陳嘉偉提醒，大盤後續恐陷入階梯式走跌，建議投資人利用反彈把握空單布局，並預估中線目標將下探33,678點。

均線全面走平空頭排列 台積電反彈無力凸顯結構弱勢

從技術面觀察，目前台股多條主要均線已呈現走平甚至下彎，季線形成明顯壓力，型態上構成高檔M頭與假突破大跌格局。陳嘉偉特別分析，權值龍頭台積電在此波反彈中的力道與角度均遠遜於加權指數，屬於結構上的弱勢股；當權值股無法提供實質支撐，大盤即便短線出現強彈，也僅是半年線向下扣抵所帶來的暫時喘息，難以複製過往強勢V轉的多頭行情。

紀律執行三段式操作 殺融資高峰精準獲利回補

面對空頭格局，陳嘉偉展示「三段式放空實戰」策略，說明短線急跌過後必須確實執行空單回補。早盤先順勢布局空單，待接近中午12點市場爆發融資斷頭潮、指數殺至最低點時，隨即全數獲利回補，順應尾盤的拉升。由於放空具有「越跌獲利邊際越小」的特性，操作上絕不能一路死抱，唯有趁急跌順勢獲利落袋，等待反彈後再重新進場放空，才能在空頭行情中極大化操作效率。

歷史修正經驗推算 下修目標看33678與26825點

針對中長期走勢，陳嘉偉根據過去台積電季線下彎的歷史修正經驗進行對稱推算。若以先前台積電季線下彎修正32.6%的幅度同等套用至加權指數，台股中線對稱跌幅目標約落在33,678點；若情境惡化至四年前修正46.2%的灰犀牛風險，終極下修目標甚至可能逼近26,825點五年線／年線關卡。他強調，目前僅為初跌段反彈，未來仍有長時間的主跌段與末跌段，投資人應切忌盲目抄底。

news.Title: Meet the Only "Magnificent Seven" Stock That's Outperforming the S&P 500 and Nasdaq This Year (Hint: It's Not Nvidia)
news.Content:
The "Magnificent Seven" was popularized in 2023 by Bank of America analyst Michael Hartnett as a term for seven rapidly appreciating tech-focused growth companies. In 2023, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) were instrumental in driving the Nasdaq Composite's (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) monster 43.4% gain -- with all seven companies posting even bigger returns.

Big gains followed in 2024, with every Magnificent Seven stock except for Microsoft outperforming the Nasdaq and S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC). But in 2025, only Nvidia and Alphabet outperformed both indexes. And after last week's sell-off, the only Magnificent Seven stock left standing above the indexes is Apple, which surpassed Nvidia as the world's most valuable company on Oct. 30.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here's what separates Apple from its Magnificent Seven stock peers, and if the tech stock is a buy now.

Apple generated $31.9 billion in trailing 12-month free cash flow

Apple is up 26.8% year-to-date, outpacing the major indexes, the broader tech sector, and its Magnificent Seven peers.
