Apple is unique because artificial intelligence (AI) capital expenditures (capex) don't make or break its investment thesis. By comparison, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta Platforms, and Tesla continue to ramp up their AI spending. And although Nvidia has low capex, its major customers are the hyperscalers , so it needs them to see a return on their chip and associated AI infrastructure investments to justify future spending.

AAPL Free Cash Flow (Quarterly) data by YCharts

At the beginning of the AI ramp-up, cash-cow companies like Amazon and Alphabet were able to support higher spending with free cash flow (FCF) alone. But spending has grown so massive that Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms are now FCF-negative.

Story Continues

Alphabet is taking on debt, diluting shareholders by issuing stock, and is guiding for even higher spending in 2027. Investors are losing patience, with Alphabet experiencing a record $505 billion market cap plunge in a single session and plummeting around a 52-week low. Apple is the exact opposite narrative.

AI enhances Apple's investment thesis rather than defining it

Apple's balance sheet is in impeccable shape. It continues to generate gobs of FCF that it can use to reinvest in the business or return to shareholders through buybacks and dividends.

Apple isn't spending record capex to build data centers. Rather, its focus is on providing products that allow consumers and enterprises to interact with AI, such as the first touchscreen MacBook Pro, its first foldable iPhone Duo, its smart home system HomeView, smart glasses, an AI-powered pendant, and more. Apple is also directly passing along higher memory chip costs to customers through price increases. To help bridge the affordability gap, it is offering a new leasing program facilitated by Klarna, in addition to the multi-year service contracts already offered by carriers.

Apple doesn't need to spend a lot on AI capex because new product updates and AI features on its devices are manageable costs. Developers depend on Apple App Store downloads to gain traction, all the while funneling more revenue to Apple in fees.

What makes Apple particularly appealing is that it is exposed to virtually all of the benefits of AI adoption with very few of the cons. Whereas frontier models like Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's ChatGPT, and Alphabet's Gemini are all competing for user engagement. Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet are racing to attract cloud spend. By comparison, Apple is a catch-all way to bet on AI innovation and productivity improvements.

Outside of AI, Apple has evolved into a modern-day consumer staples company more than a tech stock. Its integrated ecosystem of products and services is essential for many users. And demand has proven incredibly sticky despite inflationary and cost-of-living pressures.

Apple has a 39.5 price-to-earnings ratio

Apple is hovering around an all-time high because AI acts as a cherry on top of its investment thesis rather than the entire sundae. If there were a cyclical slowdown in AI spending or an AI-driven stock market correction, Apple would be one of the best-positioned tech stocks to weather it.

The problem with buying the stock now is that Apple trades at 39.5 times earnings and 36.1 times forward earnings -- which is a significant premium compared to its 10-year median price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 27.6. However, Apple's valuation is digestible for investors who truly view Apple as a recession-proof, consumer staples/tech hybrid. Especially when compared to recession-resistant companies like Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) and Costco Wholesale (NASDAQ: COST), which are even more expensive than Apple. Walmart fetches a 42.8 forward P/E, and Costco's is 44.4.

Investors willing to pay a premium price for a safe stock may want to consider buying Apple, even around an all-time high. But investors who believe that AI spending will eventually pay off for hyperscalers will find stocks like Alphabet and Amazon at far more attractive valuations.

news.Title: IBM Plummets 18.5% in the Past Year: Time to Reassess the Stock?
news.Content:
International Business Machines Corporation IBM has declined 18.5% over the past year against the industry's growth of 81.3% due to macroeconomic challenges and a potent threat from AI firm Anthropic that threatens its core legacy businesses. The stock has lagged peers like Microsoft Corporation MSFT and Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN. While Microsoft has gained 2.2%, Amazon has remained flat on average over this period.

One-Year IBM Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Ails IBM?

IBM has long positioned itself as the dominant provider of mainframe systems optimized for high-volume, mission-critical workloads characterized by AI. Over decades, the company has built a durable revenue stream around maintaining, upgrading and modernizing legacy COBOL environments for large enterprises. The complexity of COBOL systems has historically served as a competitive moat. Many organizations hesitate to rewrite or replace these systems due to cost, operational risk and the shrinking pool of developers familiar with the language. But it appears that the moat may now be facing AI-driven erosion.

Anthropic's Claude Code tool can reportedly modernize legacy COBOL systems — a foundational programming language deeply embedded in IBM's mainframe ecosystem. With Claude Code proposing to substantially automate code exploration, documentation, refactoring and security analysis, it threatens to reduce enterprises' reliance on specialized legacy service providers like IBM, putting its sustenance at stake. COBOL remains deeply embedded in global infrastructure and continues to run in production daily across financial institutions, airlines, retailers and government systems. If Claude Code meaningfully reduces the cost and complexity of analyzing and migrating legacy systems, it could compress pricing power in IBM's Consulting segment, introducing a new competitive dynamic into a space that has historically been a labor-intensive and high-margin business for the company.

Margin Woes Dent IBM's Prospects

To add to the woes, IBM is facing competition from Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure. Increasing pricing pressure is eroding margins, and profitability has trended down over the years, barring occasional spikes. Weaknesses in its traditional business and foreign exchange volatility remain significant concerns.

IBM's frequent acquisitions have also escalated integration risks. Buyouts have negatively impacted the company's balance sheet, resulting in high levels of goodwill and net intangible assets. Moreover, a highly leveraged balance sheet has been troubling IBM over time.

Story Continues

Hybrid Cloud, AI Demand: IBM's Likely Saviors

Despite the setbacks, IBM is poised to benefit from healthy demand trends for hybrid cloud and AI, which drive the Software and Consulting segments. The company's growth is expected to be aided by analytics, cloud computing and security in the long run. A combination of a better business mix, improving operating leverage through productivity gains and increased investment in growth opportunities will likely boost profitability.

With a surge in traditional cloud-native workloads and associated applications, along with a rise in generative AI deployment, there is a radical expansion in the number of cloud workloads that enterprises are currently managing. This has resulted in heterogeneous, dynamic and complex infrastructure strategies, which have led firms to undertake a cloud-agnostic and interoperable approach to highly secure multi-cloud management, translating into a healthy demand for IBM hybrid cloud solutions.

The buyout of HashiCorp has significantly augmented IBM's capabilities to assist enterprises in managing complex cloud environments. HashiCorp's toolsets complement IBM RedHat's portfolio, bringing additional functionalities for cloud infrastructure management and bolstering its hybrid multi-cloud approach. IBM's watsonx platform is likely to be the core technology platform for its AI capabilities. watsonx delivers the value of foundational models to the enterprise, enabling them to be more productive.

Estimate Revision Trend

IBM is currently witnessing an uptrend in estimate revisions. Earnings estimates for IBM for 2026 have moved up 1.5% to $12.41 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has increased 1.3% to $13.24. The positive estimate revision portrays bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

End Note

IBM has invested heavily in its own AI capabilities and could incorporate generative AI into its consulting workflows to improve efficiency rather than lose relevance. A strong emphasis on quantum computing and hybrid cloud is driving value for customers. With improving earnings estimates, the stock is witnessing positive investor perception.

However, IBM's growth is dented by high operating costs and stiff competition that reduce its profitability. The company faces a potent threat from Anthropic and needs to fine-tune its business model to remain competitive. news.Title: 4 Semiconductor Stocks to Buy as Q3 Sales Soar on Robust AI Demand
news.Content:
AI-related chip stocks have been taking a beating lately, but the semiconductor industry as a whole hasn't been impacted much. Chip stocks have been the market's darling and have been largely responsible for the broader rally.

As demand for semiconductors remains elevated, sales have been skyrocketing. Continued heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is expected to create significant growth opportunities for the semiconductor industry.

Against this backdrop, semiconductor stocks such as Analog Devices ADI, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM, Texas Instruments TXN and NVIDIA Corporation NVDA appear well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand, making them attractive investment options with strong growth potential this year.

Chip Sales Hit New All-Time High

Global semiconductor sales totaled $517.7 billion in the third quarter, a surge of 24.1% from the second quarter, the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) said on Tuesday.

Year over year, semiconductor sales hit $172.6 billion in September, up 146.8%. Month over month, sales jumped 7.9% from the August total of $159.7 billion.

The solid jump in September and the third quarter comes after semiconductor sales surpassed the $1 trillion mark for the first time through August.

Michael Robbins, SIA president and CEO, said, "The global chip market grew substantially throughout the third quarter of this year, with worldwide sales increasing by more than 20% quarter-to-quarter for the third consecutive quarter."

AI-related chip stocks have been suffering lately as investors have been spiraling out of riskier assets on concerns over stretched valuations of AI stocks and questions about the sustainability of the sector's rapid expansion.

However, the fears are temporary as the semiconductor industry has played a major role in supporting broader stock market gains in recent years. Semiconductor sales have now recorded year-over-year growth in each of the first nine months of the year.

Heavy spending by major technology companies has renewed confidence in AI's long-term prospects. Several leading chipmakers benefiting from the AI boom have also reported strong quarterly earnings and issued optimistic guidance, helping ease investor concerns and drive semiconductor stocks higher.

The sector's strong showing in the third quarter followed an exceptional first half of 2026. Global semiconductor sales totaled $403.3 billion in the second quarter of 2026, following $298.5 billion in the first quarter, with sequential growth of 33.1% and 25%, respectively.

Story Continues

Semiconductors are increasingly essential to both established and emerging technologies, powering developments in fields such as the Internet of Things, 6G connectivity and artificial intelligence.

Rising demand from the automotive industry has provided another source of momentum for chip sales. At the same time, AI remains in the early stages of its growth cycle, prompting major technology companies to allocate billions of dollars toward research, development and infrastructure to advance the technology.

4 Semiconductor Stocks with Growth Potential

Analog Devices

Analog Devices is an original equipment manufacturer of semiconductor devices, specifically analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing ("DSP") integrated circuits. ADI's product line comprises amplifiers and comparators; analog-to-digital converters; digital-to-analog converters; video encoders and decoders; embedded processing products and DSPs; MEMS and temperature sensors; RF/IF components and converters; power and thermal management ICs, audio/video converters, amplifiers, CODECs, filters and processors. Analog Devices also offers analog, digital and RF switches and multiplexers; analog microcontrollers; clock and timing products.

Analog Devices' expected earnings growth rate for the current year is 66.9%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings has improved 0.3% over the past 60 days. ADI currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited is the world's largest dedicated integrated circuit foundry. TSM manufactures ICs for its customers based on their proprietary IC designs using its advanced production processes. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited's goal is to establish itself as one of the world's leading semiconductor companies by building upon the strengths that have made it the world's leading IC foundry.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited's expected earnings growth rate for the current year is 3.3%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings has improved 0.7% over the past 60 days. TSM presently carries a Zacks Rank #1.

Texas Instruments

Texas Instruments is an original equipment manufacturer of analog, mixed-signal and digital signal-processing integrated circuits. TXN has manufacturing and design facilities, including wafer fabrication and assembly/test operations in North America, Asia and Europe. Management strategy has been to build assets that would be fully utilized through their lifetimes and outsource any excess demand in peak situations to outside foundries.

Texas Instruments' expected earnings growth rate for the current year is 63.1%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings has improved 5.6% over the past 60 days. Currently, TXN carries a Zacks Rank #1.

NVIDIA Corporation

NVIDIA Corporation is the worldwide leader in visual computing technologies and the inventor of the graphics processing unit, or GPU. Over the years, NVDA's focus has evolved from PC graphics to AI-based solutions that now support high-performance computing, gaming and virtual reality platforms.

NVIDIA has an expected earnings growth rate of 95% for the current year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings has improved 0.5% over the last 60 days. NVDA currently has a Zacks Rank #2.

news.Title: If You Invested $10,000 in Intel Stock at Its Dot-Com-Era Peak, Here's How Much You'd Have Today
news.Content:
In the late 1990s, Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) was one of the most important companies in the technology industry. Its processors powered millions of personal computers, and its dominance in semiconductor manufacturing made it a compelling choice for investors looking to capitalize on the internet revolution.

On Aug. 31, 2000, Intel stock closed at a then-record $74.88. More than 26 years later, that optimism has delivered surprisingly disappointing results. As of the closing bell on Nov. 2, Intel shares traded at $59.97. This means a $10,000 investment made at its peak during the dot-com boom would be worth approximately $8,009 today, excluding dividends.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

INTC data by YCharts

Intel's struggles have become apparent throughout the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. Recently, shares collapsed nearly 29% on Oct. 30 following the company's third-quarter earnings report.

What went wrong with this former semiconductor powerhouse, and could its latest sell-off represent a lucrative opportunity for investors?

Intel's earnings reveal a complicated turnaround

Intel's third-quarter earnings report initially looked encouraging. Revenue increased 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) reached $0.52, more than doubling from the prior-year period.

Its Data Center and AI (DCAI) segment was particularly impressive, growing 78% year over year to $7.3 billion in revenue. Demand for Intel's Xeon server processors has strengthened as AI developers expand computing infrastructure to support more sophisticated applications across agentic AI workloads.

However, the company's PC business is facing challenges. Revenue from its Client Computing and Physical AI (CCPG) segment declined 5% to $8.1 billion. Even more concerning was management's outlook. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, below the $17 billion target Wall Street had anticipated. Adjusted earnings guidance of $0.25 also disappointed investors.

Intel's sharp sell-off shows that investors are reassessing how quickly the company's turnaround can realistically translate into sustainable growth across the entire business.

Why is Intel struggling?

For decades, Intel enjoyed competitive advantages in processor design and manufacturing. However, several strategic missteps gradually weakened its position.

Story Continues

Intel struggled to capitalize on the smartphone revolution. This allowed competitors to develop processors using alternative chip architectures. Meanwhile, manufacturing delays enabled Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing to establish itself as the industry's leading foundry for advanced chips.

These setbacks have become particularly noticeable as demand for AI infrastructure accelerates. Unlike Nvidia , whose graphics processing units are essential for training and deploying AI models, Intel remains heavily dependent on traditional central processing units (CPUs).

Indeed, CPUs remain critical components of accelerated computing systems, and Intel's latest data center results underscore that AI is driving meaningful demand for its products. With that said, the company hasn't captured the same economic opportunity as Nvidia, which stitches together accelerators with networking technology, CUDA software, and a developer ecosystem through an extensive roster of open-source models.

Intel's manufacturing strategy introduces another headache. The company is investing heavily in its foundry business in hopes of manufacturing advanced semiconductors for outside customers. Unfortunately, this transformation remains costly.

Intel Foundry generated $6.7 billion in revenue during the third quarter but posted an operating loss of $1.9 billion. In addition, most of the company's foundry revenue comes from internal products rather than external customers.

Is Intel stock a bargain or a value trap?

Intel isn't necessarily a lost cause. The company's latest financial performance indicates strong demand for server processors. Intel also benefits from the strategic importance of domestic semiconductor manufacturing, which has attracted government support.

Nevertheless, the company's long-term performance offers an important warning. The distinction between a cheap stock and an attractive investment is particularly relevant today in the AI era. Following its latest sell-off, Intel might look inexpensive relative to recent trading levels, but its valuation needs to be considered alongside manufacturing losses, ongoing capital expenditures (capex), the competitive landscape, and uncertain earnings growth.

For now, I see Intel as a speculative turnaround rather than a dependable long-term compounder. While its data center business is encouraging, the company still needs to prove its foundry investments will generate sustainable profitability.

Investors seeking exposure to semiconductor stocks have several alternatives with greater durability. Overall, Intel's disappointing performance since 2000 shows why investors should regularly reassess their investment theses. The company has opportunities to recover, but buying shares simply because they've fallen sharply risks confusing a potential bargain with a value trap.

news.Title: MRVL Plunges 36% in a Month: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL shares have lost 35.9% in the past month compared with the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry and the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's decline of 22% and 14.1%, respectively.

MRVL One-Month Performance Chart

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Despite the downward movement in MRVL's stock price, MRVL has remained at a premium valuation. MRVL stock is trading at a P/S multiple of 8.58X, much higher than the industry's multiple of 3.08X. The premium valuation is further substantiated by a Zacks Value Score of F.

MRVL Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Given the dynamics, investors must be wondering if it's the right time to invest, retain or sell the stock. Let's discuss the fundamentals of the company to get a better insight.

MRVL Stock Faces a Temporary Setback Amid Long-Term AI Growth

The decline in MRVL's stock price has come amid a broader sell-off in AI-related stocks spanning hyperscalers, semiconductor companies and AI infrastructure providers, as investors increasingly question whether massive AI investments will generate sufficient returns. Since MRVL supplies its solutions to these infrastructure providers, MRVL's stock has also been affected.

Marvell's recent stock decline coincides with the announcement of its proposed $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum Holdings LITE. Under the terms of the all-stock deal, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each Lumentum share held, raising investor concerns over valuation, shareholder dilution and the transaction's potential impact on earnings.

However, in the long term, the acquisition of Lumentum will add a substantial portfolio of optical and photonic technologies used in AI data centers, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications networks and advanced manufacturing. Lumentum's Optical Circuit Switching, high-speed transceivers and laser components are of the most strategic importance for MRVL.

Marvell's accelerating AI-driven growth provides a favorable backdrop for its proposed acquisition of Lumentum. Marvell's second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues increased 37% year over year to $2.74 billion, led by a 46% increase in data-center revenues to $2.17 billion, which accounted for 79% of total sales. Management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue growth outlook to approximately 45%, or roughly $12 billion, while expecting data-center revenues to increase about 60%, up from its prior expectation of approximately 50%.

Story Continues

Within Marvell's portfolio, custom silicon is emerging as an increasingly important growth driver as hyperscalers expand their demand for specialized XPUs and XPU-attach products. AI connectivity also remains strong, with demand for 800G optical DSPs continuing and 1.6T products ramping rapidly. Marvell's scale-out switching business is on track to more than double in fiscal 2027, driven by growing adoption of 51.2T switches across a broader customer base. Meanwhile, increasing customer interest in scale-up optics and switching solutions could provide additional growth opportunities as AI infrastructure architectures evolve.

MRVL to Benefit From a Broader Portfolio

The integration of MRVL's electrical and optical interconnect, switching and custom silicon technologies with Lumentum's high-performance lasers, optical transceivers and optical circuit switching capabilities is expected to create a comprehensive connectivity portfolio spanning scale-across, scale-out, scale-up and scale-in architectures. These factors will strengthen MRVL's competitive positioning relative to Broadcom AVGO and enhance its ability to compete with Coherent COHR.

Broadcom is a leader in the domain of custom silicon solutions for data centers. Broadcom's advanced 3.5D XDSiP packaging platform is critical to ensure the performance and efficiency of custom AI XPUs. Combining Marvell's custom silicon, switching and DSP technologies with Lumentum's lasers, transceivers and optical switching could help MRVL compete with Broadcom's integrated AI connectivity portfolio.

Coherent is a vertically integrated manufacturer of lasers, transceivers, optoelectronic devices and modules and engineered materials that serve communications, industrial, instrumentation and electronics markets. Lumentum's optical components and laser technologies would strengthen MRVL's optical portfolio, enabling it to compete more effectively with Coherent in high-performance lasers and optical connectivity.

Amid these developments, investors need to keep a close eye on Marvell's ability to translate the acquisition of Lumentum into meaningful competitive gains. MRVL's profitability remains sensitive to product mix as newer data center platforms ramp up. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MRVL's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $4.21 per share, implying year-over-year growth of 48%. Estimates have remained unchanged for the past 30 days.

Conclusion

The recent decline in Marvell's stock price may present an opportunity for investors seeking exposure to the expanding AI infrastructure market. MRVL's strengths in custom silicon, optical connectivity, switching and data-center interconnect, along with its proposed acquisition of Lumentum, could support its long-term growth prospects.

However, the proposed acquisition also introduces integration, shareholder dilution and execution risks. Investors should closely monitor the transaction's progress, MRVL's profitability trends and the company's ability to translate its expanding portfolio into sustainable earnings growth.

Currently, MRVL stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: SpaceX inks Qualcomm deal, putting Starlink closer to becoming the fourth major US wireless carrier
news.Content:
SpaceX's ( SPCX ) goal of turning its Starlink service into a major US mobile carrier is one step closer to becoming a reality.

On Wednesday, Qualcomm ( QCOM ) announced that SpaceX has selected its Dragonwing Cellular Infrastructure platforms to power Starlink Mobile's nationwide terrestrial 5G cellular network.

Starlink already has the largest satellite-based network, and the ground-based stations will allow it to better compete with AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ).

Last month, the company announced an agreement to purchase licenses for 800 MHz spectrum.

"While Starlink Mobile's global 2 GHz mid-band spectrum will provide high-bandwidth capacity in the United States, this new low-band spectrum will provide a coverage layer that ensures Starlink Mobile's signal penetrates through obstacles, such as walls, and can provide service to customers' devices even when they are in buildings," the company said at the time.

According to Qualcomm, the new deal will allow both companies to begin deploying advanced 5G service and provide "an opportunity to lay the foundation for AI-native 6G in the years ahead."

The company says the effort will require SpaceX to deploy its chip technology across tens of thousands of cellular towers nationwide.

"Our agreement with SpaceX is structured in such a way that as the deployment begins, starting from next year, it's going to ramp up pretty rapidly from there onwards," said Durga Malladi, EVP and GM for technology planning, edge solutions, and data center at Qualcomm.

"So it's a multi-year agreement that we have with them in terms of the deployment capability as we ramp up all the way to nationwide coverage," he added.

Earlier this month, The Washington Post reported that SpaceX was in talks with EchoStar ( ECHO ) to operate its own carrier through EchoStar's Boost Mobile brand.

The company made the move after AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon reportedly rejected its requests to use their network capacity through a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) deal.

An MVNO rents capacity from existing carriers and sells it under its own branding. But an operator like Starlink Mobile could prove a particularly potent challenger to the Big Three network carriers, leaving them little incentive to work with Elon Musk's firm.

news.Title: Docusign vs. Okta: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As digital workflows become standard, many investors are choosing between the leader in electronic signatures and the titan of identity security. Here is how Docusign (NASDAQ:DOCU) and Okta (NASDAQ:OKTA) compare today.

Docusign focuses on automating agreement workflows through its Intelligent Agreement Management platform. Okta operates as a leader in identity security, ensuring only authorized users access corporate systems. While both provide critical cloud services, their growth profiles and market valuations offer distinct paths for investors looking ahead to 2027.

The case for Docusign

Docusign provides cloud-based software that simplifies the way organizations prepare, sign, and manage agreements. According to its latest annual report, filed for the period ending in early 2026, its Intelligent Agreement Management platform serves over 1.8 million customers globally. The company relies on deep integrations with partners like Salesforce (NYSE:CRM), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and SAP (NYSE:SAP) to drive its product adoption.

In fiscal 2026, revenue reached nearly $3.2 billion, representing growth of approximately 8.2% over the prior year. This steady expansion is supported by a broad international presence in over 180 countries. The company reported net income of roughly $309.1 million during this period, showing continued profitability even as it invests in new artificial intelligence agreement features to remain competitive.

Docusign maintains a healthy balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1, which measures total debt against shareholder equity. As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is 0.7, which compares a company's short-term assets to its short-term liabilities. Free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, reached approximately $1.1 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 53.4% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, as SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Okta

Okta provides identity and access management solutions to more than 20,000 customers globally, including large Fortune 50 enterprises and government agencies. Its latest annual report highlights a land-and-expand sales model used to increase its footprint among tech stocks . It manages an extensive integration network featuring over 7,000 connections with various cloud and mobile applications.

In fiscal 2026, revenue reached nearly $2.9 billion, representing approximately 11.8% growth over the previous year. This double-digit revenue increase remains higher than that of its e-signature peer, reflecting strong demand for cloud-based identity security. The company reported net income of roughly $235 million, a significant improvement from the fiscal year ended in 2024, when it reported a net loss.

Story Continues

Okta maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1, indicating its total debt is low relative to its shareholder equity. As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is 1.4, suggesting the company has ample short-term assets to cover its upcoming liabilities. Free cash flow for the period was approximately $863.0 million. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 61.5% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, as SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Docusign faces intense competition, particularly from Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE), which offers a rival document platform. Potential disruptions to the business model could arise from rapid advancements in artificial intelligence. Furthermore, the company deals with long and unpredictable enterprise sales cycles that make forecasting future revenue difficult. It also relies on third-party cloud service providers for infrastructure, which presents operational risks.

Okta must contend with intense competition from larger, well-established companies such as Microsoft. Any future cybersecurity incidents or service outages could harm the brand and lead to the loss of customer trust or regulatory scrutiny. Additionally, the company faces the ongoing challenge of maintaining its competitive advantage as AI-driven security threats evolve. Managing international operations also introduces complexity regarding global data privacy regulations.

Valuation comparison

Docusign appears cheaper than Okta when comparing their forward P/E and P/S ratios.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

One key difference between Okta and Docusign is how important their offerings are to keeping an organization running. I have personally used Docusign in the past, but I've also used other e-signature platforms that weren't all that different. They are all alike enough that I couldn't even tell you the specific software names. So there is a question in my mind of whether Docusign customers could simply substitute some other platform that's just as good (or close enough).

Okta, on the other hand, provides critical software to maintain organizational security and identity management. It's more important than ever for companies to lock down data for reputational, regulatory, and legal reasons. I think this makes Okta's products and services stickier than Docusign.

Now, let's turn to the tape:

DOCU data by YCharts

Okta stock has handily outperformed Docusign and the S&P 500 over the past decade or so. Okta's valuation is considerably higher than Docusign's, but I think the chart above indicates why investors are willing to pay that premium. Okta looks more attractive to me.

Likely Winners

Health insurers and hospitals: Democrats favor more healthcare spending. Centene Corp (CNC) rose 4.5% and Molina Healthcare Inc (MOH) rose 6%. HCA gained 3.7% and Universal Health Services 2.2%. BNP Paribas cautions that Democrats probably can't restore major parts of the Affordable Care Act. Concessions in budget talks are more realistic.

Hearings and investigations are more likely, though analysts doubt legislation could meaningfully stall construction. Core Scientific fell 2.8% and Iren 1.4%. news.Title: Texas, Ohio and Georgia data center risks after Democratic election wins
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Three of the most important data center states elected Democratic governors on Nov 3, 2026. That includes Texas, Ohio and Georgia . Democrats also won the Senate seats in Texas and Ohio, and Georgia's Sen. Jon Ossoff was re-elected ( Reuters , Nov 4, 2026, 01:11 EST; Reuters , Nov 4, 01:58 EST). Reuters called the results "more like a referendum on AI" than on President Trump. The stakes are large: Texas alone holds about a quarter of US capacity due by 2030, per GLJ Research ( Reuters , Nov 4, 04:58 EST).

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The three states differ in how far each has already moved and what each winner has promised.

Texas: Pause Meets Mandate

The prior regime was already tight. Gov. Greg Abbott froze grid approvals on Aug 3–4. On Sept 21 he barred the state environmental agency from issuing data center permits until the grid audit finishes. ERCOT was reviewing about 474 GW of requests, over five times record peak load, and roughly 90% came from data centers ( Reuters , Aug 4; Reuters , Sept 21).

The winner wants more. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa dismissed Abbott's steps as political theater. She wants an immediate halt to new projects until lawmakers strengthen community protections, plus an end to tax breaks ( Reuters , Nov 4, 07:10 EST). Democrats also took the lieutenant governor, attorney general, comptroller and railroad commissioner offices ( Reuters , Nov 4, 07:21 EST). Only 30% of Texans would support a data center in their community (Texas Politics Project, August).

Texas moves from a pause to "conditional permission," with higher costs and no incentives.

Ohio: The Most Explicit Mandate

Ohio's signals are the most direct of the three:

Acton's platform: Gov.-elect Amy Acton supports a data center moratorium . She promised lower energy bills and a utilities commission "not beholden to utility companies." Ohio residential bills rose more than 20% in two years, per EIA data ( Reuters , Oct 31). Her opponent Vivek Ramaswamy instead promised nearby residents would pay nothing toward the bills.

Brown's win: Sherrod Brown beat Sen. Jon Husted after branding him "data centers' best friend" ( Reuters , Nov 3, 11:17 PM EST).

Existing brakes: Gov. Mike DeWine suspended new data center tax-exemption applications, but lawmakers didn't act on reforms before recess. A group called Conserve Ohio is pursuing a 2027 constitutional amendment to ban data centers above 25 MW ( Reuters , Sept 20).

Industry stake: Amazon says it has invested nearly $40B in Ohio since 2015, and Meta over $2.3B since 2018.

Story Continues

Ohio carries the clearest moratorium risk, though it is a smaller hub.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Georgia: Rules Over Bans

Georgia is the most uncertain. Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, beat billionaire Rick Jackson and ends 20+ years of Republican control ( Reuters , Nov 3, 9:33 PM EST). No reporting on her specific data center platform was found. Reuters did say Democratic candidates in Texas and Georgia campaigned partly on a moratorium, but that cannot be attributed to Bottoms individually.

Why Georgia may differ:

Ratepayer-protection deals exist. Equinix (EQIX) signed a 20-year take-or-pay deal covering 100% of grid costs for its Hampton project ( Investing.com , Aug 6).

Utility-side pipeline: Georgia Power (GPJA), a subsidiary of Southern (SO), filed a ~$900M-benefit nuclear uprate deal with Alphabet (GOOGL), pending PSC approval ( Investing.com , Sept 21).

Federal support: A record $3.3B USDA loan went to Oglethorpe Power, which could indirectly serve data centers ( Reuters , Oct 16). A Democratic Congress may scrutinize that kind of support.

Regulator elections: Utility commission seats in Georgia were on the ballot. Those results were not available, and they matter for rates and approvals.

CBRE calls Atlanta the most active US data center construction market. Georgia's risk is a rule rewrite, not necessarily a freeze.

The pre-market drop erases most of Monday's gains. It also follows about $5T of value lost from 47 AI and chip stocks since Oct 6 ( Investing.com , Nov 4, 05:57 EST).

Bear Case

Shrinking safe harbors: Texas and Georgia hold roughly a third of US AI data center investment. Ohio and the Midwest were a fallback. Losing all three raises costs and delays.

Incentive loss: Hinojosa's no-tax-break stance and Ohio's suspended exemptions hit project returns, not just timelines.

Financing: Vantage Point's Nick Ferres said ROI and financing risks "have likely become more challenging."

SpaceX: It aims to scale from 1.7 GW toward 13 GW, and Boca Chica faces local resistance.

Bull Case

Demand remains: BNY's Kevin Shea said policy "can disrupt the timing and the cost" but won't derail the theme ( Reuters , Oct 22). AMD guided server revenue to double in 2027.

Scarcity value: Energized and permitted capacity gains pricing power as new supply is delayed.

Cost-sharing as a template: Equinix-style agreements may become the price of admission, and the best-capitalized operators can absorb them.

Gridlock: Analysts doubt federal legislation could meaningfully stall construction.

What To Watch

Texas: Hinojosa's legal route and the ERCOT audit timeline. The next regular legislative session is probably January 2027 (an assumption, not stated in the sources).

Ohio: Acton's first moves on DeWine's suspension and the 2027 amendment push.

Georgia: Bottoms' first signals on large-load rules, and whether the Georgia Power PSC filings proceed.

Federal: Hearings from the new House oversight leadership.

Bottom line: Three states, three degrees of risk. Ohio shows the highest moratorium risk, Texas the largest dollar exposure, and Georgia the most room for a negotiated outcome. These are inferences from campaign positions and coverage, not forecasts.

news.Title: Venture Global Wants to Be an "AI Utility." Its 10-Gigawatt Plan Still Needs Customers.
news.Content:
Hyperscalers are spending staggering amounts on capital expenditures. In their rush to build data centers across the U.S., technology companies face a massive bottleneck that could limit the compute capacity they can bring online: electricity.

The demand for power is creating opportunities across the energy and industrial sectors for companies that can meet these needs and supply the fuel to run them. Venture Global (NYSE: VG), a top-tier exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG), is getting in on the action as the company looks to transform into a vertically integrated "AI utility."

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The company has laid out a plan to bring on 10 gigawatts (GW) of data center compute capacity over roughly the next decade through modular "power islands" and has framework agreements with equipment suppliers, but it has yet to sign a firm agreement with a major hyperscaler.

How Venture Global leverages its expertise to build "power islands" for hyperscalers

Venture Global exports U.S. shale gas globally and has taken a unique approach to its business. Traditionally, LNG exporters would build massive liquefaction trains to cool methane gas into LNG.

Building these liquefaction trains is a massive, capital-intensive undertaking, and Venture Global took a different approach with smaller, modular trains that can be prefabricated and shipped on-site. In addition, the Gulf Coast regional grid couldn't supply the electricity needed to freeze and liquefy methane, so Venture has or will soon have 4.5 GW of its own gas-fired power generation capacity.

This laid the foundation for Venture's "AI utility" pivot. Management realized data centers face similar requirements: multi-gigawatts of reliable baseload power and a power grid that cannot meet this capacity demand. By leveraging this expertise, Venture aims to bring on 10 GW of compute capacity through 16 combined-cycle "power islands" by 2034.

What makes this endeavor appealing for Venture is that it also controls the natural gas pipeline interconnects and related logistics, and can provide the power islands along with the natural gas fuel they require. The shale boom has also created a glut of natural gas , which Venture can turn around and sell to its data center customers at better margins -- if energy demand remains strong.

Story Continues

What's next for Venture Global?

Venture Global has secured framework agreements with GE Vernova for gas turbines and power equipment, and Baker Hughes for systems and controls, spanning 2028 to 2034. The company looks to convert its first reservation into a binding order by the end of this year, with power projected to first come online in 2028 to 2029.

Venture Global's pivot to an AI utility builds on its history of constructing massive power-generation facilities in its LNG business. Next, Venture Global needs to turn this into firm customer commitments from major hyperscalers, which could rewrite the investment thesis for the company. This gives Venture Global strong upside potential, but risks are also high as it invests heavily in building out these power islands.

news.Title: AMD's AI megadeals with OpenAI and Meta just cost it $1.1 billion: Chart of the Day
news.Content:
OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) and Meta ( META ) could buy 320 million AMD ( AMD ) shares for a penny apiece. That's $3.2 million for stock worth about $155 billion, and AMD just got its first bill for the deal.

The chipmaker beat Wall Street's estimates on Tuesday, with record data center sales of about $8.5 billion, nearly double a year ago, and a forecast of about $17 billion in fourth quarter revenue. The stock jumped as much as 9% in after-hours trading after closing at $484 before turning lower in premarket trading.

But tucked into the results was a $1.1 billion charge tied to that penny promise, which comes in the form of warrants — contracts that let the holder buy a company's stock at a set price. The charge came to $0.66 per share in the results. Last quarter, that line was zero.

Here's the deal: OpenAI and Meta each agreed to buy AMD chips for data centers drawing up to 6 gigawatts. That's about five DeLoreans' worth of the 1.21 gigawatts Doc Brown needed to time travel in the 1985 movie "Back to the Future."

In return, each can buy up to 160 million shares at a penny. The shares unlock as the chips ship, and the final batch requires AMD's stock to hit $600, according to company filings for OpenAI and Meta . Fully unlocked, the two would own about 16% of the enlarged company, by Yahoo Finance calculations. The Motley Fool ran the share-count math in October.

So why now? AMD began booking the warrants as it shipped its new MI450 chips, CFO Jean Hu said on Tuesday's call. The charge mostly reflected "the increase in our share price and the changes in the estimated probability of meeting the warrant conditions," she said. The stock rose about 21% last quarter and finished on Sept. 25 at $630, above that $600 line.

And the tab is likely to grow. Hu said she expects the charge "to increase as we and our customers progress under this agreement," with amounts swinging on AMD's stock price. Every rally and every chip shipment can add to it.

It's all on paper, though. The charges "will not affect our non-GAAP results or free cash flow ," Hu said.

AMD is stocking up for a $17 billion quarter

Meanwhile, AMD is loading up for what it expects to be its biggest quarter ever. Inventory jumped about $3 billion to a record $11.5 billion, four times the largest quarterly increase since at least 2009, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from company filings.

That build came at a price. Free cash flow shrank to about $550 million, compared with the nearly $2 billion analysts expected, according to Bloomberg. Debt more than doubled to about $7 billion after an August bond sale.

Story Continues

The warrants do come with a consolation prize for shareholders. The shares only unlock if OpenAI and Meta keep buying chips and the stock keeps climbing. AMD says the buying is just getting started.

"Based on our current visibility, we now expect revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027," CEO Lisa Su said on the call.

news.Title: SpaceX, Tesla slide as election risks mount, Morgan Stanley turns bullish
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Shares of SpaceX and Tesla fell Wednesday as Democrats' strong showing in the US midterm elections raised fresh questions about Elon Musk's political influence and the regulatory future of his sprawling business empire.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

SpaceX shares dropped about 5%, while Tesla declined 5.6%, as investors weighed the possibility of increased scrutiny of Musk's companies and complications for a potential combination of the rocket maker and electric-vehicle manufacturer.

The declines came despite a markedly more optimistic assessment of SpaceX from Morgan Stanley. Analyst Adam Jonas has sharply increased his financial forecasts for the company, arguing that its improving earnings outlook is not yet fully reflected in its valuation.

The election results present a new complication for Musk, who has closely aligned himself with President Donald Trump and reportedly contributed nearly $450 million to Republican political causes. Democrats' gains could strengthen their ability to scrutinize Musk's business activities, particularly as his companies expand into artificial intelligence and defense-related infrastructure.

SpaceX is especially exposed to Washington's decisions. The company generates billions of dollars from government contracts, while its Starlink satellite network has become strategically important in military and geopolitical affairs. Greater congressional scrutiny could also complicate the regulatory environment for its expanding AI operations.

Barclays analysts flagged potential implications for the AI infrastructure buildout in Texas, where SpaceX and Tesla have major operations. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on a moratorium on new data-center construction until the state legislature can establish additional requirements. Her proposed conditions include union labor, greater community input and transparency, protections for local water and electricity supplies, and requirements that data-center operators cover their own infrastructure costs rather than passing them on to taxpayers and households. The proposals could introduce another layer of uncertainty for companies planning large-scale computing investments in the state, particularly as demand for AI infrastructure accelerates.

Tesla faces a different but related risk. Its recent rally has been supported partly by investor enthusiasm for Musk's AI ambitions and speculation about a possible combination with SpaceX.

Story Continues

Tesla shares have climbed 34% since their late-July lows, helped by expectations surrounding autonomous driving, robotics and the prospect of bringing Musk's businesses closer together. A merger could combine Tesla's vehicle, robotics and AI operations with SpaceX's launch capabilities, satellite network and computing infrastructure.

But the transaction remains exploratory, and a more hostile political environment could make regulatory approval more difficult. Bloomberg has reported that there has been an effort to announce a deal in the first half of next year, potentially allowing it to close while Trump remains in office.

Even without the merger, the election outcome introduces another source of uncertainty for investors who have increasingly valued Musk's companies around expectations of future AI growth.

Morgan Stanley raises SpaceX forecasts

The political concerns stand in contrast to Morgan Stanley's increasingly bullish financial outlook for SpaceX.

In a research update, Jonas said the bank had nearly doubled its 2027 revenue and operating income estimates in less than four months since initiating coverage. It has also brought forward its forecast for free-cash-flow breakeven by four years and reduced its projected borrowing requirements by roughly $280 billion.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Morgan Stanley now expects SpaceX to generate $175 billion in revenue in 2027 and $289 billion in 2028, increases of 93% and 84%, respectively, from its previous forecasts. Its 2028 operating income estimate has risen 72% to $119 billion.

The bank now expects the company to turn free-cash-flow positive in 2031, compared with its previous forecast of 2035. Its estimate of cumulative external borrowing has fallen from $670 billion to approximately $390 billion.

Jonas pointed to growth across SpaceX's businesses, including satellite connectivity, launch services and artificial intelligence, as supporting the improved outlook.

He also identified the next Starship flight, expected this month, as a potentially important catalyst. SpaceX plans to attempt to catch both the spacecraft and its Super Heavy booster after launch, a major test of the company's ambitions to make the system fully reusable.

Musk has said the attempt is more likely than not to succeed, according to Jonas. A successful demonstration could improve the economics of launching satellites and expand the potential applications for Starship.

A valuation argument built around AI

Morgan Stanley's bullish case also rests on the argument that investors are undervaluing SpaceX's AI business.

At a share price of roughly $140 and a market capitalization of $1.91 trillion, Jonas calculates that SpaceX trades at 17.6 times projected 2028 adjusted earnings. That is slightly below the bank's 17.7 times estimate for the S&P 500.

Morgan Stanley forecasts earnings growth of roughly 150% annually between 2026 and 2030 and has set a $300 price target, implying potential upside of about 114% from the $140 reference price.

Jonas argues that investors are largely assigning value to SpaceX's space and connectivity businesses while giving relatively little credit to its AI operations. In his model, those established businesses account for approximately $123 of the share price, leaving just $17 attributable to AI.

That implies an unusually low valuation for the AI business relative to other infrastructure companies, in Morgan Stanley's view.

The contrast is becoming increasingly important for investors. SpaceX and Tesla are facing renewed political uncertainty just as expectations for their technological and financial ambitions continue to rise.

For now, the election-driven selloff suggests that political exposure remains a meaningful part of the valuation of Musk's companies, even as Wall Street's earnings forecasts for SpaceX move sharply higher.

news.Title: 川普期中考被當！謝金河提醒須重新評估AI未來：台股5萬恐等明年
news.Content:
美國期中選舉在今（4）日揭曉，民主黨奪得參、眾兩院勝利。對此，財信傳媒董事長謝金河晚間發文表示，「川普期中考被活當！世界重新找回方向」。同時，他還提到，德州變天，衝擊SpaceX創辦人馬斯克，因為美國總統川普是AI建置的推手，跛腳後會不會影響AI發展的未來？必須重新評估。

謝金河在臉書粉專發文表示，川普不服氣表示，此次失利是因為選票上沒有他的名字才會輸，但其實冰凍三尺非一日之寒，美國債券殖利率一直飆升，物價持續飛漲，人民的生活壓力越來越大，川普的敗選已在預料之中。

他進一步指出，資本市場從10月以來跌跌不休，先反映的是川普的可能敗選，共和黨失去參、眾兩院。另一個是龐大的Ai軍備競賽，四大CSP大廠今年資本支出7450億美元，造成沉重的自由現金流的大流出，Amazon的12個月自由現金流為負423.6億美元，把大家嚇出冷汗，並開始擔心龐大的AI支出，何時能轉化成強大的獲利？

謝金河還提到，市場也擔心民主黨掌控的很多州，都抵制資料中心及電力系統的建設，更擔心德州可能變天，結果共和黨失利，首當其衝的將是馬斯克。因為川普是AI建置的大推手，如今跛腳，會不會影響AI的未來？大家都必須重新評估。

另外在財報衝擊方面，他表示，除了Google，Amazon，這次令市場震驚的是Intel，公布財報當天股價大跌28.58%，台灣許多大型企業像台達電，國巨都受到波及，國巨這次跌到417元，比7月從1220元跌下來的「買到國巨，來生再聚」的低點更低。

謝金河還談到，大陸長鑫科技的4F²打趴記憶體股價，南韓的三星，海力士才剛從兩倍槓桿撞擊下挺過來，現在又挨了一記重擊，大陸的華虹，中芯國際，兆易創新都慘跌。台股這兩天也是風聲鶴唳，其實把全球巿場比對一下，印尼股市今年最慘，南韓接近腰斬，大陸的深圳股市跌幅逾三成，上海，香港大約跌兩成。

他最後認為，台股今年漲幅最大，這一次下跌8113點，跌幅16.24%，已算是全球表現最強勢的市場。接下來，全球將進行調整，鞏固整頓，尋找新方向，台股要挑戰5萬大關，可能要等到明年。

news.Title: AMD beats Q3 earnings expectations, with data center revenue climbing 97%
news.Content:
AMD ( AMD ) reported its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines, as the company's data center revenue grew 97%.

"Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production," CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years."

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 on revenue of $13.38 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $1.97 on revenue of $13.08 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.

AMD's Data Center arm generated sales of $8.5 billion, ahead of estimates of $8.19 billion. It reported revenue of $4.34 billion in the same period last year.

Last month, the company announced its Helion reference design, a server rack designed to be outfitted with various configurations of AMD's CPUs and GPUs based on customers' needs.

AMD's Client business revenue, which includes PC sales, hit $2.9 billion. Wall Street was looking for $3.06 billion.

The chipmaker's gaming business sales, however, came in at $773 million, down 40% year over year. Analysts were estimating revenue of $655 million.

The company's gaming division includes products ranging from PC graphics cards to custom silicon for game consoles. Both categories are facing higher prices due to the ongoing memory and storage shortage, depressing customer demand.

AMD's report comes after rival Intel reported better-than-anticipated Q3 results , but issued guidance well below analysts' projections last week. The news sent Intel stock plummeting nearly 29% .

The company blamed the outlook on a worse-than-anticipated decline in the PC market.

The industry is contending with two overlapping factors: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.

news.Title: GlobalFoundries Inc. (GFS) Q3 Earnings and Revenues Beat Estimates
news.Content:
GlobalFoundries Inc. (GFS) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.53 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.51 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.41 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +3.92%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this company would post earnings of $0.44 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.46, delivering a surprise of +4.55%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

GlobalFoundries, which belongs to the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, posted revenues of $1.9 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.63%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.69 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

GlobalFoundries shares have added about 22.8% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 10.6%.

What's Next for GlobalFoundries?

While GlobalFoundries has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for GlobalFoundries was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.58 on $2.01 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $1.96 on $7.32 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

news.Title: Tech Sell-Off: 2 Growth Stocks Investors Might Regret Not Buying on the Dip
news.Content:
After almost tripling from its 2022 bear market low point, the technology-heavy Nasdaq-100 index is now facing a big test. Investors are increasingly concerned about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) spending boom, placing pressure on semiconductor stocks like Nvidia and Micron Technology , which are among the largest members of the index.

As a result, the Nasdaq-100 was down 9% from its peak as of the market close last Friday, and the decline could get worse if investor sentiment doesn't improve. However, history suggests this could be a great buying opportunity for investors, because the broader market has always recovered to new highs over the long term.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

I'm going to share two stocks investors might regret not buying when they look back on this moment in a few years' time.

1. Zscaler: Demand for cybersecurity will only grow from here

Hackers have started using AI to stage highly sophisticated cyber attacks on corporate networks, but enterprises are also placing themselves at risk by exposing their valuable data to third-party AI models without the appropriate guardrails. Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) was one of the early pioneers of the zero trust cybersecurity architecture, which has become one of the best defenses in the AI era.

Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange protects the entire enterprise, starting with the identity layer. It treats every network login attempt as hostile, analyzing the user's credentials, their location, and the device they are using, which maximizes the odds of catching an imposter. Further, the Zero Trust Exchange only allows users to access the applications they need to do their jobs, so even if a hacker bypasses the identity layer, they won't have unrestricted access to the entire network.

Zscaler introduced new tools to the Exchange earlier this year, which protect enterprises when they are deploying AI. There is AI Broker, which constantly monitors communications between AI agents, and Endpoint AI Security, which protects the computers and devices employees are using to run AI software.

Zscaler believes a "Zero Trust Everywhere" approach is the best way to protect against AI threats. Hackers can't attack what they can't see, so keeping critical data, applications, and agents hidden behind the Exchange is the ultimate form of preventative security.

Story Continues

Zscaler had a record year in fiscal 2026 (ended July 31), with revenue growing by 25% to $3.35 billion. Its stock is trading at a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 11.3, so it's already cheaper than competitors like CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks . Therefore, if a further sell-off in the broader market drags Zscaler stock down with it, investors might be presented with a fantastic long-term buying opportunity.

CRWD PS Ratio data by YCharts

2. Meta Platforms: AI is expanding the social media giant's addressable market

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) is the parent company of the Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads social media platforms. Over 3.6 billion people use at least one of them every single day, and considering that is almost half the world's population, it's getting harder for the company to find new signups. As a result, it's trying to lift engagement instead -- if each user spends more time online, they will see more advertisements, and Meta will make more money.

AI is a big part of that strategy. It's embedded in the recommendation algorithms on Facebook and Instagram, where it learns what types of content each user likes to see, and feeds them more of it. According to Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg, engagement hit record highs on those apps during the third quarter (ended Sept. 30), so the AI-led strategy appears to be working.

However, there is an even bigger opportunity in the pipeline, and it transcends social media. Meta launched a personal AI agent called Muse in September, and it has already attracted over 10 million users. Zuckerberg recently said one-quarter of them are using it as a personal shopper, with an average purchase value of $200, while others are using it to manage emails, among other things.

Zuckerberg believes Muse could eventually serve billions of people, and it will be capable of improving every area of their lives, whether they want to learn new skills or automate some of life's everyday tasks. This will substantially increase Meta's addressable market, because it could replace the need for traditional internet search engines like Alphabet 's Google Search.

Meta stock is down 20% from its peak amid the recent tech sell-off. It's now trading at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 20.9, so it's much cheaper than the Nasdaq-100 which has a P/E of 29.9. Therefore, this already looks like a good buying opportunity for long-term investors.

news.Title: Bull of the Day: Texas Instruments (TXN)
news.Content:
While the leading-edge, high-performance semiconductors powering the AI boom have garnered most of the attention in recent years, some of the less flashy analog and embedded chips are also playing a critical role in the expansion of advanced technologies and infrastructure.

Texas Instruments TXN, the world's largest analog semiconductor manufacturer, has been enjoying accelerating fundamental growth, significant earnings upgrades and increasingly bullish stock price momentum.

After sitting out much of the AI boom, TXN had been weighed down by cyclical headwinds as its automotive and industrial customers worked through large inventories accumulated following the pandemic. However, the stock emerged from that slump earlier this year, and the bullish catalysts continue to mount.

Furthermore, amid a particularly volatile stretch for large segments of the semiconductor industry, Texas Instruments and several other major analog chipmakers have demonstrated notable relative strength. Although there have certainly been bumps along the way, these stocks have generally held up well during recent bouts of selling in former market leaders.

Below, we'll review the emerging opportunities for Texas Instruments, its improving earnings outlook and the valuation picture.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Emerging Opportunities for Texas Instrument

Texas Instruments is positioned to benefit from several powerful trends, including industrial automation, automotive electrification, expanding data center infrastructure and the broader recovery in semiconductor demand.

Unlike the advanced processors developed by Nvidia and other AI leaders, analog semiconductors perform essential functions such as managing power, converting signals and interfacing with real-world systems.

These chips are required across virtually every modern electronic system, and their importance only increases as devices and infrastructure become more sophisticated.

The automotive industry offers a clear example as the average number of semiconductors per vehicle doubled between 2017 and 2021, reaching roughly 1,700, with demand continuing to rise as electrification, advanced safety systems and autonomous driving features become more widespread

The expansion of AI data centers of course is interesting as well. While GPUs capture the headlines, these facilities also require enormous amounts of power management, monitoring and supporting electronics, creating additional demand for analog components.

Meanwhile, the company's industrial and automotive markets are recovering from a prolonged inventory correction, providing a more cyclical source of growth.

Story Continues

Texas Instruments also enjoys a structural manufacturing advantage through its investments in 300mm wafer fabrication, which can reduce production costs substantially compared with traditional 200mm manufacturing.

The company recently began production at its newest fab in Sherman, Texas, part of a broader $60 billion US manufacturing expansion spanning seven facilities in Texas and Utah. With additional capacity coming online, TXN is positioning itself to capture rising demand while benefiting from greater economies of scale and tighter control over its supply chain.

TXN Stock Jumps on Earnings Beat and Upgrades

Texas Instruments' latest quarterly results offered compelling evidence that the recovery continues to gain momentum.

Third quarter revenue increased 28% year over year to $6.06 billion, while earnings per share surged 77% to $2.62. Operating profit climbed an impressive 73%, highlighting the substantial operating leverage in the business.

Importantly, the strength was broad-based, with management reporting continued growth across industrial, automotive and data center markets. The company's analog segment was particularly strong, generating 32% revenue growth, while embedded processing revenue increased 21%.

Over the last 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for current year earnings has increased 5.6% to $8.89 per share, while next year estimates have jumped 13% to $11.12. These developments have contributed to a powerful trend in analyst earnings upgrades, earning TXN a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Even more encouraging, revisions have been overwhelmingly positive, with no downward adjustments among the revisions recorded across the current and next fiscal years.

That combination of accelerating earnings growth and consistently rising estimates is precisely what we look for when identifying stocks with the potential to outperform.

Shares of TXN Trade Near Historical Average

Despite its impressive rally this year, Texas Instruments' valuation is becoming more reasonable as earnings expectations catch up with the stock price.

TXN currently trades around 34x forward earnings, a premium to the broader market and respective industry, though one that should be considered in the context of its accelerating profit growth, strong market position and cash generating capabilities.

The company generated $7.4 billion in free cash flow over the trailing 12 months.

Although the stock is hardly a bargain on conventional valuation measures, the sharp increase in forward earnings estimates has helped moderate its valuation even as shares have advanced.

Should Investors Buy Shares of TXN?

Texas Instruments offers investors exposure to several important secular growth themes without relying exclusively on the more speculative corners of the AI trade.

The combination of recovering industrial demand, expanding data center opportunities, improving margins and powerful earnings revisions makes for an increasingly compelling fundamental picture.

Of course, the cyclical nature of the semiconductor industry and the stock's premium valuation remain important risks. That said, most evidence points to an early stage of cyclical recovery.

Nevertheless, with earnings momentum accelerating and shares demonstrating impressive relative strength, TXN looks well positioned to continue outperforming in the months ahead.

news.Title: Is Google's New Cryptocurrency Service a Reason to Buy Ethereum or Solana?
news.Content:
There will soon be a new crypto security service offered by Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL), and it could well provide a mild boost for Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL). Google's new cryptocurrency platform, which it calls Google Multi-Party Compute (MPC), was announced on Oct. 28, and Alphabet is already using it to secure its own digital assets parked on both of those blockchains. MPC's commercial launch is scheduled for early 2027.

Google argues its relationships with traditional financial institutions will give it an edge in providing cybersecure crypto custody, but how that will help Solana and Ethereum is another matter. Let's analyze the situation.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Google is aiming to help financial institutions get confident in holding crypto

MPC is only Alphabet's latest bid to compete more in cryptocurrency.

Google now also runs its own blockchain, the Google Cloud Universal Ledger (GCUL), which Google unveiled in 2025, and which is also aimed at financial institutions and other approved participants.

The technical basis for the new service is splitting a crypto wallet's private key, the secret code that confers control of the wallet, into fragments that are then held on separate computer systems. This makes it much more difficult for an attacker to assemble a complete private key and proceed with the subsequent theft of funds. Google's tool is also supposed to check each incoming transaction against a list of a financial institution's rules, like spending and transfer limits, before allowing the transaction to proceed.

The fit between this product and its target market is already pretty plainly obvious: In a 2026 survey by American Banker, 47% of the surveyed financial institutions cited cybersecurity as a top barrier to their adoption of blockchain tech . That issue is particularly salient at the moment. On Oct. 29, the largest crypto exchange, Binance, was hacked, and the cyberthieves made off with $6.3 billion.

Google plans to support two different transaction signing methods that institutions can use at launch.

One is the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA), which Ethereum uses and which is very widely used elsewhere, and the other is Ed25519, which Solana and many other networks use. Importantly, ECDSA also secures Bitcoin , and the ledger behind XRP , so the company's approach doesn't favor any specific chain.

Story Continues

Should you buy these coins because of Google's new service?

The bullish factor here for Solana and Ethereum is that Alphabet already uses the platform to secure some of its own digital assets on both chains. It's a minor boost at best.

Offering safer storage to institutions won't make anyone want these coins who does not want them already. Big investors already have custodied access through crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs) , and demand there is both volatile and frequently soft. In the first seven trading days of October 2026, Ethereum ETFs experienced $635 million in net outflows, while Solana ETFs saw $24.8 million in net outflows.

Furthermore, coinholders gain mainly from new net buying and new network usage. Parked coins in long-term storage are rarely used for transactions, adding little to the network activity backing what makes these cryptocurrencies valuable.

Google's GCUL network will be competing for capital and activity, too. Google is pitching the GCUL as a "credibly neutral" permissioned network that any bank can use for payments and asset tokenization, or transforming the ownership rights of stocks and bonds into tradeable crypto. Every bank that chooses to do its work there is business that Ethereum and Solana don't win, and assets they don't get to have parked on their networks.

Therefore, investors should treat this service launch as a small positive, and as a confidence-building step that could eventually lead to some more institutional capital heading to crypto.

In the first half of 2027, watch both coins' ETF flows, and watch for bank announcements of crypto operations naming Google's service as a collaborator. If net ETF inflows return right as banks are signing on, it means that the asset custody story is giving way to new demand, and the situation will be more bullish than it is now.

news.Title: 5 Value Stocks to Buy as AI Volatility Reshapes the Market
news.Content:
The U.S. market has entered November with renewed volatility, as investors question whether the massive spending on artificial intelligence will ultimately produce meaningful revenues and profits. Persistent inflation and elevated long-term yields have also made borrowing more expensive, forcing investors to reassess the valuations of high-growth companies. The Democrats' midterm sweep adds fresh policy uncertainty. Meanwhile, oil prices and tensions in the Middle East could stoke inflation fears and market sentiment.

In this environment, value investing offers a prudent approach. It focuses on businesses with tangible earnings, reasonable valuations and resilient cash flows rather than speculative narratives.  Buying strong businesses at prices below what they are actually worth builds in a cushion, which can help a portfolio hold up when markets swing.

Cenovus Energy Inc. CVE, Micron Technology MU, Sandisk Corporation SNDK, Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE and Honda Motor HMC are a few value stocks with high earnings yield.

Using the Earnings Yield Metric

Earnings yield is an interesting ratio that you can consider for picking attractively valued stocks. This metric, expressed in percentage, is calculated as annual earnings per share (EPS) divided by market price. It measures the anticipated return from earnings for each dollar invested in a stock today. When comparing stocks, if other factors are similar, the ones with a higher earnings yield are considered undervalued, while those with a lower earnings yield are seen as overpriced.

While earnings yield is nothing but the reciprocal of the P/E ratio, it also facilitates the comparison of stocks with fixed-income securities. Investors often compare the earnings yield of a stock to the prevailing interest rates, such as the current 10-year Treasury yield, to get a sense of the return on investment it offers compared to virtually risk-free returns.

If the yield on a stock is lower than the 10-year Treasury yield, it would be considered overvalued relative to bonds. Conversely, if the yield on the stock is higher, it would be considered undervalued.

Setting the Right Filters

We have set an Earnings Yield greater than 10% as our primary screening criterion but it alone cannot be used for picking stocks that have the potential to generate solid returns. So, we have added the following parameters to the screen:

Estimated EPS growth for the next 12 months greater than or equal to the S&P 500 : This metric compares the 12-month forward EPS estimate with the 12-month actual EPS.
