news.Title: MPWR's AI Power Boom Accelerates as Enterprise Data Sales Surge 164.6%
news.Content:
Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. MPWR is becoming increasingly tied to the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure. Third-quarter 2026 Enterprise Data revenues surged 164.6% year over year as demand for AI and server power solutions accelerated.

That growth is reshaping MPWR's revenue mix and supporting operating leverage. It also raises a key question for investors: how durable can the current AI-driven expansion remain as Enterprise Data becomes a larger share of the business?

MPWR's Enterprise Data Growth Reshapes the Mix

Enterprise Data generated $506.7 million in third-quarter revenues, up 33.2% sequentially and 164.6% year over year. The segment accounted for 42.1% of total revenues, compared with 38.8% in the second quarter.

Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. Price and Consensus

Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. Quote

The shift makes AI and server power applications materially more important to MPWR's growth profile. Total third-quarter revenues rose 63.1% year over year to $1.20 billion, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded 320 basis points to 38.6% as sales grew faster than operating expenses.

AI Power Modules Drive MPWR's Revenue Surge

Higher-value power modules, increased power content per computing platform and broader customer engagement are supporting Enterprise Data growth. Management has cited rapid expansion among application-specific integrated circuit customers, which are increasingly using modules as power requirements rise.

Management raised its 2026 Enterprise Data revenue growth floor to 150% from 130%. It also expects strong demand across existing customers to continue into 2027, while customer diversification and additional content gains provide more routes for expansion.

MPWR Adds Capacity for the Next Demand Wave

MPWR surpassed $6 billion in annual revenue-supporting capacity during the third quarter and is targeting $8 billion by the second half of 2027. Its fabless model and broader front-end and back-end supplier network can help expand output without requiring a comparable increase in capital intensity. A long-term manufacturing agreement with GlobalFoundries is another part of that expansion.

Volume production at GlobalFoundries' advanced 300mm facility in Singapore is expected to begin in early 2027 and support power solutions for AI and cloud infrastructure, automotive systems and industrial robotics.

Concentration Raises MPWR's Data-Center Risk

Enterprise Data's 42.1% share of third-quarter revenues increases MPWR's sensitivity to AI infrastructure spending cycles. Management has not provided a 2027 growth rate for the segment, so the pace of expansion beyond the current year remains an execution variable even as demand indicators stay favorable.

The broader analog semiconductor market also remains competitive. Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN reported continued growth in data center, industrial and automotive markets in the third quarter of 2026. Analog Devices, Inc. ADI said Data Center and Industrial led its fiscal third-quarter year-over-year revenue growth. MPWR must sustain its design wins and content gains while managing manufacturing costs and inventory.

Story Continues

MPWR's Strong Signal Comes With Mixed Style Scores

The near-term earnings signal remains favorable. MPWR currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), a rating driven by positive earnings estimate revisions over the one- to three-month horizon.That signal is less uniform across the Zacks Style Scores. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

MPWR has a Value Score of F, Growth Score of D, Momentum Score of C and VGM Score of F. news.Title: ON Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong AI Data Center Aids Top Line
news.Content:
ON Semiconductor ON, popularly known as onsemi, reported third-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of 90 cents per share, up 42.9% year over year and beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.27%. Stronger demand, favorable product mix and improved manufacturing performance supported bottom-line growth.

Revenues increased 11.1% year over year to $1.722 billion, surpassing the consensus mark of $1.706 billion by 0.94%. AI data center revenues surged 39% sequentially, while improving industrial demand and disciplined execution supported the top line.

ON's Power Solutions Group Leads Revenue Growth

Power Solutions Group revenues reached $889.9 million, increasing 21% year over year and 7% sequentially. Strengthening demand for differentiated power technologies supported growth across AI data center and industrial applications.

ON Semiconductor Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

ON Semiconductor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | ON Semiconductor Corporation Quote

Analog and Mixed Signal Group revenues increased 2% year over year and 9% sequentially to $597.3 million. Intelligent Sensing Group revenues rose 2% year over year and 3% sequentially to $235.1 million.

ON's AI Data Center Momentum Accelerates

AI data center revenues reached $180 million, surging 175% year over year. The company now expects approximately $620 million in AI data center revenues for 2026, representing 140% growth, and anticipates another doubling in 2027.

New platform ramps, including shipments to Google, are expanding ON's presence across power supply units and voltage-conversion applications. The transition toward 800-volt data center architectures creates additional opportunities for silicon carbide, silicon MOSFETs and vertical gallium nitride technologies.

The announced acquisition of Ferric for $600 million, plus potential milestone payments of up to $175 million, strengthens onsemi's integrated voltage regulator capabilities. The transaction prompted management to raise its 2030 AI data center revenue target by $500 million to more than $3 billion.

ON's Automotive Business Faces Supply Constraints

Automotive revenues totaled $777 million, declining 1% both sequentially and year over year. The sequential weakness reflected temporary supply reallocation toward faster-growing AI data center and industrial markets rather than deterioration in underlying automotive demand.

ON continues expanding its automotive content through traction inverter, onboard charger and zonal architecture wins. New silicon carbide traction inverter designs at NIO and Geely Zeekr support its position in China's high-voltage electric vehicle market.

Management expects automotive revenues to decline by a high-single-digit percentage sequentially in the fourth quarter. Supply availability should normalize in early 2027, supporting a return to the company's long-term automotive growth trajectory.

Story Continues

ON's Industrial Business Benefits From Energy Demand

Industrial revenues increased 9% year over year and 10% sequentially to $467 million. Strength in energy infrastructure, factory automation and broader industrial applications drove the improvement.

Growing electricity requirements associated with AI infrastructure are supporting demand for grid modernization and energy storage solutions. The company also expanded hybrid EliteSiC and IGBT module wins with customers including Sungrow and Sineng.

ON expects industrial revenues to increase by a low-double-digit percentage sequentially in the fourth quarter, reflecting continued demand momentum across these applications.

ON Expands Margins Through Mix and Utilization

Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 320 basis points year over year and 190 basis points sequentially to 41.2%. Favorable product mix and manufacturing improvements supported the fifth consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion.

Non-GAAP operating expenses reached $309.5 million compared with $296.8 million in the preceding quarter. Non-GAAP operating margin improved to 23.2% from 19.2% a year earlier and 20.8% sequentially.

Manufacturing utilization remained at 83%. Management expects higher utilization, differentiated product ramps and manufacturing footprint optimization under its Fab Right initiative to support further margin expansion.

onsemi Generates Strong Cash Flow

Cash from operations reached $516.4 million, increasing 23.3% year over year. Free cash flow rose 31% to approximately $489 million, representing 28% of revenues.

Cash and short-term investments totaled approximately $4.4 billion at quarter-end. Total liquidity stood at $5.9 billion, including $1.5 billion available under the revolving credit facility.

Capital expenditures were $27.8 million, while share repurchases totaled approximately $20 million. Management intends to prioritize debt reduction following the planned Synaptics acquisition.

ON's Q4 Outlook Signals Further Earnings Growth

For the fourth quarter of 2026, ON expects revenues between $1.715 billion and $1.815 billion. The $1.765 billion midpoint implies approximately 2.5% sequential growth.

Non-GAAP gross margin is projected between 41.5% and 43.5%, while non-GAAP operating expenses are expected between $303 million and $318 million.

Non-GAAP earnings are forecast between 95 cents and $1.07 per share. Capital expenditures are projected between $40 million and $50 million.

Management anticipates continued revenue growth and margin expansion into 2027, supported by higher manufacturing utilization, new product ramps and improving demand across key markets.

Zacks Rank & Upcoming Earnings to Watch For

Currently, ON carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Forgent Power, Telos and NVIDIA are expected to report their quarterly results on Nov. 12, 9 and 17, respectively. Forgent Power shares have dropped 15.3% year to date (YTD). Telos shares have inched up 2.2% YTD, while NVIDIA shares have climbed 8.4% YTD.

news.Title: Why Amazon Stock Can Keep Rising Through 2035
news.Content:
Most of the attention on Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) goes to its cloud business, Amazon Web Services (AWS). But the company's online stores are quietly becoming more profitable, thanks to automation and robotics. That's a big reason the stock can keep rising through 2035.

On the third-quarter earnings call, CEO Andy Jassy said, "There has never been a business with a trillion dollars of annual revenue. Amazon is on a path to have two of them in AWS and stores." He added that some folks are "sleeping a bit" on how much progress the retail business has made.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Amazon's robots are making every package cheaper to ship

That progress shows up in profit margins. Jassy said Amazon's North America and International segments have each expanded operating margins by nearly 10 percentage points over the past few years. The company is also on track to lower its cost to serve each unit, or deliver each item, for a fourth straight year.

Robotics is a big driver. Amazon has more than 1 million robots in its fulfillment network, and its newest facilities, including same-day delivery sites, are "very heavy on robotics." In the third quarter, shipping costs, excluding fuel and long-haul inflation, grew about four percentage points slower than units shipped. Jassy said the economic impact on its business so far is "small compared to what it is going to be in the next five years."

Amazon's cash flow multiple is the lowest since 2008

Lower costs on a sales base this large, with Amazon's online store generating $286 billion in annual revenue, can free up a lot more cash. Over the past 12 months, operating cash flow , the cash the business brings in before investments, grew 29% year over year to $168 billion. It has compounded about 25% a year over the past five years, and with Amazon's automation push still early, that cash flow has room to keep growing for years. And over time, Amazon's stock price tends to follow cash flow.

Yet the stock trades at about 16 times operating cash flow, based on the Oct. 29 close. That's near the lowest multiple Amazon stock has traded since the 2008 bear market -- a discount for a business whose cash flow is still growing rapidly and has room to expand.

The risk: A $220 billion spending bill

The risk is heavy spending. Amazon expects capital expenditures of about $220 billion in 2026, mostly for Amazon Web Services, and management expects to spend "meaningfully more" in 2027. High capital spending has pushed free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures) negative over the past year.

Story Continues

If those investments don't earn strong returns, free cash flow could stay low and weigh on the stock. Still, with retail becoming a second profit engine and the stock trading at a discount, Amazon shares could deliver excellent returns over the next 10 years.

news.Title: AMD to report Q3 results as chip stocks rebound following last week's steep selloff
news.Content:
AMD ( AMD ) will announce its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, as chip stocks stage a comeback after steep declines following Intel's ( INTC ) disappointing earnings last week.

AMD stock rose more than 4% in early trading on Tuesday.

While Intel reported better-than-anticipated Q3 results , it provided Q4 revenue estimates of between $15 billion and $16 billion, well below analysts' projections of $17 billion.

The news sent Intel stock plummeting nearly 29% .

The company blamed the outlook on a worse-than-anticipated decline in the PC market.

The industry is contending with two overlapping factors: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.

While AMD generates the majority of its revenue via data center sales, a drop in PC demand would still hurt its bottom line.

For the third quarter, analysts anticipate AMD to report earnings per share of $1.97 on revenue of $13 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates. The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.

AMD's Data Center arm is expected to see sales of $8.19 billion, an 88% increase from the $4.34 billion it reported last year.

Last month, the company announced its Helion reference design, a server rack designed to be outfitted with various configurations of AMD's CPUs and GPUs based on customers' needs.

The company's Client business revenue, which includes PC sales, is set to top $3.06 billion, up 11% year over year, but flat sequentially.

AMD's gaming business, however, could take a major hit, with Wall Street predicting a 49% revenue decline to $655 million.

The company's gaming division includes products ranging from PC graphics cards to custom silicon for game consoles. Both categories are facing higher prices due to the ongoing memory and storage shortage, depressing customer demand.

news.Title: FN Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Data Center Demand Aids Revenues
news.Content:
Fabrinet FN reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $4.34 per share, up 48.6% year over year. The figure surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.58%.

Revenues surged 50.7% year over year to $1.47 billion, beating the consensus mark by 5%. Results benefited from broad-based demand across data center, communications infrastructure and industrial markets. Data center revenues jumped 78% year over year to $777 million, driven by strong demand for transceivers, data center interconnect and high-performance computing products.

Fabrinet Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Fabrinet price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Fabrinet Quote

FN's Data Center Revenues Drive Robust Growth

Data center revenues increased 16% sequentially and accounted for approximately 53% of total revenues. Growth was supported by continued momentum in data center interconnect, expanding transceiver demand and high-performance computing applications.

FN highlighted increasing customer demand and improving visibility across the data center market. New hyperscale-direct and merchant transceiver programs are beginning to ramp, providing additional growth opportunities alongside existing customer engagements.

Fabrinet's Communications and Industrial Sales Rise

Communications infrastructure revenues climbed 35% year over year to $444 million, reflecting broad-based strength across telecom systems, optical components and satellite communications. Revenues increased 8% sequentially.

Automotive, industrial and other revenues advanced 20% year over year to $253 million, increasing 8% from the preceding quarter. Industrial lasers contributed the most to sequential growth as Fabrinet expanded relationships with customers that previously relied on in-house manufacturing.

FN's Margins Reflect FX and Compensation Pressures

Non-GAAP gross margin contracted 20 basis points (bps) year over year to 12.1%, primarily due to foreign exchange headwinds. Sequentially, gross margin declined 10 bps, reflecting annual employee merit increases.

Non-GAAP operating expenses represented 1.3% of revenues, unchanged sequentially.

Operating margin expanded 20 bps year over year to 10.8%, benefiting from disciplined spending and operating leverage, despite gross margin pressure.

Fabrinet Expands Manufacturing Capacity to Meet Demand

Fabrinet continued expanding its manufacturing footprint to support existing programs and new customer opportunities. The company completed the acquisition of a second Santa Clara campus for $77 million, more than doubling its Silicon Valley capacity.

In Thailand, Building 10 at the Chonburi campus is expected to be completed in January 2027. The facility will add approximately 2 million square feet and $3.5 billion in annual revenue capacity. Initial production revenues have already commenced.

Fabrinet expects total annual revenue capacity to reach approximately $10 billion in January compared with $5.8 billion at the end of fiscal 2026. Construction of Building 11 is scheduled to begin in January, adding approximately 1.5 million square feet and $3 billion in incremental annual revenue capacity when completed around the end of fiscal 2028.

Story Continues

FN's Cash Flow Reflects Elevated Capital Investments

Fabrinet ended the quarter with approximately $755.75 million in cash and short-term investments, compared with $875.06 million at the end of the preceding quarter.

Operating cash flow totaled $21.29 million, down from $102.57 million in the year-ago quarter. Capital expenditures increased to $158.70 million from $45.27 million, reflecting manufacturing expansion and the Santa Clara acquisition.

Free cash outflow totaled $137.41 million, compared with positive free cash flow of $57.30 million a year earlier.

Fabrinet repurchased approximately 77,000 shares for $29 million during the quarter. The board subsequently authorized an additional $103 million for repurchases, bringing the remaining authorization to approximately $200 million.

Fabrinet's Q2 Outlook Signals Sustained Growth

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Fabrinet expects revenues between $1.6 billion and $1.65 billion, implying approximately 43% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.

Non-GAAP earnings are projected between $4.77 and $4.92 per share.

The company anticipates continued growth across all three major revenue categories, led by data center interconnect and transceiver programs. New optical circuit switching and multi-rail opportunities are beginning to contribute, while near-packaged and co-packaged optics programs are expected to generate revenues later in fiscal 2027.

Operating margins are expected to improve with increasing scale and operating efficiencies. However, tight component availability and spending on additional manufacturing capacity remain important considerations as Fabrinet supports accelerating customer demand.

Zacks Rank & Upcoming Earnings to Watch For

Currently, Fabrinet carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

news.Title: Dear Qualcomm Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 4
news.Content:
Qualcomm (QCOM) is navigating an increasingly complicated semiconductor landscape, one that looks markedly different from the environment that fueled its earlier growth. While smartphones remain a cornerstone of its business, changing industry conditions, escalating component costs, and Apple (AAPL) efforts to develop its own modem technology are introducing fresh uncertainties into the company's growth outlook.

These headwinds have also taken a toll on Qualcomm's shares. On Friday, Oct. 30, QCOM stock tumbled 11.2% after Intel's earnings triggered sectorwide concerns about memory shortages and slowed consumer spending in the PC market. Last month was particularly rough, as QCOM was caught up in a technology-led selloff, as inflation concerns, rising Treasury yields, and a broader shift toward risk aversion rattled investors.

More News from Barchart

Ford and GM Are Taking Different Roads, but 1 Stock Races Ahead

This Data Center and Storage Stock Just Raised Its Dividend by Nearly 17%

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

The pressure is not limited to demand, though. Rising memory prices and supply constraints, partly fueled by the growing appetite for components from artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, are increasing smartphone manufacturing costs. This could complicate production schedules and further strain consumer demand, particularly among price-sensitive Android OEMs.

However, there is another side to Qualcomm's business. Its growing automotive, Internet of Things (IoT), data-center computing, and AI infrastructure operations are opening up opportunities beyond smartphones.

So, when the company publishes its Q4 and FY2026 results on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after the market closes, it will offer a fresh look at how these businesses are developing alongside its established operations.

About Qualcomm Stock

Qualcomm develops and commercializes wireless technologies across global markets, with a diversified portfolio spanning semiconductor solutions, intellectual property licensing, and strategic investments. Beyond its core technology operations, the company also delivers network security, government services, and data center solutions, supporting its roughly $176 billion valuation.

Qualcomm's recent price performance has been less encouraging. Shares of the San Diego, California-based tech giant have fallen 9% over the past 52 weeks. The decline has continued into 2026, with the stock down 4% year-to-date (YTD), while in the past month alone, shares have plunged 11%.

Story Continues

From a valuation perspective, QCOM stock is currently trading at 15.66 times forward adjusted earnings, below the industry average. The discount points to Qualcomm's relatively modest valuation compared with its peers, despite the challenges affecting its recent performance.

The company has also increased its dividend for 22 consecutive years and currently distributes an annual dividend of $3.68 per share, representing a yield of 2.23%. Most recently, on Wednesday, Oct. 21, Qualcomm announced a quarterly cash dividend of $0.92 per common share. The payment is scheduled for Thursday, Dec. 17, to stockholders of record at the close of business on Thursday, Dec. 3.

A Closer Look at Q3 Earnings

On July 29, Qualcomm reported mixed financial results for Q3 FY2026. Revenue came in at $9.95 billion, down 4% year-over-year (YoY), but ahead of the Street's estimate of $9.66 billion. Non-GAAP EPS, meanwhile, declined 20.2% YoY to $2.21, narrowly missing analysts' expectations of $2.22.

Although revenue reached the upper end of management's guidance, earnings highlighted the mounting pressure from softer handset demand, more expensive memory components, and elevated manufacturing costs. The biggest weakness came from Qualcomm CDMA Technologies (QCT), where revenue declined 5.4% YoY to $8.5 billion.

Within this segment, Handset revenue dropped 19.6% YoY to $5.09 billion, reflecting an industry contraction compounded by memory-related supply constraints and rising component expenses. However, Qualcomm's diversification efforts offered some welcome relief.

Automotive revenue jumped 61.4% from the year-ago value to $1.59 billion, while IoT revenue increased 8.9% from the last year's quarter to $1.83 billion. These gains underscore the growing contribution of businesses outside the traditional smartphone market.

Profitability, however, remained under pressure. Non-GAAP operating income declined 22.4% YoY to $2.8 billion, while non-GAAP net income dipped 22.5% from the prior year's period to $2.4 billion. Looking ahead, management expects Q4 FY2026 revenue to land between $9.7 billion and $10.5 billion, with non-GAAP EPS projected at $2.05–$2.25.

Analysts, however, are taking a more cautious view of the near-term earnings trajectory. Estimates call for Q4 FY2026 EPS to decrease 43% YoY to $1.46. For full FY2026, analysts project EPS to plunge 23.4% from the previous year to $7.71, followed by another 7% decline to $7.17.

What Do Analysts Expect for QCOM Stock?

Despite the recent share-price weakness and near-term earnings concerns, Wall Street's overall assessment of Qualcomm remains relatively constructive. Analysts covering the stock have assigned it an overall rating of "Moderate Buy."

Of the 34 analysts following QCOM stock, 10 recommend a "Strong Buy," while two maintain a "Moderate Buy" rating. Another 18 recommend "Hold" on QCOM. On the more cautious end, one analyst has issued a "Moderate Sell" rating, while three have assigned a "Strong Sell."

To that end, the average price target stands at $199.38, implying potential upside of 23%. Meanwhile, the Street-high target of $400 points to a potential gain of 147% from current levels.

news.Title: Apple Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates, iPhone Drives Top-Line Growth
news.Content:
Apple AAPL reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings of $2.10 per share, up 13.5% year over year. Excluding a 5-cent benefit from tariff refunds, earnings were $2.05 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.5%.

Net sales increased 11.7% year over year to $114.48 billion, surpassing the consensus mark by 1.3%. The results reflected strong iPhone and Mac demand, alongside record Services revenues. Apple's installed base exceeded 2.5 billion active devices, reaching an all-time high across major product categories and geographic segments.

Apple Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Apple Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Apple Inc. Quote

AAPL's iPhone and Mac Revenues Drive Growth

Product sales increased 12.5% year over year to $82.90 billion and accounted for 72.4% of total revenues. iPhone remained the primary growth driver, with sales rising 17.5% year over year to $57.58 billion, setting a September-quarter record despite supply constraints and foreign exchange headwinds.

Mac revenues surged 23.7% year over year to $10.79 billion, driven by MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro. Apple achieved a September-quarter record for customers new to Mac. Management highlighted strong emerging-market performance, with all-time revenue records in India and Southeast Asia.

Apple's Services Reach New Revenue High

Services revenues advanced 9.8% year over year to an all-time record of $31.57 billion. The business represented 27.6% of total sales, supported by strong performance across video, cloud services, payment services and advertising.

Paid subscriptions exceeded 1.5 billion, growing double digits during the quarter. Transacting and paid accounts also reached record highs. However, foreign exchange headwinds, mobile gaming weakness and App Store business model changes in certain markets remained challenges.

AAPL's Other Product Categories Show Weakness

iPad sales declined 10.4% year over year to $6.23 billion, reflecting supply constraints and a difficult comparison with the prior-year launch of the A16-powered iPad. Nevertheless, the installed base reached a record, and more than half of quarterly buyers were new customers.

Wearables, Home and Accessories revenues decreased 7.9% year over year to $8.30 billion. The decline reflected challenging comparisons with the previous year's launches of Watch SE 3 and AirPods Pro 3. The wearables installed base nevertheless reached an all-time high.

Apple's Geographic Revenues Grow Across Markets

Americas revenues increased 10.2% year over year to $48.68 billion, remaining Apple's largest geographic market. Europe sales climbed 11.5% to $32.01 billion.

Greater China revenues jumped 21% to $17.54 billion, supported by strong iPhone and Mac performance. Japan sales declined 1.4% to $6.54 billion, while Rest of Asia Pacific revenues increased 15.0% to $9.71 billion. Management highlighted a quarterly revenue record in Greater China and an all-time record in India.

Story Continues

AAPL's Margins Face Higher Memory Costs

Gross margin expanded 70 basis points (bps) year over year to 47.9%, including approximately 1 percentage point of favorable impact from tariff refunds. Products gross margin was 37.2%, while Services gross margin reached 76.0%, increasing 40 bps sequentially.

Operating expenses increased 20.6% year over year to $19.19 billion. Research and development expenses surged 32.3% to $11.73 billion, reflecting continued investments in AI. Selling, general and administrative expenses rose 5.8% to $7.46 billion.

Operating income increased 9.9% year over year to $35.63 billion.

Apple's Cash Flow Supports Shareholder Returns

Apple ended the quarter with $137 billion in cash and marketable securities and $80 billion in total debt. Operating cash flow totaled $28.1 billion, reflecting strong cash generation despite higher operating costs.

The company returned $28 billion to shareholders, including $24 billion through share repurchases and $3.9 billion in dividends and equivalents. The board declared a quarterly dividend of 27 cents per share, payable Nov. 16, 2026.

AAPL's Outlook Reflects Supply and Cost Pressures

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Apple expects revenues to increase 7% to 10% year over year, reflecting continued supply constraints. Services revenues are projected to grow 8% to 9%, with foreign exchange and third-party licensing creating sequential headwinds.

Gross margin is expected between 45% and 46%, primarily reflecting higher memory costs and expenses associated with Siri AI. Operating expenses are projected between $20.4 billion and $20.8 billion.

Apple expects continued memory-related pressure despite offsets from product pricing adjustments, carry-in inventory and lower non-memory component costs. Supply constraints on Mac and iPad are also expected to persist during the December quarter, while investments in AI continue.

Zacks Rank & Upcoming Earnings to Watch For

Currently, Apple carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Forgent Power Solutions FPS, Telos TLS and NVIDIA NVDA are some better-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. While Forgent Power and Telos sport a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) each at present, NVIDIA carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Forgent Power, Telos and NVIDIA are expected to report their quarterly results on Nov. 12, 9 and 17, respectively. Forgent Power shares have dropped 15.3% year to date (YTD). Telos shares have inched up 2.2% YTD, while NVIDIA shares have climbed 8.4% YTD.

news.Title: Dear Arm Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 4
news.Content:
The artificial intelligence (AI) rally has lost some of its shine in recent weeks, with several of its biggest beneficiaries facing a sharp reversal after an extended run-up. The staggering sums being committed to AI development have come under closer scrutiny, particularly as questions surrounding stretched valuations and the returns on these investments begin to weigh on the sector's growth narrative.

Amid this turbulence, Arm Holdings (ARM) is approaching an important earnings milestone. Its upcoming results should offer a clearer picture of how much traction its technology is gaining from the AI boom, particularly whether customer commitments are translating into actual chip shipments and how royalty income is progressing alongside licensing revenue.

More News from Barchart

Ford and GM Are Taking Different Roads, but 1 Stock Races Ahead

Micron vs. SanDisk: China's DRAM Scare Hit Both Stocks, but 1 Is the Better Buy

Nvidia Stock Looks Surprisingly Cheap. Why NVDA Could Rise 61%.

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

That being said, Arm Holdings is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 results on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after the market closes. While the financial figures will naturally take center stage, the company's commentary on AI demand, customer adoption, and its forward outlook could be just as revealing in assessing the sustainability of its recent growth.

About Arm Holdings Stock

Based in Cambridge, United Kingdom, Arm Holdings develops and licenses semiconductor intellectual property (IP), covering a broad range of technologies, including central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), and AI processors.

With a market cap of nearly $220 billion, its reach extends across smartphones, automotive, robotics, networking, and data centers, giving the company exposure to several fast-evolving technology markets.

On the price performance front, Arm's shares have delivered a rather eventful performance. The stock surged 21% over the last 52 weeks and skyrocketed 86% in 2026. However, the recent pullback has been difficult to overlook, with shares plunging 34% over the last month.

The sharp correction has done little to change the stock's premium valuation. ARM stock is currently trading at 92.39 times forward adjusted earnings and 36.31 times sales, with both multiples above their respective industry averages.

Surpasses Q1 Earnings

Story Continues

Arm entered FY2027 with considerable momentum, delivering a strong set of Q1 results on Jul. 29. Both revenue and earnings exceeded analyst estimates, with total revenue reaching $1.29 billion, up 22.4% year-over-year (YoY).

Royalty revenue increased 22.2% from the year-ago value to $715 million, with data center royalties more than doubling as hyperscalers expanded their use of ARM-based servers. The growing adoption of Armv9 architecture and Compute Subsystems (CSS) also contributed to the improvement, as higher royalty rates helped strengthen revenue from the company's existing technology portfolio.

Licensing revenue added to the positive performance, climbing 22.6% from the last year's quarter to $574 million. Demand for next-generation architectures and multiple high-value customer agreements supported the increase.

For a more consistent view of licensing momentum, annualized contract value (ACV) offers a useful reference point. This measure increased 13% YoY to $1.73 billion, indicating continued progress beyond the impact of large agreements.

Profitability also rose, with non-GAAP operating income up 28.9% YoY to $531 million. The operating margin improved to 41.2% from 39.1%, while non-GAAP EPS climbed 28.6% YoY to $0.45, exceeding the upper end of management's guidance and reflecting stronger operating performance.

The stronger results came alongside higher spending, with operating expenses increasing 18.4% YoY to $733 million. Research and development (R&D) investment rose 20.5% as Arm expanded its engineering teams and continued developing next-generation architectures and its AGI CPU portfolio.

Going ahead, management has projected Q2 revenue of $1.38 billion, plus or minus $50 million, alongside non-GAAP EPS of $0.47, plus or minus $0.04. Operating expenses are expected to reach approximately $780 million, reflecting continued investment in engineering and product development.

On the other hand, analysts expect Q2 FY2027 EPS to increase 46.7% YoY to $0.22. Their full-year FY2027 projections call for EPS growth of 33.7% YoY to $1.15, followed by a much stronger 65.2% increase to $1.90 in FY2028.

What Do Analysts Expect for ARM Stock?

Arm Holdings' outlook remains broadly positive, with several analysts highlighting the chipmaker's position in the rapidly expanding AI and advanced computing markets. Christopher Rolland of Susquehanna has maintained a "Buy" rating on the stock, accompanied by a price target of $320.

David O'Connor of Piper Sandler has also assigned ARM stock a "Buy" rating and a $320 price target.

The broader analyst community shares a similarly constructive view, giving ARM stock an overall rating of "Moderate Buy." Of the 32 analysts covering the name, 20 recommend "Strong Buy," three assign "Moderate Buy," eight recommend "Hold," and one has issued a "Strong Sell" rating.

To that end, the average price target stands at $289.14, implying potential upside of 42%. At the more optimistic end of the spectrum, Bernstein's David Dai CFA has set a Street-high target of $480, pointing to a potential gain of 137% from current levels.

news.Title: Is Wall Street Bullish or Bearish on Marvell Technology Stock?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL) is a fabless semiconductor company that designs, develops, and sells data-infrastructure chips for data centers, cloud computing, networking, storage, security, and communications. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, the company has a market capitalization of $154.05 billion.

Marvell's stock has risen over the past year mainly because investors see it as a major beneficiary of hyperscalers' spending on AI data centers. Over the past 52 weeks, the stock has gained 82.9%, while it has risen 101.7% year-to-date (YTD). The company's shares reached a 52-week high of $329.88 on June 18, but are down 48% from that level.

More News from Barchart

Meanwhile, the broader S&P 500 Index ($SPX) has gained 10.3% and 10.2% over the same periods, respectively, indicating the stock has outperformed the broader market. Next, we compare the stock with its own sector. The State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) has increased 15.9% over the past 52 weeks and 21% YTD. As a result, the stock has outperformed its sector.

Recently, Marvell announced plans to acquire Lumentum Holdings Inc. (LITE) in an all-stock transaction, aiming to combine Marvell's custom chips and networking technology with Lumentum's lasers and optical components for AI infrastructure. However, investors disliked the idea, and the stock fell 12.7% intraday on Nov. 2.

Lumentum holders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, leaving them with roughly 33% of the combined company. That is expected to materially increase Marvell's share count and dilute existing holders. The deal has an enterprise value of $115 billion, including a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's unaffected share price. Meanwhile, the companies anticipate more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost savings and higher adjusted EPS for Marvell in the first year after closing.

Marvell reported better-than-expected results for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (quarter ended Aug. 1). For the third quarter, Wall Street analysts expect Marvell's EPS to increase 27.4% YOY to $0.79 on a diluted basis. EPS is expected to increase 41.2% annually to $3.05 for fiscal 2027, followed by a 99.7% improvement to $6.09 in fiscal 2028. The company surpassed consensus EPS estimates in two of the four trailing quarters.

Story Continues

Among the 39 Wall Street analysts covering Marvell's stock, the consensus is a "Strong Buy." That's based on 29 "Strong Buy" ratings, three "Moderate Buys," and seven "Holds." The rating configuration has become more bullish than a month ago, with 29 "Strong Buy" ratings, up from 28.

However, following the Lumentum deal announcement, analysts at TD Cowen downgraded Marvell from "Buy" to "Hold" and lowered the price target from $350 to $175. TD Cowen estimates the deal will dilute EPS by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2028. The firm also sees 2027 optical-transceiver consensus of $100 billion as too high versus its $47 billion forecast. If demand disappoints and inventories build, weaker 2028 orders could hurt Lumentum's margins and EPS, and worsen Marvell's deal-related EPS dilution.

Marvell's mean price target of $337.32 implies 96.8% upside from current market prices. Moreover, the Street-high price target of $450 implies a potential upside of 162.5%.

news.Title: Analysts downgrade Marvell and slash price targets over Lumentum deal
news.Content:
Investing.com -- TD Cowen and Bank of America both downgraded Marvell Technology on Tuesday, citing concerns about the chipmaker's all-stock acquisition of Lumentum.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

TD Cowen cut Marvell to Hold from Buy and slashed its price target to $175 from $350. Analyst Sean O'Loughlin expects the deal to dilute EPS by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2028, its first year, and worries it may come at or near the peak of an optical mini-cycle.

"Our downgrade is driven primarily by our negative view of the transaction itself in terms of structure and timing, rather than the quality of the asset Marvell is acquiring," O'Loughlin wrote.

He said Lumentum is likely to become a "crown jewel" within Marvell's portfolio. However, he noted that bottom-up consensus implies a roughly $100 billion optical transceiver market in 2027, compared with TD Cowen's $47 billion forecast. If the cycle turns, Lumentum's operating leverage could worsen the dilution.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Bank of America downgraded Marvell to Neutral from Buy and cut its price target to $225 from $400. Analyst Vivek Arya cited a potential extended stock overhang from the deal, along with a 19% drop in the SOX index over the past month.

BofA said the deal has strategic merit, creating a broader electrical-to-optical connectivity platform.

However, it flagged a lengthy regulatory process, with closing expected in the first half of 2028, limited EPS accretion as $1 billion in cost cuts falls short of offsetting about 50% share dilution, and potential customer conflicts.

"There was no mention of any large M&A in MRVL's recent analyst day, so the news comes as a considerable surprise," Arya said. "We question the impact on LITE's valuation once its laser shortages are inevitably resolved."

news.Title: Is NVIDIA's Cheap Valuation an Opportunity to Invest in the Stock?
news.Content:
NVIDIA Corporation 's NVDA stock appears attractively valued compared with the broader technology sector and several major semiconductor competitors. The stock currently trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 14.26, well below the Zacks Computer and Technology sector average of 17.80.

NVIDIA Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

NVIDIA also looks cheaper than some of its major semiconductor peers, including Intel Corporation INTC, Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD. Intel, Marvell Technology and AMD currently trade at forward P/E multiples of 30.33, 26.00 and 33.31, respectively.

The valuation gap largely reflects NVIDIA's relatively weak stock performance this year. NVDA shares have gained just 8.4% year-to-date, significantly underperforming Intel, Marvell Technology and AMD, which have surged 62.6%, 101.7% and 118%, respectively.

NVIDIA YTD Price Return Performance

This underperformance raises an important question: Is NVIDIA's relatively low valuation a buying opportunity, or does it signal concerns about the company's future growth?

We believe the current valuation offers an attractive entry point. NVIDIA remains the leading supplier of graphics processing units (GPUs) used to train and run AI models. Its products are essential to the expansion of AI infrastructure across data centers, cloud computing platforms and enterprises. With companies continuing to invest heavily in AI computing capacity, NVIDIA is well-positioned to benefit.

Its latest financial results show that AI demand remains strong, while its expanding product portfolio and growing customer base provide additional opportunities for revenue growth.

NVIDIA's Q2 Results Highlight the Strength of AI Demand

NVIDIA's second-quarter fiscal 2027 results reinforce the strength of its AI business. Revenues surged 106% year over year and 18% sequentially to $96.22 billion. The Data Center business remained the biggest growth driver, with revenues jumping 117% year over year and 18% sequentially to $89.02 billion.

Demand for NVIDIA's Blackwell platform remains strong, particularly among hyperscalers and other AI infrastructure customers. This demand is translating into impressive financial performance. Non-GAAP gross margin increased to 75% from 72.5% in the prior-year quarter, while non-GAAP operating income climbed 124% to $63.96 billion.

The bottom line was equally impressive. Non-GAAP net income rose 118% year over year to $53.95 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) surged 120% to $2.22.

Story Continues

NVIDIA Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NVIDIA Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NVIDIA Corporation Quote

NVIDIA's third-quarter guidance suggests that this momentum is unlikely to fade anytime soon. Management expects revenues of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, indicating another strong sequential increase. The company expects non-GAAP gross margin of 74%, plus or minus 50 basis points.

This revenue outlook does not include any Data Center compute revenues from China. This means NVIDIA's near-term growth expectations are not dependent on a recovery in the Chinese market.

The continued adoption of Blackwell and the rollout of its next-generation Vera Rubin platform provide growth support. NVIDIA started production shipments of Vera Rubin in August, and major hyperscalers and AI infrastructure providers have already begun adopting the platform. Management expects Vera Rubin to contribute approximately 20% of Data Center revenues in the third quarter.

NVDA's AI Ecosystem Creates New Revenue Opportunities

NVIDIA's growth opportunity goes well beyond selling GPUs. The company is building a complete AI computing platform that includes central processing units (CPUs), networking products, software and integrated AI factory systems. This strategy allows NVIDIA to capture a larger share of customer spending as companies build and expand their AI infrastructure.

The financial opportunity from each new generation of products is also increasing. NVIDIA estimates that its revenue opportunity per gigawatt of deployed computing capacity has grown from approximately $18 billion with Hopper to $25 billion with Blackwell and $40 billion with Vera Rubin. This rising revenue potential could support stronger growth as AI infrastructure investments increase.

Another positive is the broadening customer base. Hyperscale revenues jumped 117% year over year to $48.71 billion in the second quarter. Meanwhile, revenues from AI clouds, industrial and enterprise customers (ACIE) surged 138% to $40.31 billion. Amazon Web Services has also announced plans to deploy an additional 2 million NVIDIA GPUs through the second quarter of fiscal 2029, highlighting the long-term demand opportunity among major cloud providers.

NVIDIA's longer-term growth outlook remains impressive. Management expects fiscal 2028 revenues to increase approximately 70%. However, this forecast reflects supply constraints, suggesting that actual demand could be even higher if the company had more capacity available to meet customer requirements.

To support this demand, NVIDIA is making substantial commitments across its supply chain. Supplier commitments increased to $279 billion at the end of the second quarter, largely reflecting memory procurement requirements. The company is also strengthening its AI ecosystem through cloud partnerships, financing initiatives and strategic investments.

Wall Street analysts remain optimistic about NVIDIA's growth prospects. news.Title: MRVL's Proposed LITE Buyout Suggests Long-Term AI Infrastructure Boom
news.Content:
On Nov. 2, AI-powered fabless semiconductor giant Marvell Technology Inc. MRVL entered into a definitive agreement to acquire photonics major Lumentum Holdings Inc. LITE in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $115 billion.

Every Lumentum stockholder will receive 4.5 Marvel shares, valuing LITE at around $1,132 per share. Post-close, MRVL and LITE shareholders will own 67% and 33% of the combined company, respectively. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2028.

Lumentum currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), while Marvell currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

The chart below shows the price performance of MRVL and LITE year to date.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Photonics Becomes New Hot Cake in AI Infra Space

Optical and photonics products are in tremendous demand for serving global cloud and AI/ML infrastructure. Large AI models require millions of graphical processing units (GPUs) working in tandem.

As a result, the ecosystem witnesses massive growth in data throughput (as high as 400 Gbps and 800 Gbps). Traditional copper wiring is unable to carry these extremely high-speed data packets properly, as it generates excessive heat slowing down the entire AI compute cluster.

Photonics technology solves this problem by transmitting data at the speed of light through fiber-optic network. Photonics enables high-speed, low-latency and energy-efficient data transfer without overheating.

Huge Synergies Likely From the Deal

The deal is targeting a $550 billion total addressable market and over $1 billion in cost synergies for the combined entity. None of the four giant AI hyperscalers trimmed their massive AI capex plan for 2026 and beyond in their last reported earnings results.

Marvell is benefiting from AI-led demand across the data center end market, with custom silicon, interconnect, switching and optics driving record revenues. MRVL's custom silicon strategy continues to benefit from hyperscaler demand for differentiated XPU and XPU-attach solutions.

On the other hand, Lumentum provides components, such as transceivers and lasers for fiber-optic networks, supporting the rapid growth of AI, cloud computing, 5G connectivity, and beyond. LITE's technology leadership in high-speed optical components has positioned it as an essential supplier to hyperscale customers deploying next-generation network architectures.

The proposed acquisition will position Marvel as a formidable player in the optical technologies and laser manufacturing space. The combined entity will enable MRVL to more rigorously compete with its closest rival — Broadcom Inc. AVGO — that offers customers a broader menu of AI data center hardware in one platform.

Story Continues

Deepening NVIDIA Ecosystem Integration

The expanded partnership with NVIDIA Corp. NVDA ties MRVL's roadmap more directly to next-generation AI system architecture. The collaboration spans optics, NVLink Fusion integration and AI-RAN, widening the platforms where Marvell silicon can participate.

In March 2026, Marvell issued $2 billion of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock to NVIDIA as part of the strategic relationship. Likewise, Lumentum has a strong collaboration with NVIDIA for developing NVDA's silicon photonics ecosystem, especially for deploying the latter's Spectrum-X Photonics networking switches. NVDA also invested $2 billion in LITE in March 2026.

Solid Estimate Revisions

Marvell has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 47.1% and 48.2%, respectively, for the current year (ending January 2027). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year's earnings has improved 0.7% over the last 60 days.

MRVL has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 65.8% and 74.8%, respectively, for the next year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for next year's earnings has improved 9.2% over the last 30 days.

Lumentum has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of more than 100% each, for the current year (ending June 2027). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year's earnings has improved 0.5% over the last 30 days.

LITE has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 60.5% and 64%, respectively, for the next year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for next year's earnings has improved 3.8% over the last 30 days.

Robust Price Upside for MRVL

Despite an enormous rally in the stock price year to date, Marvell is currently trading at a huge 48% discount to its 52-week high price. The short-term average price target of brokerage firms represents an increase of 98% from the last closing price of $171.41. The brokerage target price is currently in the range of $220-$450. This indicates a maximum upside of 162.5% and no downside.

news.Title: The S&P 500's Record Profits Are Hiding a Problem Investors Haven't Seen Before
news.Content:
Record corporate earnings have been the primary driver of higher stock prices for the past several quarters. Current estimates suggest year-over-year earnings growth for the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) could hit 29% in Q3. Above-average earnings growth is expected to continue, especially within the mega-cap names, for the next couple of years.

But there's a risk hiding underneath those numbers. And it raises questions about just how sustainable some of those earnings really are. The way companies account for those investments and the revenue associated with them could be creating a problem that won't show up until far into the future.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The hidden cost of the AI investment boom

Imagine a situation where a tech company decides to make a major investment into AI development. It needs chips. It needs servers. It needs other equipment and infrastructure. Let's say it spends $1 billion in total.

The companies selling those things recognize the revenue as they deliver those products. That spending then can also immediately support sales and earnings further down the AI supply chain.

But the company developing that project doesn't recognize the full $1 billion as an expense on its income statement right away. Instead, it usually chooses to depreciate the construction and equipment costs over their useful lives, which could be several years or more. Plus, depreciation usually doesn't begin until those projects are ready for use.

That creates a potential problem for the big AI companies . The revenue and earnings are showing up now, but the expense won't come until later. What happens when that earnings growth finally slows right at the time that expenses are increasing?

The markets are finally concerned about AI capex spending

Not long ago, huge planned spending for AI development was viewed as a positive by Wall Street. Tens, if not hundreds, of billions of dollars of capex commitment by all of the big hyperscalers resulted in big rallies in their stock prices.

Now we're on the other side of the mountain. The markets are focused on the return on investment (ROI) from all that spending. Revenue and earnings growth rates have been strong thus far and are expected to continue into 2027 and beyond. But free cash flow is the number that people are watching and they're getting more anxious about what they're seeing.

Story Continues

For example:

Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) just suffered an historic single-day drop and now sits 30% below its 2026 high after reporting ballooning infrastructure spending. It had a negative free cash flow of over $9 billion in the quarter, reiterated its 2026 capex forecast of around $200 billion and said spending could ramp up further next year.

Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) shares tanked by more than 25% following a weaker-than-expected Q4 outlook and a warning that they probably won't be free cash flow positive in 2027.

Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) fell sharply after it said it had negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, a massive capital expenditure forecast of roughly $220 billion for the year, and the expectation that spending will be higher in 2027.

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) dropped sharply as well on similar concerns around heavy AI development spending and negative free cash flow expectations.

Suddenly, investors have moved past the "AI optimism" phase and are looking for results.

What this means for S&P 500 investors

As Warren Buffett would point out, there's a difference between a company whose stock price is falling because the business model is failing and one whose stock price is falling because economic conditions are changing.

The big tech stocks fall into the latter category. They're not going anywhere, and they still generate massive revenue and profits. But there is a legitimate risk that they've pushed too far, too fast. They might be in the second half of the boom/bust cycle that often occurs with these revolutionary new technologies. Their stock prices may have suffered the brunt of it already.

But I think long-term asset allocations should remain intact. Investments in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO) and the Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (NYSEMKT: VTI) are still sound even if there will be some heightened volatility. More risk-averse investors might seek out the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (NYSEMKT: RSP) to spread out exposure risk.

Free cash flow looks like the signal here, though. The longer that stays negative and the longer tech companies keep spending hundreds of billions of dollar on capex, the longer that risk remains elevated.

news.Title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Apple, Qualcomm, AMD, BMW, Ferrari, Deutsche, Lufthansa and Ryanair
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 3, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Apple AAPL, Qualcomm QCOM, Advanced Micro Devices AMD, BMW BAMXF, Ferrari RACE, Deutsche Lufthansa DLAKY and Ryanair RYAAY.

Here are highlights from Monday's Analyst Blog:

U.S. Midterm Elections: Global Week Ahead

What happens across this Global Week Ahead ?

Different market themes collide in the coming week, with —

·        U.S. midterm elections

·        Key macro-economic data

·        Major tech earnings, and

·        A run of central bank meetings

— All set to test investors.

The U.S. midterms will shape the political landscape for the next two years, while October nonfarm payrolls data will offer fresh clues on the health of the world's biggest economy.

Earnings from major tech and AI companies also come in as enthusiasm for the AI trade shows signs of fading.

Elsewhere, several major ‌central banks are due to meet, while investors continue to assess developments in key emerging markets, including Brazil and Indonesia.

Next are Reuters' five world market themes, re-ordered for equity traders—

(1) Tech Giant Apple Headlines This Week's Earnings Calendar

Apple , one of the "Magnificent 7" big tech giants, headlines the earnings calendar this afternoon, along with some stars in the AI galaxy later in the week.

The AI trade is in particular focus after disappointing results from Google parent Alphabet, Amazon and Intel triggered sharp share-price ‌declines.

Upcoming reports from Qualcomm and rival Advanced Micro Devices , could either reinforce or challenge concerns that investor enthusiasm for AI is losing momentum.

Over in Europe, investors will also hear from companies exposed to Trump's tariffs and higher energy prices stemming from the Iran war, including automakers BMW and Ferrari and airlines Deutsche Lufthansa and Ryanair .

(2) On Tuesday, the U.S. Midterm Elections Happen

Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections will determine whether Democrats can wrest control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican party, potentially reshaping the policy outlook for markets.

Democrats are widely expected to win the House of Representatives, while control of the Senate remains less certain. Republicans have controlled both chambers during Trump's first two years in office.

Should Democrats prevail, the prospect of tougher regulation on AI, including pushback on data center expansion, is on investors' radar, along with potentially greater scrutiny of Wall Street banks and crypto firms.

Story Continues

The outcome could also influence expectations for fiscal spending, while defense and healthcare stocks may be particularly sensitive to the result.

(3) Friday Morning, U.S. Federal Nonfarm Payroll Data for October Lands

Friday's October non-farm payrolls report caps a busy week for the U.S. economy and could provide fresh guidance on the Federal Reserve's next move.

September data showed the economy added a lower-than-expected +29,000 jobs.

The labor market has remained resilient. Unemployment stood at 4.2% last month, while weekly jobless claims are hovering near 57-year lows.

The Fed on Wednesday left rates unchanged and upgraded its assessment of the economy to "strong" from "solid."

Markets are pricing about an 80% chance of a Fed rate hike in December, reflecting some uncertainty over the timing of the next move. The payrolls number could bring some clarity.

(4) Trailing the FOMC Last Week, More Central Bank Meetings Happen

Another week brings another packed schedule of central bank meetings.

The Reserve Bank of Australia announces its policy decision on Tuesday, followed by Sweden's Riksbank on Wednesday and the Bank of England and Norges Bank on Thursday.

The Fed, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan all left policy unchanged this week, but markets expect the RBA, Riksbank and BoE to raise rates.

It would be the fifth increase this year for Australia's central bank as it battles stubborn inflation, but the first for Sweden and Britain.

Both have so far adopted a wait-and-see approach, but growing inflation risks are increasing the case for action.

Norway's central bank is further along the tightening path, having already raised rates twice this year.

(5) Brazil and Indonesia Central Banks Set Policy, Amidst Major Complications

Brazil's central bank faces a more complicated backdrop after a dramatic election campaign overturned market expectations.

Flavio Bolsonaro's first-round victory initially buoyed markets, but Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's comeback win in the runoff reversed those gains, sending the Brazilian real and equities sharply lower.

The political uncertainty has complicated an easing cycle that has brought interest rates down to 13.75%, making Wednesday's policy decision and accompanying guidance a key focus for investors. Markets will also be watching for Lula's choice of finance minister for signals on future fiscal policy.

In Indonesia, third-quarter GDP data due on Thursday will offer a fresh gauge of economic momentum.

With the rupiah near record lows, investors are looking for signs of strain in Southeast Asia's largest economy amid concerns over President Prabowo Subianto's policies and his ambitious 8% growth target.

news.Title: Google Recently Warned That Quantum Computers Could Crack Bitcoin. Now It's Selling Protection.
news.Content:
One day, it's technically possible that a hacker equipped with a quantum computer could crack the encryption that underpins Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC). That day may be drawing nearer; in March 2026, security researchers at Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) estimated that a future quantum machine could break Bitcoin's wallet cryptography in less than 10 minutes, and that a quantum computer of sufficient power could be far easier to create than what had previously been believed. And now, on Oct. 28, Google Cloud previewed its new crypto custody system targeting banks that offer crypto products to their clients, positioning the quantum threat to Bitcoin as one of the risks that justify buying its services.

So what does this mean for Alphabet's stock, and what does this mean for Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

This move is aimed at cutting down on the biggest type of crypto theft

Google's new custody system is designed to protect crypto assets from one particular threat: theft of users' private keys.

In case you aren't familiar, a private key is the secret password that enables the control of a crypto wallet. According to Chainalysis data, hacked or otherwise illegally obtained private keys accounted for 43.8% of the crypto stolen in 2024.

Google's new service is called Multi-Party Compute (MPC), and it's useful for preventing that because it splits each private key into fragments which are then stored on separate systems, making it much more difficult to gain access to the keys by hacking individual networks or computers. Commercial launch of MPC is planned for early 2027.

But as of now, there's little reason to expect MPC to be very beneficial for Alphabet shareholders.

Per Alphabet's third-quarter earnings, Google Cloud revenue climbed 103% year over year to $30.7 billion, accounting for 24% of the company's total revenue. As there's no information available on the service's pricing yet, and plenty of other crypto custody options and cybersecurity services that appeal to institutional investors, it's unclear how the new initiative will capture much market share or generate much revenue at all.

And the entire endeavor's connection to quantum cybersecurity is, to some degree, a long shot; most timelines don't expect quantum computers that are powerful enough to be relevant to cryptocurrency encryption to even exist until five years from now at the earliest, and some estimates only see that happening after a decade or two.

Story Continues

Does Google's product make Bitcoin safer from quantum computers?

Aside from the above, it's also important for investors to temper their concerns (and expectations) for Google's involvement in the quickly evolving field of quantum cybersecurity.

In theory, sufficiently sophisticated quantum computers could crack Bitcoin's encryption and steal funds by working backward from a public key, which is a wallet's cryptographic identifier that is visible to everyone on the blockchain, to get to the private key behind it. An attack like that wouldn't need to steal any key fragments, so it isn't helpful to split the keys across systems like Google's approach does.

More than 6 million bitcoins, a substantial portion of the 21 million coins that can ever exist (almost 29%), are held in wallets with exposed public keys, and those are the coins that are most at risk as quantum computing companies improve the technology over the coming years. A successful attack would likely mean that Bitcoin would lose a dramatic amount of value overnight as holders fled to safer assets.

Furthermore, Google has given no timetable for when post-quantum cryptography, encryption built to resist quantum attacks, will be implemented in its service, though it's clearly on the agenda to develop at some point. So for now, the quantum security pitch is ahead of what the product can actually do as it's presently known and envisioned.

Alphabet investors can thus treat MPC as a small bonus for now, although it probably isn't worth loading up on the stock due to this new offering.

On the other hand, if quantum computers continue developing faster than anticipated, there could be a growing demand (and perhaps even a market panic causing a clamor) for a quantum-safe custody option, which Google would in turn be well positioned to deliver on, especially if its service gains some early traction in advance of that.

news.Title: ASML Surges 48% in the Past Year: How Should You Play the Stock Now?
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. ASML has gained 48.1% over the past year compared with the sector's growth of 9.5%. It has outperformed Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. AEIS but lagged Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO. While AEIS has gained 11.4%, SIMO soared 103.6% over this period.

One-Year ASML Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ASML Rides on Strong AI Demand

ASML is benefiting from growing AI infrastructure investments, which are encouraging leading semiconductor manufacturers to expand their production capabilities. The company's Installed Base Management revenues reached €3.29 billion in the third quarter of 2026, increasing from €2.76 billion in the preceding quarter, driven by strong demand for productivity upgrades. New lithography system sales increased to 113 units from 86 in the second quarter.

Management highlighted improving order momentum, with some customers expressing interest in placing equipment orders for 2029 and 2030. The combination of capacity growth and higher lithography content gives ASML multiple structural avenues for revenue expansion through 2026 and beyond.

The company's dominant position in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography technology provides a competitive advantage, particularly as chipmakers expand production of advanced logic and memory chips. ASML's expanding technological capabilities, strategic partnerships and improving financial outlook further strengthen its investment appeal. The company is advancing High Numerical Aperture (High-NA) EUV technology, which is expected to support next-generation semiconductor manufacturing and drive long-term equipment demand. Its expanding collaborations with Intel, Samsung and TSMC reinforce its position in advanced chipmaking.

Estimate Revision Trend

Earnings estimates for ASML for 2026 have moved up 54.4% to $46.54 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has increased 61.9% to $62.54. The positive estimate revision depicts bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

ASML Growth Marred by Long Order Visibility

Despite the positives, management attributes the current demand environment primarily to AI-related investment and the resulting need for more advanced Logic and Memory capacity. This has produced unusually long order visibility for ASML, but it also makes the growth profile increasingly dependent on customers maintaining those expansion plans. A slower pace of customer investment would therefore affect both system demand and utilization of the larger production footprint ASML is preparing.

The planned scale-up requires manufacturing capacity, suppliers and trained employees to rise together. This leaves future profitability dependent on converting the larger cost base into the expected shipment volumes. Moreover, a uniform adoption schedule across Logic and DRAM customers is yet to be established. High-NA therefore remains both a technology opportunity and an execution variable, with the pace of wider insertion dependent on customer qualification and manufacturing decisions rather than ASML's roadmap alone.

Story Continues

Other Headwinds

ASML also faces operational challenges related to capacity expansion, supply-chain constraints and the growing complexity of its advanced lithography systems. In its third-quarter 2026 update, management indicated that planned production capacity for 2027 and 2028 would not fully meet anticipated customer demand, highlighting potential execution risks as the company scales manufacturing operations. Expanding capacity requires substantial investments, specialized components and a highly skilled workforce, while supplier bottlenecks could delay system deliveries and revenue recognition. In addition, developing and commercializing next-generation High-NA EUV technology requires significant R&D spending that could weigh on ASML's growth prospects.

End Note

ASML's technological leadership in EUV lithography, healthy order trends and expanding installed-base revenues reinforce its long-term investment appeal. With upward earnings estimate revisions, the stock is witnessing positive investor sentiment. However, export-control uncertainties, capacity-expansion challenges and long order visibility remain headwinds.

Stiff competitive pressure and supply-chain bottlenecks also plague the company's growth prospects. High operating and R&D expenses remain an overhang as well. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), ASML appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and investors could be better off if they trade with caution.
