news.Title: Elon Musk sends incredible news to Micron stock investors
news.Content: One post from Elon Musk was enough to jolt Micron Technology stock. The Tesla and SpaceX CEO replied on X to an analyst at Citrini Research, a firm that offers thematic equity and macro trading insights. Musk noted that the amount of memory humanoid robots need "will exceed everything else on Earth." Micron shares rose about 2.5% after the remark. The timing could hardly be better for the memory maker. Micron fell about 6% on Oct. 22 as another AI sell-off hit chip stocks, the same day the company held a technology webinar for analysts. Musk's comment gave bulls a new story to tell, and this one has nothing to do with data centers. It is about machines that walk, lift, and work alongside people. Robots could become memory's next big customer Musk made the remark on Oct. 26, in a post that quickly spread across investor circles. His post listed the robot chip's memory as LP5, a low-power type of DRAM that also goes into phones and laptops, Benzinga reported . The robot memory story still assumes builders can actually get the chips they need. Also read: Nvidia and Micron are about to lord their successes all over Wall Street Research firms see a big runway. Counterpoint Research expects DRAM demand from humanoids to climb more than 20 times between 2026 and 2030, with memory in each robot rising from about 19GB today to 39GB by the end of the decade, according to The Motley Fool . That would add a fresh source of demand on top of data centers, smartphones, vehicles, and personal computers. Musk thinks that may still be too low. In early October, he said in X that Tesla halved the memory on its AI5 chip to 72GB and cut the AI6 chip by a third to 144GB, calling it "the only way to get enough volume for Optimus production." He added that the cuts should have a negligible effect on performance, since memory bandwidth matters more than total capacity. Even after the cuts, both chips carry far more memory than Counterpoint's per-robot estimate. The cuts also showed how tight supply has become. JPMorgan said the memory shortage is lasting longer than analysts expected, and Micron's management believes DRAM and NAND markets will stay tight beyond 2027. Citi raised its own target to $1,300, citing stronger DRAM pricing and continued undersupply, TheStreet reported . Tesla and Toyota are building toward scale Tesla is moving from talk to production. The company has started early production of Optimus at its Fremont, California, factory and targets initial customer shipments towards the end of 2027, with Musk saying delivery is likely toward the end of next year. Story Continues Early buyers will likely use the robots for dangerous and repetitive industrial work, according to Manufacturing Dive . The line is built for real volume. Tesla's Fremont robotics line is capable of producing 1 million units a year, though Musk estimated it would take a year or longer to reach that pace as Tesla works through the design. Other manufacturers are lining up, too. Toyota told investors it may need about 400,000 robots, both humanoid and conventional, to modernize its factories. The effort requires spending as much as $6.4 billion a year starting in 2028. The plan covers Toyota, its group companies, and major suppliers, Reuters reported . Wall Street is raising its forecasts to match. Goldman Sachs lifted its 2035 humanoid shipment estimate nearly fivefold to about 6.5 million units, putting the market at around $138 billion. The bank also sees each robot carrying thousands of dollars in chip content, with memory makers among the suppliers that could benefit. Micron is already preparing for physical AI Micron has been pointing at this market for weeks. On its fiscal fourth-quarter call , CEO Sanjay Mehrotra called self-driving cars "the first major deployment of physical AI" and said humanoid robots should have similar memory and storage needs. The market is still small, with about 7,000 humanoids sold worldwide in 2025, The Motley Fool noted . The numbers behind that view are large. Mehrotra said Level 4 and higher autonomous vehicles typically need more than 200GB of memory and multiple terabytes of storage, far more than today's semi-autonomous cars. More Micron: Morgan Stanley revisits Micron stock price target amid stellar growth Bank of America resets Micron stock forecast as AI 'memory tax' rises Micron just sent a stark memory chip warning to tech stock investors Does Micron pay dividends? Its yield and payouts explained He also said several physical AI customers are already sampling Micron's next-generation products, and that physical AI could become a significant driver of memory and storage demand by the end of the decade, driven by more memory in each device and more units sold, according to The Motley Fool. Meanwhile, the core business is booming. Micron posted fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of about $54.2 billion, up 379% from a year earlier, and guided well above expectations for the current quarter. Micron's GAAP gross margin reached about 87%. Related: Who owns Micron Technology? A look at its top investors Micron stock still looks cheap, despite the hype Micron's valuation leaves room for upside, even after worries about the pace of AI infrastructure spending weighed on chip stocks. The stock trades at about 13 times earnings and roughly 5 times forward earnings, while the stock has more than tripled over the past year. Analysts are lining up behind it. TradingView confirmed that D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria kept a Buy rating and a $3,000 price target after the Oct. 22 drop, arguing that AI should drive memory demand for three to five years, helped by longer customer commitments. There are risks to that view, including faster new supply from Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix; slower AI spending; or more efficient memory use. Rosenblatt is bullish, too. Analyst Kevin Cassidy raised his target to $1,900, pointing to constrained supply and 10 new strategic customer agreements that improve visibility. Low earnings multiples can overstate the value of a cyclical business near peak profits. Still, if robots end up needing as much memory as Musk expects, Micron may have found its next big growth engine. news.Title: Lumentum Goes From $1 Billion Spinoff to $115 Billion Takeover
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- In 2015, executives at the Silicon Valley hardware firm known then as JDSU spun off a division making optical components and commercial lasers, believing the unit would be better off chasing growth opportunities on its own.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Ray-Ban Heir Rejects $3.9 Billion Offer for Stake in Family Firm

Wall Street Eyes Biggest Treasury Sales Overhaul in Years

Anthropic Commits to $895 Billion in Spending as Mega-IPO Nears

S&P 500 Falls as Chip Rout Offsets US-Iran Hopes: Markets Wrap

Wash Trades and 5,000% Gains: Inside Indonesia's MSCI Hustle

They were right.

When Lumentum Holdings Inc. began trading later that year, it had a roughly $1 billion market value and was reporting quarterly adjusted net income of about $15.3 million. A decade later, the company is generating more than $1 billion of sales in a single quarter, saw $461.1 million of adjusted profits last quarter and is now on track to become one of the largest tech takeovers of all time: On Monday, Marvell Technology Inc. agreed to an all-stock purchase that values Lumentum at $115 billion.

The allure of Lumentum has always been its lasers. Telecom firms have for years relied the San Jose, California-based company for lasers, modules and switches to move data over fiber-optic cables across long distances. With the unprecedented expansion of data centers worldwide to power advanced AI systems, Lumentum's technology has taken on a greater purpose: moving massive amounts of data across chips and servers at incredibly high speeds.

Such demand from AI data centers is now so strong that some of Lumentum's components are "completely sold out" through early 2029, Chief Executive Officer Michael Hurlston said in a Bloomberg interview last month. Customers were already starting to lock in orders for 2030, Hurlston said at the time.

There was only one clear way of jumping Lumentum's line: buy the entire company. As analysts at Wolfe Research put it on Monday, the main rationale for Marvell's historic takeover of Lumentum is "vertical integration" in a now "famously tight" laser market.

Bringing Lumentum's capabilities in-house also stands to turn Marvell into an even more formidable rival against Broadcom Inc., which makes its own laser components. Optical interconnects represent almost half of Marvell's revenue targets for the fiscal year 2031, Wolfe Research wrote, so "making sure they have a secure supply of the industry's highest performance lasers would provide a competitive advantage."

Even so, Marvell shares declined as much as 14% to $168.82 on Monday, and Lumentum was down as much as 19% to $685 in New York, reflecting broader investor concerns about a potential AI bubble. Analysts are also questioning the cost-cutting potential between the two businesses' operations. The anticipated 2028 timeframe for completing the tie-up also suggests gaining clearance won't be easy.

Story Continues

Lumentum's rise tracks the emerging popularity of so-called silicon photonics, which rely on the types of lasers that Lumentum makes and use light to transmit data.

Traditional interconnects use copper to transmit data through the pulses of electrons, and they continue to be the cheap and fast over short distances. But AI systems require ever more data to move between chips and servers, and copper is running into limits on how much information it can carry efficiently.

Lasers themselves can consume significant power, but integrating optics more closely with silicon can lower costs and eliminate the need for expensive equipment. As copper reaches its limits and optical technology gets cheaper, the extra cost of using optics is becoming easier to justify.

It's for this reason that Nvidia Corp., the world's largest supplier of AI chips, has been pushing the adoption of optical connections between components. The more efficiently data can travel across Nvidia's chips and servers, the more valuable the company's chips are.

One of the largest impediments to wider-spread adoption of optical interconnects has been the fact that they're still much more expensive to build than copper ones. In part to help bolster the supply chain, accelerate manufacturing and achieve economies of scale of silicon photonics, Nvidia sank $2 billion into both Marvell and Lumentum earlier this year.

For its part, Lumentum has been actively looking for places to expand manufacturing. Earlier this year, it was targeting older electronics facilities that could be repurposed. The company was looking to buy a facility in Japan and was considering subsidies to expand, Hurlston said last month.

At the time, Hurlston said, his company may need to consider an acquisition to grow.

news.Title: Why Marvell Technology Plunged Today
news.Content:
Shares of communications semiconductor giant Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) plunged 10% as of 12:54 p.m. EDT, after the company announced that it had agreed to purchase optical laser leader Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE).

The deal is all-stock, and Marvell will be purchasing Lumentum at roughly a $115 billion valuation, or a 24% premium.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

While not an egregious premium, Lumentum's stock had already rocketed higher over the past two years, with Marvell's purchase price representing more than five times Lumentum's share price just one year ago. So, investors fear Marvell may be paying a steep price for the asset.

Why Marvell loves Lumentum

Marvell likely coveted Lumentum for the same reason Lumentum's stock has rallied over the past year: its proprietary optical laser technology is increasingly sought and required by next-gen artificial intelligence systems.

Artificial intelligence not only requires many more optical interconnects between data centers, but as speeds increase, server racks will also begin replacing traditional copper interconnects with near-packaged and co-packaged optics inside racks, and eventually even inside servers.

This is likely where Marvell sees risks and opportunities. While Marvell is already producing a co-packaged optics solution, it appears that Marvell management sees more opportunity in combining Marvell's technology suite of digital signal processors and XPU-attach connectivity with Lumentum's indium phosphide laser technology to yield highly differentiated products for next-gen AI systems.

Image source: Getty Images.

Investors aren't sold

The market is definitely not in the mood for an announcement like this, as investors have recently been dumping AI-related stocks amid a host of potential fears ahead of the mid-term elections. However, AI-related stocks are volatile and have seen severe sell-offs from time to time, yet as long as the long-term AI story remains intact, these stocks have recovered.

As of now, while there is a lot of fear and concern, the recent reports from major tech companies still show booming AI-related revenues, with guidance for strong growth in 2027 and 2028. As such, both Marvell and Lumentum may be worth a look during this severe sell-off.

news.Title: Why Free Cash Flow Matters More Than Ever: 5 Tech Stocks to Watch
news.Content:
With Alphabet GOOGL) and Amazon AMZN) reporting negative free cash flow amid massive AI infrastructure spending, free cash flow (FCF) is becoming one of the most important metrics for evaluating technology stocks heading into 2027.

Five companies that stand out for their strong cash generation are Nvidia NVDA), Broadcom AVGO), Microsoft MSFT), Apple AAPL), and Adobe ADBE ) .

The distinction is compelling: While hyperscalers spend aggressively to build AI infrastructure, semiconductor suppliers and capital-efficient technology companies are generating substantial cash to support future growth, dividends, and share repurchases.

Notably, Alphabet reported negative FCF of $9.1 billion in Q3, although its trailing 12-month FCF remained positive at $19.7 billion. Amazon's trailing 12-month FCF fell to negative $42.4 billion, reflecting its massive AI investments.

Importantly, negative FCF doesn't necessarily signal financial distress, but it highlights the importance of evaluating capital expenditures and cash-generating efficiency.

Nvidia & Broadcom: AI Leaders Generating Enormous Cash

Nvidia has emerged as one of the biggest cash generators, producing $21.34 billion in free cash flow during its latest reported quarter, up nearly 59% year over year. This brought FCF for the first-half of its current fiscal 2027 to an impressive $69.9 billion, underscoring Nvidia's exceptional profitability and capital-efficient semiconductor design business.

Nvidia's accelerating cash generation is particularly impressive, with annual free cash flow surging from $27 billion in FY24 to nearly $100 billion in FY26. Furthermore, FCF has climbed to approximately $127 billion on a trailing 12-month (TTM) basis, highlighting Nvidia's extraordinary ability to capitalize on booming AI infrastructure demand.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Broadcom is another standout, generating a record $13.7 billion in FCF during its latest quarter, up 95% YoY and representing an impressive 46% of revenue. Broadcom converted approximately 96% of operating cash flow into FCF, benefiting from strong demand for custom AI chips, networking equipment, and high-margin infrastructure software.

Broadcom's annual FCF surged from $19.4 billion in FY24 to $27 billion last year, with TTM FCF approaching $40 billion. This impressive growth further illustrates Broadcom's ability to convert soaring AI infrastructure demand into substantial cash generation.

In other words, both companies are direct beneficiaries of the massive AI infrastructure investments pressuring cash flow at hyperscalers.

Story Continues

Apple's Exceptional Capital Efficiency

Apple stands out for its remarkably capital-efficient business model, supported by its global iPhone ecosystem, growing Services business, and outsourced manufacturing strategy.

Apple generated approximately $136.7 billion in FCF over the trailing 12 months ended June 2026, while capital expenditures totaled just over $10 billion. This translates to an impressive FCF margin near 29%, with 93% of operating cash flow converted into FCF.

With Apple set to report its fiscal Q4 results after the market closes on Monday, investors will be watching whether strong iPhone demand and Services growth can sustain its impressive cash generation heading into FY27.

Apple also boasts an exceptionally high return on invested capital (ROIC) of around 55%, highlighting its ability to generate substantial profits relative to the capital invested in its business.

Microsoft & Adobe: Strong Cash Flow From Software and Cloud

Microsoft generated approximately $18.6 billion in FCF during its latest quarter, despite aggressive spending on AI infrastructure. Its recurring Microsoft 365 subscriptions and rapidly expanding Azure cloud business provide substantial cash generation, with management expecting to remain FCF-positive throughout its current FY27 despite rising capital expenditures.

Meanwhile, like Apple, Adobe offers another attractive capital-light business model, supported by recurring Creative Cloud and Acrobat subscriptions. Adobe generated $2.44 billion in FCF during its latest quarter, up nearly 15% YoY and representing an impressive 36% of revenue. With 97% of operating cash flow converted into FCF, Adobe's capital efficiency makes it an appealing alternative to more capital-intensive AI investments.

Bottom Line: Cash Flow Matters More Than Ever

With AI infrastructure spending accelerating, investors should increasingly focus on free cash flow margins, cash conversion, return on invested capital, and valuation rather than revenue growth alone.

Nvidia and Broadcom offer exceptional cash generation tied directly to AI demand, while Apple's capital efficiency makes it particularly compelling. Microsoft and Adobe also provide substantial cash-generating capabilities through their recurring software and cloud businesses.

Together, these five technology leaders offer investors exposure to AI and digital innovation without necessarily sacrificing strong underlying cash flow.

news.Content:
Lumentum (LITE) shares are in focus on Nov. 2 after Marvell Technology (MRVL) said it's buying the optical components specialist in an $115 billion all-stock transaction. Investors will receive 4.5 MRVL shares for each LITE share, with the acquisition expected to close in the first half of 2028.

While Lumentum stock has been nothing short of a blockbuster investment in 2026, it is currently down about 35% versus its year-to-date high in early October.

Why Is Marvell Paying a Premium for Lumentum?

Marvell's offer values LITE shares at about $1,132 each, representing a nearly 35% premium on their previous close.

The strategic logic centers on a bottleneck: powerful artificial intelligence (AI) processors require faster connections to exchange increasingly enormous volumes of data.

Lumentum's lasers and optical technologies complement Marvell's networking and semiconductor capabilities. Combining them could help customers design more efficient systems and bring them to market faster.

In the press release, management estimated an addressable market of $550 billion, more than $1 billion in annual cost synergies, and adjusted earnings accretion in the very first year after closing.

Is It Too Late to Invest in LITE Shares?

Buying Lumentum shares now increasingly means underwriting MRVL's prospects, alongside the possibility that the announced transaction fails.

Importantly, the $1,132-a-share headline figure is not a guaranteed cash payout. Since the exchange ratio is fixed, the overall valuation of this deal shifts with Marvell's share price. A 10% decline in MRVL stock, for example, would reduce the buyout price by 10%, all else equal.

It's also worth mentioning that shareholder and regulatory approvals are yet to be secured, with closing targeted for 2028.

Investors must therefore compare LITE's price with 4.5 times Marvell's prevailing price and weigh the remaining spread against the wait and completion risk.

What's the Consensus Rating on Lumentum Stock?

Heading into Nov. 2, Wall Street had a consensus "Strong Buy" rating on LITE stock, with a mean price target of about $1,172.

news.Title: Tower Semiconductor Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Tower Semiconductor Ltd.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record Q3 performance: Revenue rose 33% year over year to $526 million, while net profit increased to $120 million and diluted EPS reached $1.05. Management expects approximately $600 million in Q4 revenue, implying about $2 billion in 2026 revenue.

Silicon photonics is driving expansion: Q3 silicon photonics revenue reached roughly $240 million, with annualized capacity expected to exceed $1.1 billion in Q4. Tower is expanding production across four sites and expects 2027 capacity to support a run rate above $2.8 billion, backed by customer commitments extending through 2029.

Strong outlook and investment plan: Tower is developing near-packaged optics and advanced heterogeneous-integration products while investing $920 million in additional capacity. The company raised its long-term model to $3.6 billion in annual revenue, $1.38 billion in operating profit and a 33% net margin.

NVIDIA Just Named AI's Next Bottleneck—And These 3 Stocks Sit Right In It

Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM) reported record third-quarter results for 2026, citing accelerating demand for silicon photonics used in AI infrastructure and data-center connectivity, along with growth across its broader analog technology portfolio.

Revenue for the quarter reached $526 million, up 33% from $396 million in the third quarter of 2025 and 14% from $460 million in the prior quarter. Net profit rose to $120 million, or a 23% net margin, compared with $54 million and a 14% margin a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share were $1.05, compared with $0.47 in the prior-year period.

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

Tower Semiconductor's AI Rally Is Built on a Light-Speed Bet

Chief Executive Officer Russell Ellwanger said the company expects fourth-quarter revenue at the midpoint of its guidance to reach $600 million. That result would bring full-year 2026 revenue to about $2 billion, compared with $1.57 billion in 2025.

Silicon Photonics Drives Growth Plans

Tower said silicon photonics revenue totaled approximately $240 million in the third quarter, representing an annualized rate near $1 billion. Ellwanger said the company expects its fourth-quarter silicon photonics annualized run rate to exceed $1.1 billion.

→ 3 Robotics ETFs, 3 Different Ways to Bet on Humanoid Robots

Aeluma's Market Is Laser-Focused on Fresh Highs—Here's Why

The company is expanding silicon photonics production across four manufacturing sites to meet demand from customers serving AI-related optical interconnect markets. Tower expects year-end capacity to be about double the level that supported third-quarter silicon photonics revenue, with the additional capacity intended to support a revenue ramp during the first and second quarters of 2027.

Story Continues

Tower is also advancing its Track-1 300-millimeter expansion in Japan. Ellwanger said all tools for the expansion have been ordered and scheduled, with full production starts targeted for the third quarter of 2027. Including that expansion, the company expects silicon photonics start capacity to reach three times the level supporting third-quarter shipments.

→ MarketBeat Week in Review – 10/26 - 10/30

Management said that capacity is substantially covered through signed agreements and contracts in advanced negotiation stages. Customer commitments now extend into 2029, when Tower expects its Track-2 expansion in Japan to be underway. The company said its planned expansions will continue to be self-funded.

In response to an analyst question, Ellwanger said capacity expected by the third quarter of 2027 could support a silicon photonics run rate "somewhere a bit above a $2.8 billion" on a start-rate basis. He noted that figure does not include potential revenue from integrated laser products and other initiatives.

New Product Opportunities

Tower highlighted growing customer activity around near-packaged optics, or NPO, a technology that can more tightly integrate optical and electrical functions than conventional pluggable transceivers. The company said it is prototyping NPO products with more than 10 top customers and expects NPO products to carry a higher initial average selling price than pluggable products.

Ellwanger said the company expects an "appreciable amount" of NPO shipments in the second half of 2027, though the timing will depend on market adoption. Tower's NPO customers are currently a subset of its existing pluggable-transceiver customer base, he said.

The company also discussed heterogeneous integration efforts, including initial production for NewPhotonics using indium phosphide laser chiplets attached to silicon photonics wafers. Tower said it is deploying similar die-to-wafer attachment techniques with materials including thin-film lithium niobate for next-generation 400-gigabit-per-lane products.

President Marco Racanelli said Tower expects competition in the expanding silicon photonics and silicon germanium markets, but cited the company's production yields, customer relationships and technology roadmap as factors supporting its position. He said customers have extended long-term agreements through 2029, providing visibility into future capacity requirements.

Other Businesses and Utilization

Beyond optical technologies, Tower reported its highest quarterly RF-SOI revenue to date from its 300-millimeter Agrate, Italy, production corridor. The company also recorded a new high in product tape-outs for Fab 10, which serves its RF-SOI business.

Demand for Tower's BCD technologies grew about 10% year over year, according to Ellwanger, supported by AI and cloud data-center applications as well as mobile and automotive markets. Several strategic customers have entered long-term agreements at higher average selling prices, with Tower forecasting blended BCD pricing in 2027 to be 20% above 2026 levels.

In image sensors and displays, Tower began production of a high-speed global shutter sensor for high-end video cameras and said it is preparing capacity for expected customer demand in OLED-on-silicon displays during 2027.

All of Tower's 200-millimeter fabs operated at utilization rates of 85% to 90% during the third quarter, while its 300-millimeter fab remained fully utilized and above the company's 85% utilization model.

Margins, Capital Spending and Long-Term Model

Chief Financial Officer Oren Shirazi said gross profit increased 92% year over year to a record $179 million, while operating profit rose 2.5 times from the prior-year period to $127 million.

Tower is executing a previously announced $920 million capital investment program for silicon photonics and silicon germanium capacity and capabilities across facilities in Israel, Newport Beach, Texas and Japan. About 65% of the investment had been paid through the third quarter, with the remaining 35% expected to be paid in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first half of 2027.

Shirazi said Tower expects a full return on investment from the $920 million program within one year. He added that quarterly incremental gross margin of roughly 62% was elevated because not all new equipment had begun depreciation, and reiterated a longer-term expectation for incremental gross profit margins of 55% to 58%.

The company updated its long-term financial model to target annual revenue of $3.6 billion, gross profit of $1.63 billion and operating profit of $1.38 billion. The model calls for annual net profit of $1.2 billion, representing a 33% net margin, based on assumptions including 85% fab utilization after planned capacity installations and qualifications are completed.

About Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM)

Tower Semiconductor Ltd. is an Israeli specialty semiconductor foundry that manufactures integrated circuits for fabless semiconductor companies, integrated device manufacturers and system companies. The company provides process technologies and production services rather than selling branded end-user electronics.

Its offerings include analog and mixed-signal technologies, radio-frequency and high-voltage circuits, power management solutions, image sensors, and specialty memory products.

news.Title: AMD to report Q3 results following disappointing showing from Intel
news.Content:
AMD ( AMD ) will report its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, giving Wall Street a look at AI chip demand as the market continues to digest a stark sell-off in the AI trade and a disappointing outlook from rival Intel ( INTC ) last week.

Intel reported better-than-anticipated Q3 earnings after the bell Thursday , but provided Q4 revenue estimates of between $15 billion and $16 billion, well below analysts' projections of $17 billion.

The news sent Intel stock plummeting nearly 29% .

The company blamed the outlook on a worse-than-anticipated decline in the PC market.

The industry is contending with two overlapping factors: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.

While AMD generates the majority of its revenue via data center sales, a drop in PC demand would still hurt its bottom line.

For the third quarter, analysts anticipate AMD to report earnings per share of $1.97 on revenue of $13 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates. The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.

AMD's Data Center arm is expected to see sales of $8.19 billion, an 88% increase from the $4.34 billion it reported last year.

Last month, the company announced its Helion reference design, a server rack designed to be outfitted with various configurations of AMD's CPUs and GPUs based on customers' needs.

The company's Client business revenue, which includes PC sales, is set to top $3.06 billion, up 11% year over year, but flat sequentially.

AMD's gaming business, however, could take a major hit, with Wall Street predicting a 49% revenue decline to $655 million.

The company's gaming division includes products ranging from PC graphics cards to custom silicon for game consoles. Both categories are facing higher prices due to the ongoing memory and storage shortage, depressing customer demand.

news.Title: Why Lumentum Stock Fell 14.9% Today
news.Content:
Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) did just about everything right this morning, and its stock got punished anyway. Shares of the laser and optics specialist were down 14.9% as of 12:55 p.m. ET.

Q1 2027 results beat Wall Street's expectations and the company agreed to be acquired by Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) in an all-stock deal. Marvell's stock fell 9.5% and both stocks are down significantly from the middle of last week, when the rumor mill started suggesting a deal was afoot.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

LITE data by YCharts

A strong quarter, overshadowed

On a normal day, I'd spend this whole article gushing over Lumentum's Q1 report. Revenue more than doubled, rising 136.5% year over year to $1.26 billion. Adjusted earnings of $4.57 per share sailed past the $4.21 consensus. Second-quarter guidance points to about $1.6 billion in sales, well above the $1.48 billion analysts expected.

The company also landed its second major near- or co-packaged optics (NPO/CPO) contract, backed by more than $5 billion in purchase commitments.

That's a tremendous quarter. It also barely matters now.

The Marvell deal sets Lumentum's price now

Under the merger terms, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share. Closing date? The first half of calendar year 2028. The companies valued the deal at $115 billion, or about $1,132 per Lumentum share, based on prices from Oct. 28 (just before the deal rumors started flying).

With a fixed exchange ratio, Lumentum's stock now moves largely with Marvell's. At Monday's midday prices, the offer is worth about $800 per Lumentum share, or roughly $81.2 billion in total. Lumentum trades about 10.6% below that implied value, compared with a 4.9% gap at Friday's close. Together, the two stocks erased nearly $28 billion of market value on Monday.

The bright side is that Lumentum's stock has still nearly doubled in 2026. But anyone buying it today is really buying Marvell stock, with a 10.6% discount and a long regulatory wait. I'd want to like Marvell a lot before signing up for that, and even then, I'd rather just buy Marvell stock.

Marvell wants to pair its electrical connectivity chips with Lumentum's lasers and optical components, as AI data centers shift from copper to light-based connections. The companies expect more than $1 billion in annual cost savings and estimate a combined market opportunity of $550 billion.

Story Continues

The fairly modest discount is not worth Lumentum's complications and the non-zero risk of a canceled deal.

news.Title: Marvell to purchase Lumentum for $115 billion in record-breaking AI tech deal, both stocks tank
news.Content:
What happened: Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) shares fell more than 10% on Monday after the chip designer announced it will acquire optical component maker Lumentum ( LITE ) in a deal valued at $115 billion. The transaction would be the largest merger between two publicly traded companies on record. Lumentum shares also fell 15% following the announcement.

What's behind the move: Lumentum stock tanked following the announcement as the deal's all-stock structure leaves investors exposed to Marvell's recent sell-off. Under the agreement, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each share owned.

While that exchange ratio initially implied a valuation of $1,132 per share based on Oct. 28 prices, Marvell's recent drop has steadily eroded the payout's actual value.

The record-breaking agreement is expected to expand the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion, according to the announcement.

"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," Matt Murphy, chairman and CEO of Marvell, said on Monday.

What else you need to know: The acquisition gives Marvell greater access to optical technologies and manufacturing capacity, which have become critical bottlenecks of the AI infrastructure build-out.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical components as increasingly powerful AI systems require faster connections. Marvell, which competes with Broadcom ( AVGO ), designs high-speed infrastructure and custom chips that enable AI computers to communicate with one another.

Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company."

The company joined the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) index in June. Marvell shares are up more than 120% year to date. Lumentum shares have rallied more than 100%.

news.Title: Cathie Wood Makes Major Shift After Big Tech Gains
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest made a notable portfolio rotation last week, loading up on Teradyne ( NASDAQ:TER ) and AeroVironment ( NASDAQ:AVAV ) while taking profits in several major winners including Advanced Micro Devices ( NASDAQ:AMD ), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( NYSE:TSM ) and Eli Lilly ( NYSE:LLY ).

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with TER.

Is TER fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The moves suggest ARK is shifting fresh capital toward robotics, defense and autonomous technologies after strong corporate results, while trimming areas where stocks have already delivered substantial gains.

Teradyne was one of the biggest additions.

On Oct. 28, ARK purchased roughly 74,700 Teradyne shares across three ETFs , including about $16.9 million through ARKK alone. The buying followed Teradyne's third-quarter earnings report and an outlook pointing to continued AI-driven demand and a larger compute ramp during 2027.

AeroVironment was another major target.

ARK added the drone and autonomous-systems company on multiple days, including roughly $8.3 million worth of shares across ARKQ and ARKX on Oct. 27 , before adding more the following day. The purchases fit ARK's growing interest in defense technology, drones and autonomous systems.

At the same time, Wood continued taking money off the table in semiconductor names.

ARK sold AMD and TSMC shares repeatedly during the week after both stocks posted strong gains earlier in the year. On Oct. 27 alone, ARK sold roughly $16.2 million of AMD and about $10.6 million of TSMC , according to trade disclosures.

Eli Lilly also became a source of cash.

ARK sold roughly $24 million of LLY shares on Oct. 30 , reducing its position after the drugmaker's strong run.

Investor Takeaway

I think the bigger story is the rotation , not any single trade.

ARK is not abandoning AI or semiconductors. Instead, Wood appears to be harvesting gains from established winners and redeploying capital toward areas where she sees more asymmetric upside, particularly robotics, drones, autonomous aviation and AI-linked industrial technology.

That is classic ARK behavior.

For investors following Wood's positioning, the key names to watch are Teradyne, AeroVironment, Archer Aviation, Joby Aviation and Kratos , while continued selling in AMD, TSMC and other large winners could show where ARK believes expectations have already become more fully priced.

Wood is still betting on disruptive technology.

She is just changing where she wants the next dollar invested.

news.Title: Why Marvell Stock Is Tumbling Today
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Marvell Technology ( NASDAQ:MRVL ) agreed to acquire Lumentum (LITE) in an all-stock transaction that values the optical networking company at approximately $1,132 per share.

Marvell shares slipped about 5% in the morning session.

Once completed, Marvell shareholders are expected to hold 67% of the combined business, with the remaining 33% belonging to Lumentum investors. The offer represents a 23.9% premium to the companies' closing prices on Oct. 28.

Marvell will retain leadership of the combined company, with CEO Matt Murphy at the helm. Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston will join an expanded board. The deal is targeted for completion in the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

news.Title: 美股這波快跌完了？大摩：這個指數六成股票已跌過兩成
news.Content:
摩根士丹利(MS-US)認為，美股自6月展開的修正已接近尾聲。該行指出，羅素3000指數成分股中，已有六成自6月以來一度回檔至少20%，近期標普500指數也開始補跌。這類個股先跌、大盤指數隨後跟進的走勢，通常出現在修正後段。11月3日美國期中選舉結果出爐後，市場可望排除一項主要不確定因素。

摩根士丹利美股首席策略師Michael Wilson領軍的團隊周一(2日)表示，接近年底之際，若選舉等不確定因素陸續消退，先前估值下修、基本面仍佳的景氣循環股，可望為布局2027年的投資人提供加碼機會。

近期賣壓集中在科技股。市場擔心AI企業財報可能引發更大範圍的修正，以科技股為主的那斯達克100指數10月市值蒸發數兆美元，一度逼近修正區間。Wilson也從這波財報看見市場評價企業的方式正在改變：投資人過去往往願意容忍自由現金流不如預期，如今更在意企業能否持續獲利，以及帳面獲利能否真正轉化為現金。他認為，這種轉變符合經濟循環進入中後期的特徵。

就選舉而言，摩根士丹利指出，從歷史經驗來看，美國大型股在期中選舉結果揭曉後的六個月，漲幅通常約為15%。該行認為，投資人已將民主黨拿下參眾兩院的情境反映在價格中，較值得留意的是選後政策風險，包括美國與伊朗的軍事衝突可能再度升高，或美方推出新關稅。

Wilson預期，聯準會(Fed)不會急於降息或採取其他措施支撐市場。短期資金面的助力可能來自美國財政部：若財政部動用現金支付政府支出，其現金餘額可望從約1.05兆美元降至年底的8,500億美元，為市場挹注流動性。

Intel INTC offers another useful comparison as Arm expands into higher-performance CPUs. news.Title: Lumentum to Join Marvell in AI Optical Connectivity Push
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Lumentum Holdings Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Marvell and Lumentum agreed to combine, aiming to create a leading provider of integrated electrical and optical connectivity for AI data centers. Lumentum's CEO and two directors are expected to join Marvell's board, while deal terms were not disclosed.

The companies are targeting growing demand for near-packaged and co-packaged optics as copper connections face bandwidth and energy-efficiency limits. Marvell estimates the combined addressable market could reach $550 billion by 2030 , while Lumentum cited a new NPO/CPO win expected to generate over $5 billion in revenue.

Marvell expects more than $1 billion in annual run-rate synergies , primarily from cost savings, with the deal projected to boost margins and non-GAAP earnings per share beginning in the first year after closing.

Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Marvell said it has agreed to combine with Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) , positioning the proposed transaction as a move to build a larger provider of optical connectivity technology for artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

Marvell Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy said the combination would bring together Marvell's electrical connectivity portfolio and Lumentum's photonics capabilities as AI data centers increasingly adopt optical technologies to address performance, bandwidth and energy-efficiency requirements.

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

The AI Sell-Off Continues—These 3 Stocks Keep Raising Guidance Anyway

"By combining the two companies, we expect to define and become a category leader for the next generation of AI connectivity," Murphy said during a conference call announcing the deal.

The companies did not discuss transaction consideration or other deal terms during the call. Murphy said Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston and two other Lumentum directors are expected to join Marvell's seven-member board after the transaction closes.

Focus on Integrated Optical Connectivity

→ 3 Robotics ETFs, 3 Different Ways to Bet on Humanoid Robots

Why Light Is the New AI Bottleneck—And 3 Photonics Stocks to Play It

Executives described an industry shift in which optical interconnects move closer to computing hardware as copper-based connections encounter physical limitations at higher bandwidths. Marvell and Lumentum said this transition extends beyond existing scale-across and scale-out data-center networks to scale-up and eventually scale-in architectures.

Story Continues

Hurlston said those emerging applications require more tightly integrated optical solutions, including near-packaged optics, or NPO, and co-packaged optics, or CPO. He said combining the companies would enable joint design across the electrical and optical signal chain, including lasers, photodetectors, digital signal processors, transimpedance amplifiers, drivers and silicon photonics.

→ MarketBeat Week in Review – 10/26 - 10/30

"The market is sending us a strong signal that the next wave of explosive growth in AI connectivity cannot be satisfied solely by discrete point solutions," Hurlston said.

Lumentum also announced what Hurlston called its second major NPO and CPO win, which the company expects to generate more than $5 billion in revenue. He did not identify the customer or provide a timeline for that revenue.

Marvell estimates that the combined company's total addressable market could reach $550 billion by 2030. Murphy said most of the incremental opportunity identified by the companies is expected to come from NPO and CPO technologies.

Manufacturing and Ecosystem Strategy

The executives emphasized Lumentum's manufacturing footprint for indium phosphide, a compound semiconductor used in lasers and other optical components. Hurlston said Lumentum owns what it describes as the world's largest indium phosphide manufacturing footprint and is investing to expand capacity for laser products.

Marvell, which is fabless, said it plans to continue working with semiconductor supply-chain partners and investing in production capacity needed to support expected demand for AI connectivity products.

Murphy said the companies would retain their existing go-to-market approach in established optical markets, including sales of components to the broader module ecosystem. Addressing analyst concerns about potential competition with module makers that use Marvell components or Lumentum lasers, Murphy and Hurlston said the industry already operates through a mix of partnership and competition.

Hurlston said Lumentum supplies lasers to many companies that also compete with it, while Marvell supplies digital signal processors and other components to module manufacturers. Both executives said they intend to continue supporting those customers.

Expected Financial Benefits

Marvell CFO Dan Durn said the companies expect more than $1 billion of run-rate synergies, primarily from cost of goods sold. He said the transaction is expected to accelerate revenue growth and be accretive to Marvell's non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating margin and non-GAAP earnings per share beginning in the first year after closing.

Based on Marvell's current-quarter guidance and Lumentum's reported results, Marvell presented pro forma annualized revenue of $17.7 billion and a non-GAAP operating margin of 39%. Murphy said that combining Lumentum's next-quarter guidance with consensus expectations for Marvell's next quarter would imply annualized revenue above $21 billion and a non-GAAP operating margin in the low-40% range.

Murphy said Marvell's previously presented standalone growth plans remain unchanged and that the Lumentum combination is incremental to those plans. He added that the companies expect revenue synergies from broader product offerings and closer customer relationships, although he did not quantify those expected revenue benefits.

Why the Companies Are Combining Now

In response to questions about timing, Murphy said the deal was not driven by short-term supply constraints in indium phosphide or elsewhere in the industry. Instead, he said both companies see the transition toward scale-up optical connectivity as already underway.

"This is fundamentally a shift in the architecture inside the data center," Murphy said, citing Marvell's view of customer designs, volumes and demand for light sources.

Hurlston said Lumentum considered remaining independent and pursuing semiconductor acquisitions of its own, but concluded that a combination with Marvell offered a more compelling route to address scale-up and scale-in opportunities. He said Lumentum expects its standalone business momentum to continue, while the combination could accelerate its ability to co-design and market integrated optical solutions.

About Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE)

Lumentum Holdings Inc is a technology company that designs and manufactures optical and photonic products for communications networks, industrial applications, and consumer electronics. Its portfolio includes optical components, modules, and subsystems used in fiber-optic networks, data centers, cloud computing infrastructure, telecommunications equipment, and high-speed connectivity systems.

The company also develops laser products for applications such as industrial processing, sensing, three-dimensional imaging, and other specialized commercial and consumer uses.

news.Title: Datadog Before Q3 Earnings: What's in the Cards for the Stock?
news.Content:
Datadog, Inc. DDOG is scheduled to report its third-quarter 2026 results before the market opens on Nov. 4.

For the third quarter, Datadog expects revenues between $1.135 billion and $1.145 billion and non-GAAP earnings between 63 cents and 65 cents per share.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for DDOG's third-quarter revenues is pegged at $1.14 billion, indicating 28.9% year-over-year growth.

The consensus mark for earnings stands at 64 cents per share, suggesting an improvement of 16.4% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings remains unchanged over the past 30 days.

Datadog, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Datadog, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Datadog, Inc. Quote

Datadog surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings in each of the trailing four quarters, delivering an average surprise of 15.39%. In the last reported quarter, the company delivered an earnings surprise of 12.07%.

Let us see how things have shaped up ahead of the upcoming announcement.

Factors Likely to Shape DDOG's Q3 Results

Accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and cloud consumption are expected to have supported Datadog's revenues in the third quarter of 2026. The company ended the second quarter with more than 750 AI customers, including hyperscalers using its platform for in-house AI labs. Meanwhile, revenue growth from non-AI customers accelerated to the high-20% range from the mid-20% range in the preceding quarter. Enterprises deploying AI workloads increasingly require unified visibility across applications, infrastructure and models. These trends are likely to have driven higher platform usage and strengthened demand for Datadog's observability solutions in the to-be-reported quarter.

Datadog's expanding enterprise footprint and multiproduct adoption are likely to have boosted revenues in the quarter under review. At the end of the second quarter, approximately 4,720 customers generated at least $100,000 in annual recurring revenues, up 23% year over year. Moreover, 58% of customers used four or more products, up from 52% a year earlier, while enterprise new-logo annualized bookings more than doubled. Stronger cross-selling, rising customer commitments and faster ramp-up of new accounts are expected to have supported additional consumption and recurring revenue growth in the third quarter.

Continued product innovation is expected to have strengthened Datadog's competitive position and upselling opportunities in the third quarter. At its June DASH event, the company introduced more than 100 capabilities, including autonomous Bits AI for incident detection, investigation and remediation, AI Guard for agent security, and Bring Your Own Cloud for customer-controlled data environments. It also made Bits Code, Bits Chat and Bits Agent Builder generally available. These enhancements broaden Datadog's relevance across DevOps, security and AI operations, likely supporting product adoption and deeper customer engagement in the quarter under review.

However, reduced consumption by Datadog's largest customer is expected to have weighed on third-quarter revenue momentum. The customer, a leading AI company using 17 Datadog products, renewed a nine-figure agreement but began reducing usage in the third quarter of 2026. Datadog incorporated the decline into its outlook. Its AI-native cohort contributed high-single-digit percentage points to companywide year-over-year revenue growth in the second quarter, highlighting sensitivity to spending shifts among major AI accounts. The usage pullback is likely to have offset some benefits from broader demand and constrained growth in the quarter under review.

news.Title: Marvell Technology Targets $550B AI Optics Market With Lumentum Deal

Key Points

Interested in Marvell Technology, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Marvell agreed to combine with Lumentum to unite Marvell's electrical connectivity products with Lumentum's optical technologies and manufacturing, targeting rising AI data-center demand for integrated optical networking.

The companies estimate a combined total addressable market of $550 billion by 2030 , driven largely by near-packaged and co-packaged optics as copper connections face growing bandwidth and distance limitations.

Marvell expects the deal to generate more than $1 billion in annual run-rate synergies and be accretive to non-GAAP margins and earnings per share in the first year after closing, although transaction terms were not disclosed.

Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) said it has agreed to combine with photonics provider Lumentum, positioning the combined company to pursue growing demand for optical connectivity in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Marvell Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy said the transaction would bring together Marvell's electrical connectivity portfolio with Lumentum's optical technologies and manufacturing capabilities. He described the deal as a step toward creating a category leader in AI connectivity, particularly as data-center architectures shift from copper-based connections toward more integrated optical systems.

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

5 Beaten-Down Growth Stocks Trading Like Value Plays as Cash Chases Mega-Caps

"The next decade of networking will be defined by optics, just as electrical SerDes defined the previous era," Murphy said during a conference call announcing the proposed transaction.

Focus on AI Infrastructure and Integrated Optics

Executives from both companies said rising bandwidth needs, performance requirements and energy-efficiency demands are pushing optical interconnects closer to computing systems. They described the industry transition through several networking domains, including scale-across, scale-out, scale-up and scale-in architectures.

→ 3 Robotics ETFs, 3 Different Ways to Bet on Humanoid Robots

Q3 Earnings Could Blow Past Consensus—Be Ready for What Comes Next

According to Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston, copper connections remain common inside racks, trays and packages, but their effective reach declines as next-generation processing units support larger AI clusters and more intensive inference workloads. He said this limitation, which the companies called the "copper wall," is increasing the need for optical connectivity nearer to the compute engine.

Story Continues

Hurlston said Lumentum recently secured its second major near-packaged optics, or NPO, and co-packaged optics, or CPO, win. The company expects that win to generate more than $5 billion in revenue, though it did not provide a timeline.

→ MarketBeat Week in Review – 10/26 - 10/30

The combined company would seek to offer co-designed products spanning lasers, photodetectors, digital signal processors, transimpedance amplifiers, drivers and silicon photonics. Executives said integrated offerings could help customers reduce power consumption, improve performance and shorten development cycles compared with sourcing components from multiple vendors.

Murphy said the companies estimate their combined total addressable market could reach $550 billion by 2030, with much of the incremental opportunity coming from NPO and CPO technologies. He said scale-up optics are expected to begin ramping next year, while scale-in opportunities are expected to emerge later.

Manufacturing and Customer Ecosystem

Lumentum brings what Hurlston described as the world's largest indium phosphide manufacturing footprint. Indium phosphide is a compound semiconductor material used in lasers and other optical components. Hurlston said Lumentum owns and operates specialty fabrication facilities and combines internal capacity with contract manufacturing for back-end assembly and testing.

Murphy said Marvell would continue its existing relationships with semiconductor supply-chain partners, including foundries and advanced-packaging providers. He said the combined company intends to continue investing "multiple billions of dollars" with supply-chain partners to support anticipated AI-connectivity demand.

Executives also addressed questions about whether the combination could create conflicts with existing optical-module customers. Marvell supplies components such as coherent digital signal processors, drivers and transimpedance amplifiers to module manufacturers, while Lumentum supplies lasers to many companies with which it also competes in certain markets.

Murphy said Marvell plans to maintain a flexible business model that supports both merchant components and modules, while Hurlston said Lumentum would continue supplying lasers across the ecosystem. Both executives said customers had expressed support for the combination.

Financial Outlook and Governance

Marvell Chief Financial Officer Dan Durn said the companies expect more than $1 billion in run-rate synergies, primarily from cost of goods sold. He said the transaction is expected to be accretive to non-GAAP gross margin, operating margin and earnings per share beginning in the first year after closing.

Murphy cited pro forma figures of $17.7 billion in annualized revenue and a 39% non-GAAP operating margin. He added that combining Lumentum's next-quarter guidance with consensus expectations for Marvell's next quarter would imply annualized revenue above $21 billion and a non-GAAP operating margin in the low 40% range.

The companies did not provide transaction terms during the call. Murphy said that following the close, Hurlston and two other Lumentum board members are expected to join Marvell's existing seven-member board.

Both leaders emphasized that the rationale for the deal extends beyond current supply constraints. Murphy said the companies view the transaction as a response to a broader architectural change in AI data centers, while Hurlston said Lumentum's standalone business remains strong but could pursue scale-up and scale-in opportunities more effectively alongside Marvell's semiconductor platform.

Its products are designed to support the movement, processing, storage and security of data across complex computing and communications environments.

The company's portfolio includes data-processing and networking processors, custom application-specific integrated circuits, Ethernet switches and controllers, storage controllers, connectivity products, and electro-optics solutions.

news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices AMD is set to release its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 3.

AMD expects third-quarter 2026 revenues of $13 billion (+/-$300 million). At the midpoint of the revenue range, this represents year-over-year growth of 41% and 13% sequentially.

Consensus Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AMD beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings in all the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 6.74%.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Quote

Let's see how things have shaped up for the upcoming earnings announcement.

Factors to Note Ahead of AMD's Q3 Results

AMD's third-quarter 2026 performance is likely to have benefited significantly from accelerating adoption of EPYC server processors across hyperscale cloud providers and enterprise customers. Growing AI inference and agentic AI workloads are driving demand for high-performance CPUs capable of managing data retrieval, workflow orchestration and AI processing tasks. The company's fifth-generation EPYC Turin and fourth-generation EPYC Genoa processors have continued gaining traction across cloud and enterprise environments. The introduction of sixth-generation EPYC Venice processors, based on Zen 6 architecture and 2-nanometer technology, is expected to have strengthened AMD's competitive positioning.

The Data Center segment is likely to have benefited from increasing adoption of Instinct MI350-series GPUs across AI training and inference workloads. Demand for MI355X accelerators has strengthened as AI developers and cloud service providers expand deployments. The initial production shipments of AMD's Helios rack-scale AI platform, powered by MI450-series GPUs, EPYC Venice processors and Pensando networking, are also expected to have contributed to third-quarter revenues. However, Helios contributions are expected to have been relatively modest in the to-be-reported quarter.

AMD's Client business is likely to have benefited from continued Ryzen processor adoption, particularly across commercial notebooks, enterprise PCs and AI-enabled systems. Expanding adoption of Ryzen AI PRO 400-series processors across systems offered by Dell, HP, Lenovo and ASUS is expected to have supported market-share gains. Growing enterprise interest in local AI inference and AI-powered productivity applications may have provided additional opportunities for the Ryzen AI portfolio. Although management anticipated softer overall PC demand, AMD expected its Client business to outperform the broader market, supported by commercial customer adoption and product competitiveness.

Meanwhile, AMD's Embedded segment is expected to have aided third-quarter performance as demand recovered across networking, communications, aerospace and defense, test and measurement and industrial applications. The growing adoption of embedded x86 processors in data center networking and control-plane functions is likely to have strengthened the segment's growth trajectory. The third-quarter profitability is likely to have benefited from a growing contribution from higher-margin EPYC server processors and a recovery in the Embedded segment. Increasing Data Center revenues are expected to have supported gross profit expansion, while rising scale across AMD's product portfolio may have improved operating leverage.

However, AMD continues to face stiff competition from NVIDIA NVDA, Broadcom AVGO and Intel INTC. AMD faces intense competition from NVIDIA in AI accelerators and Intel in server and client processors. The growing adoption of internally developed AI accelerators by hyperscalers, along with Arm-based server processors, adds competitive pressure. Broadcom is increasing competitive pressure on AMD by strengthening its position in custom AI accelerators and high-performance networking for hyperscale customers.

Story Continues

AMD Stock Outperforms Sector & Peers

Advanced Micro Devices shares have surged 135.7% year to date (YTD), outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 9.7%. The company's shares have outperformed Intel, NVIDIA and Broadcom YTD. Shares of Intel and NVIDIA have appreciated 78.2% and 9.8%, respectively, while Broadcom dropped 5.8%.

AMD's Share Price Performance

The AMD stock is not so cheap, as its Value Score of F suggests a stretched valuation at this moment.

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, AMD is currently trading at 10.27X, higher than the sector's 5.17X, NVIDIA's 8.03X and Intel's 4.85X, but lower than Broadcom's 14.64X.

AMD Stock's Valuation

AMD Rides on Strong Portfolio Amid Stiff Competition

AMD is positioned to capitalize on accelerating investments in AI infrastructure as hyperscalers, cloud providers and enterprises expand AI training, inference and agentic computing capabilities. The company expects the Data Center AI accelerator market to reach approximately $1.4 trillion by 2030, growing at an annual rate exceeding 45%. Increasing demand for GPUs, server CPUs and networking solutions provides AMD with a substantial opportunity to expand its presence across AI infrastructure. The company expects Data Center segment revenues to more than double year over year in 2027, supported by the increasing scale of AI deployments and strong demand for EPYC processors.

AMD's transition toward integrated rack-scale AI infrastructure represents a significant long-term growth catalyst. The Helios platform combines MI450-series GPUs, EPYC Venice CPUs, Pensando networking and ROCm software to deliver competitive AI inference performance and economics. The company expects substantial Helios shipment growth beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026 and accelerating throughout 2027. Strategic relationships with OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic provide multi-generation deployment opportunities, while Microsoft's Azure adoption broadens AMD's presence among major cloud providers. Beyond Helios, the planned MI500-series GPU platform, along with Verano CPUs and next-generation networking technologies, is expected to strengthen AMD's ability to compete for increasingly complex AI workloads.

Conclusion

AMD's strong AI infrastructure portfolio, accelerating EPYC adoption and expanding hyperscaler partnerships position it well for long-term growth. However, stiff competition from NVIDIA, Broadcom and Intel, alongside a stretched valuation, remains a concern. Moreover, the stock's impressive year-to-date rally suggests that much of the optimism surrounding its AI growth prospects may already be priced in. Investors should therefore adopt a cautious approach and wait for greater clarity on the Helios ramp and earnings growth before taking fresh positions in AMD stock.

AMD currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Will Analog Devices (ADI) Beat Estimates Again in Its Next Earnings Report?
news.Content:
Looking for a stock that has been consistently beating earnings estimates and might be well positioned to keep the streak alive in its next quarterly report? Analog Devices (ADI), which belongs to the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry, could be a great candidate to consider.

When looking at the last two reports, this semiconductor maker has recorded a strong streak of surpassing earnings estimates. The company has topped estimates by 5.26%, on average, in the last two quarters.

For the last reported quarter, Analog Devices came out with earnings of $3.45 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.33 per share, representing a surprise of 3.60%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $2.89 per share and it actually produced earnings of $3.09 per share, delivering a surprise of 6.92%.

Price and EPS Surprise

For Analog Devices, estimates have been trending higher, thanks in part to this earnings surprise history. And when you look at the stock's positive Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction), it's a great indicator of a future earnings beat, especially when combined with its solid Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Analog Devices has an Earnings ESP of +2.23% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on November 24, 2026.

With the Earnings ESP metric, it's important to note that a negative value reduces its predictive power; however, a negative Earnings ESP does not indicate an earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, but that may not be the sole basis for their stocks moving higher. On the other hand, some stocks may hold their ground even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

news.Title: Is UCTT Worth Buying as Growth Accelerates but Cash Flow Weakens?
news.Content:
Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. UCTT is benefiting from accelerating semiconductor equipment demand, with earnings and profitability moving sharply higher. The investment question is whether that operating momentum can overcome weak cash conversion and a capital-intensive expansion cycle.

That trade-off is especially important because stronger reported profits have not yet translated into equally strong cash generation or capital returns. Investors must weigh improving estimates and margins against funding needs, customer concentration and execution risk.

UCTT's Earnings Momentum Is Building

Third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings reached $1.15 per share, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 91 cents by 26.4%. Revenues increased 48.8% year over year to $759 million and exceeded the consensus estimate by 4.6%.

The outlook points to another step up if current expectations hold. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for fiscal 2027 revenues of $3.788 billion and earnings of $6.63 per share, compared with projected 2026 revenues of $2.768 billion and earnings of $3.40 per share.

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Quote

Ultra Clean Has a Clear Margin Opportunity

Profitability is improving as higher volumes increase factory utilization. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 17.3% in the third quarter, up from 16.7% sequentially, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 9% from 7%.

Management continues to target roughly 20% gross margin at about $4 billion of annual revenues. Higher utilization, greater vertical integration, a richer mix of engineered products and more production in lower-cost regions are expected to support that goal as capacity fills.

UCTT's Cash Conversion Is the Main Warning

The earnings improvement has not yet produced healthy cash conversion. Trailing 12-month cash-flow conversion was negative 244.4%, while free-cash-flow conversion was negative 418.5%, well below UCTT's historical medians.

Working capital is absorbing substantial cash. Inventory rose to $723.3 million, and operating activities used $42.3 million in the third quarter as Ultra Clean built critical components and safety stock. Trailing 12-month return on invested capital of 4.6% also remained below its 10-year company median of 9.8%.

Ultra Clean Still Carries Concentration Risk

Customer concentration remains a structural risk. Lam Research Corporation LRCX represented 39% of third-quarter revenues, while Applied Materials, Inc. AMAT accounted for 22%. Together, the two customers contributed 61%, leaving UCTT sensitive to their production schedules, sourcing decisions and wafer-fab-equipment spending.

Both customers are operating in supportive end markets. Lam reported September-quarter revenues of $8.22 billion and said AI was driving higher semiconductor demand and device complexity. Applied Materials posted record fiscal third-quarter revenues of $9.12 billion and cited AI-driven demand across leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging. Their strength supports the industry backdrop, but it does not remove UCTT's dependence on a small customer base.

Story Continues

UCTT's Ratings Favor Momentum Over Growth Quality

The bottom line is that UCTT offers accelerating earnings and a credible margin-expansion path, but the investment case is not clean. Cash conversion, low capital returns and concentration risk argue for discipline even as semiconductor demand strengthens.

UCTT currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which is favorable from an earnings-estimate revision perspective. Its Momentum Score of A adds support for near-term price and earnings momentum. However, the Growth Score of D, Value Score of C and VGM Score of C indicate a less consistent profile across growth quality, valuation and combined style characteristics. That mix favors investors who prioritize momentum while recognizing that cash-flow and execution issues remain unresolved.
