news.Content:
Nobody has to double their money every year to build real wealth. An investor who puts $10,000 into a stock that returns 15% annually and holds it for 40 years ends up with about $2.7 million. That takes patience, not a lucky guess.

Reaching for stocks that promise to multiply overnight makes that outcome less likely, not more, because a single collapse can wipe out years of compounding. That tension is the subject of our look at whether Sandisk can keep climbing after a 1,322% gain in a year .

Hedge funds work from the opposite instinct. On average, they don't load up on lottery-ticket stocks. They back companies they judge most likely to deliver higher returns for an amount of risk they can live with.

Bubble Warnings Spread as Retail Traders Pull Back

Veteran voices are urging care. Yahoo Finance reported on October 9 that Bridgewater Associates' Ray Dalio said the market is close to bubble territory. Panmure Liberum head market strategist Joachim Klement expects the AI bubble to burst in either 2027 or 2028, according to Bloomberg . Meanwhile, Bank of America Securities' Jill Carey Hall wrote in a client note that retail clients were net buyers, the first retail inflows since late July.

Everyday traders have cooled off since then. Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider wrote in a note that retail trading volumes have fallen about 20% since mid-summer, and retail made up 9% of US equity volume, near its lowest level since 2020, according to Yahoo Finance on October 26. You might also be interested in reading our piece on whether Palantir can justify a multiple five times its sector's .

The speculative money has not gone quiet, though. Snider's note showed retail trading in leveraged index funds running at roughly double the pace of ordinary funds tracking the same indexes, and Robinhood data pointed to retail options trading nearly doubling over the past year.

So, what are the best meme stocks to buy? For an expanded list, check out 10 Best Meme Stocks to Invest In . We provided the top 5 meme stocks below. As you will notice last year's meme stocks such as AMC, GameStop (GME), and Opendoor (OPEN) didn't make our list.

Our Methodology

To compile this list, we searched Instagram Reels for stocks promoted by financial influencers and tallied how often each one was pitched. We kept the 20 most frequently pitched stocks, excluding any company with a market cap above $500 billion, and ranked the 10 with the most hedge fund holders in ascending order. Hedge fund data is as of Q2 2026, from our database of 1,006 hedge funds.

Story Continues

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 599.2% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 372 percentage points ( see more details here ).

5 Best Meme Stocks to Invest In

5. Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET)

Market Cap: $212.97 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 91

Arista Networks' second quarter was its first above $3 billion in revenue, at $3.036 billion. Sales grew 37.7% from a year earlier and 12.1% from the first quarter, and the company's own forecast calls for about $3.3 billion this quarter. Chief executive Jayshree Ullal said customers see networking as the center of how their infrastructure runs.

Arista makes the switches that connect servers inside data centers, and AI clusters need a lot of them. The company has built a line of AI networking products that sit at the heart of its strategy, and its balance sheet shows the demand building. Current deferred revenue stood at $5,100.7 million at the end of June, up from $4,002.6 million at the end of 2025. The long-term portion grew too, from $1,369.8 million to $1,765.2 million. Both balances were higher at the end of June than at the start of the year.

Arista reports its next quarter this week, so fresh numbers are only days away.

Readers can see how that cash cushion plays out in our breakdown of Arista's deferred revenue and cash flow .

4. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL)

Market Cap: $172.22 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 96

Marvell chief executive Matt Murphy said AI-related bookings remain exceptionally strong and that he expects revenue growth to speed up through the rest of the fiscal year. The quarter already shows it in the numbers. Revenue rose 37% from a year earlier to a record $2.739 billion, about $39.0 million above the midpoint of the company's own guidance, and growth in the data center business accelerated to 46%.

For the current quarter, Marvell guided to $3.150 billion in revenue, plus or minus 5%. Murphy pointed to strong demand for its connectivity products and a significant acceleration in the custom chip business starting in the second half of the fiscal year.

Murphy described the strength as broad-based across the data center portfolio. Marvell also raised its revenue outlook again, for both this fiscal year and the next, compared with the guidance it gave last quarter. With connectivity and custom chips both gaining at once, the company has two growth drivers feeding the same data center buildout.

Our analysis of whether Marvell's growth can justify its premium covers that story in more depth.

3. GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV)

Market Cap: $227.06 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 106

GE Vernova's orders nearly doubled in the third quarter. They reached $29 billion, up 96% on an organic basis, led by equipment orders at its Power business while services stayed strong. The backlog grew by $20 billion from the previous quarter to $197 billion. Chief executive Scott Strazik said he now expects the backlog to pass $200 billion in the fourth quarter, with better margins on the work.

Gas turbines are a big part of that pile, and the Power business is leading the way. Gas Power equipment backlog and slot reservation agreements rose from 116 gigawatts to 122 gigawatts, and the company expects to reach at least 130 gigawatts by the end of 2026. Strazik also pointed to rising demand for electricity infrastructure around the world.

Management raised its 2026 guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow, and the board doubled the share repurchase authorization from $10 billion to $20 billion. Chief financial officer Ken Parks said the higher guidance reflects that momentum.

The stock's price measured against that demand gets a full look in our analysis of GE Vernova's backlog and valuation .

2. Vistra (NYSE:VST)

Market Cap: $46.44 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 111

Vistra will be the preferred power supplier to a new data center venture backed by KKR, Kuwait Investment Authority and Nvidia, and the company has committed up to $1.0 billion to it. The venture, called Helix Digital Infrastructure, gives Vistra a direct line to large technology buyers that need dependable electricity.

The core business is earning more. Second-quarter adjusted EBITDA from ongoing operations reached $1,767 million, up from $1,349 million a year earlier, a gain of more than 30%. Management reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8 billion to $7.6 billion, and about 100% of expected 2026 generation was already hedged. That guidance leaves out both the pending Cogentrix acquisition and the agreements with Meta.

Vistra has signed power purchase agreements with Meta, and part of them is expected to add to 2027 earnings. Chief executive Jim Burke said the fleet was available more than 97% of the time during recent extreme heat in Texas and the PJM grid. Vistra has also bought back about $6.5 billion of its stock since late 2021.

Management's own buying drew attention in our piece on how Vistra's CEO bought stock after the selloff , which asked whether AI power demand is mispriced.

1. Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK)

Market Cap: $166.34 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 128

Sandisk's revenue for the fiscal first quarter jumped 378% from a year earlier to $11,031 million, and management guided to $12,200 million to $12,600 million for the next quarter. Gross margin was 85.0%, which means most of each sales dollar stayed with the company.

Data center was the standout. Revenue there reached $4,802 million, up 61% from the previous quarter. Chief executive David Goeckeler said the company is executing on the strategy it laid out at its investor day, and he credited its technology leadership, customer partnerships and disciplined financial management. The aim, he said, is growing and durable free cash flow.

Sandisk also announced an 8-for-1 stock split, which it said is meant to make the shares more accessible, including to employees. Holders of record on the set date will receive seven additional shares for each share they own, and split-adjusted trading is expected to begin later this month. The company noted that the split does not change its market capitalization or anyone's ownership percentage.

Investors who want to test the bullish case against the stock's forward earnings multiple can read our analysis of whether Sandisk's forward multiple already prices in a peak .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of SNDK as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than SNDK that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock .

news.Title: AMD Stock Got Caught in Intel’s Selloff. What to Watch This Week.
news.Content:
Oct. 22 was one of the worst days of the year for chip stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ($SOX) fell 6.7%, its biggest drop since June. Intel (INTC) and AMD (AMD) each lost more than 8% even though neither company had any news that day. Instead, the selloff was triggered by chip equipment maker Lam Research (LRCX) warning that the supply bottlenecks were limiting its shipments. Meta's (META) results also added to the pressure. Its heavy AI spending pushed free cash flow negative for the first time in more than a decade. Both these factors made investors nervous about the AI trade again.

Fast forward a week, on Oct. 29, Intel reported its earnings, and things went from bad to worse. The company beat its guidance, and its data center business grew 78%. However, it guided a weak Q4 outlook, and the stock crashed about 29% in a day, its worst day in over 50 years. This made a direct impact on AMD too. Intel warned about weak PC demand and tight supply. And since AMD also sells PC chips and is struggling to make enough server chips, that was enough to drive another selloff. AMD's stock fell almost 11% in a single trading session.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Buy the Pullback in Alphabet Stock

Micron vs. SanDisk: China's DRAM Scare Hit Both Stocks, but 1 Is the Better Buy

Trump Warns of a '1929-Style Economic Depression' Ahead of the Midterms. The S&P 500 Has Risen After All 19 Midterms Since 1950.

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

AMD reports earnings tomorrow, Nov. 3. It guided about $13 billion in Q3 revenue, which is a growth of 41% year-over-year (YoY) and 13% from the last quarter. So it has a higher bar to clear than Intel, which guided roughly flat and ended up beating its own guidance for the eighth straight quarter.

What Do Intel's Problems Mean for AMD?

One of the issues Intel is facing is that it can't make enough Xeon server chips. I think this could be an opportunity for AMD, since customers may turn to its EPYC chips. But AMD has supply limits too. As I covered earlier, like Intel, AMD is nearly sold out of high-core chips, so it can't simply take every customer Intel can't serve.

There's a lot riding on AMD's earnings report. Investors will be interested to see its data center business growing. But we saw that Intel's data center had its best growth in 15 years and that wasn't enough to save the stock. What will matter more is its Q4 guidance, any comments from management on PC demand, and early Helios deployments. Helios, AMD's full AI server rack, was expected to begin shipping at the end of Q3. So investors will want an update on shipments and how fast the rollout is going.

Story Continues

About AMD Stock

Advanced Micro Devices is a semiconductor company that designs high-performance chips for data centers, PCs, and gaming. Its product portfolio includes EPYC server CPUs and Instinct AI GPUs, which drive its data center growth, along with Ryzen processors. Its EPYC server chips compete directly with Intel's Xeon, which is why Intel's warning hit AMD's stock too. Founded in 1969, the company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

AMD stock is up about 97% over the past year as investors now see it as a serious challenger to Nvidia (NVDA) in AI chips. Large orders from OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic, booming data center sales, rapid profit growth, and tight chip supply have lifted its prospects. Over the past six months, the stock has gained 40%. It reached a 52-week high of $658 in early October, but is down roughly 23% from that level.

Growth Story Is Getting Bigger

Advanced Micro Devices reported its second-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings on Aug. 4. In the second quarter, the company's data center revenue rose 107% year-over-year (YoY) to $6.7 billion, as its AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPUs continued to see strong demand. AMD's total revenue rose 50% YoY to $11.54 billion, above the $11.28 billion Wall Street analysts expected. AMD also highlighted that data center operations account for 58% of its topline. Hence, while the client and gaming segment grew modestly, the data center segment more than made up for it.

Looking forward, the company expects revenue to be approximately $13 billion in Q3. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to be 56%, with non-GAAP operating expenses to be approximately $3.65 billion. The company sees strong customer demand in server CPUs and expects revenue to grow more than 80% YoY in the second half of 2026 and more than 70% for the full year 2027.

What Do Analysts Expect for AMD Stock?

In October, Susquehanna raised the firm's price target on AMD stock from $550 to $620 and kept a "Buy" rating. Ahead of semiconductor companies' earnings reports, the firm expects most companies to slightly beat Q3 earnings expectations and provide stronger-than-expected guidance for Q4.

Chip giant AMD is a widely followed name on Wall Street, with analysts awarding it a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. Of the 47 analysts rating the stock, a majority of 37 analysts have given it a "Strong Buy" rating, two analysts rated it "Moderate Buy," and eight analysts are taking the middle-of-the-road approach with a "Hold" rating. The mean price target of $656.12 represents a 30% upside from current levels.

news.Title: 3 Tech Stocks Boosting Buyback Capacity in the Face of the Sector's Recent Tumble
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Amphenol Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Amid a tech sector sell-off, NXP Semiconductors, Amphenol and F5 announced large buyback authorizations signaling confidence in their future prospects.

NXP added $5 billion in buyback capacity as data center demand grows, while Amphenol unveiled a $4 billion repurchase program alongside a 20% dividend increase.

F5 announced an additional $1.5 billion buyback despite a 20.4% post-earnings stock drop, and analysts see over 40% upside for Amphenol shares.

Investors have hit tech stocks hard over the past few weeks. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSEARCA: XLK), a commonly used proxy for the sector's performance, is down more than 7% in October. Fears around the AI buildout's sustainability and disappointing earnings reports from Big Tech have been key drivers of the decline.

Amid the sell-off, three notable tech stocks are signaling confidence in the future by announcing substantial buyback authorizations. This list includes one name that has ridden the AI wave higher and higher, and others that are just now starting to participate more meaningfully.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

NXP's Data Center Demand Picks Up, Adds Huge Buyback Capacity

First up is NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ: NXPI), a chip stock that is up approximately 17% in 2026. NXP's business primarily serves automotive and industrial customers. While NXP has not been a huge AI winner thus far, data center demand is starting to pick up, with the company expecting its data center revenue to exceed $500 million in 2026. NXP believes this business will scale to over $1 billion in the coming years, and sees physical AI as a long-term growth opportunity.

During its latest earnings call, the firm made a significant buyback announcement, adding an incremental $5 billion in repurchase capacity. This brings the company's total buyback capacity to $6.3 billion. With a market capitalization near $66 billion, this represents around 9.5% of the firm's value, giving it substantial buyback firepower.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

The company also notes that the authorization positions it to accelerate buybacks beginning in Q4, suggesting that its repurchases will increase compared to recent quarters. In Q3, the company spent $103 million on buybacks, significantly below its long-term average.

The planned acceleration suggests the company may see its shares as a strong value at recent levels.

Story Continues

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

AI Winner Amphenol Announces $4 Billion Buyback Program

In contrast to NXP, Amphenol (NYSE: APH) has been a massive beneficiary of the AI boom so far. The stock has posted a moderate but still strong return near 18% in 2026. This comes after shares soared 41% in 2024 and another 96% in 2025.

The connector, cable and sensor maker saw its revenue rise 65% year-over-year (YOY) last quarter to a record $10.2 billion. The company's acquisition of CommScope significantly increased its growth rate, but sales still grew by 37% YOY on an organic basis. Meanwhile, orders increased 99% YOY, with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.19:1, signaling continued demand momentum.

Amphenol indicated confidence in its long-term outlook by announcing a three-year, $4 billion repurchase program. This plan will become effective at the beginning of 2027, with the firm expecting to exhaust the capacity under its previous program by the end of 2026.

Given Amphenol's size, the program represents only about 2.1% of its market capitalization. However, the company is also returning more capital to shareholders through higher dividends. Amphenol announced a 20% dividend increase, after accounting for its recent stock split, moving its payout to 15 cents per share. Amphenol's forward yield is approximately 0.77%.

F5 Holds Huge Buyback Capacity After Dramatic Sell-Off

Last up is cybersecurity company F5 (NASDAQ: FFIV). Despite the market clobbering shares after its latest earnings report, F5 has performed strongly in 2026, up around 32%. Prior to its 20.4% post-earnings drop, F5 shares were up around 80% on the year.

This decline came even as F5 handily beat estimates on sales and earnings per share (EPS). Revenue increased by 13% YOY to $917 million, around $33 million higher than expected. Meanwhile, EPS of $4.42 was 16 cents higher than expected. The company also saw its AI-related offerings exceed $100 million in bookings, up 300% YOY. The bookings primarily came from AI data delivery offerings.

F5 pointed to a slowdown in its forecast for fiscal year 2027, projecting revenue growth of 8% to 9%, down from 11% in 2026.

The company also cited margin pressure as it grapples with higher component costs and invests in pursuing AI opportunities. These factors influenced the stock's sell-off.

During its earnings call, F5 announced an additional $1.5 billion share repurchase program, bringing its total capacity to $1.8 billion. One silver lining of F5's stock price decline is that this added capacity can now buy back many more shares than it otherwise could. F5's buyback capacity is now equal to around 9% of its market capitalization, a hefty figure.

Analysts Eye 40% Upside in Amphenol

Analysts see substantial upside ahead for Amphenol, even after the stock's impressive gains over the past few years. The MarketBeat consensus price target near $112 implies more than 40% upside.

IT datacom sales represented 48% of the company's revenue last quarter, and three-fourths of those sales were related to AI. IT datacom also drove massive growth, increasing 117% YOY in the United States. In turn, Amphenol's fortunes largely depend on the continued expansion of AI data centers, making hyperscaler capital expenditure guidance for 2027 critical to watch.

news.Title: 美股閉眼買都賺的時刻到了？ 選後行情將開跑 專家卻示警3大警訊
news.Content:
美國期中選舉即將登場，美股一項延續超過70年的歷史上漲紀錄，今年恐怕面臨考驗。標普500指數過去在期中選舉後6個月及12個月均呈現上漲，但今年選前漲勢已相當強勁，加上AI投資回報疑慮、油價上揚及政治風險升高，市場能否延續過往行情備受關注。

據英國《金融時報》報導，超過75年來，投資人在期中選舉前最後一個交易日買進美股，持有6個月或12個月均能獲利，上一次選後出現下跌已要追溯至1946年。相較之下，自1950年以來，其他年份相同期間約有三分之一的時間呈現下跌。

選前漲勢強勁 歷史反彈條件與過去不同

過去期中選舉後美股經常上漲，主要原因在於選舉前的不確定性消退，投資人得以重新評估政治格局、政策及企業基本面。不過，今年選前市場表現與過去有所不同。

《金融時報》指出，自1942年以來，標普500指數在期中選舉年的平均高點回落幅度約18%，但今年截至選前最大跌幅僅約9%，顯示市場表現相對強勢。

估值方面，標普500指數的循環調整本益比（CAPE）已達40.7，不僅高於1998年期中選舉前的前次高點33.8，也遠高於自1942年以來約20的平均值。此外，今年前9個月僅5檔股票就貢獻標普500指數超過一半的漲幅，市場漲勢集中於少數大型企業。

AI投資、油價與伊朗局勢增添壓力

除了估值偏高，AI投資能否帶來相應回報，也是市場隱憂。10月科技股遭遇賣壓，投資人擔心AI產生的獲利不足以支撐龐大資金投入，第三季財報也尚未消除相關疑慮。

地緣政治方面，油價上周再度回升至4月以來未見水準，市場猜測美國總統川普可能在選舉結束後加強對伊朗的軍事行動。Jefferies經濟學家Mohit Kumar認為，川普選後重啟轟炸行動的風險偏高，也因此對短期風險資產採取審慎態度。

國會版圖牽動美股 專家解析歷史報酬

政治版圖同樣可能影響選後行情。卡森投資研究公司（Carson Investment Research）的資料顯示，自1951年以來，共和黨總統執政、國會由兩黨分別掌控時，標普500指數平均年報酬率為13.7%；若共和黨總統執政，民主黨同時掌控眾議院與參議院，平均年報酬率則僅有4.9%。

摩根士丹利財富管理美國政策與地緣政治策略主管Monica Guerra指出，重大政策變動減少，可能意味著市場受到的干擾也會降低。

摩根大通全球市場策略師Jordan Jackson則認為，選舉結束後政治格局更加明朗，市場通常能重新聚焦基本面與政策。

不過，今年美股面臨的高估值、AI投資回報疑慮及地緣政治風險，與過去選前市場疲弱的情況不同。即使選舉後不確定性消退，標普500指數能否延續長達數十年的上漲紀錄，仍有待市場檢驗。

news.Title: Morgan Stanley stands by Sandisk as CFO flags a low-end pullback
news.Content:
If you bought $1,000 worth of Sandisk Corp. (SNDK) stock at Wednesday's close, it was worth about $819 by Friday's close. Two trading days were all it took.

Shares fell roughly 18% across Thursday, October 29, and Friday, October 30, 2026, ending at $1,150.89 , according to StockAnalysis data . With about 142 million shares outstanding, that erased roughly $36 billion in market value.

The selling followed a record quarter. Sandisk's fiscal first-quarter revenue hit $11 billion, up 378% from a year earlier, according to its earnings release .

Also read: Sandisk CFO admits higher prices are hurting consumer sales

Sandisk's weak spot is the cheap end of the market

Edge, Sandisk's biggest unit, sells flash memory to phone and PC makers, and it grew just 7% from the prior quarter. Chief Financial Officer Luis Visoso explained why on the earnings call . He described resilience in premium and mainstream devices, "partially offset by contraction at the lower end."

That is the admission that matters, and it reaches past the consumer sales slump . Sandisk's quarterly filing shows Edge customers bought 20% less flash by volume than a year earlier. They still paid far more in total, because the price per gigabyte soared.

The squeeze is industry-wide. HP Inc. (HPQ) planned PC price hikes over memory costs, Reuters reported , and IDC says smartphone shipments fell a record 22% last quarter.

Big buyers aren't flinching. "To the contrary, we're seeing very strong demand from our customers," Visoso told Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan. To me, that split explains Friday's selling better than any headline number.

Morgan Stanley is betting cloud demand covers it

Morgan Stanley isn't worried, according to a research note shared with TheStreet. Analyst Joseph Moore kept an Overweight rating and a $1,750 price target in the October 30 report, titled " Earnings power grinding higher. " Like every price in this story, that target is pre-split; Sandisk's 8-for-1 stock split takes effect November 20.

Moore's case rests on supply, not shoppers. The note says consumer and client products fell to 56% of revenue from 90% a year earlier, a share it expects to keep shrinking.

In his view, data center growth "should ease concerns about a slowdown in consumer devices upsetting supply and demand." Put simply, cloud buyers will absorb whatever chips shoppers stop buying.

I agree with the math, but the note also reveals a cost. Sandisk's average selling prices rose only about 9% last quarter, trailing other memory makers, because it locked in contracts early, Moore wrote.

Story Continues

The bigger surprise sits in his model. Moore raised his 2027 earnings estimate to about $271 a share, from $212, yet left his target unchanged.

That's because Morgan Stanley values Sandisk on through-cycle earnings of $62.50 a share, less than a quarter of that estimate. Its model even shows fiscal 2029 earnings falling about 21%, so this bull expects leaner years too.

More SanDisk:

5-star analyst sets jaw-dropping price target on SanDisk stock

5-star analyst resets SanDisk stock price target by $175

Sandisk has $93.9 billion in deals: Now comes the hard part

The stock looks cheap until you check the math

Sandisk trades at 4.75 times forward earnings, per StockAnalysis. Against Morgan Stanley's through-cycle figure, Friday's price is about 18 times earnings, a more ordinary multiple.

The stock sits about 51% below its 52-week high of $2,354.39 but roughly six times its 52-week low of $183. It also closed Friday just 5% above Morgan Stanley's $1,100 bear case.

Options traders gave that level close to even odds of breaking within a year, the note shows.

Morgan Stanley sits below the Street. Sandisk carries a Buy consensus from 25 analysts with an average target near $2,105 , per StockAnalysis:

$3,000 is among the highest targets , set by Bernstein's Mark Newman with a Buy rating before the report.

$1,750 is Morgan Stanley's target , rated Overweight.

$1,000 is the lowest target on the Street , and three analysts rate the stock Hold while one says Sell .

After the split, Morgan Stanley's target works out to about $219. The bank also discloses a stake of 1% or more in Sandisk and investment banking ties to the company.

What Sandisk holders should do now

The split changes nothing about what you own; it cuts the same pie into more slices. Moore expects about $30 billion in buybacks next year, which he says "should continue to help keep a floor under the stock as long as end-market demand remains strong." That floor rests on demand investors now question.

If I held the stock, I'd watch two things before adding. One is whether the December quarter lands inside the 84.5% to 85.5% gross margin guide. The other is whether low-end weakness spreads to premium phones, where Moore's thesis would crack first.

The $1,100 bear case also works as a line in the sand. A sustained break below it would tell holders the market doubts even the bank's cautious through-cycle math.

Memory makers have chased an escape from boom and bust for decades, and Sandisk's long-term contracts are its answer.

Morgan Stanley still values the company on through-cycle earnings, a quiet sign that even its bulls expect the cycle to return. The next signal may come soon, since only about $10.5 billion remains on Sandisk's buyback authorization and Moore expects another large one.

news.Content:

Wingstop（WING.US）： 成交價164.77美元，上漲10.04%，開盤153美元，盤中高點167.15美元，盤中低點153美元，均價162.55美元，成交量3.22萬股。

Wingstop近14日內未見新的財報、財測調整、展店里程碑或產品策略更新，現有資料不足以指出短期內有哪一項公司事件正在改變營運方向。對連鎖餐飲股而言，真正能重寫成長預期的通常是同店銷售、加盟展店速度、新品帶動客流，或國際市場擴張效率，但目前輸入資料沒有提供這些新增線索。因此，現階段較難僅憑公司面資訊判斷Wingstop是否出現新的需求轉折，後續仍需等待更直接的營運數字或管理層展望。

Harley-Davidson（HOG.US）： 成交價33.03美元，上漲5.8%，開盤31.6美元，盤中高點33.22美元，盤中低點31.6美元，均價32.13美元，成交量14.7萬股。

Harley-Davidson近14日內同樣未見新的財報、出貨指引、重機產品發布或通路調整消息，資料沒有顯示足以重新界定公司營運方向的新增事件。以機車製造商來看，真正重要的變化通常來自零售銷售、經銷庫存、融資需求與高毛利車款組合，但目前都缺乏最新佐證。換言之，現在可確認的不是Harley-Davidson出現了明確新轉折，而是公司近期尚未提供足夠的新資訊，讓外界重新判讀其北美需求與品牌營運節奏。

Jones Lang LaSalle（JLL.US）： 成交價380.95美元，上漲5.88%，開盤365美元，盤中高點381.13美元，盤中低點365美元，均價372.71美元，成交量1.71萬股。

Jones Lang LaSalle目前沒有新的租賃、投資管理、物業服務或併購進展揭露，短線可確認的主軸仍是外界等待下一次財報更新商用不動產景氣。現有資料顯示，華爾街對截至2026年9月這一季預估營收為73億美元、EPS為6.18美元，且公司過去4季都高於共識，代表後續焦點仍會放在交易量、租賃活動與企業設施管理需求是否延續回升。由於近14日未見新的公司公告，現階段仍難從公司面辨識單一新的成長催化劑。

Jefferies Financial Group（JEF.US）： 成交價48.72美元，上漲5.64%，開盤46.81美元，盤中高點48.77美元，盤中低點46.32美元，均價47.83美元，成交量5.12萬股。

Jefferies Financial Group近期較具體的變化，不在單一新產品，而是股東結構與資本支持訊號更明確。資料顯示，SMFG近6個月兩度買進Jefferies股票，合計約1233萬股、金額約6.287億美元，屬於少見的大額增持。另一方面，外部整理資料也提到，公司先前曾表示投資銀行與股票交易業務單季表現創下紀錄，顯示其核心資本市場業務仍具韌性。相較單純評等調整，這類實際持股增加與業務表現訊號，更能說明Jefferies近期的營運故事仍圍繞交易與投行業務。

RH（RH.US）： 成交價153.49美元，上漲4.66%，開盤148.55美元，盤中高點155美元，盤中低點148.55美元，均價151.52美元，成交量2.26萬股。

RH近期主線仍是把RH Estates推成下一階段成長引擎。先前資料顯示，管理層預期這條產品線未來5年可占總供應量50%，並有機會讓品牌可服務市場翻倍，代表公司不只是在既有高端家具品類中求成長，而是試圖擴大整體產品版圖。財務面上，公司2026財年第二季淨營收為9.222億美元，並認列5510萬美元關稅收益，用來抵消供應鏈額外成本。就目前線索看，RH的核心變化不是短期促銷，而是新品類擴張與供應鏈成本管理同步推進。

YETI Holdings（YETI.US）： 成交價45.37美元，上漲3.93%，開盤44.87美元，盤中高點45.78美元，盤中低點44.99美元，均價45.35美元，成交量4.48萬股。

YETI Holdings近期較具體的新增訊號，是分析師把評級由持有調升至買進，目標價也由45美元調高到50美元，但比起券商動作，更值得留意的是公司先前財報反映的需求結構。資料顯示，YETI Holdings 2026年第二季調整後EPS為0.67美元，高於預期的0.54美元，營收年增9%至4.839億美元，其中國際與批發通路表現較強，核心DTC業務則成長7%。另外，當季獲利優於預期有部分來自關稅退稅淨收益，代表短期獲利改善不完全來自終端需求全面轉強，後續仍要看直營消費動能能否再加速。

news.Title: 韓股翻紅大漲，台股卻失守4萬5！郭哲榮揭布局契機：逢低搶進這幾檔
news.Content:
台股失守4萬5千點，韓股卻逆勢大漲，亞洲股市走勢呈現明顯反差。面對台股短線震盪， 摩爾投顧投資長郭哲榮（哲哲） 認為，台股短線拉回屬正常修正，第四季多頭格局並未因此改變，投資人不必因為短線下跌恐慌出場，反而可以留意AI供應鏈的逢低布局機會，點名 鴻海（2317）、聯發科（2454）、智原（3035）、環球晶（6488）、華邦電（2344） 及 南亞科（2408） 等相關個股。

【韓股大漲台股仍收黑 郭哲榮：別在低點恐慌砍單】

台股今（2）日開低走高，早盤一度大跌812.73點，最低來到44,399.10點，隨後低接買盤進場，指數最高反彈至45,156.17點，盤中一度重新站回4萬5千點，終場仍未能守住整數關卡，下跌291.69點收在44,920.14點，成交金額約7,588.75億元。

相較之下，韓國股市在SK海力士回購計畫等消息帶動下，開低走高，終場上漲2.24%。郭哲榮認為，台股短線拉回屬於市場修正，不代表多頭行情就此結束，尤其第四季仍有機會延續多頭走勢，投資人不應因為幾天的下跌，就在相對低點恐慌賣股。

郭哲榮也提醒，投資最重要的是控制風險，應以現股操作為主，避免使用融資槓桿，並做好持股分散。只要沒有過度擴大槓桿，就不必因為短線震盪而承受過大的心理壓力，反而可以趁市場拉回重新檢視持股，尋找具備長期成長動能的標的。

【資安外洩事件頻傳 企業防衛型AI需求升溫】

郭哲榮看好AI產業的另一個重要理由，是AI應用已經從生成式工具，逐步延伸到企業資安防禦。隨著AI技術進步，駭客也能運用自動化工具發動攻擊，企業為了保護客戶資料、商業機密及內部系統，勢必得投入更多資源升級資安設備與AI防禦系統。

近期台灣電商服務商91APP發生資安事件，調查指出，可能影響近480萬名消費者；日本無印良品也公告，官方App部分顧客資料有外洩風險，顯示企業資料安全已成為不能忽視的課題。

郭哲榮認為，這類資安威脅將進一步推升企業對地端AI、運算設備及防禦系統的需求。換句話說，AI不只是企業提升效率的工具，也 逐漸成為維護營運安全的重要基礎建設，相關硬體供應鏈有機會持續受惠。

郭哲榮指出，鴻海先前已表示，AI伺服器市占率超過4成，並持續朝50%目標努力，顯示其在AI伺服器市場仍有擴

news.Title: Prediction: This Will Be Sandisk’s Stock Price After 1 Year
news.Content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks are witnessing a bloodbath on the market due to various reasons, including hotter-than-expected inflation, higher interest rates, concerns about access to financing amid higher capital costs, and the aggressive spending on AI infrastructure by hyperscalers that's hurting their cash flow.

Shares of Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) have been caught in the broader tech rout, and a strong earnings report from the company didn't help it arrest the slide. Let's take a closer look at Sandisk's results and check if its fortunes will turn around in the coming year.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Sandisk's latest results indicate that its red-hot growth is here to stay

Sandisk released fiscal 2027 first-quarter results (for the three months ended Oct. 2) on Oct. 29. The stock plunged over 13% the next day amid a broader sell-off in tech stocks . However, Sandisk's drop isn't justified when we take a closer look at its earnings and guidance.

Sandisk's revenue jumped by a whopping 378% year over year to $11.03 billion. Meanwhile, non- GAAP earnings per share (EPS) increased from just $1.22 in the year-ago period to $49.51 in the previous quarter. The numbers comfortably exceeded Wall Street's expectations. Even better, Sandisk's guidance for the current quarter is better than what analysts were looking for.

The company expects $12.4 billion in revenue in the current quarter at the midpoint of its guidance range. It anticipates earnings per share of $56.00. Analysts were looking for $54.69 in earnings per share on revenue of $12.29 billion. Moreover, Sandisk's outlook clearly suggests that its red-hot growth is sustainable.

The company reported $3 billion in revenue and $6.20 in non-GAAP earnings per share in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. So, its top and bottom lines are poised for an exponential jump once again. It is worth noting that Sandisk's revenue increased at a much slower pace of 61% in the same quarter last year, while earnings increased by 5x year over year.

So, Sandisk's growth continues to accelerate, which explains why analysts anticipate its bottom line to jump by 220% in fiscal 2027 to $226.85. However, Sandisk's EPS growth in Q1 and the guidance for Q2 indicate that it could outpace analysts' expectations, and that could set the stock up for big gains over the coming year.

Story Continues

Wall Street expects big gains from Sandisk, but it could do better

Sandisk's 12-month median price target of $2,167 implies 88% gains, which is quite healthy. However, the stunning earnings growth the company has been clocking indicates that it can do better than that.

I say this because of the stock's dirt cheap valuation. Sandisk trades at just 9 times earnings, well below the S&P 500 index's earnings multiple of 23. The S&P 500's average earnings are anticipated to increase by 33% this year. Sandisk, therefore, deserves to trade at a premium to the S&P 500.

Let's say the stock trades at even 15 times earnings at the end of fiscal 2027, which will end in early July next year, and it clocks $226.85 in EPS (in line with consensus expectations); its price could reach $3,403. That's nearly 3x Sandisk's price right now, indicating that it has the potential to become a multibagger given its red-hot growth and attractive valuation.

news.Title: 油價暴跌 台指期夜盤45K失而復得 道指飆漲600點
news.Content:
（23：20更新）伊朗最高領袖批准政府開啟談判，有望化解擾亂中東能源供給、持續數月的衝突，消息帶動油價大幅走低，跌幅逾6%。原本陷入多空交戰的台指期夜盤瞬間狂拉近300點，一度報45487點。但在美股開盤後，隨著費半驟跌，台指期夜盤一度暴跌近400點，報44832點，而隨著費半早盤翻紅走強，台指期夜盤又重新站上45000點以上。

周一（2日）美股一開盤，主要指數同步走高。道瓊工業指數早盤大漲逾600點，那斯達克指數強彈逾300點。與台股連動密切的費城半導體指數開盤小漲後，突然回落，但早盤迅速翻紅，漲幅逾1%。

截至台北時間2日晚間11點20分，道瓊工業指數上漲582.44點（或1.13%），暫報52352.75點；那斯達克指數上漲280.016點（或1.10%），暫報25717.014點；標普500指數上漲66.30點（或0.87%），暫報7646.37點；費城半導體指數上漲102.58點（或0.96%），暫報10791.38點。

5大科技巨頭當中，僅蘋果走跌1.03%，谷歌母公司Alphabet漲2.17%，微軟漲1.09%，亞馬遜漲5.09%，臉書母公司Meta漲0.81%。半導體類股普遍走強，輝達漲2.29%，超微漲0.27%，台積電ADR漲1.08%，聯電ADR漲1.11%。

上周五科技股遭遇猛烈拋售後，周一出現止跌回彈跡象。與此同時，國際油價下跌也為股市提供了支撐，幫助市場在新的一個月迎來相對積極的開局。

不過荷蘭國際集團首席投資策略師Simon Wiersma指出，這次反彈的幅度相對於上周五的拋售來說較為溫和，「我目前還不會將其解讀為具有說服力的『逢低買入』訊號。圍繞AI投資、利率及地緣政治的不確定性依然充足，足以令投資者保持謹慎。」

Portfolio fundamentals were solid in the quarter, with 21 out of 22 holdings exceeding earnings forecasts, six raising guidance, and several boosting dividends. KLA Corporation closed at $157.91 on October 30, 2026, holding a $205.75 billion market capitalization. Up 31.69% year-to-date, the stock has traded within a 52-week range of $107.20 to $307.37.

"KLA Corporation (NASDAQ:KLAC) and Applied Materials were the largest detractors, falling 35.3% and 29.2%. Analysts raised their earnings estimates for both companies over the quarter, so the declines reflected lower valuations rather than weaker expectations. news.Title: Marvell Buys Lumentum in $115 Billion AI Connectivity Deal
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Marvell Technology Inc. ( MRVL , Financials ) The semiconductor and data-infrastructure business has agreed to buy Lumentum in an all-stock deal that values the optical networking company at roughly $115 billion.Lumentum owners will get around 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own.When the transaction closes, Marvell shareholders will own approximately 67% of the combined firm and Lumentum investors would possess around 33%.The firms said the deal boosts their combined addressable market to around $550 billion and improves Marvell's position in optical connection for AI infrastructure.The purchase is expected to be accretive to adjusted profits within one year of completion and management estimates annual run-rate synergies of more than $1 billion.Lumentum also posted adjusted earnings of $4.57 per share on revenue of $1.26 billion in the fiscal first quarter, increasing 136% from a year earlier.The company's sales projection of $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion for its fiscal second quarter also hints to ongoing progress.The deal is likely to finalize in the first half of 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory clearances.

news.Title: 單日再砍349億元！台積電外資持股比創20年新低 鉅額交易卻驚現漲停價
news.Content:
權值龍頭台積電（2330）2日繼續遭外資無情調節，單日面臨逾1.5萬張提款、賣超金額高達349.7億元。盤中股價一度重挫至2,310元，距離2,300元整數大關僅差10元；尾盤雖在政策買盤加碼護盤下收斂跌幅，終場仍下跌40元，收在2,330元。值得市場關注的是，盤後鉅額交易意外出現以「漲停價」2,605元成交的紀錄，引發多頭「仙人指路」的聯想。

台積電今年以來持續面臨外資拋售壓力。據統計，截至2日收盤，外資持股比率已進一步滑落至68.45％，寫下自2005年底以來、近20年的歷史新低紀錄；今日盤中低點險守2,310元，市場對2,300元關鍵防線是否失守的擔憂情緒顯著升溫。

與集中市場疲弱走勢形成對比的是，台積電今日鉅額交易頻現多空對峙。盤後出現1筆以今日漲停價2,605元成交的配對交易，共計10張。由於台積電過往強勢時，鉅額高價成交常被市場視為多方先行指標，本次高價交易是否意在為股價突圍指路，備受投資人關注。

另外，16筆盤後鉅額交易中，有6筆配對、合計201張成交價低於收盤價的2,330元，其中最低成交價為2,300.47元，精準壓在2,300元整數心理關卡之上。

據證交所統計，台積電今日鉅額交易總計成交16筆、共2,078張，成交總金額達48.5億元，平均每股成交價格為2,334.11元。法人分析，在外資籌碼持續鬆動之際，鉅額交易多空分歧擴大，後續2,300元整數支撐能否有效築底，仍將是短線盤勢多空的觀察指標。

news.Title: 台股失守4萬5千點！外資賣超735億 美期中選舉牽動後市
news.Content: 財經中心／綜合報導 台股震盪加劇，外資賣壓持續籠罩市場！台股最新交易日開低走低，儘管尾盤跌幅收斂，終場仍下跌291點，收在44,920點，失守45,000點整數關卡。隨著美股回檔，加上美國期中選舉即將登場，市場觀望氣氛升溫。不過，儘管短線股市承壓，AI產業長期成長趨勢仍受到關注，後續法人資金動向及企業基本面，將成為影響台股走勢的重要關鍵。 受到美股走弱及科技股賣壓影響，台股近期持續修正。從法人籌碼觀察，外資單日賣超高達735億元，連續3個交易日站在賣方，成為壓抑大盤的重要因素。不過，外資期貨空單也同步減少2,862口，淨空單降至89,379口，顯示部分空方部位開始回補。相較之下，投信則持續站在買方，單日買超達360億元，寫下史上第三大買超紀錄，並連續15個交易日加碼，形成外資賣、投信買的不同調局面。短線台股仍容易受到外資賣超權值股影響，造成指數震盪，但從中長期角度觀察，企業營運表現與產業發展趨勢，仍是評估個股投資價值的重要依據。 美國11月3日登場的期中選舉，進一步牽動美股及台股表現。（圖／民視財經網）除了外資動向，美國11月3日登場的期中選舉，也成為全球金融市場關注焦點。若選後國會權力結構改變，可能影響美國未來政策推動，進一步牽動美股及台股表現。從歷史統計來看，過去23次美國期中選舉年當中，有20次第四季美股呈現上漲，比例約87%。其中，政治不確定性逐步消除，被視為推動市場回穩的重要因素之一。不過，今年市場環境與過往不同，除了利率壓力仍在，部分選舉結果也可能已提前反映在股價當中，加上郵寄選票可能拉長計票時間，一旦選舉結果遲遲無法確定，恐怕進一步加劇金融市場波動。 近期AI概念股也出現明顯修正，引發市場對產業成長動能的疑慮。不過，目前AI供應鏈面臨的挑戰，除了股價估值調整，也包括部分關鍵零組件供應不足，導致下游廠商無法按照原定時程出貨。包括CPU、高頻寬記憶體（HBM）等關鍵零組件供應吃緊，都可能影響AI伺服器組裝進度。從供應鏈營收表現觀察，先進封裝、銅箔基板（CCL）等上游產業需求仍相對強勁，但部分零組件及組裝廠商的月營收卻出現下滑，反映出貨排程可能受到影響。因此，接下來公布的10月營收，將成為觀察AI供應鏈能否改善缺料、恢復正常交貨的重要指標。若中下游廠商營收重新轉強，將有助於確認出貨動能回升；反之，若上游與下游營收同步走弱，就需要進一步留意需求是否出現變化。 另一方面，隨著AI技術快速發展，網路攻擊及資訊安全問題也受到市場關注。日本近期遭遇密集資安攻擊事件，凸顯企業在數位轉型過程中，必須更加重視系統防護與第三方供應商管理。AI技術不只帶動運算需求，也可能增加企業面臨的資安威脅，促使政府及企業提高資訊安全預算，進一步帶動資安軟體、系統防護及相關服務需求。不過，資安支出增加也可能提高企業營運成本，因此相關商機能否轉化為實際獲利，仍有待後續觀察。

Options Sentiment Remains Bullish for AMD Stock

While a 73% YoY growth is solid by any stretch of the imagination, the derivatives market believes much of the earnings upside is already baked into AMD shares at their current price.

According to Barchart's data, the put-to-call ratio on options contracts expiring Nov. 6 is set at 1.04 as of this writing, and a reading above 1.00 is often characterized as in favor of the bears.

And the lower price on those contracts sits at $454 currently, indicating potential for a nearly 9% post-earnings decline in Advanced Micro Devices.

In his latest research note, Rolland maintained the Nasdaq-listed firm at "Buy" – and raised his price target to $650, signaling potential upside of more than 30% from current levels.

According to him, continued data-center strength will help Advanced Micro Devices report a better than expected Q3 and offer upbeat guidance, which would drive its share price higher through the remainder of 2026.

AMD still has billions in pending authorization for buybacks, which makes it even more attractive as a long-term holding, the analyst concluded.

news.Title: 跌破半年線慘了！陳嘉偉示警台股剛進「初跌段」　揭這時間爆奪命回馬槍
news.Content:
台北股市近期隨國際走勢陷入劇烈震盪，分析師陳嘉偉於《股市總司令》節目中指出，加權指數在跌破半年線關鍵支撐後，市場氣氛已正式「由多轉空」，宣告行情僅剛進入「初跌段」。他分析，大盤近期雖靠金融與塑化等非電子股撐盤，但電子權值股與高槓桿標的早已率先下修；投資人應採取鋸齒狀空頭思維，在大跌時適度回補過度超跌的個股，並把握美國大選期間可能出現的急彈逃命波（奪命回馬槍）重新佈局空單，慎防後續「年線對稱跌幅」的長線修整壓力。

鋸齒狀下跌靈活應變 空單獲利回補等待再放空

針對短線的操作策略，陳嘉偉強調股市下跌必定呈現「鋸齒狀走勢」，當個股出現長黑急殺且短線跌幅已達 30% 以上時，盲目追空容易遭遇強烈反彈吞噬獲利。因此，團隊在上週五已將連跌數日、獲利豐厚的晶圓代工與記憶體族群（如聯電、世界先進、華邦電、南亞科及矽晶圓等）空單進行獲利回補，鎖定戰果；然而針對矽光子與被動元件等族群則維持空單，預期在 10 月營收陸續公布後，基本面壓力將持續加重相關個股的補跌風險。

台積電三個缺口露疲態 灰犀牛引爆融資籌碼賣壓

針對大盤指標台積電，陳嘉偉直言其技術面已呈現典型的大空頭架構，不僅短線連續留下三個跳空缺口，季線與月線更相繼下彎，但市場融資餘額卻逆勢創下新高，籌碼面極度不安。他指出，這次大盤的重挫並非無法預期、急跌後會創新高的「黑天鵝」，而是市場長期無視 AI 資本支出過熱與籌碼過度槓桿所導致的「灰犀牛」風險；當灰犀牛利空開始發酵，即便權值股也難以單靠市場樂觀情緒抵禦整體產業的修正週期。

美選恐現「奪命回馬槍」 長線慎防年線對稱跌幅

展望後續行情，陳嘉偉預測隨著美國期中選舉等政治變數登場，台股在短期連續重挫後，極可能隨國際消息面順勢拉出一根急強反彈的長紅 K 棒，即所謂的「奪命回馬槍」。但他特別提醒，此類急彈絕非趨勢翻多止跌，而是提供多頭逃命與空方絕佳的加碼空點。若對照 1997 年亞洲金融風暴與 2008 年金融海嘯等歷史經驗，大盤在失守半年線後，未來恐面臨「年線對稱跌幅」、甚至向五年線尋求支撐的深層修正風險，投資人切勿輕易盲目摸底。

news.Title: Is QCOM Stock a Smart Investment Option Before Q4 Earnings Release?
news.Content:
Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM is scheduled to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings after the closing bell on Nov. 4. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for sales and earnings is pegged at $10.15 billion and $2.16 per share, respectively. Earnings estimates for QCOM for fiscal 2026 have remained unchanged over the past 60 days, and those for fiscal 2027 have decreased 0.5% to $10.02.

QCOM Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Earnings Surprise History

The chip manufacturer delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 2.5%, on average, beating estimates on three occasion. In the last reported quarter, the company delivered a negative earnings surprise of 0.45%.

Earnings Whispers

Our proven model does not conclusively predict an earnings beat for Qualcomm for the fiscal third quarter. The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) increases the chances of an earnings beat. That is not the case here. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they're reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

Qualcomm currently has an ESP of -0.51% and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Factors Shaping Upcoming Results

During the quarter, Qualcomm completed the acquisition of Modular, adding an AI-native software platform designed to optimize and deploy generative and agentic AI workloads across CPUs, GPUs, NPUs and custom silicon. The transaction expands Qualcomm's software capabilities across devices, edge infrastructure and data centers.

The company introduced the Dragonwing Q-2390 and IQ-2390 processors to broaden access to edge AI across consumer, commercial and industrial devices. The platforms integrate AI, vision, connectivity and real-time processing, with customer engagement underway and evaluation kits expected in early 2027. It has also announced a multi-generational collaboration with Amazon to develop customized silicon for AI inference and advanced optical connectivity for AWS data centers. Despite these positive developments, Qualcomm's prospects are impacted by several factors.

Memory pricing, supply constraints and OEM builds continue to weigh on the smartphone business. The semiconductor supply chain is operating near full utilization, with shortages and cost increases across wafers, assembly, test, advanced packaging, memory and other materials. Qualcomm is responding with broad price increases that management described as double-digit, but contract terms and product cycles mean the benefit will phase in over the next couple of quarters.

Story Continues

Price Performance

Over the past year, Qualcomm has declined 2.1% compared with the industry's decline of 16.1%, outperforming competitors like Intel Corporation INTC but underperforming Advanced Micro Devices AMD. While AMD has gained 47.8%, Intel has declined 31.3% over the said time frame.

Key Valuation Metric

From a valuation standpoint, Qualcomm appears to be relatively premium compared to the industry and below its mean. Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 16.11 forward earnings, higher than 10.22 for the industry but lower than the stock's mean of 19.11.

Investment Consideration

Qualcomm's increasing exposure to automotive, IoT and data center markets offers opportunities to diversify its revenue base. These initiatives may not be enough to offset the challenges facing its core handset business in the near term. Persistent weakness in the Android smartphone market, rising memory costs and lower expected contributions from Apple could continue to weigh on QCT revenues. Moreover, the company's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes it to demand fluctuations and potential revenue losses as manufacturers increasingly explore in-house chip development.

Profitability also remains a concern. Higher costs across wafer fabrication, assembly, testing and advanced packaging have already weakened QCT margins, while the benefits of product price increases are likely to take time to materialize.

Moreover, Qualcomm's expansion into data center infrastructure involves considerable execution risks. Its ambitious revenue targets will require successful product development, timely commercialization and sustained customer adoption.

End Note

Qualcomm's efforts to establish a stronger presence in automotive, IoT and AI computing markets have expanded its long-term growth opportunities. However, the company's dependence on the smartphone market, declining Apple-related revenues and industry-wide supply constraints continue to create significant challenges. The pressure on QCT margins, combined with higher operating expenses and the uncertain profitability of its emerging data center business, raises concerns about the sustainability of earnings growth. The company carries a Zacks Rank #4. Investors should avoid investing in this stock at present.

news.Title: 00949擬配3.02元配息率衝破13% 掀起日股ETF高息話題
news.Content:
近期全球科技股波動加劇，市場資金開始重新檢視投資組合的風險分散與收益來源。日股ETF配息表現也成為市場關注焦點，其中復華日本龍頭(00949-TW)最新宣布配發每受益權單位3.02元，以今(2)日收盤價 22.1 元推算，年配息率突破 13%，不僅展現亮眼的收益表現，更寫下台灣掛牌日股ETF的配息新紀錄。

過去台灣掛牌的日本股票ETF，多以追蹤日本主要股價指數、掌握日股長期成長機會為訴求，配息並非市場關注的主要焦點。相較之下，00949此次宣布配發3.02元，以推估年配息率超過13%的水準來看，明顯有別於過往日股ETF的配息表現。若與市場既有日股ETF歷史配息紀錄比較，過去尚未出現年化配息率突破10%的案例，此次配息因此格外受到矚目。

值得注意的是，近期美國大型科技股及AI相關族群受到市場對企業資本支出、獲利成長與評價水準的重新檢視，股價波動明顯加大。在全球股市連動性提高的環境下，投資人若過度集中於單一市場或科技產業，投資組合可能承受較大的短期波動。因此，透過不同國家與產業的資產配置分散風險，重要性也隨之提升。

日本股市近年受惠於企業治理改革、股東報酬意識提升，以及企業積極推動資本效率改善，逐漸吸引國際資金關注。相較於高度集中在少數大型科技企業的投資組合，日本市場涵蓋金融、工業、消費、汽車及電子等多元產業，可作為投資人拓展海外股票配置的選項之一。

市場人士指出，對於已持有美股科技ETF、台灣科技型ETF或AI相關投資部位的投資人而言，適度納入日股ETF，不僅有助於拓展投資區域，也能增加不同產業與企業獲利來源的曝險。若搭配具備配息機制的產品，更可兼顧海外股市參與及現金流需求，提升投資組合的配置彈性。

不過，投資人仍須留意，ETF配息率並不等同於投資報酬率，單次高額配息也不代表未來能持續維持相同水準。評估日股ETF時，除觀察配息金額與年化配息率外，也應綜合考量基金淨值變化、配息來源、總報酬表現、匯率風險及標的指數特性，避免單純以高配息率作為投資依據。

news.Title: AMD Threatens False Breakout Ahead of Earnings
news.Content:
Two years ago, the question about Advanced Micro Devices was whether it could compete at all in artificial intelligence accelerators.

Nvidia had the hardware, the software moat, and effectively the entire customer list. AMD had a roadmap and a lot of goodwill from its CPU comeback.

That question has been answered, and not in the way the skeptics expected. AMD now holds multi-gigawatt commitments from three of the most demanding buyers of compute on earth. The question heading into Tuesday afternoon's third-quarter report is entirely different, and in some ways harder: can the company actually deliver what it has already sold?

Image Source: StockCharts

The Contracts Are Signed

Start with the scale of what has been committed. In October of last year, OpenAI agreed to deploy up to six gigawatts of AMD Instinct accelerators, beginning with one gigawatt of MI450 silicon in the second half of 2026. This past February, Meta signed a definitive multi-year agreement for up to six gigawatts of its own, built around a custom Instinct GPU based on the MI450 architecture, paired with sixth-generation EPYC processors and AMD's Helios rack-scale design. Anthropic rounds out the anchor group.

These are not evaluation orders. They are capacity reservations measured in power rather than units, which tells you how the buyers now think about the problem.

Both deals carry an unusual feature. AMD issued Meta a performance-based warrant for up to 160 million shares of its own stock, vesting in tranches as shipments scale toward six gigawatts and as AMD's share price clears defined thresholds. OpenAI received a similar structure. Against roughly 1.85 billion shares outstanding, the Meta warrant alone represents potential dilution near 9%.

The structure aligns incentives beautifully — Meta profits if AMD succeeds, which gives Meta reason to make AMD succeed. It also means AMD is paying for a meaningful share of its own demand in equity rather than in price concessions. Shareholders should understand they are funding part of this ramp. The vesting hurdles mean it only triggers if things go very well, which is the right way to structure it, but the dilution is real.

What the Numbers Say Heading In

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the September quarter stands at $1.94 per share, representing growth of 61.7% over the year-ago period. Revenue is pegged at $13.12 billion, up 41.9%. Company guidance called for roughly $13 billion give or take $300 million, with non-GAAP gross margin near 56%, so the Street and management are closely aligned.

Story Continues

The full-year picture is more striking. The 2026 consensus sits at $7.55 per share on $50.71 billion in revenue — earnings growth of 81% on revenue growth of 46%. And the forward estimate has been moving fast. The 2027 consensus now stands near $15.24 per share, up from $14.78 just sixty days ago. That is a 3.11% upward revision to next year's earnings in just two months, which is the kind of move that tends to precede sustained outperformance.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AMD has also exceeded the consensus in each of the past four quarters, with an average beat of 6.5%, and currently carries a positive Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) of +3.49% heading into Tuesday's print. This proprietary indicator has proven to be very useful for finding positive surprises. In fact, when combining a Zacks Rank #3 or better and a positive Earnings ESP, stocks produced a positive surprise 70% of the time according to our 10-year backtest.

The One Line That Matters

Within that report, a single number carries disproportionate weight: Data Center revenue. Analysts are modeling $8.27 billion, which would represent growth of 90.6% and place the segment at roughly two-thirds of total company revenue.

Here is why investors who do not own AMD should still read this report carefully.

The market spent October questioning whether AI capital spending converts into revenue and cash flow. The debate shifted from capability to financing, and it took real casualties among the companies carrying debt to fund the buildout. AMD AMD reports Tuesday, well ahead of Nvidia, which makes it the first substantial read on accelerator demand since those doubts surfaced.

A Data Center number at or above $8.27 billion, paired with constructive commentary on the Helios ramp, would suggest the spending is landing on real silicon and real revenue. A miss on that line, or any sign that supply constraints in wafers, packaging or high-bandwidth memory are pushing deliveries to the right, would validate the more skeptical view and likely travel well beyond AMD's own shares.

Bottom Line

One caution before Tuesday. After the fourth-quarter 2025 report, AMD beat on earnings by roughly 16% and the stock fell more than 17%. Expectations are high, the shares have advanced better than 135% this year, and the company carries a market capitalization over $800 billion. A good quarter may not be enough; the market will want the Helios ramp confirmed and the 2027 trajectory defended.

AMD no longer needs to prove the technology is competitive — the contracts settled that argument. It needs to prove it can ship at scale, hold margin through a ramp where AI accelerators run below the corporate average, and navigate a supply chain that is tight in every direction at once.

That is a far better problem to have than the one the company faced two years ago. It is also a problem that gets settled quarter by quarter, in public, starting Tuesday afternoon.

news.Title: SK hynix Says Memory Demand Beats Supply Through 2030—What It Means for Micron and SanDisk
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in SK hynix Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

SK hynix reported record fiscal Q3 2026 revenue and operating margin, driven by rising DRAM and NAND prices and 14 long-term customer agreements.

Long-term, take-or-pay contracts from SK hynix, Micron, and SanDisk are reshaping the cyclical memory industry by locking in capacity and pricing through 2030.

Aggressive capital expenditure plans could create oversupply risk if new fab capacity arrives just as AI spending slows and existing contracts expire.

Few industries have benefited more from the AI buildout than memory chip makers, who continue to report record demand for a wide range of products. Only a handful of companies can produce the memory needed for complex data center operations, and hyperscalers have crowded out typical customers and turned the industry on its head. But now that the AI trade appears shaky, companies need to do more than report record sales or backlogs. Customer quality is becoming a key investment theme this earnings season, and AI companies with dependable clients and reliable contracts may be better positioned to weather market volatility. And based on the Q3 reports from Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ: META) and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL), investors can expect this theme to stay front and center into Q4.

SK hynix Inc. (NASDAQ: SKHY) is one of the "big three" memory companies, and since its Nasdaq listing in July 2026, its earnings reports have been a focal point for AI investors. Memory is typically a cyclical, volatile industry, and investors are looking for any sign the music is about to stop. But if SK hynix's Q3 report is any indication, they may need to wait a few more years.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

Contract Quality Boosts Outlook But Spending Plans Counter Market Narrative

SK hynix reported its fiscal Q3 2026 results on Oct. 28, with record revenue of KRW 104.62 trillion (about $78.9 billion) and operating profit of ₩83.3 trillion (about $62.8 billion). Sales rose an astonishing 328% year-over-year (YOY) and 32% quarter-over-quarter (QOQ). Operating margin rose to 80% from 76% in Q2, driven by double-digit QOQ growth in selling prices for both DRAM and NAND memory. Management also reported long-term agreements with 14 major customers, including cloud service providers. With a typical length of five years, these 14 contracts now cover more than half of the company's 2027 and 2028 capacity, and CFO Woo-hyun Kim expects demand to outpace supply through 2030. Shares jumped more than 13% on the earnings news, with Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: MU) and SanDisk Corp. (NASDAQ: SNDK) also posting gains following the report.

Story Continues

SK hynix also increased capital expenditures (CapEx) at a time when many hyperscalers are cutting back. In addition to approximately $75 billion in planned shareholder returns for 2026, including dividends and share repurchases, the company also has an aggressive expansion plan. Management expects "significantly" more CapEx in fiscal 2027 versus 2026 to fund new fabs and increase output. So far in 2026, SK Hynix has spent $23.4 billion in CapEx, with a full-year projection of about $30 billion. Some of the new output would come online in 2028 and 2029, right at the tail end of many of the company's long-term agreements.

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

Why Multiyear Contracts Matter and What It Means for Micron and SanDisk

Before the AI data center boom, memory prices shifted like a commodity. The industry was volatile and highly cyclical, and investors typically sold when companies hit peak margins, expecting prices to roll over. But unprecedented demand and multi-year contracts are now testing that thesis, giving these companies revenue visibility that was previously unattainable. Customers who expect prices to rise and fall in a typical cycle don't lock in five-year agreements with upfront deposits, and structured contracts allow fabs to be built with capacity already claimed.

Micron is another memory maker locking in long-term agreements, with 26 contracts representing more than 35% of expected revenue through 2030 as of fiscal Q4 2026. It also reveals how these agreements are usually structured.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Micron's "strategic customer agreements" are take-or-pay, meaning customers must pay the full price regardless of how much memory they use.

The deals also typically include a price band with a floor and ceiling, and Micron claims even the floor prices generate gross margins above anything seen at previous cycle peaks.

The impact of the recent labor dispute in Taiwan on margins or capacity remains uncertain.

For SanDisk, the future is less certain.

It doesn't sell the high-bandwidth DRAM AI hyperscalers crave and is more exposed to the consumer electronics market through NAND memory products.

This market could be more vulnerable to weaker demand if prices rise, and SanDisk reported a 29% sequential decline in consumer revenue in its fiscal Q1 2027 report on Oct. 29.

However, its data center segment is also entering long-term agreements, and management claims that half of fiscal 2027 and two-thirds of fiscal 2028 NAND bit output are covered.

Shortage Versus Supply Is the Story Entering 2027

Long-term agreements have reshaped the memory industry, but they haven't rewritten the rulebook. Pricing bands can limit upside on contracted volumes during sudden price spikes. They also don't necessarily end the cycle; they just push it further out. A key risk in these CapEx proposals is that new capacity comes online just as current long-term agreements run out. If AI spending has slowed significantly during the new contract-renewal period, memory makers could be left with excess supply and a sudden dearth of customers.

As we move into the next quarter, investors should watch whether NAND and DRAM contract prices continue to rise to confirm that shortages persist. More long-term agreements with deposits and a broader customer base would also show that capacity will continue to be gobbled up beyond 2030. But if hyperscalers begin cutting CapEx, it could signal a market shift that leaves memory companies building up supply while margins have already peaked.

news.Title: TSEM: Tower Semiconductor is Ahead of Schedule on Capacity Expansion
news.Content:
By Lisa Thompson

NASDAQ: TSEM

READ THE FULL TSEM RESEARCH REPORT

Tower reported another record quarter, beating on revenues and earnings and guiding higher than street estimates for Q4, where they have good visibility. This was driven by 176% growth in RF Infrastructure sales, of which 83% was from SiPho. For Q4 2026, Tower guided to revenues of $600 million plus or minus 5%, another company record. Furthermore, it believes that Q1 2027 will be up sequentially rather than the typical seasonality it has experienced in the past when revenues dropped from Q4 levels. This could result in accelerating year-over-year growth and even higher margins.

Its income statement is revealing the inherent operating leverage of a foundry. Revenues for the quarter at $526 million were up 33%, gross margin was up 92%, and operating income rose 151%. Based on guidance, Q4 should be up at least 36%, an accelerating number.

In its July announcement of Japanese expansion, Tower targeted a $3.6 billion revenue run rate sometime in 2028 and $1.2 billion of net profit, which would result in approximate EPS of $10.25. Since right now the company can sell as much as it can produce of photonics products, it is doing all it can to increase capacity and said it was ahead of schedule on its Track 1 plans.

We are raising our 2026 estimates to reflect sales and earnings beat and the guidance. The revenue estimate for 2026 is now $2.0 billion, and for 2027 is $2.7 billion. Estimates for adjusted EPS have been increased to $4.05 for this year and $6.60 for 2027. As of last night's closing price, the company trades at an enterprise value of $17.4 billion, or 6.4x EV to estimated 2027 sales. As a photonics/AI data center play, we see catalysts in: potential increased guidance and continued beat and raises, increased target model, and announcements of new large customers. Right now, the only gating factor is capacity, and the revenue risk is in future pricing. If investors assume $3.6 billion in revenues, with an 8.1x EV to Sales, and $500 million of the cash spent, the stock price would be $266 per share. Since its low of $28.54 on April 4, 2025, the stock is up 483%.

news.Title: 台積電供應鏈迅得對半導體設備出貨走揚 10月營收改寫歷史次高
news.Content:
台積電(2330-TW)供應鏈設備大廠迅得(6438-TW)營收在半導體業務推進一如預期，10 月營收維持在 6 億元以上高檔，今(2)日揭露以 6.73億元改寫歷史單月次高，也創同期新高，月減3.15%、年增28.08%；累計 2026 年 1-10 月營收達61.86億元，年增 10.93%。

迅得 2026 年第三季營收達 19.45 億元，季增 6.64%、年增 13.62%，單季營收刷新歷史紀錄。法人預估，第四季營收將可維持在此一歷史高檔水準之上。

迅得投資 1.5 億元取得南科友上科技 23% 股權後，公司高層透露，目前仍有其他投資案持續推進中。同時，為因應持續湧入的設備訂單，迅得最快將於今年底至明年初在台灣南部取得土地興建新廠，全面提升產能供給。

在營運效益方面，迅得營運總部遷入新生廠後產能已達滿載，進一步推升獲利表現。2026 年上半年營收 35.68 億元，年增 11.99%，毛利率 26.13%，稅後純益 3.11 億元，每股純益(EPS)達 3.79 元。2026 年第二季營收 18.24 億元創高，稅後純益 1.66 億元，優於首季的 1.45 億元，單季 EPS 為 2.03 元。

隨著迅得安排出貨的半導體設備於第四季步入出貨高峰，加上產品組合優化，下半年營運將顯著優於上半年。法人預估，迅得 2026 全年營收將較 2025 年的 64.67 億元成長 10%–15%，續創歷史新高；在產品組合有利因素加持下，獲利成長幅度更有望達到營收增幅的倍數呈現。

迅得同時具備半導體與 PCB 設備雙重成長動能，在 PCB 領域，公司鎖定高階載板與板廠需求，目前已握有臻鼎-KY(4958-TW)及景碩(3189-TW)等大廠確立訂單。

news.Title: Micron vs. SanDisk: China's DRAM Scare Hit Both Stocks, but 1 Is the Better Buy
news.Content:
The AI memory boom just hit a wall of worry as big as China this month. When word broke that Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) had achieved a breakthrough in DRAM technology, it triggered shockwaves through the industry. Fears surged that a strong new rival might soon shake up established players, spark a price war, and flood the market with fresh supply. Investors wasted no time dumping top memory stocks like Micron Technology (MU) and SanDisk (SNDK), even though each faces a very different threat from this news.

The reaction highlights just how high the stakes have become in an industry powering the AI revolution, where soaring demand has sent both stocks rocketing to triple-digit gains in 2026. But is China's advance a real threat to their profits, or is the market jumping the gun? For investors anxious about the future of these memory stocks, understanding the differences between Micron and SanDisk's business models could reveal which is the smarter pick for the decade ahead.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Buy the Pullback in Alphabet Stock

Dear Roku Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

Dear ON Semiconductor Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

The Case for Micron (MU)

The selloff followed reports that China's CXMT is developing a breakthrough DRAM design that packs more memory into the same space. With plans to launch its server-focused technology by the end of 2026, the company has sparked concerns that Chinese manufacturers could soon disrupt the market, challenge established players, and drive prices down.

MU stock fell 16% in October alone, despite surging 213% year-to-date (YTD).

Micron is a major manufacturer of DRAM, NAND flash memory, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). Its products power computers, smartphones, data centers, and AI accelerators. NAND provides long-term data storage, DRAM serves as working memory, and HBM delivers the high-speed data access that demanding AI workloads require. This broad product portfolio gives Micron multiple ways to benefit from AI spending. However, this same advantage has also exposed it directly to China's ambitions in DRAM.

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Micron's revenue soared to a record $54.23 billion, up 379% year-over-year (YoY) and 31% sequentially. DRAM generated a record $39.8 billion, making up 73% of total sales. NAND contributed $14.1 billion, about 26% of revenue. DRAM revenue rose 27% sequentially, while NAND revenue climbed 42%. Since DRAM makes up nearly three-quarters of Micron's sales, any sustained increase in competing supply could pressure its pricing power and profitability.

Story Continues

But DRAM is not a single, interchangeable product. Micron also delivers HBM, the powerhouse fueling AI computing by channeling data to processors at lightning-fast speeds. HBM revenue is included in Micron's DRAM total. Micron's Q4 earnings call highlighted HBM's growing importance as AI demand expands. Management said the company secured agreements covering the vast majority of its HBM bit supply for calendar year 2027. These commitments provide greater visibility into future demand and reflect the strategic significance of advanced memory to AI customers.

Investors should understand that China's progress in conventional DRAM does not automatically translate into the ability to match Micron's advanced HBM products. HBM production requires demanding manufacturing processes, sophisticated packaging, and strict performance standards.

However, the bigger vulnerability is pricing. Micron's DRAM revenue soared 27% sequentially in fiscal Q4, driven by average selling prices that climbed sharply into the high teens. This stresses just how much pricing still drives the company's revenue engine. If CXMT accelerates production and rolls out attractive alternatives at tempting prices, a flood of new supply could chip away at Micron's hard-won pricing power in conventional DRAM.

That said, Micron has spent years perfecting its processes and forging strong ties with leading tech giants. It has built a formidable HBM business that may be harder to replace in the near term. Still, this advantage cannot fully shield the company from any new shifts that may reshape the DRAM supply-and-demand landscape.

For now, Micron's financial results offer investors plenty of reassurance. Adjusted gross margin reached 87%, while adjusted diluted earnings per share climbed to $33.42. The company generated $43.97 billion in operating cash flow and $33.20 billion in adjusted free cash flow in Q4. Management expects momentum to continue into fiscal year 2027 because memory supply could remain tight through calendar years 2027 and 2028. That outlook reveals that the current upcycle still has room to run even as investors begin to price in tougher competition ahead.

The Case for SanDisk (SNDK)

SanDisk's selloff tells a somewhat different story. Distinguished for its NAND flash memory and storage expertise, the company powers data centers, computers, and countless other devices with its solid-state drives (SSDs).

Unlike Micron, SanDisk doesn't manufacture DRAM, yet it still suffered the fear-driven consequences of a widespread selloff across the memory sector. SNDK stock is down 31% this month alone, even though it has soared 405% so far this year.

SanDisk's recent fiscal Q1 earnings show why the selloff wasn't justified. Revenue reached $11.03 billion, up 23% sequentially and 378% YoY. Adjusted earnings climbed to $49.51 per share from $39.25. About 60% of the sequential increase came from higher bit shipments, and 40% came from pricing. Data center revenue rose 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion, reflecting the increasing contribution of AI-related demand.

As AI inference workloads expand, data centers need more capacity to store and retrieve information. SanDisk believes NAND will play an increasingly important role in meeting these needs and is developing High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) to complement HBM. It expects to provide samples of its first HBF products in 2027. A key pillar of SanDisk's strategy rests in its New Business Model (NBM) agreements. By forging these long-term partnerships, the company locks in customer commitments and protects itself from the uncertainty of fluctuating quarterly orders. Management says these agreements already account for roughly half of its bits in fiscal 2027 and will cover two-thirds by fiscal 2028. This approach gives SanDisk a much clearer view of future demand.

On the balance sheet, SanDisk ended the quarter with $5.1 billion in cash and no debt. It also generated $5.7 billion in adjusted free cash flow and repurchased $5 billion worth of shares during the quarter. The memory maker remains committed to using all excess cash for shareholder returns.

Overall, SNDK stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating on Wall Street. Of the 25 analysts covering the stock, 21 recommend "Strong Buy," one recommends "Moderate Buy," and three suggest "Hold." Based on its average target price of $2,125, analysts expect the stock to rise 77% from current levels. Its high price estimate of $3000 suggests the stock could climb 150% over the next 12 months.

Which Is the Better Buy for the Next Decade?

While SanDisk is less directly exposed to CXMT's DRAM advances, its business remains more concentrated in NAND. Therefore, Micron remains the better buy for investors seeking diversified exposure to AI memory. With its blend of DRAM, HBM, and NAND, Micron unlocks opportunities in multiple market segments. Its strong cash flow and enduring customer partnerships further reinforce its edge over competitors.

On Wall Street, MU stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. Out of the 42 analysts covering MU, 34 rate it a "Strong Buy," five rate it a "Moderate Buy," and three recommend a "Hold." Its average target price of $1,563.22 still gives it room for 76% more growth. And the high price target of $3,000 suggests MU stock has an upside potential of 238% from current levels.

news.Title: 〈美國期中選舉〉國會若換手哪些美股受影響？一次看懂軍工、醫療、加密貨幣與AI
news.Content:
洛克希德馬丁(LMT-US)約七成營收來自美國政府，但未來十年供應850架F-35戰機的計畫，仍須國會批准並撥款。這也是華爾街關注本周期中選舉的原因：若民主黨拿下參眾兩院任一院，就能在預算談判中爭取讓步，並取得委員會調查權。從軍工廠能拿到多少訂單、健保業者能保住多少收入，到AI資料中心該由誰負擔電網升級費用，都可能受到影響。

摩根士丹利(MS-US)統計，在共和黨總統執政期間，若期中選舉後兩黨分掌參眾兩院，標普500指數在選後一年平均上漲23%；若民主黨掌控兩院，平均漲幅為16%。不過，該行美國公共政策研究主管Ariana Salvatore認為，這次未必會重演歷史走勢。即使民主黨取得國會多數，總統川普仍握有否決權，在關稅及聯邦監管上也保有相當大的裁量空間。

軍工看訂單 醫療看給付

白宮已為2027會計年度提出1.5兆美元國防預算要求，另為2026會計年度尋求876億美元追加撥款，主要用於與伊朗相關的軍事行動。若民主黨在國會取得優勢，可能檢視部分涉及伊朗及以色列的支出，同時爭取增加對烏克蘭的援助。相較之下，嚇阻中國、核武現代化及飛彈防禦都有跨黨派支持。以洛克希德馬丁為例，該公司與五角大廈簽的是F-35採購框架協議，國會是否授權多年期採購並編列經費，才決定這批戰機能否成為正式訂單。

醫療業對聯邦預算同樣敏感。健康政策研究機構KFF根據國會預算處估算，川普去年簽署的減稅與支出法案，到2034年將使聯邦醫療補助計畫(Medicaid)支出累計減少9,110億美元。健康保險商Molina Healthcare(MOH-US)去年有322億美元保費收入來自Medicaid，占其保費收入的75%。民主黨即使只拿下一院，也能在預算談判中爭取延後部分刪減，協助保險商維持投保人數，並減輕醫院照護無保險病患的負擔。但同一批議員也可能加強檢視保費、藥價與業者獲利，醫療股受到的影響並不一致。

幣圈等立法 銀行看資本規定

加密貨幣業希望把川普任內的監管政策寫進法律，降低政策隨政府更迭而改變的風險。9月，川普支持的加密貨幣市場結構法案《CLARITY法案》未能在參院取得進展，交易平台Coinbase(COIN-US)與穩定幣發行商Circle(CRCL-US)股價當時一度跌達11%。若民主黨席次增加，業界要爭取法案過關，可能得接受更嚴格的消費者保障，以及對付息型穩定幣的限制。

銀行業則關注資本規定。聯邦監管機構估計，現行提案可使大型銀行的資本要求降低約4.8%，騰出數十億美元用於放款或回饋股東。相關規則由聯準會(Fed)訂定，參院則能透過人事同意權影響未來由誰填補職缺。民主黨若掌控任一院，也可透過委員會調閱企業文件、傳喚高層出席聽證會。部分民主黨議員已就白宮宴會廳捐款及關稅豁免索取資料。

AI資料中心擴建 電網升級誰買單

摩根士丹利估計，微軟(MSFT-US)、亞馬遜(AMZN-US)、Google母公司Alphabet(GOOGL-US)(GOOG-US)及臉書母公司Meta(META-US)等雲端業者，2027年資本支出將超過1兆美元。隨著資料中心用電需求攀升，居民也愈來愈在意電費。《CNBC》10月調查顯示，63%的登記選民反對在住家方圓10英里(約16公里)內興建資料中心，僅13%支持。

爭議已進入國會。眾院9月以417票對3票通過一項法案，要求各州監管機構評估是否應由大型資料中心負擔新增的電力設施成本。部分民主黨議員主張應訂定強制規範，該案最終未能跨過參院程序表決門檻。若選後民主黨影響力上升，科技公司可能得承擔更多電網升級費用；至於個別設施能在哪裡接上電網、何時動工，仍取決於州政府、地方政府及公用事業。

news.Title: 台股失守4萬5！外資狂賣「這檔」逾11萬張　葉育碩：接下來盯緊3大訊號
news.Content:
台北股市今（2）日開盤遭遇強烈賣壓，盤中一度狂瀉 812 點、最低下探至 44,399 點，直接跌破 45,000 點大關。所幸低檔買盤隨後進場承接，終場台股大盤跌幅收斂，下跌 291.69 點，收在 44,920.14 點，跌幅 0.65%，成交金額為 7,588.75 億元。面對盤勢大幅震盪與外資持續瘋狂提款， 財經專家葉育碩 指出，大盤展現出出乎預期的韌性，但外資爆砍單一檔 ETF 超過 11 萬張，投資人接下來必須密切關注 「三大觀察點」 。

【韓股反彈與暗盤訊號 恐慌情緒早盤逐步收斂】

葉育碩分析，今日台股走勢雖然開低跌破關鍵整數關卡，但呈現「開低走高」的抗跌態勢，從早盤最低點到收盤已成功拉回超過 500 點。事實上，從假日部分交易所的暗盤交易即可提前觀察到個股反彈跡象；加上今日早盤韓國股市隨著三星、SK海力士等記憶體權值股反彈帶頭翻紅，有效緩和了亞洲市場的恐慌氣氛。提前掌握暗盤等資訊，能幫助投資人避免在開盤恐慌時將持股砍在最低點。

【外資連3日提款2548億 00406A慘遭狂砍11萬張】

news.Title: STMicroelectronics Could Reach New Highs—Here's What Needs to Happen
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in STMicroelectronics N.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

STMicroelectronics stock, despite a near 50% correction in 2026, is technically positioned for a third Elliott Wave move toward fresh all-time highs.

The company posted Q3 revenue of $3.76 billion, up 17.9%, with widening margins, surging free cash flow, and bullish guidance pointing to mid-20% growth in Q4.

Analysts maintain a consensus Moderate Buy rating with 50% upside potential.

STMicroelectronics (NYSE: STM) stock price action is set up for a big move that could take it to all-time highs. While STM suffered an ugly price correction of nearly 50%, which suggested a market implosion, investors shouldn't get it wrong.

The correction that took place in Q2 and Q3 2026 was a mechanism within a rapidly swelling market.

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

STM's fundamental story is a legacy business becoming a next-gen AI enabler, with rapidly expanding margins and ample free cash flow, cementing its already central position in the tech landscape.

The stock price story follows suit: a legacy market transitioning to one in which free cash flow is growing at a high triple-digit pace, expected to remain strong in the coming year and underpin capital returns.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

The shift is reflected in trading volume, which took a decidedly bullish turn in 2024 and has trended higher ever since.

Technically, STM is in the midst of an Elliott Wave cycle that has yet to play out.

→ 3 Robotics ETFs, 3 Different Ways to Bet on Humanoid Robots

The initial and second upwaves are complete, and the market is set up for a third move that could take STM's price to fresh highs.

Strong Q3 Results and Bullish Guidance Set the Stage for 2027

STMicroelectronics posted a solid Q3, with revenue up 17.9% to $3.76 billion, narrowly beating consensus. Growth was broad across channels, led by a 46% increase in the RF Optical segment, critical for data centers and high-speed data transmission. By end market, sales to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) grew 10.2%, while sales to distribution centers rose nearly 39%, and total sales are expected to remain strong in the coming quarters as demand outpaces supply.

Margin news was mixed, but with a silver lining. The company missed consensus for adjusted earnings because higher capital expenditure (CapEx) obscured strengths revealed by internal metrics. Gross and operating margins widened by more than 400 basis points, driving triple-digit increases in cash and free cash flow. Operating cash flow more than doubled to $1.02 billion, leaving free cash flow (FCF) at $351 million, despite higher CapEx, up 2.7x from the prior year and a 9.3% FCF margin.

Story Continues

Guidance is a catalyst for this market, likely to be compounded by similarly strong results and forecasts in the upcoming quarters. STM provided a hot guide for Q4, expecting revenue above consensus, up more than 10% sequentially and accelerating into the mid-20% range versus last year. Factors suggesting the guide is cautious and that strengths will continue include the book-to-bill ratio, which came in well above 3. At this pace, the backlog is growing at three times the pace of revenue, setting the stage for a robust 2027.

Analysts and Institutions See 50% Upside for STMicroelectronics

Analysts expressed some caution in their initial responses to the earnings release, highlighting high expectations and the potential for investors to be dissatisfied with the gross margin, as good as it was.

That said, the net response reaffirmed the consensus Moderate Buy rating and the forecast for 50% upside, with analysts focused on the growth trajectory, cash flow, and expansion plans.

CapEx increases fund a multi-year AI-focused expansion plan. It aims to optimize existing capacity and focus on optical connectivity, the key to unlocking AI's power.

Institutions and other sell-side interests reflect confidence in this stock and its value. Institutions own about 75% of the stock across U.S. and home-listed shares and are accumulating it at discounted prices.

Short-sellers, the other sell-side interest, are largely absent, providing no headwind for share prices. The likely outcome is that institutions continue to support the market at or near $45, if not slowly lift support over time, providing a base for the next big rally.

STMicroelectronics Has Major Catalysts Ahead

STMicroelectronics has three big catalysts that can trigger its rebound and sustain the upward trajectory: margin recovery, an EV inflection, and monetizing its investments in optical connects.

Margin recovery is expected to continue in Q4, potentially to pre-expansion levels. If so, it signals successful optimization and may prompt aggressive re-rating from analysts.

The EV inflection is an industry-wide phenomenon underpinned by inventory normalization and may generate a definitive data point in STM's upcoming report, another catalyst for analysts.

Monetization of AI investments is the final piece, cementing the company's transition to a next-gen AI enabler.

Risks include execution, with manufacturing footprint changes key to expansion, customer concentration, and end-market cyclicality. Clients are centered in big-name hyperscalers and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), which accounts for a low-double-digit percentage of revenue, while market cyclicality may soon end. The automotive market is the root of cyclical weaknesses, which may be mitigated by the rise of physical AI and the Internet of Things (IoT), which will rely on many of the same microcontrol products.

news.Title: PTC Heads Into Q4 Earnings as Schneider Buyout Looms: What's in Store?
news.Content:
PTC Inc. PTC is scheduled to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 4, after market close.

For the fiscal fourth quarter, PTC estimates revenues in the $630-$690 million band. Non-GAAP EPS is projected in the range of $1.63 to $2.21.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues is pegged at $657.6 million, down 26.4% from the year-ago reported number. The consensus estimate for earnings is pegged at $2.00 per share, down 42.4% from a year ago.

The company's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in three of the trailing four quarters, while missing once, with the average earnings surprise being 25.9%.
