news.Title: MPWR Q3 Earnings Surpass Estimates on Enterprise Data Strength
news.Content:
Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. MPWR reported third-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $8.19 per share, which increased 73.2% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $7.80 by 5%. Revenues surged 63.1% to $1.20 billion, beating the consensus mark of $1.16 billion by 3.6%.

Record sales reflected strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) and server power solutions, supported by expanding customer relationships and higher module content. Enterprise Data revenues jumped 164.6% year over year, accounting for 42.1% of total sales.

MPWR's Profitability Expands Despite Higher Costs

GAAP net income increased 50.8% to $271.1 million, or $5.51 per share, from $179.8 million, or $3.74 per share, a year earlier. Non-GAAP net income climbed 77.3% to $402.7 million. GAAP operating income rose to $357.7 million from $195.2 million.

Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 20 basis points (bps) year over year to 55.7%. Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 38.4% to $205.3 million, while the non-GAAP operating margin improved 320 bps to 38.6%.

Stock-based compensation and related expenses totaled $106.3 million compared with $53.5 million in the preceding quarter. Management reiterated its preference for gradual gross margin expansion while maintaining pricing discipline amid rising supplier costs.

Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. Quote

Monolithic's Enterprise Data Business Accelerates

Enterprise Data revenues reached $506.7 million, up 33.2% sequentially. Higher sales of power management solutions for AI and server applications drove growth, supported by stronger demand across existing customers.

Management raised its 2026 Enterprise Data revenue growth floor to 150% from 130%. Increasing adoption of power modules, customer diversification and higher content per computing platform remain major drivers. Application-specific integrated circuit customers have also contributed to demand for higher-value modules.

Storage and Computing revenues increased 3% year over year to $192.2 million but declined 3.8% sequentially. DDR5 power management products and storage applications supported sales, while weaker notebook demand, partly related to downstream memory constraints, remained a headwind.

MPWR's Communications and Automotive Sales Rise

Communications revenues surged 134.7% year over year to $187.4 million, representing 15.6% of total sales. Sequential growth of 42.5% reflected higher demand for power solutions used in optical modules and network switches.

Management expects optical module upgrades, including the transition to 1.6-terabit technology, and additional switching applications to support growth into 2027. Communications is expected to remain the company's second-fastest-growing end market.

Automotive revenues advanced 19.2% to $180.7 million, primarily benefiting from higher sales of advanced driver-assistance system power solutions. Monolithic received initial orders for its 48-volt power products, with 48-volt and zonal electrical architectures expected to drive further design opportunities in 2027.

Story Continues

Monolithic Broadens Its Industrial Product Portfolio

Industrial revenues increased 29% year over year to $71.4 million, reflecting higher sales of power sources. The company began ramping robotics solutions featuring sensors and motor control products across multiple geographic markets.

Consumer revenues declined 11.6% year over year to $64 million, although sales improved 12.6% sequentially. Management continues to prioritize new design wins across industrial and consumer applications to support future revenue opportunities.

The company also secured its first major data converter design win, with revenues ramp-up expected in 2027. Its expanding high-speed memory portfolio includes additional clock driver and registered clock driver products, which management expects to contribute in 2027 and 2028.

MPWR Expands Capacity and Maintains Liquidity

Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled $1.09 billion at September quarter-end, down from $1.41 billion in the preceding quarter. Operating cash flow increased to $289.9 million from $227.9 million.

Inventories increased to $764.9 million from $675.8 million, while inventory days based on current-quarter revenues declined to 130 from 140. The company repurchased $453.4 million of shares during the quarter.

Annual revenue-supporting capacity exceeded $6 billion, with management targeting $8 billion by the second half of 2027. The company also began sampling gallium nitride solutions for 800-volt data center architectures, complementing its silicon carbide offerings.

Monolithic Projects Higher Q4 Revenues

For the fourth quarter of 2026, management expects revenues between $1.315 billion and $1.385 billion. Non-GAAP gross margin is projected between 55.5% and 56.1%, while non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be in the range of $216.8 million to $220.8 million.

GAAP operating expenses are forecast between $334 million and $342 million. Management expects a non-GAAP tax rate of 15% for 2026.

In October, the board authorized an additional $500 million in share repurchases, bringing the total current authorization to $1 billion after third-quarter buybacks.

news.Content:
Navitas Semiconductor NVTS is scheduled to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 3, 2026.

Navitas Semiconductor anticipates revenues of $13.5 million (+/- $0.5 million) for the third quarter of 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for second-quarter revenues is pegged at $13.48 million, suggesting a year-over-year increase of 33.3%.

The consensus mark for loss is pegged at 4 cents per share for the third quarter of 2026, unchanged over the past 30 days. NVTS reported a loss of 5 cents per share in the year-ago quarter.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Navitas Semiconductor's bottom-line results have matched the Zacks Consensus Estimate in three of the trailing four quarters, while beating once, with the average surprise being 5%.

Navitas Semiconductor Corporation Price and EPS Surprise

Navitas Semiconductor Corporation price-eps-surprise | Navitas Semiconductor Corporation Quote

Earnings Whispers for NVTS

Our proven model does not conclusively predict an earnings beat for Navitas Semiconductor this time. The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) increases the odds of an earnings beat, which is not the case here.

Navitas Semiconductor has an Earnings ESP of 0.00% and carries a Zacks Rank #3 at present. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they are reported with our Earnings ESP Filter. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Factors Likely to Influence NVTS' Q3 Results

Navitas Semiconductor is a well-known provider of power semiconductors, driven by its gallium nitride (GaN) business, under GaNFast, GaNSafe and GaNSense brands, along with silicon carbide (SiC) devices. Navitas Semiconductor is expected to have benefited from the growing demand for power that is served by the company's GaN and SiC technologies.

Navitas Semiconductor is shifting its focus toward high-power markets, such as artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, performance computing, energy and grid infrastructure, and industrial electrification. Its GaN and SiC chips are well-suited for new high-voltage systems that need more efficient power use. This strategic move aligns with the company's Navitas 2.0 strategy, under which the company is reallocating resources toward high-power markets, pruning lower-margin mobile business and working more closely with hyperscalers, graphics processing unit vendors and system OEMs.

Navitas Semiconductor's inclusion in NVIDIA's new 800-volt AI factory ecosystem is an important step. The new architecture shifts data center power distribution from traditional AC/DC stages to a high-voltage DC approach that requires faster, more efficient power electronics. This creates an opening for Navitas Semiconductor's GaN and high-voltage SiC technologies, both of which are now part of the NVIDIA-led ecosystem.

Story Continues

Navitas Semiconductor remains one of the few companies offering both GaN and SiC solutions across the power chain, from the grid to the data center rack. During the second quarter of 2026, management noted increasing adoption of GaN in high-end computing applications, including chargers above 200 watts and a recently launched 1,600-watt platform for high-performance gaming systems. As AI infrastructure spending continues to grow, Navitas Semiconductor remains well-positioned to benefit from higher demand for its GaN and SiC products. The above-mentioned factors are likely to have contributed to the company's prospects in the to-be-reported quarter.

However, NVTS' Navitas 2.0 strategy involves moving away from mobile charging and consumer electronics toward higher-power AI and industrial markets. While this may improve long-term growth, it also introduces meaningful near-term revenue volatility. The company is effectively walking away from markets where it already had product traction and revenue history in exchange for newer markets with longer design cycles and more demanding qualification requirements. This transition could create revenue volatility over the next several quarters.

NVTS Price Performance & Stock Valuation

Navitas Semiconductor shares have plunged 31.7% over the past year, underperforming the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's growth of 13.9%. Compared to other major players in the semiconductor space, NVTS has underperformed Lam Research LRCX, FormFactor FORM and Applied Materials AMAT. Over the past year, shares of Lam Research, FormFactor and Applied Materials have rallied 61.5%, 77.3% and 80.8%, respectively.

One-Year Price Return Performance

Navitas Semiconductor is currently trading at a higher price-to-sales (P/S) multiple compared with the industry. NVTS' forward 12-month P/S ratio sits at 36.67X, significantly higher than the industry's forward 12-month P/S ratio of 4.50X.

NVTS Forward 12-Month P/S Ratio

Navitas Semiconductor stock also trades at a higher P/S multiple compared with other industry peers, including Lam Research, FormFactor and Applied Materials. At present, Lam Research, FormFactor and Applied Materials have P/S multiples of 8.61X, 7.34X and 6.46X, respectively.

Investment Consideration for Navitas Semiconductor

Navitas Semiconductor is in a good position to benefit from the fast growth of AI data centers. Its GaN and SiC chips are well-suited for new high-voltage systems that need more efficient power use. Navitas Semiconductor's inclusion in NVIDIA's next-generation 800-volt DC "AI factory" positions NVTS in a large, fast-growing market where power design is becoming a priority, which bodes well for the company's prospects.

However, NVTS faces near-term challenges due to weakness in its China business, where the company has decided to prune its low-margin mobile business and low-end consumer business, which have not yet been fully offset by growth in high-power segments. These are likely to have hurt the company's prospects in the near term.

Conclusion: Hold Navitas Semiconductor Stock Right Now

Navitas Semiconductor is well-positioned to ride on the long-term growth in the AI data center market. The company's GaN and high-voltage SiC products now play a role in NVIDIA's new 800-volt power setup, which shows that the technology is relevant and in demand. If the company executes well, it could see better margins, a stronger product mix and a clearer path to stable long-term growth.

However, near-term risks from its decision to deprioritize its lower-margin mobile and consumer business, along with the company's high valuation, warrant a cautious approach to the stock.

Twilio witnessed continued adoption of its AI-enabled communications capabilities, including Conversation Relay, Conversational Intelligence and Branded Calling. Management highlighted growing demand from AI-native businesses deploying voice agents and expanding their usage across multiple communication channels.

The company secured several notable customer agreements during the quarter. Ushur signed a seven-figure expansion involving voice AI capabilities, while Gong renewed a seven-figure agreement. Twilio also secured its first eight-figure Conversations deal with a health insurance provider, underscoring growing enterprise interest in AI-powered customer engagement.

Story Continues

Management noted that voice AI represents approximately 1% of overall voice interactions, highlighting the early stage of adoption. Twilio is also developing identity verification capabilities for AI agents, with an offering currently in private beta and general availability planned for 2027.

TWLO's Profitability Improves Despite Carrier Fees

Non-GAAP gross profit increased 18% year over year to $767.8 million. However, non-GAAP gross margin contracted 90 basis points year over year to 49.2%, primarily due to $53 million of incremental U.S. carrier pass-through fees. Excluding these fees, gross margin would have expanded 80 basis points.

Non-GAAP income from operations surged 39% year over year to $325.7 million. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 290 basis points to approximately 21%, reflecting strong gross profit growth and cost efficiencies. Operating income benefited from approximately $11 million in platform credits.

Twilio's Cash Generation Remains Strong

Net cash provided by operating activities reached $389.2 million compared with $263.6 million in the prior-year quarter. Free cash flow increased approximately 49% year over year to $369.6 million, with a free cash flow margin of 24%, up from 19%.

Twilio ended the third quarter with $1.06 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $1.83 billion in short-term marketable securities. Long-term debt stood at $993.6 million. The company repurchased $127.2 million of shares during the quarter, leaving approximately $700 million under its existing authorization.

TWLO Raises Its 2026 Outlook

For 2026, Twilio raised its reported revenue growth outlook to 20% from 18-18.5% and its organic revenue growth projection to 15% from 13-13.5%. The company also increased its non-GAAP income from operations and free cash flow guidance to $1.19-$1.20 billion each compared with the previous range of $1.135-$1.155 billion.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Twilio expects revenues between $1.595 billion and $1.605 billion, indicating reported growth of 17-17.5% and organic growth of 11-12%. Non-GAAP income from operations is projected at $300-$310 million, with non-GAAP earnings of $1.48-$1.53 per share.

Twilio Provides an Upbeat 2027 Preliminary Outlook

Management expects organic revenue growth of at least 10% in 2027, exceeding its earlier long-term framework of 7-8%. Non-GAAP gross profit growth is anticipated to remain broadly aligned with organic revenue growth.

Twilio also projects non-GAAP income from operations and free cash flow of at least $1.35 billion each in 2027.

news.Title: ASE Technology Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI-Driven LEAP Growth
news.Content:
ASE Technology Holding ASX reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of 37 cents per ADS, which increased 125.3% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 8.8%.

Revenues surged 44.8% year over year and 27.8% sequentially to NT$244.16 billion. In U.S. dollar terms, revenues of $7.64 billion surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.3%. Results reflected robust artificial intelligence (AI)-driven demand for Leading-edge Advanced Packaging (LEAP) services, with Assembly, Testing and Materials (ATM) revenues climbing 51% year over year.

ASX ATM Growth Accelerates on LEAP Demand

ATM revenues totaled NT$151.49 billion, up 20.1% sequentially and 51% year over year. Packaging revenues surged 52.5% to NT$122.95 billion, while testing revenues advanced 42.8% to NT$26.30 billion.

Management cited strong demand across LEAP and conventional semiconductor services, with capacity operating at or near full utilization. Faster-than-expected installations of LEAP capacity supported revenue growth, while demand continued to exceed available supply across advanced and mainstream packaging operations.

ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. Quote

ASE Technology Revenue Mix Shifts Toward Computing

Computing represented 34% of ATM revenues, up from 25% in the year-ago quarter. Communication's contribution declined to 38% from 45%, while automotive, consumer and other applications accounted for 28%.

By service type, bumping, flip-chip, wafer-level packaging and system-in-package services contributed 51% of ATM revenues. Wire bonding accounted for 24%, testing represented 17%, other services contributed 6%, and materials made up 2%.

Management expects computing applications to remain a major growth driver through 2027 and 2028, supported by increasing LEAP adoption in high-performance computing and other advanced semiconductor applications.

ASE Technology's EMS Results Stay Mixed

Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) revenues increased 35.4% year over year and 42.1% sequentially to NT$93.47 billion. Consumer applications represented 41% of EMS revenues, computing contributed 21%, and communication accounted for 19%.

EMS gross margin declined 60 basis points sequentially to 8.3%, reflecting higher pass-through component costs and product-mix changes. However, operating margin improved to 3.3% from 2.4% in the prior quarter, supported by operating expense leverage.

Story Continues

Management noted that growing demand for AI accelerators contributed to computing revenue expansion, while elevated component costs continued to weigh on profitability.

ASE Technology Margins Expand

Consolidated gross profit increased 86.9% year over year to NT$53.97 billion. Gross margin expanded 500 basis points to 22.1%, reflecting stronger ATM revenues, favorable LEAP product mix and currency benefits.

Operating income surged 151% to NT$33.14 billion, while operating margin improved 580 basis points to 13.6%. Operating expenses increased to NT$20.82 billion, mainly due to higher headcount, profit-sharing expenses and research and development spending.

ATM gross margin reached 30.6%, up from 22.6% a year earlier, while operating margin expanded to 20% from 10.8%. Management indicated that increasing LEAP contributions have pushed profitability beyond the segment's previous structural margin ceiling.

ASX Investment Spending Moves Higher

Equipment capital expenditures totaled $2.10 billion during the third quarter, including $991 million for packaging operations, $1.07 billion for testing, $41 million for EMS and $5 million for interconnect materials and other activities.

The company additionally invested approximately $1.8 billion in facilities and land during the quarter. Management raised its 2026 capital expenditure budget to $11.5 billion from $10.5 billion, reflecting continued investment in semiconductor capacity expansion.

ASE Technology has 22 ongoing building projects in Taiwan, with more than half expected to begin supporting revenues by 2027. Management anticipates higher capital expenditures in 2027 as capacity constraints persist.

ASX Balance Sheet Remains Healthy

As of Sept. 30, 2026, ASE Technology held NT$107.94 billion in cash, cash equivalents and current financial assets. Total interest-bearing debt increased to NT$406.46 billion, while unused credit facilities totaled NT$457.28 billion. The net debt-to-equity ratio was 0.66.

Net cash generated from operating activities reached NT$50.46 billion during the quarter.

ASX Outlook Remains Strong

For the fourth quarter of 2026, management expects consolidated revenues to increase 6-8% sequentially in New Taiwan dollar terms. Gross margin is projected between 23% and 24%, while operating margin is expected in the 14.5-15.5% range. ATM revenues are forecast to grow 11-13% sequentially, with gross margin improving 100-200 basis points. EMS revenues are expected to remain relatively flat, with operating margin around 2%.

Management raised its 2026 LEAP revenue outlook to more than $4 billion and expects LEAP revenues to double in 2027. Full-process packaging revenues are projected to exceed $1 billion in 2027, while co-packaged optics revenues are expected to surpass $500 million, supported by sustained demand for advanced semiconductor technologies.

news.Title: What to Expect From Apple’s Q4
news.Content:
Apple (AAPL) will report its fourth-quarter earnings on Nov. 2. Strong demand for the iPhone and Mac is expected to support the company's performance, although supply constraints could limit sales growth.

AAPL stock has gained 28% so far this year and hit a new 52-week high of $351.73 on Oct. 23. The rally, supported by strong momentum in Apple's products and services businesses, has pushed the stock's valuation higher ahead of the Q4 earnings announcement. Let's take a closer look.

More News from Barchart

Elon Musk Invests $1 Billion in Skydance Stock. He Could Be Setting the Stage for a Major Starlink Deal.

'I Still Live A Great Life': Floyd Mayweather Says a Man 'Acting Like He Was A Friend' Stole $200 Million From Him

MRVL Stock Sinks as Marvell Technology Reportedly Considers Acquiring Lumentum

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Supply Challenges Could Hurt Apple's Q4 Growth

Apple's Q4 report will likely reflect slower growth despite sustained demand for its core hardware products. During the Q3 earnings call, management indicated that customer demand for the iPhone and Mac remained robust but cautioned that supply constraints were expected to intensify sequentially, impacting growth.

Consequently, management projected total revenue growth of 9% to 11% year-over-year (YOY) for Q4. That signaled moderation from the stronger growth reported in the preceding quarter.

Apple delivered revenue of $109.4 billion in Q3, up 16% YOY. Performance remained broad-based, with every geographic segment recording double-digit growth. Product revenue increased 18% YOY to $78.7 billion, supported by strong contributions from the iPhone and Mac.

The iPhone remained Apple's largest revenue contributor, generating $54.3 billion, up 22% YOY. The iPhone 17 lineup drove growth, with double-digit gains across most markets. Apple also reported an all-time high in its active iPhone installed base and a June-quarter record for customers upgrading their devices. These indicators suggest that the company continues to benefit from customer retention, upgrade demand, and the strength of its broader ecosystem.

Mac revenue rose 29% YOY to $10.4 billion in Q3. The performance reflected strong demand for the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro, with growth across both developed and emerging markets.

Although Apple expects iPhone demand to remain strong in the September quarter, management anticipates supply constraints and unfavorable foreign exchange movements will weigh on the reported growth rate. The company projected mid-teens YOY growth in iPhone revenue, below the 22% YOY growth achieved in Q3.

Story Continues

Apple's Services segment is expected to sustain momentum. Management indicated that Services revenue should grow at a pace broadly comparable to Q3. The segment generated $30.7 billion in Q3, an increase of 12% YOY.

The business benefits from Apple's extensive installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices, which provides a substantial platform for recurring revenue generation. Paid subscriptions now exceed 1.5 billion, while both transacting accounts and paid accounts reached new quarterly records. The company also reported double-digit growth in these account categories across emerging markets. Advertising, the App Store, AppleCare, Apple Music, Apple TV+, cloud services, and payment-related offerings are among the businesses supporting this expansion.

The company's earnings outlook also suggests a more moderate growth trajectory in Q4. Slower revenue growth and higher memory costs could pressure margins and constrain earnings growth. Analysts expect Apple to report EPS of $1.98, representing about 7% YOY growth. This would mark a notable deceleration from the 29% increase in earnings reported in Q3. However, the previous quarter's comparison included a $0.11 per share benefit from tariff refunds.

Is Apple Stock a Buy?

Apple's Q4 performance is likely to be supported by resilient iPhone and Mac demand and continued Services growth, although supply constraints and higher memory costs could moderate revenue and earnings growth. With expected EPS growth slowing to 7% and AAPL stock trading near record highs, investors should take caution before going long on Apple shares ahead of earnings.

Overall, Wall Street analysts maintain a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating for Apple stock.

news.Title: VICR Gains From Hardware Boom and Rising Backlog: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Vicor Corporation VICR is benefiting from rising demand for high-density power delivery solutions as AI processors, data centers, industrial platforms and defense applications require more efficient power conversion. Growth in Advanced Products, a rising backlog and expanding licensing income are supporting its revenue outlook. However, manufacturing capacity constraints, customer program timing and uneven royalty recognition remain key challenges.

Vicor's second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 1.6% year over year to $143.4 million, exceeding the consensus estimate by 3.13%. Excluding $45 million in patent litigation settlement revenues recorded in the year-ago quarter, revenues increased 49.3%. Advanced Products revenues surged 45% sequentially to $94.2 million, accounting for 65.7% of total revenues. Product revenues rose 31.8% year over year to $112.9 million, while royalty revenues increased to $30.4 million from $10.4 million.

Demand momentum remains strong across high-performance computing, industrial, aerospace and defense markets. Vicor's book-to-bill ratio remained above 1, while its 12-month backlog increased 145% year over year to approximately $379.7 million. Management expects third-quarter revenues to grow nearly 10% sequentially, supported by double-digit sequential growth in Advanced Products. Vicor is targeting more than $600 million in 2026 revenues, reflecting product growth and licensing income.

Vicor is expanding manufacturing capacity to support rising demand. Its first fabrication facility, Fab 1, is approaching full capacity utilization, with additional equipment being installed to increase output. The company is also evaluating sites for a second fabrication facility, which management considers necessary to achieve its long-term revenue objective of $2.5 billion.

Technology differentiation and intellectual property licensing provide additional growth opportunities. Vicor's Factorized Power Architecture and Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) technologies are designed to improve power efficiency and current density for increasingly demanding AI processors. Second-generation VPD development with its lead customer has reached an initial chipset baseline, while development systems are being introduced to additional original equipment manufacturers and hyperscalers.

How Competitors Fare Against VICR Stock

Vicor competes with Monolithic Power Systems MPWR and Analog Devices ADI. MPWR competes in high-performance power management for AI processors and data centers, while ADI competes in analog and power-management solutions for industrial, communications and computing applications.

Story Continues

Monolithic Power is benefiting from expanding power content across AI infrastructure, enterprise data and communications as customers adopt higher-density designs and module solutions. New customer ramps, platform refreshes and DDR5 orders expand its market, while sampling for 800-volt data-center architectures adds a growth avenue.

Analog Devices is benefiting from a broad-based recovery as Industrial demand improves and AI-related data center activity expands across optical and power applications. Long-cycle exposure to automation, test, aerospace and defense, energy systems and vehicle electrification supports durable growth.

VICR's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Vicor have gained 88.5% year to date against the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Components industry's decline of 20.2%.

news.Title: Can Advanced Packaging Demand Drive KLAC's Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
KLA Corporation KLAC is seeing strong demand for its process control products as AI infrastructure investment increases the need for advanced semiconductors. As chips become more complex, manufacturers need better inspection and measurement tools to identify defects and improve production yields. Advanced packaging is becoming an important growth driver for KLAC, as new chip designs require more sophisticated manufacturing processes.

KLAC expects revenues from its advanced packaging process control systems to reach approximately $1.1 billion or more in 2026, suggesting growth of more than 70% year over year. This is nearly twice the expected growth rate of the advanced packaging market. The company is benefiting from the growing use of advanced packaging in AI infrastructure. Packaging technologies are also adopting more complex wafer manufacturing processes, which increase the need for KLAC's inspection and measurement solutions.

Demand for more advanced inspection tools is also increasing. Hybrid bonding and complex logic devices require higher inspection sensitivity to identify smaller defects. KLAC is seeing demand shift toward more advanced systems, including laser scanning and Gen 4 tools, while its macro inspection products continue to serve as key solutions. The company believes its existing technology portfolio and research and development investments position it well to meet these changing customer needs.

Looking ahead, KLAC expects its advanced packaging business to continue growing faster than the market in 2027. Strong AI infrastructure investment and rising chip complexity should support demand for its process control solutions. As of now, the company will need to manage supply constraints and increase production capacity to meet customer requirements. Overall, advanced packaging is emerging as an important growth driver for KLAC and could support its broader growth outlook over the next few years.

KLAC Faces Tough Competition

Onto Innovation ONTO is seeing strong demand for its advanced packaging inspection and metrology solutions as AI chip designs become more complex. In the second quarter of 2026, Onto Innovation's revenues increased 35% year over year to $343 million, while its inspection business grew 30% sequentially, driven by 2.5D logic and high-bandwidth memory applications. The company raised its 2026 advanced packaging growth outlook to approximately 80%, up from its previous expectation of 50%.

Applied Materials AMAT is also benefiting from increased investment in advanced packaging. The company expects its packaging revenues to grow more than 70% in 2026, supported by demand for HBM, 3D chiplet stacking and AI-related semiconductor technologies. Applied Materials is expanding its portfolio with new plating, chemical mechanical planarization and e-beam systems for advanced packaging. It also expects its process diagnostics and control business, which includes inspection and metrology solutions, to grow more than 50% in 2026 as chipmakers focus on improving production yields and output.

news.Title: Intel Surpasses Q3 Earnings Estimates on Robust Data Center Demand
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC reported solid third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted earnings and revenues beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Strong demand for server processors, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, supported top-line growth despite weakness in the PC market.

Non-GAAP earnings surged 126.1% year over year to 52 cents per share, surpassing the consensus estimate of 39 cents by 33.33%. Revenues increased 20.9% to $16.51 billion, beating the consensus estimate of $16.44 billion by 0.44%. Data Center and AI revenues jumped 78% year over year, reflecting strong demand across hyperscale, enterprise and neo-cloud customers. However, a soft fourth-quarter outlook overshadowed the feel-good factor for investors and shares plunged more than 25% in pre-market trading.

Intel Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Intel Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Intel Corporation Quote

Data Center Business Drives Growth

Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenues increased to $7.32 billion from $4.12 billion in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, revenues improved 17%, supported by higher server CPU output and robust demand for AI infrastructure. Purpose-built silicon revenues increased more than 50% sequentially and more than doubled year over year.

DCAI operating income rose to $3.04 billion from $964 million a year ago, with operating margin expanding to 41.5% from 23.4%. Higher revenues and lower operating expenses aided profitability. Granite Rapids became the largest product family in Intel's server portfolio, while Clearwater Forest began generating revenues. Management highlighted strong customer interest in Diamond Rapids and the new Intel GPU D-series for AI workloads.

Client Business Faces Memory Shortages

Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) revenues declined 5% year over year to $8.1 billion from $8.54 billion. Revenues fell 9% sequentially as industry-wide memory shortages, higher component prices and constrained IT budgets weakened PC demand. Customers also reduced purchases to manage inventories amid softer consumption.

Despite these headwinds, AI PC revenues grew 35% year over year. Wildcat Lake processor shipments increased approximately 70% sequentially, with available supply sold out. CCPG operating income declined to $2.29 billion from $2.69 billion, while operating margin contracted to 28.2% from 31.6%. Management expects challenging PC market conditions to persist until memory availability and pricing normalize.

Story Continues

Foundry Operations Show Improvement

Intel Foundry revenues climbed 58% year over year to $6.7 billion from $4.24 billion, driven by higher manufacturing volumes and improving execution. Sequential revenues increased 16%, supported by better-than-expected growth in Intel 3 and Intel 18A production. External foundry revenues were $411 million, increasing $118 million sequentially, primarily due to a non-recurring customer program.

The segment reported an operating loss of $1.85 billion compared with a loss of $2.32 billion a year ago. Improved manufacturing yields, shorter production cycles and higher factory utilization helped reduce wafer costs. Intel 18A manufacturing costs declined approximately 40% since the first quarter. The company also released its Intel 14A process design kit in October, advancing its next-generation manufacturing roadmap.

Operating Margins Expand

Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 44.1% from 40% a year ago, reflecting a more favorable product mix and lower manufacturing costs. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 19.6% from 11.2%, supported by higher revenues and disciplined spending.

Non-GAAP operating income increased to $3.23 billion from $1.52 billion, while adjusted net income attributable to Intel rose to $2.76 billion from $1.02 billion. Non-GAAP research and development and marketing, general and administrative expenses increased to $4.05 billion from $3.93 billion. On a GAAP basis, net income attributable to Intel declined to $3.32 billion from $4.06 billion.

Cash Position Strengthens

Intel generated $5.08 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter compared with $2.55 billion a year ago. Adjusted free cash flow improved to $1.64 billion from $896 million, despite continued investments in manufacturing capacity and advanced process technologies.

As of Sept. 26, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $21.85 billion, while short-term investments totaled $32.16 billion. Long-term debt was $46.32 billion. The company completed a $23 billion equity offering in August, strengthening its financial flexibility to fund capacity expansion and address growing server demand.

Soft Fourth-Quarter Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Intel expects revenues between $15 billion and $16 billion. At the midpoint, non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 38%, with adjusted earnings of 25 cents per share. GAAP earnings are expected to be 10 cents per share.

Management expects DCAI revenues to increase by a mid-teens percentage sequentially, while CCPG revenues are projected to decline more than 20%. Guidance incorporates an estimated $300 million revenue impact from a manufacturing disruption at its Israel facility. Intel expects 2026 gross capital expenditures of $20 billion, with spending projected to increase significantly in 2027 to support expanding production capacity.

Zacks Rank

news.Content: Carvana Co. CVNA reported earnings of 39 cents per share for the third quarter of 2026, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 47 cents. Earnings rose 85.7% year over year. Retail units sold advanced 38.9% to a record 217,385, marking the company's first quarter above 200,000 units. news.Title: Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend Analysis
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . A Closer Look at the Upcoming Payout, Dividend History, and Growth Outlook for the Semiconductor Leader Texas Instruments Inc ( NASDAQ:TXN ) recently announced a total dividend of $1.52 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-10-30. This amount consists of a $1.52 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-11-10. For income-focused investors, the ex-dividend date is a key marker: shareholders must own the stock before that date to qualify for the payment. As investors look forward to this upcoming distribution, the spotlight also shines on the company's dividend history, yield, and growth rates. Using data from GuruFocus, let's look into Texas Instruments Inc's dividend performance and assess its sustainability. What Does Texas Instruments Inc Do? Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TXN. High Yield Dividend Stocks in Gurus' Portfolio This Powerful Chart Made Peter Lynch 29% A Year For 13 Years How to calculate the intrinsic value of a stock? Is TXN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Texas Instruments designs and manufactures semiconductors sold to electronics designers and manufacturers worldwide, generating $17.68 billion of revenue in 2025. Its Analog segment (about 79% of revenue) supplies power management and signal chain chips that condition, amplify, convert, and manage electrical signals and power in nearly every type of electronic equipment; its Embedded Processing segment provides microcontrollers and processors. TI's portfolio exceeds 80,000 products serving industrial, automotive, personal electronics, data center, and communications markets, sold largely through its own direct channel. Its competitive advantages include internal manufacturing and technology, highlighted by a multi-year investment cycle in 300-millimeter wafer fabs in Texas and Utah, portfolio breadth, channel reach, and product longevity. Founded in 1930 and headquartered in Dallas, TI manages the business to maximize long-term free cash flow per share. A Glimpse at Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend History Texas Instruments Inc has maintained a consistent dividend payment record since 1985, and dividends are currently distributed on a quarterly basis. More importantly, the company has increased its dividend each year since 2001. The stock is thus listed as a dividend aristocrat, an honor given to companies that have raised their dividend each year for at least the past 25 years. For value investors, such a long record signals disciplined capital allocation and a management team committed to returning cash to shareholders through complete business cycles. Story Continues Below is a chart showing annual Dividends Per Share for tracking historical trends. Breaking Down Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend Yield and Growth As of today, Texas Instruments Inc currently has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.92% and a 12-month forward dividend yield of 2.04%. The gap between the two suggests an expectation of increased dividend payments over the next 12 months. The trailing yield reflects dividends actually paid over the past year, while the forward yield incorporates the most recent dividend rate annualized, so a higher forward figure implies the payout has recently been raised. Over the past three years, Texas Instruments Inc's annual dividend growth rate was 5.50%. Extended to a five-year horizon, this rate increased to 8.00% per year. And over the past decade, Texas Instruments Inc's annual dividends per share growth rate stands at an impressive 15.20%. This pattern of decelerating growth from the 10-year to the 3-year window is worth noting: it may reflect a more mature payout policy or a period of heavier capital investment in manufacturing capacity. Based on Texas Instruments Inc's dividend yield and five-year growth rate, the 5-year yield on cost of Texas Instruments Inc stock as of today is approximately 2.82%. Yield on cost estimates the effective return on today's investment after five years of assumed dividend growth, offering a forward-looking complement to the current yield. The Sustainability Question: Payout Ratio and Profitability To assess the sustainability of the dividend, one needs to evaluate the company's payout ratio. The dividend payout ratio provides insights into the portion of earnings the company distributes as dividends. A lower ratio suggests that the company retains a significant part of its earnings, thereby ensuring the availability of funds for future growth and unexpected downturns. As of 2026-09-30, Texas Instruments Inc's dividend payout ratio is 0.73. And this may suggest that the company's dividend may not be sustainable, since a ratio approaching three-quarters of earnings leaves a narrower cushion for reinvestment and adverse conditions. Texas Instruments Inc's profitability rank offers an understanding of the company's earnings prowess relative to its peers. GuruFocus ranks Texas Instruments Inc's profitability 8 out of 10 as of 2026-09-30, suggesting good profitability prospects. The company has reported positive net income for each year over the past decade, further solidifying its high profitability. This earnings consistency is an important counterweight when judging whether the current payout level can be maintained. Growth Metrics: The Future Outlook To ensure the sustainability of dividends, a company must have robust growth metrics. Texas Instruments Inc's growth rank of 8 out of 10 suggests that the company's growth trajectory is good relative to its competitors. However, the headline rank should be read alongside the underlying operating trends discussed below, which have been uneven in recent years amid a cyclical semiconductor downturn and heavy capital spending. Revenue is the lifeblood of any company, and Texas Instruments Inc's revenue per share , combined with the 3-year revenue growth rate , indicates a strong revenue model. Texas Instruments Inc's revenue has increased by approximately -3.60% per year on average, a rate that underperforms approximately 63.15% of global competitors. The negative figure reflects the recent industry correction rather than a structural loss of demand, but it does temper the growth picture. The company's 3-year EPS growth rate showcases its capability to grow its earnings, a critical component for sustaining dividends in the long run. During the past three years, Texas Instruments Inc's earnings increased by approximately -16.80% per year on average, a rate that underperforms approximately 67.5% of global competitors. Lastly, the company's 5-year EBITDA growth rate of -6.00% underperforms approximately 69.47% of global competitors. Next Steps for Dividend-Focused Investors Texas Instruments Inc's dividend story is one of strong foundations and near-term tension. On the positive side, the company has paid dividends since 1985, raised them every year since 2001, and holds dividend aristocrat status, backed by a profitability rank of 8 out of 10 and a decade of positive net income. The forward yield of 2.04% exceeding the trailing 1.92% points to continued increases, and a 5-year yield on cost of roughly 2.82% rewards patient holders. Yet a payout ratio of 0.73, combined with negative three-year revenue and EPS growth and a -6.00% five-year EBITDA trend, suggests the dividend consumes a meaningful share of earnings during the current downturn. For value investors, the key question is whether Texas Instruments Inc's long-term free cash flow per share can resume growth as analog demand recovers and the 300-millimeter fab investment cycle matures. A payout ratio near 0.73 is not alarming for a cyclical semiconductor leader, but it warrants monitoring alongside cash flow rather than earnings alone. Readers should watch upcoming quarterly reports for signs of revenue stabilization and capital spending discipline. news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉滬指二連跌 失守三千六大關 連六周收黑 十月累跌逾6%
news.Content:
中國A股三大指數周五(30日)齊步收低，上證指數( SSEC )連2日收黑，失守3600點大關，本周跌2.48%，周線連六跌，月線累跌逾6%，創業板指與科創50指數月線均跌逾23%，深證成指( SZI )也連六周報跌，本周收黑7.2%，月線收低15.94%。

滬指周五收低1.44%至3599.02點，深指收跌2.73%至10833.78點，創業板指收黑4.13%至2413.63點，科創50指數重挫5.48%，全市場成交額1兆6744億元(人民幣，下同)，較上一日放量1179億元。

盤面上，光通訊族群領跌兩市，科瑞思、燦勤科技、會暢科技、德科立、移遠通信等跌停或跌超10%，太辰光、新易盛、勝宏科技均跌超13%；影視院線類股亦重挫，文投控股、橫店影視、慈文傳媒、奧飛娛樂、捷成股份觸及跌停；軟體、半導體、軍工類族群亦跌幅居前，通達海、指南針、道通科技、財富趨勢、華大九天、三維天地等逾20股跌停或跌超10%。

上漲族群方面，白酒族群全天強勢表現，黑芝麻、瀘州老窖、新乳業、皇台酒業、古井貢酒、迎駕貢酒、青島食品、好想你等股漲停；港口航運股掀漲停潮，錦江航運、中遠航運等漲停；銀行族群續揚，西安銀行暴漲8.64%，青農商行大漲5.57%，蘇州銀行、長沙銀行等漲超2%。

根據Wind統計數據，滬深兩市及北交所共893檔股票上漲，4598檔下跌，平盤82檔。另據大智慧VIP，滬深北三市共61檔股票漲幅在9%以上，266檔股票跌幅在9%以上。

東海證券表示，滬指收復5日線後再失守，量能略放，大單資金未能延續淨流入，而是大幅淨流出超256億元，日線KDJ尚未死叉，日線MACD尚未黃金交叉，日線指標延續矛盾。指數再度趨近下方555日均線支撐，與120周均線3618點也是一步之遙。目前指數日線技術條件尚未明顯向好，分鐘線指標再度走弱。目前指數上有5週、10週均線壓力，下有120週均線支撐，短線或呈區間震盪態勢。

中原證券認為，當前滬指與創業板指數的平均本益比分別為16.14倍、37.37倍，處於近三年中位數平均上方，適合中長期佈局。中國國家統計局數據顯示，今年前三季GDP年增4.6%，高技術製造業占規模以上工業增加值的比重同比提升1.6個百分點，新動能對經濟成長貢獻率保持在40%以上，滬指繼續震盪整理的機率較大，結構再平衡為核心特徵，宜密切關注宏觀經濟數據、海外流動性變化以及政策動向，短線建議關注航天裝備、軍工電子、風電設備及銀行等產業的投資機會。

萬聯證券亦稱，從經濟數據看，國民經濟運行平穩，宏觀調控維持適度寬鬆的基調。資本市場方面，10月A股流動性指標表現分化，市場投資者情緒與風險偏好受多因素影響，市場改善仍需更多支持。隨著相關部門持續深化資本市場投融資綜合改革，擴大耐心資本、長期資本和戰略資本供給，預計市場韌性有望增強，流動性環境有望改善。多重利多政策提振下，市場信心有望修復。從業績看，今年第三季財報披露接近尾聲，結構性亮點湧現。一方面，新質生產力領域，在技術創新與產業鏈協同帶動下保持高景氣增長。另一方面，具備技術、成本與供應鏈優勢的出海龍頭企業展現出較強的盈利韌性。

news.Title: SanDisk Corp (SNDK) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Highlights: Revenue Surges 378% as Data Center Demand ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Release Date: October 29, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Revenue of $11 billion exceeded guidance, up 23% sequentially and 378% year-over-year, driven by strong demand and pricing.

Non-GAAP gross margin reached 85.1%, above guidance, and non-GAAP EPS was $49.51, significantly beating the $44-$46 range.

Data center revenue grew 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion, with three U.S. hyperscalers as customers, and is expected to represent over 55% of the market in 2027.

New business model (NBM) partnerships provide long-term demand visibility, with 50% of bits under NBM for fiscal 2027 and two-thirds for fiscal 2028, and a pipeline exceeding supply through 2030.

Generated $5.7 billion in adjusted free cash flow (52% margin) and returned $5 billion to shareholders through buybacks, with no debt and $5.1 billion in cash.

Negative Points

Consumer revenue declined 29% sequentially to $397 million as the market adjusts to higher pricing.

Edge revenue growth was only 7% sequentially, with contraction at the lower end partially offsetting resilience in premium and mainstream markets.

PC and smartphone unit volumes are declining, with PC units down this year and expected to be slightly down next year, impacting near-term demand.

Fiscal Q3 is historically the weakest sequential quarter, and management advised conservatism for sequential growth from Q2 to Q3.

HBF and other new NAND technologies are still in early stages, with no revenue contribution included in the long-term financial model, and timing of meaningful revenue remains uncertain.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Can you elaborate on the NBM pipeline exceeding supply through the end of the decade, and how is that changing your thought process around bit supply and CapEx plans? A : CEO David Goeckeler said the process is working, with a robust pipeline now extending through 2030 and beyond as customers offer demand signals and financial commitments. He noted these agreements could eventually inform supply decisions, but negotiations and commitments are still underway. CFO Luis Visoso added that gross CapEx is expected at a mid-single-digit percentage of revenue for fiscal 2027.

Q : You signed two NBMs before the last call. Should we expect many more, and what percentage of bits is under contract for the next few years? A : Goeckeler said the NBM pipeline is very strong and growing, and it has become the predominant way SanDisk deals with customers. About 50% of bits are under NBM for fiscal 2027 and about two-thirds for fiscal 2028, with that percentage expected to rise. Visoso noted 95% of NBM partners are investment grade and generated about $130 billion in operating cash flow.

Story Continues

Q : Data center revenue is up almost 20x year-over-year and 61% sequentially. What is driving that penetration, and will data center reach half of your own mix? A : Goeckeler credited the BiCS8 node and CBA architecture, the right TLC and QLC products at the right time, and more refined AI inference architectures. He said customers are increasingly using TLC, QLC, and even SLC in different parts of the architecture. He added SanDisk is working to catch up to the market's data center bit mix and expects a substantially higher mix than in fiscal 2026.

Q : In fiscal Q1, about 60% of revenue growth came from volume and 40% from pricing. How do you expect that mix to progress in guidance? A : Visoso said both volume and pricing are expected to contribute in the next quarter, with modest like-for-like price increases. He added pricing is expected to continue increasing modestly throughout the year.

Q : Can you provide more detail on HBF progress and customer discussions, and how do you view new NAND tiers such as StorageNext and CMX context memory? A : Goeckeler said HBF customer conversations are robust and ongoing, with samples expected to reach customers next calendar year. He described the proliferation of new NAND tiers as healthy, saying AI inference architectures are being relentlessly refined for economics, which is pulling NAND into more parts of the architecture. He said SanDisk is staying close to the customers spending money to scale infrastructure.

Q : Are you looking to accelerate the BiCS transition from 8 to 9 and 10 to accelerate bit growth and satisfy strong customer demand? A : Goeckeler said SanDisk remains committed to its mid-to-high-teens bit growth plan. He noted node transitions require extensive planning, tool purchases, and line setup, and the fab plan is already set for that bit growth. He said there are no plans to change it at this point.

Q : Are there limits to increasingly allocating bits to data center? A : Goeckeler said there are constraints because fabs produce a certain mix of TLC, QLC, and die types, making it a constant fitting exercise to get the right product to the right customer. Visoso added that over the short term it is almost impossible to change allocation because it takes about 120 days to produce a wafer, but there are more degrees of freedom over the longer term.

Q : With PC units under pressure, are you seeing more NBM interest from the PC market? A : Visoso said SanDisk cannot discuss specific customers but has NBMs in data center and edge, and the construct is offered to any customer that wants it. Goeckeler said PC units are down this year and slightly down next year, with the current two calendar quarters representing the trough of year-over-year compares. He expects PC exabytes to grow next year as content per device rises.

Q : How do you see enterprise SSD content per server progressing in 2027 amid agentic AI proliferation? A : Goeckeler said SanDisk sees roughly 60 to 90 gigabytes of NAND demand per CPU in inference and agent orchestration applications. He said more NAND is being pulled into the inference architecture across TLC, QLC, and high-endurance solutions, and SanDisk will continue working on TAM analysis and trade-offs.

Q : Do you have an updated view on enterprise SSD share goals? A : Goeckeler said he has deliberately avoided setting specific share goals because they can lead to perverse portfolio choices. He said SanDisk will clearly mix higher into data center, noting 17x year-over-year growth, and expects that mix to go higher through 2027, but declined to provide a specific target.

Q : What is the prevailing TLC versus QLC mix among CSP customers, and will it shift meaningfully later this decade? A : Goeckeler said the mix remains about 70-30 TLC to QLC and is expected to stay there at least for the rest of the fiscal year. He said customers are discussing a reacceleration of QLC in different use cases, and the QLC product has been very well received with qualifications complete and customers ramping.

Q : Given double-digit mobile unit declines this year, can your mobile bits still grow next year? A : Goeckeler said the low end of the mobile market is under pressure, leading to unit declines, but content per unit is increasing. He expects exabyte growth in that market next year on a slightly declining unit count and said SanDisk will manage its portfolio with agility and balance.

Q : Are credit concerns around neo clouds filtering back to you, and who are the leading AI companies you referenced? A : Visoso said SanDisk has not seen any credit concerns and demand from customers is strengthening. He said the largest customers are basically all investment grade with strong cash generation. He added SanDisk sells to hyperscalers, model makers, and everybody in the business.

news.Title: Applied Materials vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: Comparing Revenue Growth Trends Between These Artificial Intelligence Companies
news.Content:
Applied Materials: A Gradual Revenue Uptrend

Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) primarily generates its revenue by designing, developing, and manufacturing the complex wafer fabrication equipment and materials engineering tools used by its diverse base of global customers to produce integrated circuits.

This year, it officially unveiled a large research and development center in California designed specifically for collaborative engineering, and it additionally appointed a new executive to serve on its board of directors.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: Consistent Revenue Expansion

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE:TSM) primarily earns its revenue by operating as a global dedicated foundry, meaning it manufactures, packages, and meticulously tests complex integrated circuits on behalf of various third-party technology clients around the world.

While operating within a complex international regulatory environment, it announced a collaborative industry initiative to transition to advanced photomasks, and its first Arizona fabrication plant successfully reached production yield rates comparable to its primary facilities in Taiwan.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue serves as the basic top-line indicator of the total capital flowing into a business from its core commercial operations before any operating expenses are deducted. Closely tracking this top-line financial figure helps investors understand the total scale and growth trajectory of a business.

Foolish Take

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, popularly known as TSMC, delivers far greater revenue than Applied Materials despite both providing essential services for the semiconductor industry. That's because TSMC is the world's dominant pure-play semiconductor foundry, controlling over 70% of the market. Applied Materials sells specialized materials engineering, deposition, and etching systems to chipmakers like TSMC.

Thanks to the artificial intelligence boom, TSMC is experiencing historic demand for its manufacturing prowess. The same tailwind is helping Applied Materials this year, as sales have taken off. Its rapid revenue growth in recent quarters was marked by the highest quarter-over-quarter revenue growth in company history during its fiscal third quarter, ended July 26.

Applied Materials was able to achieve this due to diligent planning and foresight. It nearly doubled its total manufacturing footprint over the past several years, capped off by opening a state-of-the-art manufacturing center in Singapore during Q3. This enabled the company to build and ship equipment at an unprecedented rate to fuel the global AI infrastructure surge.

news.Title: The Case Against a SpaceX and Tesla Merger
news.Content:
While we don't know what terms, if any, are on the table for a potential merger, there's a strong case that now isn't the best time for Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) to pursue a merger with Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX). The argument rests on two main ideas. First, it runs contrary to market trends; second, Tesla is on the cusp of delivering significant shareholder value after years of disappointment.

Different risk and capital profiles

Over the last decade, the major trend with industrial conglomerates such as General Electric, United Technologies Corporation, Honeywell , 3M , Danaher , Johnson Controls , and Emerson Electric has been to break them up. While each company had its own circumstances, three themes apply to all:

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Separating companies allows for greater management and operational focus.

The market has tended to apply a so-called conglomerate discount, and investors increasingly value the ability to make targeted investments.

Each company has its own specific risk and its own capital allocation priorities, and they are better served as stand-alone companies.

Given the incredible complexity inherent in managing Tesla (EVs, robotaxi/Cybercab, Optimus, energy generation/storage, charging infrastructure, and a host of investments in building its own supply chain) and SpaceX (launch services, artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, Starlink, defense networks), it's not hard to see how complex a merged entity would become.

The argument over the conglomerate discount is admittedly subject to change, as conglomerates once commanded a premium. However, that's not the case now, and until it changes, there's no strong reason to believe a merger will lead to an immediate market-valuation rerating of the merged entity. On the contrary, the opposite could occur.

Different risk profiles and capital profiles

The argument from specific risk and capital profiles is the strongest. Tesla is on the cusp of beginning a multiyear journey to scale its robotaxi service and generate a long stream of recurring revenue from robotaxi/Cybercab. Investors can disagree on its profit potential amid competition, but robotaxi/Cybercab is baked into the valuation, and if you are holding the stock, you presumably believe in the potential of autonomous driving.

Story Continues

While it will obviously require significant upfront capital investment to build out the network, Tesla has the resources to do so and create a company with significant long-term cash flows. The same argument, albeit a few more years out, applies to Optimus. Tesla does not need SpaceX to achieve its own goals.

In contrast, SpaceX operates in a high-risk sector that requires even more massive capital investment. Moreover, while Starlink is currently SpaceX's profit generator, its revenue driver is the Super Intelligence business. The former is effectively funding growth in the latter.

Tesla is moving toward becoming a company with a long-term stream of recurring revenue, scaling robotaxi/Cybercab and, in time, Optimus, and a play on physical AI. In contrast, SpaceX is a business that requires massive, ongoing, and uncertain capital expenditures and is a play on AI infrastructure.

Regarding the uncertainty of capital expenditures, consider orbital data centers and SpaceX. Their depreciation rate is likely to be high because they realistically can't be serviced in space and, unlike terrestrial data centers, which can replace servers and chips, will likely last only as long as their graphics processing units (GPUs) remain useful. A high depreciation rate implies higher maintenance capital spending.

Tesla hasn't released value from robotaxi/Cybercab yet

To understand this argument, consider how private equity might run Tesla. Their typical model is to generate value from the investment and sell the asset only once the business is firing on all cylinders, and it can optimize the price.

If you believe Tesla will evolve into a company generating billions of recurring revenue from its Cybercab fleet and then from Optimus, it makes sense to hold the asset, at least until the company proves the doubters wrong and releases value from the robotaxi rollout. At which point, Tesla shareholders will be in a stronger position to demand a healthier premium for the business.

What it means to investors

Again, while it's true that we don't know what kind of offer or what deal it will be, or even if there will be a proposal at all, the reality is the value of Tesla will key off of its current market price, and if you think it's undervalued and/or want to wait until the company releases value from robotaxi, then an offer now is unlikely to lead to a favorable outcome for you.

All told, in a merger, Tesla investors would dilute their claim on cash flows from robotaxi, EVs, and robotics (physical AI) in favor of using that cash to support space exploration and cloud computing (AI infrastructure). This creates a merged company with a significantly different risk and capital-allocation profile from Tesla, and they might not get full value for their Tesla shares until robotaxi scales.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

news.Title: Monolithic Power Systems Inc (MPWR) (Q3 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Revenue Tops $1 Billion ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Revenue: $1.2 billion in Q3 2026, up 22% sequentially and 63% year-over-year; first quarter exceeding $1 billion.

Capacity: Surpassed $6 billion in annual revenue support; $8 billion expected by second half of 2027, targeting $10 billion.

Share Repurchases: Over $450 million of company stock purchased in Q3.

Enterprise Data: Strong demand across existing customers, expected to continue into 2027.

Automotive: First orders received for 48-volt power solutions; design wins expected to drive 2027 growth.

Robotics: Began ramping sensor and motor control solutions across multiple geographies.

High-Speed Memory: Continued SAM expansion with product ramp.

Data Converters: Landed first large design win, expected to ramp next year.

High-Voltage Portfolio: Began sampling GaN-based solutions for 800-volt data center architectures, complementing silicon carbide designs.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with MPWR.

Is MPWR fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: October 29, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) exceeded $1 billion in quarterly revenue for the first time, with Q3 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 22% sequentially and 63% year-over-year.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) expanded capacity to support over $6 billion in annual revenue and expects $8 billion by the second half of 2027, with a path to $10 billion.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) raised its enterprise data growth floor to 150% year-over-year, driven by customer diversification, module adoption, and content gains.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) achieved its first large data converter design win, expected to ramp next year, and continues to increase its SAM with high-speed memory products.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) repurchased over $450 million of its own stock in Q3, reflecting confidence in its growth trajectory.

Negative Points

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) expects notebook strength to be limited in the short term due to memory constraints, with segment growth roughly flat to up slightly year-over-year.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) does not expect 800-volt GaN revenue until late 2027 or 2028, and the technology requires shipping about 50 million units to prove reliability.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) is absorbing some cost increases and not raising prices, which could pressure margins if costs continue to rise.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) faces competitive risk from integrated voltage regulators and industry consolidation, such as Analog Devices' acquisition of Empower.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) noted that its building automation opportunity, though large, will take time to materialize and the path to $50 billion revenue is still unclear.

Story Continues

Q & A Highlights

Q : Tore Svanberg of Stifel asked for elaboration on the "accelerated growth" commentary and when the $10 billion capacity target might be in place, given the company is on track to grow 50%-60% this year. A : CEO Michael Hsing said the company sees an "explosive growth period in the next few years" with no signs of slowing down. CFO Tony Balow added that growth is broadening across multiple end markets, including auto (ramping since Q2) and robotics, giving confidence that growth will continue beyond existing businesses.

Q : Quinn Bolton of Needham asked whether the company could raise its floor for enterprise data growth and offer thoughts on 2027. A : CFO Tony Balow said that given Q3 results and Q4 guidance, the company is comfortable raising its enterprise data growth floor to 150% year over year, up from 130%. He said it is too early to put a percentage on 2027, but all growth drivers remain intact, including customer diversification, module growth, and content gains, with Agentic AI workloads potentially an added tailwind.

Q : Rick Schafer of Oppenheimer asked about the storage and compute segment, including the split between DDR5, HDD, SSD, and PC vCore power, given PC units tracking down about 20% in the second half. A : CFO Tony Balow said DDR5 PMIC solutions are the biggest growth driver, with healthy growth also in HDD and SSD storage. Notebook strength is weaker due to downstream memory constraints, but he remains bullish long-term given good technology and share. He characterized the segment overall as roughly flattish to up a couple of points year over year, "a tale of two cities" with strong storage offset by a limited notebook TAM.

Q : Rick Schafer of Oppenheimer asked how the new CFO views OpEx growth and whether the company could see material operating leverage at 50%-60% top-line growth. A : CEO Michael Hsing said he never believed big R&D dollars equate to bigger results, calling it "inversely proportional" and emphasizing good ideas and people. CFO Tony Balow said the model won't change, but at current growth rates the company will fall below its OpEx model range because it simply cannot spend money that fast.

Q : Will Stein of Truist asked about gross margin, specifically whether the company could exceed its historical 10-20 basis points per quarter expansion given the growth. A : CFO Tony Balow said Q3 gross margin rose 10 basis points and Q4 guidance implies another 10 basis points, keeping the company squarely in its 55%-60% sweet spot with slow, methodical expansion. CEO Michael Hsing added that during capacity constraints the company does not gouge customers, aiming for consistent performance year over year.

Q : Chris Caso of Wolfe Research asked how the company is dealing with rising costs, including higher wafer prices, and whether it is passing costs along to customers. A : CEO Michael Hsing said the company absorbs some cost increases, does not raise prices, and shares cost increases with customers, noting customers "have a very long memory." CFO Tony Balow added that pricing is not a significant contributor to revenue growth; the focus is on not diluting gross margin.

Q : Tore Svanberg of Stifel asked for more detail on the 800-volt GaN product sampling, including the technology type and timing of revenue. A : CEO Michael Hsing said the GaN solution is based on in-house development, following earlier silicon carbide work, and customers can choose between GaN and SiC. He stressed caution on reliability, targeting below 1 ppm failures and wanting to ship roughly 50 million GaN units before declaring it proven. CFO Tony Balow said 800-volt architecture ramps are expected in late 2027 with more in 2028.

Q : Joshua Buchalter of TD Cowen asked about the diversity of the enterprise data business, including GPU versus ASIC and modules versus discrete. A : CEO Michael Hsing said modules are increasingly used because of high power demand across server applications. CFO Tony Balow said since mid-2025 there has been rapid growth in ASIC customers, primarily using modules with higher ASPs, and that AI-driven design tools will let the company address a longer tail of smaller customers that may become large ones.

Q : Sebastien Naji of William Blair asked about integrated voltage regulators and Analog Devices' acquisition of Empower, and whether MPS sees competitive risk in AI data centers. A : CEO Michael Hsing dismissed much of the discussion as "BS talks," saying MPS has its own solutions and can deliver whatever customers want. He noted GPU power levels and power delivery architectures evolve quickly, and the company does not discuss products until it clearly sees where revenue will come from.

Q : Kelsey Chia of Citi asked about the switching business, its contribution to communications growth, the 2027 ramp, and whether it is accretive to gross margins. A : CFO Tony Balow said switching is likely the fastest-growing sub-end market within communications on a percentage basis, though from a small base, and optical modules should remain a significant growth driver into 2027. On margins, he said all end markets operate around the corporate average, so growth in any one market should not take the company out of its 55%-60% model.

Q : Joe Quatrochi of Wells Fargo asked about working capital and go-to-market investments needed to support the expansion to $8 billion in capacity. A : CFO Tony Balow said the fabless model means the company does not have to "dig a hole and pour concrete," so he does not anticipate a large increase in capital intensity to support the capacity expansion, nor a change to the capital structure.

Q : Gary Mobley of StoneX asked whether the $8 billion capacity target exiting fiscal 2027 signals revenue velocity, and about inventory levels. A : CFO Tony Balow said the company is signaling that capacity will stay ahead of the business, as it has for 20 years, and that it sees demand coming, though it is too early to map capacity to a 2027 quarterly revenue ramp. On inventory, he said channel inventory remains at the lean end of the normal 5-8 week range and internal inventory is not limiting the business.

Positive Points

Adjusted gross margin reached 48.9%, the highest in over 25 years, expanding 530 basis points year-over-year despite investments and higher compensation.

Strong demand environment with book-to-bill significantly above one, backlog up more than 35% sequentially and more than doubling year-over-year.

Adjusted EBITDA margin exceeded 30% and is expected to reach ~31% in Q4, demonstrating strong operating leverage with EBITDA growth outpacing revenue growth.

Record operating and free cash flow of $224 million, enabling early repayment of the 2029 term loan and reducing net leverage to 2.9x, with further improvement expected.

Negative Points

Q1 2027 revenue is expected to decline mid-single-digit percentage sequentially due to seasonality and fewer selling days, despite year-over-year growth.

KSP facility remains dilutive to gross margins through most of 2027, and Colorado facility will be dilutive for about a year behind KSP, impacting near-term profitability.

Mainstream utilization remains the most underutilized part of the market, with memory tightness potentially capping near-term growth in mainstream applications.

Supply chain pinch points exist, notably in CMP pads where capacity is constrained, requiring selective CapEx to unlock.

No material pricing benefits were included in Q3 or Q4 guidance, and pricing actions are limited to new orders, not backlog, limiting near-term margin upside from pricing.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Melissa Weathers of Deutsche Bank asked what drove the upside in the quarter versus guidance incremental supply coming online or strengthening demand? A : CEO David Reeder attributed the revenue beat primarily to execution: demand was strong, and the team increased production and throughput beyond expectations, converting more backlog into revenue. Strength was broad-based, particularly in CapEx-related businesses. CFO Sukhi Nagesh added that the higher sales volume drove roughly 130 basis points of sequential gross margin expansion through factory absorption, yield initiatives, and lower inventory, scrap, and rework despite higher incentive compensation and labor investment.

Q : Melissa Weathers asked for initial thoughts on 2027, including MSI and CapEx growth. A : CEO David Reeder said the industry setup is "incredibly constructive" across all major demand drivers, with momentum exiting 2026 expected to extend well into 2027. Industry forecasts call for MSI growth broadly consistent with 2026, and all indications point to another strong double-digit growth year for both WFE and fab construction. More detail will come at the November 9 Capital Markets Day.

Q : Elizabeth Sun of Citi asked whether the strong growth can continue into next year given the growing backlog, and whether suppliers can keep up. A : CEO David Reeder said the lion's share of momentum is company performance rather than market-driven, with initiatives launched in late 2025 bearing fruit in 2026. He reiterated that Entegris has significantly more than $1 billion of incremental capacity in its network to support 2027 demand and beyond. The company is working closely with customers to validate demand and cascade it into the supply chain; some pinch points are inevitable but are being proactively identified and addressed.

Q : Aleksey Yefremov of Barclays asked about strong incremental margins and whether they are sustainable given investment needs, plus differences between segments. A : CFO Sukhi Nagesh said incremental gross margin of close to 60% and incremental EBITDA margin above 40% are in line with targets, driven largely by self-help execution productivity, yield, inventory and scrap control. He expects the trend to continue into next year. CEO David Reeder added that most of the sequential increase came from Entegris' ability to satisfy demand already in front of it, weighted somewhat toward CapEx-related revenue, with more unit pull than originally expected.

Q : Timothy Arcuri of UBS asked for a preview of the growth-versus-market rubric (historically 4 to 6 points of outgrowth) ahead of Capital Markets Day. A : CEO David Reeder said the framework will be "somewhat consistent" with what Entegris has articulated in the past, deferring fuller detail to the November 9 Capital Markets Day.

Q : Timothy Arcuri asked about the margin impact from the Colorado and KSP facilities and what clean gross margin would look like without the dilution. A : CFO Sukhi Nagesh said KSP reached gross profit breakeven in Q3, a big accomplishment, with an exciting ramp expected in Q4 and 2027. The Colorado facility is operational and producing samples, with revenue expected to begin next year roughly a 12-month lag behind KSP South. CEO David Reeder added that KSP remains dilutive to enterprise gross margins through most of 2027, becoming roughly neutral as the company exits 2027, with Colorado about a year behind; current results are fully burdened by both facilities.

Q : James Schneider of Goldman Sachs asked whether Entegris has enough capacity for revenue growth over the next couple of years given ramps in Colorado and KSP, and whether it is rethinking manufacturing footprint optimization. A : CEO David Reeder said Entegris has run the demand profile against internal capacity models and feels good about 2027 and 2028, with substantial capacity left to unlock through network optimization, centralized procurement, yield, and productivity. The company will selectively spend CapEx to relieve pinch points.

Q : Chris Parkinson of Wolfe Research asked about momentum and share position in MS and CMP, including slurries and pads, across geographies. A : CEO David Reeder noted broad geographic strength in Q3 North America up 22%, Taiwan up 41%, Southeast Asia up 51%, and Japan up 29% year over year.
