news.Title: TSM vs. MU: Which Semiconductor Stock Is the Better Buy Post-Earnings?
news.Content:
Despite delivering strong earnings and revenues that exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM, or TSMC, and Micron Technology MU have pulled back. TSM and MU have dipped 7% and 15.2%, respectively, so far this month, potentially offering investors an opportunity to gain exposure to the booming AI semiconductor market at more attractive prices.

TSMC delivered third-quarter 2026 earnings of $4.60 per ADR, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.4%, while revenues surged 41.2% year over year to $46.72 billion, surpassing estimates by 2.4%. Riding strong demand for advanced chips, particularly for AI applications, the company expects fourth-quarter revenues of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, signaling continued momentum into year-end.

Micron reported an impressive fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 performance, with adjusted EPS of $33.42 exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 5.73%. Revenues soared 379.3% year over year to $54.23 billion, beating estimates by 6.33%, as surging AI infrastructure investment fueled demand for memory products, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM).

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

While both companies continue to benefit from substantial earnings growth and the expanding AI ecosystem, broader concerns about intensifying Chinese competition in the memory market, rising U.S. inflation and interest-rate expectations and the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending weigh on semiconductor stocks.

Against this backdrop, the recent pullbacks in TSMC and Micron raise an important question — could this dip present a timely buying opportunity and which semiconductor stock should investors prioritize? Let's delve deeper.

Investment Case for TSM

TSMC is positioned to benefit from sustained AI infrastructure investment. In the third quarter, revenues surged 41.2% year over year, while EPS per ADR rose 57.5%, exceeding expectations. High-performance computing revenue rose 22% sequentially and accounted for 68% of total revenues, while advanced technologies contributed 79% of wafer revenues.

The outlook remains encouraging. TSMC expects fourth-quarter revenues of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, implying approximately 58% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Its financial position is also robust, with $126 billion in cash and marketable securities at quarter-end and approximately $28.8 billion in quarterly operating cash flow.

However, gross margin declined sequentially from 67.7% to 66.4% as 2-nanometer production ramped up. Overseas fabrication facilities are another source of pressure, with management expecting their gross-margin impact to widen to 3–4 percentage points over the next few years.

Story Continues

Investment Case for Micron

Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results were strong, showing the earnings potential of the AI-driven memory market. Revenues soared to $54.23 billion from $11.32 billion a year earlier, while adjusted EPS reached $33.42, up from $3.03. Core Data Center revenue climbed to $18 billion from $1.58 billion a year earlier, reflecting surging demand for memory to support AI infrastructure.

The company expects further acceleration in fiscal first-quarter 2027, forecasting revenues of $61.5 billion (+/- $1.5 billion) and adjusted EPS of $38.15 (+/- $1). This outlook indicates Micron's opportunity to capitalize on demand for high-bandwidth memory, server DRAM and other data-center products. Liquidity is another strength. Micron generated $43.97 billion in operating cash flow during the fourth quarter and ended fiscal 2026 with $73.48 billion in cash, marketable investments and restricted cash.

However, the principal risks are the sustainability of exceptional memory pricing and earnings, the capital required to expand manufacturing capacity, and the cyclical nature of the memory industry. Micron's forecast of continued growth is encouraging, but it needs to be analyzed whether demand and pricing can sustain such elevated profitability as supply expands.

MU Looks Cheaper Than TSM, but Is Its Low Valuation Sustainable?

TSMC trades at a forward 12-month P/E of 19.76, below its historical median of 21.14 and marginally above the Computer and Technology sector's 18.86. Micron appears significantly cheaper at 4.97X forward earnings versus its historical median of 10.07 and the sector's 18.86.

At present, MU offers greater valuation appeal following its recent pullback, while TSMC trades closer to its historical median. However, Micron's unusually low multiple may reflect cyclical memory earnings and peak-profitability concerns.

Our Take

Both TSMC and Micron sport a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), reflecting favorable earnings estimate revisions following their strong quarterly results and upbeat outlooks. While MU appears more attractively valued based on its forward P/E, its earnings remain more exposed to memory pricing fluctuations and industry cyclicality.

If investors had to choose just one, TSMC gets a marginal edge for its strong position in advanced chip manufacturing, diversified exposure to AI-driven demand across high-performance computing and other end markets and more established earnings visibility. Although margin pressures from advanced-node ramp-ups and overseas expansion warrant monitoring, TSMC offers a balance of AI-driven growth, competitive positioning and financial strength. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

news.Title: SCI Stock Surges More Than 111% in 6 Months: Can the Momentum Continue?
news.Content:
SCI Engineered Materials, Inc. 's SCIA investors have been gaining from the stock over the past few months. Shares of the Columbus, OH-based global supplier and manufacturer of advanced materials for Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) thin-film applications surged 111.3% in the past six months against the industry's 11.2% decline. It has also outperformed the sector and the S&P 500's gains of 6.6% and 6.4%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Two major developments of SCIA in recent months include the installation of a Plasma Spheroidization System or PSS (in August) and the announcement of its promising second-quarter 2026 results (in July).

In the second quarter, SCI reported record revenues and strong earnings growth, supported by higher raw material input costs, favorable product mix and increased volume. Higher revenues boosted gross profit, operating income and net income. However, gross margin contracted due to elevated raw material costs and product mix.

Management highlighted improving demand, new customer additions and growing traction in key markets. SCIA also expanded its workforce and ordered manufacturing equipment to support future growth, while interest in its specialized services continued to increase.

SCIA's Six-Month Price Comparison

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Over the past six months, the stock's performance has remained strong, outperforming its peers like Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL and Cirrus Logic, Inc. CRUS. Marvell Technology and Cirrus Logic's shares have gained 52.6% and lost 30.5%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Despite risks related to significant customer concentration, fluctuating raw material costs and tariff uncertainties, SCI's favorable share price movement reflects positive investor sentiment.

SCIA primarily serves the photonics industry, supplying advanced materials for PVD thin-film applications. Its target markets include aerospace, automotive, defense, glass, optical coatings and solar. SCI collaborates with end users and original equipment manufacturers to develop customized material solutions.

SCIA's Growth Opportunities

SCI's expanding order backlog reflects improving business activity and provides greater visibility into potential future revenues. The backlog increased both sequentially and year over year at the end of the second quarter, indicating a stronger pipeline of customer orders. This development could support production planning and help sustain business activity as pending orders are fulfilled. Continued execution of these orders remains important for maintaining growth momentum.

Story Continues

SCI's installation of a PSS in August expanded its advanced materials manufacturing capabilities. The equipment enables the production of high-purity spherical powders suitable for additive manufacturing, including those derived from high-value precious metals. These capabilities could create opportunities in aeronautical, defense and biomedical applications, where material quality and performance are critical. Planned targeted marketing initiatives may help SCIA establish a stronger presence in these specialized markets.

SCI's toll manufacturing business offers additional opportunities beyond conventional material sales. Its capabilities include diffusion bonding, indium bonding, powder processing and vacuum hot pressing, addressing customers' specialized production requirements. Revenue from toll manufacturing and related services improved in the previous fiscal year, alongside growing demand for engineering-related projects. These customized offerings could deepen customer relationships and support additional business opportunities.

SCI's Financial Strength

SCI's operating cash flow strengthened during the first half of the year, supported by improved profitability and higher customer deposits. Cash reserves and working capital also increased from the previous year-end, reinforcing its liquidity position. These resources provide flexibility to meet operational requirements, fund equipment investments and pursue growth initiatives. The availability of an undrawn credit facility further supports its financial flexibility without immediately increasing borrowing obligations.

SCIA's ongoing share repurchase program reflects its commitment to shareholder-focused capital allocation. The company continued purchasing common shares during the first half of the year, reducing its share count and supporting earnings per share. Continued repurchases, subject to management discretion and business requirements, could further benefit per-share financial metrics.

Challenges Ahead of SCIA

SCI relies heavily on a limited number of major customers, exposing revenues to potential order reductions, delays or cancellations. The absence of minimum purchase commitments further heightens uncertainty regarding future sales visibility and business stability. SCIA's gross margins remain vulnerable to elevated raw material costs and unfavorable product mix. Its ability to protect profitability depends partly on passing higher input costs to customers without adversely affecting demand or competitive positioning.

SCI Stock's Valuation

SCI's trailing 12-month EV/Sales of 1.2X is lower than the industry's average of 13.3X but is higher than its five-year median of 0.6X.

Marvell Technology and Cirrus Logic's trailing 12-month EV/Sales currently stand at 21.8X and 2.3X, respectively.

Our Final Take on SCIA

SCI's impressive stock rally reflects strengthening business fundamentals and expanding growth opportunities. Its improving order pipeline, broader manufacturing capabilities and healthy financial position provide a supportive backdrop for continued business growth. However, customer concentration and cost-related pressures remain important considerations that could influence future performance.

From a valuation perspective, SCIA appears relatively inexpensive compared with the broader industry, suggesting potential room for further appreciation. However, its premium to historical valuation levels indicates that investors are already assigning greater value to its improving business prospects. This raises expectations for future performance and leaves less room for operational disappointments.

Overall, SCIA's positive momentum could continue if the company sustains operational improvements and capitalizes on emerging opportunities. Existing shareholders may consider maintaining their positions, while prospective investors may consider waiting for a more attractive entry point, given the sharp rally and valuation premium relative to historical levels.

news.Title: Equities Bounce: 3 Top Ranked Stocks to Buy Now (TER, LRCX, ATI)
news.Content:
After a sharp bout of volatility, the stock market appears to be finding its footing ahead of a busy week of corporate earnings, central bank meetings and critical economic data.

While these selloffs can be painful, it is worth remembering just how consistently the market manages to climb the proverbial wall of worry. Whether it's concerns over AI, tariffs, elections or geopolitical tensions, the resilience of the US stock market has been remarkable.

And while it can be tempting to follow every headline and attempt to anticipate every possible scenario, investors are often better served by tuning out the noise and focusing on what matters most: buying high-quality companies at attractive valuations, particularly when earnings expectations are moving higher.

That combination of strong fundamentals, reasonable valuations and positive earnings revisions has historically been a powerful formula for long-term investment success.

With that in mind, three stocks currently stand out to me as particularly compelling opportunities. Teradyne (TER), Lam Research (LRCX) and ATI INC (ATI) are established industry leaders with impressive long-term track records, favorable earnings revision trends and exposure to powerful secular growth opportunities.

All three have delivered tremendous returns over the years, but recent market volatility has created potentially attractive entry points for investors looking to capitalize on the next leg higher.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Teradyne Stock: Exceptional Growth at a Fair Price

Teradyne is a leading provider of automated test equipment used to verify the performance and reliability of semiconductors, along with advanced robotics systems for industrial automation. The company is a major beneficiary of the AI infrastructure boom, as increasingly sophisticated chips and memory components require more extensive testing.

The growth outlook is exceptional. Analysts expect sales to surge 58.9% this year, followed by another 20.9% increase next year. Meanwhile, earnings are projected to grow at an annualized rate of 54.4% over the next three to five years.

Despite that tremendous growth outlook, Teradyne trades at 33.9x forward earnings, giving it a remarkably attractive PEG ratio of just 0.62 . That suggests investors are paying a relatively modest premium for the company's anticipated earnings growth.

With a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , Teradyne offers a compelling combination of powerful secular tailwinds, explosive earnings growth and a valuation that looks increasingly reasonable following the recent pullback.

Story Continues

Lam Research Stock: A Semiconductor Powerhouse

Lam Research is one of the world's leading suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, specializing in the technologies used to deposit, etch and clean materials on silicon wafers. Its equipment is essential to producing advanced logic chips and memory, making Lam a critical supplier to the ongoing AI infrastructure expansion.

The company is particularly well positioned to benefit from the memory supercycle, as demand for high-bandwidth memory and increasingly complex chip architectures drives greater investment in semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

Analysts expect sales to grow 49.7% this year and another 19% next year, while earnings are projected to compound at an annualized rate of 28.2% over the next three to five years.

Even with that impressive growth profile, Lam trades at just 24.8x forward earnings , giving it a PEG ratio of 0.88. For a company with such an entrenched competitive position and exposure to one of the market's strongest investment themes, that valuation looks attractive.

Lam currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , reinforcing its favorable earnings outlook and making it another compelling opportunity for long-term investors.

ATI Stock: Aerospace Growth at a Compelling Valuation

ATI INC is a leading producer of high-performance specialty materials, including titanium alloys, nickel-based superalloys and advanced components used in aerospace, defense and other demanding industrial applications.

The company occupies an attractive position in the aerospace supply chain, providing critical materials used in jet engines, aircraft structures and defense systems. Rising commercial aircraft production, growing defense spending and demand for next-generation engines create a long runway for growth.

ATI's earnings outlook is particularly impressive, with analysts forecasting annualized EPS growth of 32.8% over the next three to five years.

Shares currently trade at 32.1x forward earnings, giving the stock a PEG ratio just below 1.0 . While that earnings multiple might initially appear elevated for an industrial company, the anticipated growth rate makes the valuation considerably more attractive.

ATI also carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , reflecting positive earnings estimate revisions and strengthening expectations for the business.

Should Investors Buy Shares in LRCX, ATI and TER?

Market volatility can be unsettling, but it also creates opportunities to buy exceptional businesses at more attractive prices.

Teradyne, Lam Research and ATI operate in different corners of the economy, yet all three share several important characteristics: strong competitive positions, exposure to durable secular growth trends and impressive long-term earnings prospects.

More importantly, their valuations appear reasonable relative to their projected earnings growth, with all three sporting PEG ratios below 1.0.

Of course, none is immune to a broader market correction, and those ambitious growth forecasts will need to be met. But with favorable Zacks Ranks, powerful industry tailwinds and compelling growth-adjusted valuations, TER, LRCX and ATI deserve serious consideration from investors looking to take advantage of the recent market volatility.

news.Title: Coherent vs. Arm Holdings: Which Tech Stock Offers More Upside Now?
news.Content:
Both Coherent Corp. COHR and Arm Holdings ARM are technology companies whose business models focus heavily on advanced hardware and innovation at the core of modern computing.

ARM is best known for its semiconductor IP, providing chip architectures that power a vast share of smartphones, servers and increasingly AI-focused processors. COHR, on the other hand, operates in the realm of photonics, lasers and optical components, enabling the ultra-fast connectivity and precision manufacturing that form the backbone of today's data and electronics industries.

The two companies compete for investor interest in high-growth, innovation-driven segments of the tech infrastructure ecosystem.

COHR's Case

The AI opportunity extends well beyond the construction of new data centers. Existing facilities must continually upgrade as newer GPUs, switches and networking platforms require greater bandwidth. As AI clusters expand, more connections are needed among processors, racks, switches and facilities, increasing the importance of high-speed optical networking.

This trend plays directly into Coherent's strengths. Its portfolio includes indium phosphide lasers, VCSELs, silicon photonics, specialty fiber, detectors and micro-optics. That broad technological base gives the company multiple ways to benefit as data-center operators shift toward faster, denser and more power-efficient network architectures.

Continued improvements in AI models, falling inference costs and broader commercial adoption could further stimulate computing requirements. As AI becomes embedded in more applications, network capacity should become increasingly critical alongside computing power.

PhotonLink could strengthen Coherent's position by moving the company further beyond individual components and into integrated optical subsystems. Combining internally developed technologies with integration, assembly and testing capabilities enables Coherent to capture a greater portion of the value created within an AI system.

This approach could also deepen customer relationships. Replacing a single component supplier is generally simpler than switching a provider whose subsystem has been designed and qualified within a broader architecture.

Coherent is also positioned across multiple technology pathways, including conventional pluggable optics, co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics and chip-to-chip connectivity. This diversified exposure reduces dependence on any single optical architecture becoming the dominant industry standard.

Story Continues

ARM's Case

The accelerating pace of AI infrastructure development presents a significant opportunity for Arm. Technology companies are committing substantial resources to build data centers, develop advanced processors and expand computing capacity to support increasingly sophisticated AI applications.

AI developer Anthropic's ambitious infrastructure spending plans underscore the massive investments required to support next-generation AI models. Meanwhile, major cloud providers, including Alphabet GOOG and Microsoft MSFT, continue investing heavily in AI infrastructure and computing technologies. These investments should support sustained demand for advanced semiconductor architectures.

Arm Holdings stands to benefit from this transition through its energy-efficient processor designs, which are increasingly relevant to cloud computing, AI inference and edge applications. As computing workloads become more demanding, the need for processors capable of delivering higher performance without excessive power consumption should strengthen the company's market opportunities.

Additionally, the growing adoption of Arm-based architectures across data centers could diversify its revenue sources beyond smartphones, supporting a more balanced long-term growth profile.

The emergence of autonomous AI agents is creating additional opportunities for central processing units (CPUs). Unlike conventional AI applications primarily focused on model training, agentic systems require considerable general-purpose processing capabilities to coordinate tasks, manage workflows and execute instructions.

This development could accelerate demand for energy-efficient CPUs alongside specialized AI accelerators. Arm Holdings' expanding processor portfolio positions it to capture opportunities as enterprises deploy more sophisticated AI systems across cloud environments.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for COHR & ARM?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for COHR's fiscal 2027 sales and EPS indicates year-over-year growth of 50% and 68%, respectively. EPS estimates have been trending flat over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ARM's current-year sales suggests 22% year-over-year growth, while EPS is expected to grow 24%. EPS estimates have been trending flat over the past 60 days.

COHR's Valuation Reflects Strong Growth Potential

While COHR appears attractively valued with a forward 12-month P/E of 20.34X versus its median of 39.95X, ARM's higher forward P/E of 82.79X, below its median of 145.78X, reflects investor confidence in its strong earnings growth potential.

Coherent Stands Out as the Better Placed

Coherent appears better positioned than Arm Holdings, supported by its accelerating exposure to AI-driven optical networking demand, diversified photonics portfolio and expanding opportunities in integrated optical subsystems. Growing investments in AI infrastructure and increasing demand for high-speed connectivity should strengthen Coherent's long-term growth prospects. Although Arm benefits from rising adoption of energy-efficient processors across data centers and AI applications, its elevated valuation leaves less room for potential disappointments. Coherent's stronger projected earnings and revenue growth, coupled with its relatively attractive valuation, gives it an edge.

COHR and ARM currently carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) each. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Amkor Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates Amid Communications Weakness
news.Content:
Amkor Technology AMKR reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of 76 cents per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.8%. Earnings rose 49% from 51 cents a year ago, reflecting a richer mix of high-value packaging despite weakness in Communications.

Net sales of $1.99 billion increased 0.2% year over year but missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.34%. Computing revenues climbed 25% sequentially to a record as the company scaled its high-density fan-out (HDFO) CPU program.

AMKR's Q3 Product Mix Shifts

Advanced products generated $1.63 billion in third-quarter sales, down 3.1% from $1.68 billion a year earlier. Mainstream products contributed $359 million, up 18.5% from $303 million. Advanced products include flip-chip, memory and wafer-level processing services, while mainstream offerings primarily comprise wirebond packaging and related testing.

Packaging services accounted for 88% of sales, down from 89% in the year-ago quarter, while test services represented 12%, up from 11%. Revenue concentration eased as the top 10 customers contributed 66% of sales compared with 73% a year earlier.

Amkor Technology, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Amkor Technology, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Amkor Technology, Inc. Quote

Amkor's End Markets Show Diverging Trends

Computing represented 26% of quarterly sales versus 19% a year ago. Revenues in this market grew 37% year over year, supported by data center demand and the HDFO CPU ramp. An additional HDFO CPU program for a hyperscaler began ramping during the quarter. Two new 2.5D programs for networking and data centers are expected to start ramping in the fourth quarter.

Automotive and Industrial also posted 37% year-over-year revenue growth, accounting for 22% of sales versus 16% last year. Demand for advanced driver-assistance systems, in-car computing and industrial applications drove a 7% sequential increase.

Communications contributed 37% of revenues, down from 51% a year ago, and sales fell 8% sequentially. The transition of system-in-package (SiP) production to Vietnam, memory constraints and changes in customer build patterns weighed on demand. Consumer sales rose 10% sequentially, although component shortages affected premium smartphones and wearables.

AMKR's Margins Widen on Richer Packaging Mix

Gross profit increased 27.8% year over year to $363.5 million. Gross margin expanded 400 basis points to 18.3%, aided by stronger Computing and Automotive contributions. Lower material costs as a percentage of sales helped, although foreign-exchange pressures and the July earthquake at Amkor's Japan facility reduced the sequential margin by approximately 60 basis points.

Operating expenses totaled $138.8 million, up from $125.6 million a year ago. Operating income rose 41.4% to $224.7 million, lifting operating margin to 11.3% from 8%. Net income attributable to Amkor increased 50.6% to $190.6 million. EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, reached $435 million compared with $340 million a year earlier.

Story Continues

AMKR's Balance Sheet & Cash Flow Details

As of Sept. 30, 2026, Amkor held $2.4 billion in cash and short-term investments against $2.5 billion in total debt. Liquidity totaled $3.4 billion, and debt was 1.7 times trailing 12-month EBITDA. The company repurchased approximately $32 million of shares during the quarter.

For the first nine months of 2026, operating cash flow reached $868.3 million versus $451.1 million in the year-ago period. Payments for property, plant and equipment increased to $1.24 billion from $472.5 million, reflecting a stepped-up investment cycle.

AMKR's Q4 Outlook Balances Growth and Weakness

For the fourth quarter of 2026, management expects revenues between $1.9 billion and $2 billion, gross margin of 18% to 19% and net income of $160 million to $185 million. Earnings are forecast at 65-75 cents per share.

Computing revenues are projected to grow at a low-double-digit sequential rate, while Automotive and Industrial should advance at a low-single-digit rate. Communications revenues are expected to decline by a high-single-digit percentage, with Consumer sales falling by a mid-teens percentage amid continuing component shortages. Management expects Computing to grow more than 50% year over year in the fourth quarter and more than 30% for 2026 overall.

Amkor's Global Packaging Expansion Accelerates

Amkor narrowed its full-year 2026 capital spending forecast to approximately $2.5 billion. Management anticipates higher expenditures in 2027 as it expands capacity in Arizona, Korea and Vietnam, with customer advance payments supporting investment.

The company's two Arizona campus phases entail an estimated $12 billion investment and more than 90,000 square meters of clean-room space. Phase 1 construction remains on track for completion by the end of 2027, while Phase 2 is slated to break ground in late 2027. In Korea, new facilities will support advanced packaging for data center customers. Management said agreements involving advance payments have been executed with about a dozen customers, improving visibility into future capacity needs.

AMKR's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

Amkor currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

ASE Technology ASX, Fortinet FTNT and Microchip MCHP are among the better-ranked stocks that investors can consider in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. Currently, ASE Technology sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), while Fortinet and Microchip carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) each. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

ASE Technology's shares have surged 147.9% year to date. ASX is scheduled to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 29.

Fortinet's shares have climbed 130.9% year to date. FTNT is slated to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 28.

Microchip's shares have gained 19.2% year to date. MCHP is scheduled to report its fiscal second-quarter 2027 results on Nov. 5, 2026.

news.Title: GLW Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Optical Communication Growth
news.Content:
Corning Incorporated GLW reported third-quarter 2026 core earnings of 91 cents per share, up 36% year over year. The figure surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 89 cents by 2.25%. Core revenues increased 19% to $5.08 billion and beat the consensus mark of $5.03 billion by 1.03%.

Growth was primarily driven by Optical Communications, where revenues surged 44% amid strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Enterprise Networks sales jumped 84%, while generative AI product sales more than doubled. Improved operating margins further supported earnings growth.

Corning Incorporated Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Corning Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Corning Incorporated Quote

GLW's Optical Sales Surge on AI Infrastructure Demand

Optical Communications remained Corning's largest growth engine, with sales climbing 44% year over year to $2.38 billion. Segment net income surged 80% to $532 million, reflecting strong demand and improved profitability.

Enterprise Networks revenues increased 84% to $1.53 billion, supported by accelerating adoption of optical connectivity solutions for AI data centers. Carrier Network sales grew 4% to $854 million, driven by demand for data center interconnect solutions.

Corning also secured four long-term, multibillion-dollar customer agreements during the quarter, including agreements with Verizon and AT&T. These commitments support the company's plans to expand manufacturing capacity and capture rising demand for optical infrastructure.

Corning's Glass Business Faces Market Headwinds

Glass Innovations generated revenues of $1.51 billion, down 3% year over year. Segment net income declined 10% to $328 million, reflecting challenging conditions across key consumer electronics markets.

Higher memory prices weighed on demand for televisions, notebooks and smartphones. Nevertheless, the company continued executing its "More Corning" strategy, increasing content adoption and outperforming underlying end markets.

Automotive revenues advanced 4% to $470 million, while segment net income slipped 1% to $67 million. Recovery in the North American Class 8 truck market offset weakness in light-duty vehicles, where market volumes declined 3%.

GLW's Solar Sales Rise Despite Production Challenges

Solar revenues climbed 37% year over year to $436 million as the company continued ramping production across its wafer and module facilities. However, the segment recorded a net loss of $7 million against a net income of $30 million in the prior-year quarter.

Production ramp-up progressed more slowly than anticipated. Management expects improving productivity to support higher output and profitability. Favorable U.S. trade developments are also strengthening demand for domestically manufactured solar products.

Life Sciences and Emerging Growth Businesses reported revenues of $290 million, up 1%. The segment recorded a net loss of $28 million compared with a loss of $15 million a year earlier, primarily reflecting investments in emerging growth programs.

Story Continues

Corning Expands Core Margins and Profitability

Core gross margin expanded 150 basis points year over year to 40.5%. Core operating margin improved 310 basis points to 22.7%, while core operating income increased to $1.15 billion from $838 million.

Core net income rose 36% to $795 million. Core return on invested capital improved 330 basis points to 16.7%, reflecting stronger returns from the company's operating and investment activities.

On a GAAP basis, operating income increased to $911 million from $589 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses declined to $563 million from $624 million, while research, development and engineering expenses rose to $314 million from $280 million.

GLW's Cash Flow Strength Supports Expansion

Corning generated $1.06 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, compared with $784 million a year earlier. Adjusted free cash flow reached $661 million, up from $535 million in the prior-year period.

Capital expenditures totaled $545 million as the company expanded capacity to address growing customer demand. Adjusted free cash flow reached $2.27 billion during the first nine months of 2026.

Cash and cash equivalents stood at $2.54 billion as of Sept. 30, 2026, while long-term debt totaled $7.27 billion.

Corning Projects Strong Q4 Growth Under Springboard Plan

For the fourth quarter of 2026, management expects core sales between $5.2 billion and $5.3 billion, representing approximately 19% year-over-year growth. Core earnings are projected between 96 cents and $1 per share, implying growth of roughly 36%.

The company expects full-year capital expenditures of approximately $2 billion and a core tax rate of around 18.5%.

Under its upgraded 20-30-40 Springboard Plan, Corning aims to reach a $30 billion annualized sales run rate by the end of 2028 and $40 billion by the end of 2030. Management expects earnings to grow faster than sales, supported by AI infrastructure expansion, solar investments and long-term customer partnerships.

Zacks Rank

news.Title: Arm vs. Western Digital: Which Tech Stock Is the Better Buy in November?
news.Content:
The surge in artificial intelligence (AI) has forced investors to choose between infrastructure providers. Choosing between Arm (NASDAQ:ARM) and Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) involves weighing architectural licensing against physical data storage solutions.

Arm provides the blueprints for power-efficient processors found in nearly every smartphone and increasingly in data centers. Western Digital manufactures the physical hardware used to store vast amounts of digital information. While both benefit from rising compute demands, they operate at opposite ends of the hardware stack with very different financial profiles.

The case for Arm

Arm designs and licenses processor architecture and software to a wide range of partners among semiconductor stocks . The company targets several high-growth markets including mobile devices, automotive systems, and cloud-based artificial intelligence. While its technology powers billions of devices, Arm does not disclose specific major customers in its regulatory filings.

Through the July 2026 quarter, trailing 12-month (TTM) revenue reached nearly $5.2 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 25% over the previous year. The company reported net income of roughly $1 billion for the period. This resulted in a net margin of close to 20%.

As of its July 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.1x. This metric measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, suggesting the company uses very little borrowed money. The current ratio, a liquidity measure indicating whether a company can cover short-term obligations, was nearly 5.3x.

TTM free cash flow, calculated as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures, reached approximately $1.5 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 69% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow.

The case for Western Digital

Western Digital specializes in hard disk drive technology and data storage solutions for cloud providers and retail consumers. The cloud end market is the most critical segment for the business, accounting for nearly 89% of net revenue as of its latest annual report filed in 2026. Customer concentration is a significant factor, as the top ten customers account for roughly 73% of net revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

TTM revenue through the October quarter reached nearly $14.5 billion, a substantial increase of approximately 43% from the prior year. The company reported net income of $10 billion during this period. This led to a net margin of approximately 69%, representing a sharp increase from previous fiscal years.

Story Continues

Based on its October 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.1x. The current ratio stood at approximately 1.4x, suggesting the company maintains enough short-term assets to cover its immediate debts.

TTMF free cash flow reached approximately $4.3 billion for the fiscal year.

Risk profile comparison

Arm faces competition from alternative architectures, such as the open-source RISC-V standard. Because the company relies on licensing its intellectual property, any shift in designer preferences could impact its long-term royalty revenue. Additionally, the business remains sensitive to the cyclical nature of the global smartphone and consumer electronics markets.

Western Digital deals with high revenue concentration, making it vulnerable to demand shifts from a small number of cloud customers. The company relies on a limited number of single-source suppliers for critical components, which creates potential supply chain disruptions. Furthermore, failing to transition successfully to new storage technologies like Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR) could hurt its competitive position.

Valuation comparison

Western Digital appears to be the more value-oriented choice because its Forward P/E , which compares price to future earnings estimates, is significantly lower than Arm's.

The P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Metric

Western Digital

Forward P/E

101.2x

14.1x

P/S ratio

46.3x

8.9x

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Which stock would I buy right now?

Western Digital is growing at a higher rate, benefiting from a strong AI-driven demand cycle. But it basically sells a commodity product that can cause sharp swings in selling prices, which can weigh on financials. I would buy and hold Arm for its more consistent operating history and opportunities to gain share in the data center market.

Agentic AI runs on CPUs, which could drive significant growth for Arm. Importantly, Arm doesn't manufacture chips. It designs them and then profits from royalties and licensing fees on every chip shipped using its chip architecture. That's an attractive business model and is why the stock generally gets rated at a high P/E.

Arm's revenue has grown at a compound annual rate of 25% over the past three years. CEO Rene Haas mentioned on the July 2026 earnings call that the addressable market for CPUs was estimated at $100 billion earlier in 2026 but could now be approaching $200 billion.

Overall, I would rather pay up for a more consistent business that generates profits from licensing fees, which is why I would rather buy Arm today to hold for the long term.

news.Title: These 2 Chip Stocks Are Piper Sandler’s Top Picks Into 2027
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Piper Sandler maintains a positive outlook on AI supply chain fundamentals despite ongoing market uncertainty, identifying two top picks in the chip sector heading into 2027. The broker expects compute companies to report slightly better results than consensus estimates, with demand visibility extending beyond two years and supply constraints persisting through 2028.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

All fundamental data points across the AI supply chain remain positive, according to Piper Sandler. The firm anticipates companies will deliver consistent messaging around three key themes: demand remains very strong with visibility extending two-plus years, the industry faces severe supply constraints through 2028, and pricing continues to increase.

While companies have already provided some outlook guidance for 2027, analysts expect them to reiterate these projections during upcoming earnings reports.

ARM Holdings

ARM ranks as one of Piper Sandler's two top chip stock picks. Investors appear to be positioning long on ARM to capitalize on the Agentic AI tailwind, though concerns remain about finding upside given supply constraints, the broker said.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The key focus centers on whether ARM can secure additional supply for its Silicon AGI business in 2027-28. Piper Sandler views the Softbank Accelerator opportunity as the main catalyst for ARM, though timing remains unclear on when additional details will emerge.

Broadcom

Broadcom represents Piper Sandler's second top pick, though the stock faces heated debate heading into earnings results. Investor concerns focus on gross margin trajectory into 2027, driven by rising HBM memory costs.

While peer Nvidia has disclosed a trough level for next year, Broadcom has not yet provided similar guidance. This remains the primary overhang on the stock, with the share loss story related to MediaTek already absorbed by the market.

Piper Sandler believes management providing a framework on gross margins for 2027 would eliminate the bear case and allow the stock to perform. The broker expects slightly better results and guidance versus consensus, but only a reiteration of the fiscal year 2027 outlook, implying revenues up 60% year-over-year to $170 billion.

news.Title: TSM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Strong AI Demand and Expansion
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM emphasized sustained artificial intelligence demand, accelerating capacity expansion and growing advanced-node adoption during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call.

Management raised its full-year revenue growth outlook while acknowledging manufacturing cost pressures, overseas expansion expenses and uncertainties in consumer markets.

TSM reported third-quarter earnings of $4.60 per ADR, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.45. Revenues totaled $46.72 billion, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $45.62 billion. Revenues increased 41.2% year over year.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. Quote

TSM Sees Robust AI Demand Beyond Accelerators

Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei emphasized that AI-related semiconductor demand remains exceptionally strong, supported by accelerating adoption of agentic AI, open-source models and advanced computing infrastructure.

During the Q&A, a Citigroup analyst questioned whether infrastructure constraints could affect growth. Wei indicated that AI accelerator growth could exceed the previously discussed mid-to-high 50% compound annual growth rate for 2024-2029.

Wei also highlighted increasing demand for CPUs and networking chips. However, management clarified that CPUs remain outside its narrowly defined AI accelerator growth projections.

TSMC Raises Revenue Outlook Despite Market Risks

Management now expects full-year 2026 revenue growth of approximately 44% in U.S. dollar terms, reflecting strong demand for leading-edge manufacturing technologies.

For the fourth quarter, TSM projects revenues between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, representing approximately 14% sequential growth at the midpoint. Gross margin is projected at 65-67%, with operating margin at 56.5-58.5%.

CFO Wendell Huang attributed margin pressure to the steep 2-nanometer ramp and overseas manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, Wei cautioned that rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainty continue to challenge price-sensitive consumer markets.

TSM Maintains Elevated Capital Spending Plans

Huang reiterated the company's 2026 capital expenditure budget of $60 billion to $64 billion, reflecting its commitment to expanding manufacturing capacity.

Management expects capital spending during 2026-2028 to be significantly higher than during the preceding three years.

Story Continues

During the Q&A, a UBS analyst questioned whether equipment inflation would increase future investment requirements. Huang acknowledged rising equipment, material and labor costs but emphasized that long-term customer demand remains the principal investment driver. He maintained that revenue growth should outpace capital spending growth.

TSMC Accelerates Advanced-Node Capacity Expansion

Wei outlined an unprecedented global expansion involving nearly 20 manufacturing facilities under development, including 13 leading-edge and advanced packaging facilities in Taiwan.

The company's 2-nanometer technology accounted for 8% of third-quarter wafer revenue. Management expects annual N2-family capacity to more than double in 2027, supported by smartphone and high-performance computing applications.

TSMC also plans additional 3-nanometer manufacturing capacity in Taiwan while preparing its A14 technology for risk production in 2027 and volume production in 2028. Wei indicated that A14 customer engagement already exceeds comparable early N2 activity.

TSM Evaluates Additional U.S. Manufacturing Opportunities

Wei confirmed that TSMC is evaluating manufacturing expansion beyond Arizona, including potential opportunities in Texas.

Responding to a JPMorgan analyst, Wei acknowledged discussions involving the proposed Terafab project. He clarified that any manufacturing collaboration would require TSMC operational control, although ownership arrangements remain under discussion.

Meanwhile, Arizona's second fab is scheduled to begin 3-nanometer volume production in the third quarter of 2027. Huang expects overseas manufacturing to dilute gross margin by 3-4 percentage points during the latter portion of the company's five-year expansion period.

TSMC Strengthens Advanced Packaging Support

Wei emphasized advanced packaging as another critical capacity priority amid increasing chip complexity and customer requirements.

He reported successful production of five-reticle-size packaging solutions, with development progressing toward nine- and 14-reticle-size configurations. He identified CoWoS as customers' preferred packaging solution.

During the Q&A, Wei also discussed collaboration with GlobalFoundries to support interposer supply. The arrangement addresses back-end capacity shortages while supporting customers' product introduction schedules.

TSM Balances Expansion With Profitability

Management's overarching message centered on meeting structural semiconductor demand through accelerated investment, manufacturing productivity improvements and capacity optimization.

Although Wei expressed confidence in the company's technology leadership and customer demand, management maintained a disciplined approach to capacity planning, factoring in infrastructure availability, supply-chain constraints and long-term profitability.

Zacks Rank and Style Scores Signal Mixed Fundamentals

TSM currently carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), indicating favorable earnings estimate revision trends and stronger near-term performance potential. Its Momentum Score of B supports this assessment, while its Value Score of F and Growth Score of C indicate less favorable characteristics in those categories. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

The stock's VGM Score of D reflects weaker combined value, growth and momentum characteristics despite its favorable Zacks Rank. The Zacks Rank can change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest results.

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. ( AMD , Financials ), the semiconductor company, was among the stocks trimmed by Cathie Wood's ARK Invest as the firm rotated capital toward electric air taxi companies.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with AMD.

ARK sold 24,796 AMD shares worth about $13.2 million and 21,894 Taiwan Semiconductor shares worth about $9.3 million.

The AMD sale comes ahead of third-quarter earnings on Nov. 3. Wall Street expects earnings of $1.94 per share on revenue of $13.08 billion.

Despite the sale, analysts remain bullish. Susquehanna recently raised its AMD target to $620, while Bernstein kept an Outperform rating with a $650 target.

ARK used part of the proceeds to add to Archer Aviation and Joby Aviation.

The firm bought about $4.8 million of Archer shares and roughly $2 million of Joby.

Both companies are still working toward commercial electric air taxi operations, making them considerably earlier-stage investments than AMD or TSMC.

For investors, the trades show ARK leaning away from semiconductor winners after large gains and adding exposure to a more speculative transportation theme.

The next catalyst is AMD's Nov. 3 earnings report and continued progress toward commercial service at Archer and Joby.

news.Title: 晶豪科第3季獲利創新高　每股純益36.79元
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中新竹2026年10月27日電）記憶體廠晶豪科 (3006) 第3季毛利率攀高至77.44%，較第2季揚升8.74個百分點，歸屬母公司淨利突破新台幣100億元大關，達到107.59億元，創下歷史新高，每股純益36.79元。

記憶體市場供不應求，產品價格持續高漲，晶豪科第3季營收突破200億元，達到221.5億元，創下歷史新高，較第2季增加58.8%。

晶豪科第3季毛利率達到77.44%，較第2季上揚8.74個百分點，第3季歸屬母公司淨利107.59億元，季增約82%，每股純益36.79元。

晶豪科累計前3季營收433.63億元，年增3.439倍，毛利率69.62%，較去年同期揚升60.08個百分點，歸屬母公司淨利187.3億元，每股純益64.54元。

記憶體廠多數預期，第4季記憶體市場可望維持供不應求態勢，產品價格也將延續上揚趨勢，營運仍將有不錯表現。

news.Title: 智原Q4營收估季持平；明年三大產品線齊向上
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-27 16:42:18 黃立安 發佈

ASIC設計服務暨矽智財(IP)廠智原(3035)今(27)日舉行法說會，總經理王國雍表示，今(2026)年第四季IP業績可望續創高，NRE業務也將顯著成長，不過量產業務可能下滑，整體單季營收將較第三季的36.6億元約略持平，毛利率則回升至45%。2027年營收將成長兩位數，包括IP、NRE和量產三大產品線均可望同步向上。此外，近期先進製程成功接下美國客戶2奈米雲端AI應用專案，總金額高達數千萬美元，成為智原史上最大規模專案。

針對該2奈米專案，王國雍表示，此為首個2奈米環繞閘極(GAA)製程專案，原本客戶計劃採用4奈米製程，但考量到產品生命週期，決定改採2奈米製程，且專案總金額達數千萬美元，預計2027年上半年將有第一筆收入入帳，後續依進度認列，此案是智原史上最大金額的專案，將採用三星的晶圓代工，另外還與聯電(2303)及記憶體廠等夥伴合作。

王國雍指出，此項AI專案對公司深具指標性意義，並於四個面向均創下公司紀錄-設計製程、設計複雜度、NRE金額規模及高階封裝技術，同時此除證明客戶對公司設計能力的肯定及信賴，亦為後續先進製程及高階封裝接單及推廣建立了重要的指標性案例。

回顧第三季表現，智原在量產業務帶動下，單季營收達36.6億元，不僅優於原先預期，更逆勢季增11%、年增13%；毛利率42.5%，季減2.7個百分點、年增9.3個百分點；營業利益為2.1億元，季減21%，雖較第二季小幅回落，但受到營收規模擴大及毛利結構改善，年增達443%；營業利益率5.8%；稅後淨利2.8億元，季增41%，年增84%，EPS為1.07元。

智原2026年第三季營運創下多項紀錄，包括IP營收創歷史新高，量產及單季合併營收雙雙寫下歷年同期新高。

以產品別來看，IP營收4.5億元，季增4%，年增8%，創下歷史新高；NRE收入為3.1億元，季減31%，年減37%；量產營收則為第三季季主要成長動能，不僅MCU相關營收再創單季新高，ASIC量產在AI相關高階封裝專案出貨動能加速下，亦同步走揚，推升量產營收季增20%，年增25%，達29.1億元，創下歷年同期高點。

力成Q4及明年營運看正向；漲價效益續顯

《美股主題週報》ASIC與GPU的競合—NVDA、AVGO、CDNS

news.Title: 智原第三季每股賺1.07元，成功搶下2奈米AI專案明年上半年開始入帳
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】智原(3035)今日召開法說會，公布第三季成績單，單季本業部分，量產業務大增，業外收益也同時進補，帶動單季每股淨利1.07元，展望第四季，估營收與前季持平，IP持續成長創新高，NRE顯著成長，量產業務下滑，至於第四季毛利率估為45%。產線斬獲部分，獲得國際客戶開案，採用2奈米GAA製程，承接瞄準雲端AI應用之大型專案，預計2027年上半年會開始有收益。智原第三季受惠量產業務大幅成長，單季合併營收達36.64億元，季增10.6%、年增13.2%；營收中，IP營收4.48億元，季增3.5%、年增8.4%；NRE營收3.09億元，季減31.3%、年減37.1%；量產業務營收則達29.07億元，季增19.6%、年增24.7%，成為推升整體營收成長的主要動能。

獲利方面，智原第三季營業毛利15.57億元，季增3.9%、年增44.9%；毛利率42.5%，雖低於第二季的45.2%，但仍明顯高於去年同期的33.2%。第三季營業利益率為5.8%，低於第二季的8.2%，但優於去年同期的1.3%。但智原第三季業外收入達到2.66億元，季增138.8%、年增53.2%，主因業外轉投資評價利益挹注，挹注第三季本期淨利增至3.69億元，季增29.2%、年增124.1%。第三季歸屬母公司業主稅後淨利為2.79億元，季增40.8%、年增83.8%，單季每股淨利1.07元，。

展望第四季，公司自估，營收與第三季相比，大致約持平，毛利率估為45%。產線方面，IP持續成長創新高，NRE顯著成長，量產業務下滑。至於在產品線的斬獲部分，智原總經理王國雍透露，藉由和聯電(2303)、三星，以及記憶體廠等廠商的合作，公司已經獲得總金額數千萬美元、美系業者的2奈米AI雲端專案訂單。而整體2027年，智原看法樂觀，營收會年增雙位數百分比，三大產線都會年增。

news.Title: 智原攜手三星、聯電　搶下美國2奈米雲端AI專案訂單
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中新竹2026年10月27日電）特殊應用晶片廠智原 (3035) 總經理王國雍今天表示，透過與三星（Samsung）、聯電 (2303) 和記憶體廠等夥伴合作，成功搶下美國廠商2奈米雲端人工智慧（AI）專案訂單，總金額高達數千萬美元，是智原史上最大規模專案。

智原今天召開線上法人說明會，王國雍說，智原客戶委託設計（NRE）業務在先進製程有新斬獲，成功搶下2奈米環繞閘極（GAA）製程雲端AI專案訂單，這對智原意義重大，是最先進的製程，也是第1個2奈米GAA製程專案，複雜度也最高。

王國雍表示，原本客戶計劃採用4奈米製程，基於延長產品生命週期考量，決定改採2奈米製程；這專案總金額達數千萬美元，預計2027年上半年將有第1筆收入入帳，後續依進度認列，是智原史上最大金額的專案。

王國雍說，智原具備設計以及統籌協調能力，是能夠搶下2奈米專案的關鍵，此案將採用三星的晶圓代工，另外還與聯電及記憶體廠等夥伴合作。

智原第3季受惠量產業務優於預期，加上矽智財（IP）業績創下歷史新高，整體第3季營收攀高至新台幣36.64億元，季增10.6%，為歷年同期新高。

受產品組合變化影響，低毛利的量產業務比重攀升，智原第3季毛利率42.5%，較第2季下滑2.7個百分點，營業利益2.14億元，季減20.8%，受惠業外轉投資評價利益挹注，智原第3季歸屬母公司淨利2.79億元，季增40.8%，每股純益1.07元。

展望未來，智原預期，第4季IP業績可望持續成長創高，NRE業務將顯著成長，量產業務可能下滑，整體第4季營收將較第3季持平，毛利率約45%。

王國雍表示，2027年營收將成長2位數，包括IP、NRE和量產3大產品線2027年營收可望同步成長。
